##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who drink Soma according to the regulation of time, together with your friends the Maruts and with the gods, drink the Soma pressed by us. Because you served the Maruts, and because the Maruts served you, you became able to slay Vṛtra; those same Maruts produced in you the strength that destroys enemies.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Drinker of the Soma in season, drink with your divine friends the Maruts, the Soma that is presented by us; those Maruts whose aid you have enjoyed (in battle), and who, following you, have given you the strength whereby you have slain Vritra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The words ऋतुपाः (*ṛtupāḥ*) and ऋतुभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ*) must be explained according to the context. For the word ऋतु (*ṛtu*) the meaning "fixed state" or "regulation of time" is current. From the offering of oblations duly, in accordance with such a fixed ṛtu-dharma, the word ऋत्विक् (*ṛtvik*) is formed. Or, according to some, the word ऋतु (*ṛtu*) means a vessel in which oblations are offered. As indicated in "को अग्निमाट्टे हविषा धृतेन सुचा यजाता ऋतुभिर्घ्रवेभिः (*ko agnimāṭṭe haviṣā dhṛtena sucā yajātā ṛtubhirghravebhiḥ*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-84-18), सुक् (*suk*), ऋतु (*ṛtu*) and ध्रुव (*dhruva*) are all three vessels for offering oblations. In places such as इंद्र सोमं पिब ऋतुना (*iṃdra somaṃ piba ṛtunā*) (1-15-1) and मरुतः पिब ऋतुना (*marutaḥ piba ṛtunā*) (1-15-2), one view is that the word ऋतु (*ṛtu*) means a vessel. But Sāyaṇa has explained ऋतु (*ṛtu*) in these contexts as the deity Ṛtu, and the Saṃhitā too shows the meaning "deity". Even in the Ṛk 1-84-18 cited above Sāyaṇa has not taken it to mean a vessel; he has given it as the seasons beginning with spring.

If the word ऋतु (*ṛtu*) is a synonym of "deity", then ऋत्विक् (*ṛtvik*) means a worshipper of the deity. In the present Ṛk, ऋतुपाः (*ṛtupāḥ*) can be explained as the Indra who drinks Soma in the seasons,

### Printed p. 98
and ऋतुभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ*) as the Indra who is united with the deities named Ṛtu. Sāyaṇa has explained them as the Marut deities. When one says ऋतुभिः देवेभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ devebhiḥ*), if ऋतुभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ*) is made an adjective of देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*), it can also mean "with the deities named Ṛtu".

> मरुत्वतीयशस्त्रे याज्या ये त्वाहिहत्य इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । ये त्वाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्धन्निति याज्या । आ. ५-१४ । इति ॥
> हे मघवन्निंद्र ये मरुतोऽहिहत्ये वृत्रहननरूपे कर्मणि त्वा त्वामवर्धन् प्रहर भगवो जहि वीरयस्वेति बलदानेनावीवृधन् । हे हरिवोऽश्ववन्निंद्र
> ये च शांबरे शंबरवधसंबंधिनि युद्धे त्वामवीवृधन् । इंद्रः शंबरमवधीदित्यस्मिन्नर्थे मंत्रवर्णः । यः शंबरं पर्वतेषु क्षियंतं चत्वारिंश्यां शरद्यन्वविंदत् । ओजायमानं यो अहिं जघान । ऋग्वे २-१२-११ । इति । तथा ये
> मरुतो गविष्टौ पणिनामकैरसुरैः सह गवार्थे युद्धे च त्वामवीवृधन् । विप्रा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Ṛk ये त्वाहिहत्ये (*ye tvāhihatye*) is the yājyā in the Marutvatīya śastra. It is prescribed by the sūtra ये त्वाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्धन्निति याज्या (*ye tvāhihatye maghavannavardhanniti yājyā*) (Ā. 5-14). O Maghavan Indra, the Maruts who in the work of slaying Ahi (Vṛtra) strengthened you by giving you strength, with words such as "strike, blessed one, slay, show your valour"; and, O Harivān (possessor of horses) Indra, those who strengthened you in the battle connected with the slaying of Śambara. That Indra slew Śambara is stated by a mantra passage: यः शंबरं पर्वतेषु क्षियंतं चत्वारिंश्यां शरद्यन्वविंदत् । ओजायमानं यो अहिं जघान । (*yaḥ śaṃbaraṃ parvateṣu kṣiyaṃtaṃ catvāriṃśyāṃ śaradyanvaviṃdat | ojāyamānaṃ yo ahiṃ jaghāna |*) (Ṛgve. 2-12-11)**NOTE**. Likewise the Maruts who strengthened you in the battle for cattle, गविष्टौ (*gaviṣṭau*), against the asuras named Paṇis; and the wise

> पूर्वपदस्वरः । अनुमदंति । मदि स्तुत्यादिश्वित्यस्य लटि व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ।
> आगमानुशासनस्यानित्यत्वान्नुमभावः । झीर्लसार्वधातुकस्वरे कृते धातुस्वरः । तिजं
> चोदात्तवतीति गतेर्निघातः ॥

The Gist for the portion of this block that stands in this window is given in the preceding paragraph, which completes the sentence ("the wise Maruts who now delight you … drink this Soma"); the remainder of the block is grammatical.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—wealthy one
- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—possessor of horses

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wealthy and possessed of horses, the Maruts who strengthened you in the work of slaying Vṛtra, who gave you strength in the battle fought with Śambara, who helped you in the recovery of the stolen cattle, and who, being wise, are now gratifying to you: united with such Maruts, drink this Soma.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
They who encouraged you Maghavan, to slay Ahi, who (aided you) in the conflict with Shambara, and in the recovery of the cattle, and who, possessed of wisdom, contribute verily to your exhilaration, with them, the troop of the Maruts, Indra, drink the Soma.

### Printed p. 100

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this Ṛk beginning ये त्वाहिहत्ये (*ye tvāhihatye*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra at the time of reciting the Marutvatīya śastra is explained by the sūkta**NOTE** of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, ये त्वाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्धन्निति याज्या (*ye tvāhihatye maghavannavardhanniti yājyā*) (Ā. 5-14).

The friendship between Indra and the Maruts, and the nature of the help that the Maruts gave Indra in many situations, have been explained fully before. Of these, three situations are indicated here.

The name of Śambara is usually joined with the asuras Śuṣṇa, Pipru and Varcin. In some Ṛks he is called a dāsa (6-26-5). It is said that for King Divodāsa, a close friend of Indra, Indra overthrew all the countless forts of the enemy Śambara and gave Divodāsa his property. These matters too have been told before. It is also said that this asura hid himself in the hills and mountains and caused great harm to Atithigva and Divodāsa, and so Indra destroyed him and gave both of them his protection. Like Ahi and Vṛtra, Śambara too can be said to be a person who represents a dense darkness.

"Sambara, meaning among other things the cloud, seems to be some mythical beings connected with the powers of darkness". Oldenberg.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, मरुत्वंतं (*marutvaṃtaṃ*)", accompanied by the Maruts; वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*), the rainer of waters by splitting the cloud; ववृधानं (*vavṛdhānaṃ*), growing through zeal in works such as the slaying of Vṛtra; akavāri, one who has many enemies**NOTE**; "or else" — the block breaks off here and the next window continues it.

> नवतरायावसे रक्षणायेह कर्मणि हुवेम । त्वामाह्वयेम ॥ नूतनाय ।
> नवतरायावतसे रक्षणायेह कर्मणि हुवेम । त्वामाह्वयेम ॥ नूतनाय ।
> नवशब्दस्य नू इत्यादेशः । त्वप्तनखःश्च प्रत्यया वक्तव्या इति तनप्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The block opens by completing the explanation of अकवारिं (*akavāriṃ*) begun on the previous page.**NOTE** A mantra is cited in support: स्वरिरमत्तो ववक्षे रणाय (*svariramatto vavakṣe raṇāya*) (Ṛgve. 1-61-9).**NOTE** Then he glosses the remaining words. दिव्यं (*divyaṃ*): dwelling in heaven. शासं (*śāsaṃ*): the ruler who governs by beneficial instruction and by warding off harm. विश्वासाहं (*viśvāsāhaṃ*): the overcomer of every adversary. उग्रं (*ugraṃ*): formidable against enemies. सहोदां (*sahodāṃ*): the giver of strength to the Maruts, his allies in battle. Indra, so endowed, we call to this rite for new, that is, fresher protection (नूतनाय (*nūtanāya*), अवसे (*avase*), हुवेम (*huvema*): "we invoke you"). The rest of the block is grammar on नूतनाय (*nūtanāya*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुत्वंतं (*marutvaṃtaṃ*)—one accompanied by the Maruts
- वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*)—one who sends down rain
- ववृधानं (*vavṛdhānaṃ*)—one who grows (with zeal)
- अकवारिं (*akavāriṃ*)—one who has abundant enemies
- दिव्यं (*divyaṃ*)—one who dwells in the world of the gods
- शासं (*śāsaṃ*)—the instructor
- विश्वासाहं (*viśvāsāhaṃ*)—one who defeats all enemies
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—the terrible one
- सहोदां (*sahodāṃ*)—the giver of strength to the Maruts, his companions
- तं इंद्रं (*taṃ iṃdraṃ*)—that Indra
- नूतनाय (*nūtanāya*)—new
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrificial rite
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who is accompanied by the Maruts, sends down rain, grows with zeal, has abundant enemies, dwells in the world of the gods, is the instructor, defeats all enemies, is terrible, and gives strength to his companions the Maruts: him we call with prayer in this sacrificial rite for fresh protection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We inovke to this sacrifice for present protection Indra, the chief of the Maruts, the showerer (of benefits) ; augmenting (in glory), overcoming many foes, divine regulator (of good and ill), the subduer of all (enemies), the fierce the bestower of strength.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Akavārim: this word has been explained as "one with abundant enemies". The word kava is formed from the root ku, which gives the sense "contemptible"; kava therefore means what is small, despised, blameworthy. From this root both forms, kava and kavāri, are formed.

### Printed p. 102

The word kuvāri**NOTE** in general means a man who is extremely selfish, miserly, performs no sacrifice and leads a contemptible life. In the present ṛk, where akavārim stands, the word kava means a small, despised person, and the compound is kava-ari: a petty enemy. One who is not a kavāri is an akavāri, that is, an enemy of great power; or an abundant number may also be indicated by it. It is an epithet showing Indra's greatness: one who can face such enemies.

## Sūkta 48 (Maṇḍala 3)

> सद्यो हेति पंचर्चं दशमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । सद्यो
> हेत्यनुक्रमणिका । अग्निष्टोमे माध्यंदिनसवने मैत्रावरुणशस्त्रे सद्यो ह जात
> इत्येतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । सद्योह जात एवा त्वामिंद्र । आ. ५. १६ । इति ॥
> चातुर्विंशिकेऽप्यहनि मैत्रावरुणशस्त्रेऽहरहः शस्यसंज्ञमेतत्तूक्तं॥ सूत्रितं च ।
> सद्यो ह जात इत्यहरहःशस्यं मैत्रावरुणः । आ. ७ ४ । इति ॥ अहर्गणे द्वितीयादिष्वहःसु माध्यंदिनसवनेऽस्मिन् शस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं । अहरहः शस्यानीति होत्रका
> द्वितीयादिष्टेव । आ. ७. १ । इति सूत्रितं ॥ साद्यस्क्र एकाहे मरुत्वतीये शस्त्रे
> सद्यो ह जात इत्याद्या सूक्तमुखीया । सूत्रितं च । सद्यो ह जातो वृषभः
> कनीनस्त्वं सद्यो अपिबो जात इंद्र । आ. ९. ५ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the tenth sūkta of the fourth anuvāka, सद्यो ह (*sadyo ha*), of five ṛks; the seer is Viśvāmitra, the deity Indra, the metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā begins सद्यो ह (*sadyo ha*). Uses: in the Agniṣṭoma, at the midday pressing, this sūkta (सद्यो ह जात (*sadyo ha jāta*)) belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra, and the sūtra says सद्यो ह जात एवा त्वामिंद्र (*sadyo ha jāta evā tvāmiṃdra*) (Ā. Sū. 5.16).**NOTE** On the Cāturviṃśika day, in the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra, this sūkta is the one called ahar-ahaḥ-śasya; the sūtra says सद्यो ह जात इत्यहरहःशस्यं मैत्रावरुणः (*sadyo ha jāta ityaharahaḥśasyaṃ maitrāvaruṇaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 7.4). In an ahargaṇa, from the second day onward, at the midday pressing, it is used in this śastra; the sūtra: अहरहः शस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेव (*aharahaḥ śasyānīti hotrakā dvitīyādiṣṭeva*) (Ā. Sū. 7.1). In the one-day sādyaskra rite, in the Marutvatīya śastra, its first ṛk सद्यो ह जात (*sadyo ha jāta*) is the sūktamukhīya (opening verse); the sūtra: सद्यो ह जातो वृषभः कनीनस्त्वं सद्यो अपिबो जात इंद्र । (*sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ kanīnastvaṃ sadyo apibo jāta iṃdra |*) (Ā. Sū. 9.5).

Anuvāda (Kannada): This sūkta सद्यो ह (*sadyo ha*) is the tenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka and has five ṛks. Its seer is Viśvāmitra, deity Indra, metre Triṣṭubh. It is stated in the Anukramaṇikā as beginning with सद्यो ह (*sadyo ha*). Its use for the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra mantras at the midday pressing of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra सद्यो ह जात एवा त्वामिंद्र (*sadyo ha jāta evā tvāmiṃdra*) (Ā. 5-6). Its use for the recitation called ahar-ahaḥ-śastra, when the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra mantras are recited on the twenty-fourth (Cāturviṃśaka) day, is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra सद्यो ह जात इत्यहरहः शस्यं मैत्रावरुणः (*sadyo ha jāta ityaharahaḥ śasyaṃ maitrāvaruṇaḥ*) (Ā. 7-4). Its use for reciting the śastra mantras at the midday pressing, from the second day onward of the sacrifice called ahargaṇa, is set out by the sūtra अहरहः शस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेव (*aharahaḥ śasyānīti hotrakā dvitīyādiṣṭeva*)

### Printed p. 103

(Ā. 7-1). Its use for the first ṛk of this sūkta, in reciting the Marutvatīya śastra mantras in the one-day sacrifice called sādyaskra, is set out by the sūtra सद्यो ह जातो वृषभ, कनीनस्त्वं सद्यो अपिबो जात इंद्र (*sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabha, kanīnastvaṃ sadyo apibo jāta iṃdra*) (Ā. 9-5).

Om.

Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 3; Varga 12.
Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5.
Ṛṣi: Viśvāmitra.
Devatā: Indra.
Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सा॒धोः पि॑ब प्रतिका॒मं यथा॑ ते॒ रसा॑शिरः प्रथ॒मं  ॒॑
> सोम्यस्य ॥ १ ॥

> *sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ kanīnaḥ prabhartumāvadaṃdhasaḥ sutasya |*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सद्यः । ह । जातः । वृषभः । कनीनः। प्रभर्तुं । आवत् । अंधसः । सुतस्य ।  
> साधोः । पिब । प्रतिकामं । यथा । ते । रसआशिरः । प.थमं । सोम्यस्य ॥ १ ॥

> *sadyaḥ | ha | jātaḥ | vṛṣabhaḥ | kanīnaḥ| prabhartuṃ | āvat | aṃdhasaḥ | sutasya |*  
> *sādhoḥ | piba | pratikāmaṃ | yathā | te | rasaāśiraḥ | pa.thamaṃ | somyasya ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषभो वृष्टिद्वारापां वर्षिता सद्यस्तदानीमेव जात उत्पन्नः कनीनः
> कमनीय इंद्रः सुतस्याभिषुतस्यांधसो हविर्लक्षणस्यान्नस्य सोमस्य प्रभर्तुं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*): he who rains down through the clouds' bursting; सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*): at that very moment; जातः (*jātaḥ*): born; कनीनः (*kanīnaḥ*): the desirable Indra. सुतस्य (*sutasya*): of the pressed अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*), the food in the form of oblation, Soma; प्रभर्तुं (*prabhartuṃ*) (the block breaks off here and continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 104

> प्रकर्षण भर्तारं संग्रहीतारं यजमानमावत् । रक्षतु । ह प्रसिद्धौ । किंच तादृशस्त्वं प्रतिकामं कामे कामे सोमपानेच्छायां सत्यां ते तव यथा कामस्य
> पूर्तिर्भवति तथा साधो रसात्मना संसिद्धं रसाशिरो गॊपयोमिश्रणोपेतं
> सोम्यस्य सोममयं रसं प्रथमं सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पुरस्तात्पिब ॥ प्रतिकामं ।
> कामं कामं प्रति । वीप्सायामव्ययाभावः । समासस्वरः । यथा । अपादांतत्वादेव
> लित्स्वरः । रसाशिरः । आज्‌पूर्वात् श्रीणातेः क्विप्यपस्पृधेथामित्यादिनाशिर् इत्यादेशः।
> बहुप्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । सोम्यस्य । सोमशब्दान्मयडर्थे मये चेति
> यप्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

प्रभर्तुं (*prabhartuṃ*): the bearer, the gatherer in abundance, the sacrificer; may Indra protect him (आवत् (*āvat*)). ह (*ha*) (both) are well-known particles. Further, O Indra, being such, whenever the desire to drink Soma arises (प्रतिकामं (*pratikāmaṃ*)), as your desire may be fulfilled, drink first, before all the gods, the Soma juice (सोम्यस्य (*somyasya*), made of Soma), perfected as juice (साधोः (*sādhoḥ*)) and रसाशिरः (*rasāśiraḥ*), that is, mixed with cow's milk. The rest is grammar on प्रतिकामं (*pratikāmaṃ*), यथा (*yathā*), रसाशिरः (*rasāśiraḥ*) and सोम्यस्य (*somyasya*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the sender-down of rain
- सद्यो ह जातः (*sadyo ha jātaḥ*)—as soon as born
- कनीनः (*kanīnaḥ*)—Indra, who has an attractive form
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—pressed
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—the food in the form of Soma
- प्रभर्तुं (*prabhartuṃ*)—the sacrificer who holds it in abundance
- आवत् (*āvat*)—may he protect (O Indra)
- प्रतिकामं (*pratikāmaṃ*)—whenever you have the wish
- ते (*te*)—to you
- यथा (*yathā*)—so as to be satisfied
- साधोः (*sādhoḥ*)—juicy
- रसाशिरः (*rasāśiraḥ*)—mixed with milk
- सोम्यस्य (*somyasya*)—Soma juice
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—before all the gods
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, the sender-down of rain, who is of a charming form as soon as he is born, protect the sacrificer who devoutly holds the pressed Soma. O Indra, whenever you wish, drink, so as to be satisfied, the juicy, milk-mixed Soma juice before all the gods.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May the showerer (of rain), who, as soon as born, is the object of affection, protect the offerer of the effused libation: drink at will, Indra, before (the other gods), of the pure Soma juice mixed with milk.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

प्रतिकामं यथा ते (*pratikāmaṃ yathā te*)—कामे कामे सोमपानेच्छायां सत्यां ते तव यथा कामस्य पूर्तिर्भवति तथा (पिब) (*kāme kāme somapānecchāyāṃ satyāṃ te tava yathā kāmasya pūrtirbhavati tathā (piba)*). O Indra, whenever the wish to drink Soma arises in you, that is, whenever you like, drink Soma juice as much as will satisfy you: so the seer prays.

### Printed p. 105

रसाशिरः (*rasāśiraḥ*)—rasa here means liquid milk. The meaning is Soma juice mixed with such milk, or gavāśira.

प्रथमं सोम्यस्य (*prathamaṃ somyasya*)—सोममयं रसं प्रथमं सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पुरस्तात्पिब (*somamayaṃ rasaṃ prathamaṃ sarvebhyo devebhyaḥ purastātpiba*). The meaning: drink the Soma, strained and prepared as juice, before the other gods drink it, that is, you first of all.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं यद्यस्मिन्नहनि जायथा अजायथाः तदहस्तस्मिन्नेवाहन्यस्य
> सोमस्य कामे पिसासायां सत्यां गिरिष्ठां गिरिस्थां पर्वतोस्कोच्चस्थाने वर्तमानमंशोः सोमलताखंडविशिष्टस्य ऋजीषस्य पीयूषमभिनवं रसमपिबः । पीतवानसि । उत्पत्तिक्षण एव सोमपाने कारणं दर्शयति । ते तव जनित्री माता योषा
> युवतिरदितिर्महो महतः पितुर्जनकस्य कश्यपस्य दमे सूतिकागृहेऽग्रे स्तन्यदानात् प्राक् तं तादृषं सोमं पर्यासिंचत् । तवास्यॆ परितोऽक्षारयत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, on the day on which you were born, on that very day, when the desire for this Soma arose, you drank the nectar, the fresh juice, of the अंशोः (*aṃśoḥ*), which is distinguished by pieces of the Soma plant, of the ṛjīṣa, गिरिष्ठां (*giriṣṭhāṃ*) (गिरिस्थां (*giristhāṃ*)), standing on the high place of a mountain.**NOTE** He shows the reason for drinking Soma at the very moment of birth: your mother (जनित्री (*janitrī*)), the young woman (योषा (*yoṣā*)) Aditi, in the lying-in chamber of your great father, your begetter Kaśyapa (महः पितुः दमे (*mahaḥ pituḥ dame*)), before giving the breast (अग्रे (*agre*)), poured that Soma around you (पर्यासिंचत् (*paryāsiṃcat*)), that is, made it flow all around your mouth.

> जायथाः । जनी प्रादुर्भाव इत्यस्य लजि बहुलं छंदसीत्यडभावः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । जनित्री । जनिता मंत्र इति निपातनाण्णेर्लोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The block contains only grammatical notes, on जायथाः (*jāyathāḥ*) and जनित्री (*janitrī*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) यत् (*yat*)—when
- जायथाः (*jāyathāḥ*)—you were born
- तदहः (*tadahaḥ*)—that very day
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Soma juice
- कामे (*kāme*)—when the desire to drink arose
- गिरिष्ठां (*giriṣṭhāṃ*)—that was at the high place of the mountain
- अंशोः (*aṃśoḥ*)—of the piece of Soma plant
- पीयूषं (*pīyūṣaṃ*)—the juice
- आपिबः (*āpibaḥ*)—you drank
- ते (*te*)—your
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—mother
- योषा (*yoṣā*)—and young woman, Aditi
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great-souled
- पितुः (*pituḥ*)—your father, Kaśyapa's
- दमे (*dame*)—in the lying-in chamber
- अग्रे (*agre*)—before (giving you) the breast
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Soma
- परि आसिंचत् (*pari āsiṃcat*)—she made you drink fully

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as soon as you were born, when the desire to drink Soma juice arose, you drank the juice of the piece of Soma plant that was at the high place of the mountain. Your mother, the young Aditi, in the lying-in chamber of the great-souled Kaśyapa, your begetter, made you drink that Soma fully before giving you the breast.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
On the day on which you were born, you drank at will the mountain-abiding nectar of this Soma plant. for your youthful parent mother (Aditi), in the dwelling of your great sire (Kashyapa), gave it to you before she gave the breast.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The first half of this ṛk explains that Indra felt the wish to drink Soma on the very day he was born and drank that nectar-like Soma juice. The second half describes how Indra's mother, a young woman, in her husband's house, as soon as Indra was born, made him drink Soma juice before nursing him at the breast. This indicates that Indra's desire to drink Soma has been great from the beginning. Here, although there is no statement of who Indra's mother is or who his father is, the commentator says that the mother of Indra is Aditi, the mother of the gods, and the father is Kaśyapa. Although this explanation agrees with the descriptions given in the Purāṇas and similar works, it cannot be said to accord with Vedic literature. For the position and status of Indra stated in the Purāṇas and similar works, and the position and status of Indra stated in the Ṛgveda

### Printed p. 107

*(continuing the Special Topics of the preceding Ṛk)*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

…the status and rank of Indra in the Purāṇas and the like also differ greatly from those stated for Indra in the Ṛgveda. In the Purāṇas and the like Indra's rank is not of the highest. It says that there are deities above him, that Indra is an ordinary deity, and that he is lord of heaven alone. In the Vedas, however, Indra's position is said to be one of sovereignty: Indra alone is the best among all the deities. It was he who created earth and the atmosphere. In many places it is said that heaven and earth, the sun and moon, all other living beings and the whole creation are obedient to Indra's command, that Indra alone is the sole lord of the whole universe, and that he is the best of all the deities. Therefore there is room to say that the Indra of the Ṛgveda is the very principle of the Supreme Brahman stated in the Vedānta texts. In the Ṛgveda there are not as many hymns addressed to any other deity as to Indra. About 250 hymns, and some portions of hymns, praise Indra. Indra is also praised together with certain other deities. Taken all together, about 300 hymns are in his honour, which means about a quarter of the Ṛgveda. Indra's greatness and his deeds of daring are described more especially than those of all the other deities.

Moreover, it is said both in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā and in the Yajurveda that Indra is a son of Aditi, the mother of the gods:

अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेर्ये जातास्तन्वंस्परि । (*aṣṭau putrāso aditerye jātāstanvaṃspari |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-8)

अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेः । ये जातास्तन्वःपरि । देवाउप प्रैत्सप्तभिः । परामार्तांडमास्यत् । सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिः । उप प्रैत्तूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्युवे तत् । परामार्तांडमाभरदिति । ताननुक्रमिष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अगंशुश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग् श्चेत्येते ॥ (*aṣṭau putrāso aditeḥ | ye jātāstanvaḥpari | devāupa praitsaptabhiḥ | parāmārtāṃḍamāsyat | saptabhiḥ putrairaditiḥ | upa praittūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyuve tat | parāmārtāṃḍamābharaditi | tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agaṃśuśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāg ścetyete ‖*)
(Tai. Ā. 1-13-2, 3)

As stated here, Aditi has eight children, and their names are given as Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Āryamā, Aṃśu, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān. Since it is clearly stated that Indra is one of these eight, there is no doubt whatever that Aditi, the mother of the gods, is Indra's mother. As for his father being Kaśyapa, that is only a statement of the Purāṇas; there is no support for it in the Ṛgveda.

गिरिस्थां अंशोः पीयूषं (*giristhāṃ aṃśoḥ pīyūṣaṃ*)—here the use of the word गिरिस्थां (*giristhāṃ*) indicates Soma plants grown on mountains. Although the Soma plant also grows on plains and on river banks, the one grown on mountains is famed as the best. Moreover, the higher it grows the better it is, and it is famed as having more juice and being more pleasant to the taste. Among the mountains where the Soma plant grows, the mountain named Mūjavat is famed, and is mentioned in many places in the Ṛgveda.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स इंद्रो मातरमुपस्थाय प्रार्थयित्वान्नमैट्ट । तामन्नमयाचत ।
> ईळिरध्येषणाकर्मति यास्कः । ततस्तस्या ऊध ऊधसि क्षीररूपेण स्थितं तिग्मं दीप्तं
> सोममभ्य पश्यत् । सर्वतोऽदर्शत् । गृत्सः । अभिकांक्ष्यते सर्वैर्देवैः शत्रुहननार्थमिति गृत्स इंद्रः । अन्यान्सपत्नान्वयवयन् स्वस्वस्थानात्पकर्षणोच्चालयन्नचरत् । सर्वत्र चरति । किंच पुरुधप्रतीकस्तेजोयोगाद्बहुधा विक्षिप्तांगो
> महानि महांति वृत्रहननादीनि कर्माणि चक्रे ॥ उपस्थाय । तिष्ठतेर्लपि घुमास्थेतीत्वे प्राप्ने न ल्यपीति प्रतिषेधः । लित्स्वरः । ऐट्ट । ईळिर्याच्छार्थः । तस्माल्लजि
> रूपं । आडजादीनामित्याडागमः । ष्टुत्वं । निघातः । तिग्मं । तिज निशाने । अस्माद्युजिरुचितिजां कुश्चति मक्प्रत्ययः कवर्गादेशश्च । प्रयवयन् । यु मिश्रणामिश्रणयोरित्यस्यण्यंतस्य शतरि रूपं । लित्स्वरः । गृत्सः । गृधु अभिकांक्षायां ।
> गृधिपण्योर्दका चेति सप्रत्ययो दकारश्चांतादेशः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः ।
> पुरुधप्रतीकः । पुरुशब्द इह संख्यावाची । संख्याया विधार्थे धेति धाप्रत्ययः ।
> ह्रस्वश्छांदसः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that this Indra, approaching his mother, asked her for food (ऐट्ट (*aiṭṭa*)): he begged her for food. Yāska says that ईळि (*īḷi*) denotes the act of requesting. Then, in her udder, he saw all around the bright (तिग्मं (*tigmaṃ*)) Soma standing there in the form of milk. गृत्सः (*gṛtsaḥ*) is Indra, because he is desired by all the gods for the slaying of enemies. Driving the others, his rivals, away, dislodging them from their several places, he moved about everywhere. Further, being पुरुधप्रतीकः (*purudhapratīkaḥ*), with his limbs spread out in many ways through union with radiance, he performed great deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra. (The rest of the block is grammatical.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- मातरं (*mātaraṃ*)—his mother
- उपस्थाय (*upasthāya*)—having approached
- अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—food
- ऐट्ट (*aiṭṭa*)—he begged
- ऊधः (*ūdhaḥ*)—that which is in her breast in the form of milk
- तिग्मं (*tigmaṃ*)—bright
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- अभि अपश्यत् (*abhi apaśyat*)—he looked at fully
- गृत्सः (*gṛtsaḥ*)—Indra, who is desired by the gods
- अन्यान् (*anyān*)—enemies
- प्रयवयन् (*prayavayan*)—driving them out of their several places
- अचरत् (*acarat*)—moves about everywhere
- पुरुधप्रतीकः (*purudhapratīkaḥ*)—spread everywhere in his form of radiance
- महानि (*mahāni*)—very great deeds
- चक्रे (*cakre*)—he performed

### Printed p. 109

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra approached his mother and begged her for food. He looked fully at the bright Soma that was in her breast in the form of milk. Indra, who is desired by the gods, moves about everywhere driving the enemies out of their several places. Spread everywhere in his form of radiance, he performed very great deeds.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Approaching his mother he asked for food, and beheld the acrid Soma upon her bosom : eager he proceeds, dislodging the adversaries (of the gods) ; and, putting forth manifold (energy), he performed great (deeds).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk it is described that Indra begged his mother for अन्न (*anna*) (food), and saw that the milk in her breast was in the form of Soma.

ऐट्ट (*aiṭṭa*)—ईळिर्याच्चार्थः । (*īḷiryāccārthaḥ |*) ईळिरध्येषणाकर्मेति यास्कः । (*īḷiradhyeṣaṇākarmeti yāskaḥ |*) The meaning is: he desired, he begged.

गृत्सः (*gṛtsaḥ*)—For the word गृत्सः (*gṛtsaḥ*), formed from the root गृधु अभिकांक्षायां (*gṛdhu abhikāṃkṣāyāṃ*), the commentator gives the etymological sense: अभिकांक्ष्यते सर्वैर्देवैः शत्रुहननार्थमिति गृत्स इंद्रः । (*abhikāṃkṣyate sarvairdevaiḥ śatruhananārthamiti gṛtsa iṃdraḥ |*) That is, since all the deities desire Indra for the work of destroying enemies, Indra is called Gṛtsa.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒ग्रस्तु॑रा॒षाळ॒भिभू॑त्योजा यथाव॒शं त॒न्वं॑ चक्र ए॒षः ।  
> त्वष्टा॑र॒मिंद्रो॑ ज॒नुषा॑भि॒भूया॒मुष्या॒ सोम॑मसिबच्च॒मूषु॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> *ugrasturāṣāḷabhibhūtyojā yathāvaśaṃ tanvaṃ cakra eṣaḥ |*  
> *tvaṣṭāramiṃdro januṣābhibhūyāmuṣyā somamasibaccamūṣu ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उग्रः । तुराषाट् । अभिभूतिओजाः । यथावशं । तन्वं । चक्रे । विषः ।  
> त्वष्टारं । इंद्रः । जनुषा । अभिभूय । आमुष्य । सोमं । अपिबत् । चमूषु ॥

> *ugraḥ | turāṣāṭ | abhibhūtiojāḥ | yathāvaśaṃ | tanvaṃ | cakre | viṣaḥ |*  
> *tvaṣṭāraṃ | iṃdraḥ | januṣā | abhibhūya | āmuṣya | somaṃ | apibat | camūṣu ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य एष इंद्र उग्रः शत्रोणां भयंकरस्तुराषाट् त्वरया शत्रोणामभिभविता
> अत एवाभिभूत्योजाः शत्रोणामभिभवनपराक्रमोपेतः सन् तन्वमात्मीयं शरीरं
> यथावशं यथाकामं नानाधिरूपोपेतं चक्रे । तथा च मंत्रवर्णः । रूपंरूपं मघना बोभवीति । ऋग्वे. ३-५३-८ । इति स इंद्रो जनुषा जन्मना सामर्थ्येन त्वष्टारं त्वष्टृनामकमसुरमभिभूय चमूषु चमसेषु स्थितमामुष्य
> चोरयित्वा सोममपिबत् । त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रमित्यादि प्रासहा सोममपिबत्। तै. सं. २-४-१२। इति तैत्तिरीयकं॥ तुराषाट् । इत्वरा संभ्रमे । क्विप् । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना ऊट् । सहेश्छंदसि सह इति ण्णिः । कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलमिति समासः ।
> तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलमिति तृतीयाया अलुक् । सहेः साडः स इति षत्वं । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । यथावशं । वशं काममनतिक्रम्येत्यव्ययीभावसमासः । समासस्वरः ।
> आमुष्य । मुष स्तेये । ल्यप् । चमूषु । चमु अदने । कृषिचमितनिधनिसर्जिखर्जिभ्य ऊरित्यूप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that this Indra is उग्रः (*ugraḥ*), terrible to enemies; तुराषाट् (*turāṣāṭ*), one who overcomes enemies with speed; hence अभिभूत्योजाः (*abhibhūtyojāḥ*), endowed with the might to overpower enemies. Being so, he made (चक्रे (*cakre*)) his own body यथावशं (*yathāvaśaṃ*), according to his wish, endowed with many kinds of forms. So too there is a mantra text: रूपंरूपं मघना बोभवीति (*rūpaṃrūpaṃ maghanā bobhavīti*) (Ṛgveda 3-53-8). That Indra, जनुषा (*januṣā*), by birth, that is, by his native power, overcame the Asura named Tvaṣṭṛ, stole the Soma lying in the ladles (चमूषु (*camūṣu*), that is, in the cups), and drank it. The Taittirīya text says: त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रमित्यादि प्रासहा सोममपिबत्। (*tvaṣṭā hataputro vīṃdramityādi prāsahā somamapibat|*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12). (The rest of the block is grammatical.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this Indra
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—being terrible
- तुराषाट् (*turāṣāṭ*)—one who defeats enemies
- अभिभूत्योजाः (*abhibhūtyojāḥ*)—possessing the brilliance that conquers enemies
- तन्नं (*tannaṃ*)—his body
- यथावशं (*yathāvaśaṃ*)—as he pleased
- चक्रे (*cakre*)—he changed
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—that same Indra
- जनुषा (*januṣā*)—by his natural power
- त्वष्टारं (*tvaṣṭāraṃ*)—the Asura named Tvaṣṭṛ
- अभिभूय (*abhibhūya*)—having defeated
- चमूषु (*camūṣu*)—that was in the ladle-vessel
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- आमुष्य (*āmuṣya*)—having carried off
- अपिबत् (*apibat*)—drank

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Indra, being terrible, a defeater of enemies, and possessed of the brilliance that conquers enemies, changed his body as he pleased. That same Indra, by his natural power, defeated the Asura named Tvaṣṭṛ, carried off the Soma that was in the ladle-vessel, and drank it.

### Printed p. 111

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Fierce, rapid in assault, of overpowering strength, he made his form obedient to his will; having overcome Twashtri by his innate (vigour), and carried off the Soma juice, he drank it (deposited) in the ladles.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तुराषाट् (*turāṣāṭ*)—त्वरया शत्रूणामभिभवता । (*tvarayā śatrūṇāmabhibhavatā |*) Because he defeats enemies very quickly, Indra has the name तुराषाट् (*turāṣāṭ*).

अभिभूत्योजाः (*abhibhūtyojāḥ*)—शत्रुणामभिभवनपराक्रमोपेतः । (*śatruṇāmabhibhavanaparākramopetaḥ |*) The meaning is that Indra is endowed with the greatest prowess for defeating enemies. That is why the epithet उग्रः (*ugraḥ*), "terrible to enemies", is stated here.

यथावशं तन्नं चक्रे एषः (*yathāvaśaṃ tannaṃ cakre eṣaḥ*)—तन्नमात्मीयं शरीरं यथाकामं नानाविधरूपोपेतं चक्रे । (*tannamātmīyaṃ śarīraṃ yathākāmaṃ nānāvidharūpopetaṃ cakre |*) Since Indra is capable of taking on, in order to defeat enemies, the various forms that he likes, it is said here that at the time of destroying enemies he assumes whatever form (shape) he pleases. On this matter:

रूपंरूपं मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कृण्वानस्तन्वं परि स्वां । (*rūpaṃrūpaṃ maghavā bobhavīti māyāḥ kṛṇvānastanvaṃ pari svāṃ |*)
रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव तदस्य रूपं प्रतिचक्षणाय । इंद्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश ॥ (*rūpaṃrūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva tadasya rūpaṃ praticakṣaṇāya | iṃdro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hyasya harayaḥ śatā daśa ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-18)

In Ṛks such as these it is said that, in order to conquer the Asuras who are masters of illusion, Indra assumes whatever forms he needs.

Regarding Indra overcoming Tvaṣṭṛ, carrying off the Soma in the ladles and drinking it: स इंद्रो जन्मना सामर्थ्येन त्वष्टनामकमसुरमभिभूय अस्य चमसपात्रेषु स्थितं सोमं चोरयित्वापिबत् । (*sa iṃdro janmanā sāmarthyena tvaṣṭanāmakamasuramabhibhūya asya camasapātreṣu sthitaṃ somaṃ corayitvāpibat |*) That Indra, by his own power, defeated the Asura named Tvaṣṭṛ, stole the Soma that Tvaṣṭṛ had placed in the ladle-vessels so that he might drink it, and drank it himself. Here Tvaṣṭṛ is described as an Asura. But this Tvaṣṭṛ is one of the Prajāpatis and the architect of the gods, and there are plenty of Ṛks in the Ṛgveda praising him. However, his son named Viśvarūpa, though priest to the gods, favoured the Asuras; therefore his father Tvaṣṭṛ too is called an Asura here. On this matter the commentator has given an itihāsa from the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as an example—

### Printed p. 112

त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रग्ं सोममाहरत्तस्मिन्निंद्र उपहवमैच्छत तन्नोपाह्वयत पुत्रं मेऽवधीरिति स यज्ञवेशसं तृत्वा प्रासहा सोममपिबत्तस्य यदत्यशिष्यत तत्त्वष्टाहवनीयमुप प्रावर्तयत्स्वाहेंद्रशत्रुर्वर्धस्वेति । (*tvaṣṭā hataputro vīṃdragṃ somamāharattasminniṃdra upahavamaicchata tannopāhvayata putraṃ me 'vadhīriti sa yajñaveśasaṃ tṛtvā prāsahā somamapibattasya yadatyaśiṣyata tattvaṣṭāhavanīyamupa prāvartayatsvāheṃdraśatrurvardhasveti |*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12-1)

The Prajāpati Tvaṣṭṛ had a son named Viśvarūpa. Indra killed him for a certain reason. Enraged at this, Tvaṣṭṛ wished for a son who would kill Indra, and began to perform a sacrifice. But in that sacrifice, out of anger at Indra, that is, out of anger that he had killed his son, he did not invite Indra to the sacrifice and did not give him the Soma-drink. Indra, enraged at this, created an obstacle to his sacrifice and forcibly drank the Soma juice that was there. Unable to bear this, Tvaṣṭṛ poured the remainder of the Soma that Indra had left after drinking into the Āhavanīya fire and wished for a son who would kill Indra; and so on. The commentator has explained the meaning thus: what is stated here is the very matter of Indra's forcibly drinking the Soma.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शु॒नं हु॑वेनु म॒घवा॑न॒मिंद्र॑म॒स्मिन्फरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सात् ।  
> शृ॒ण्वंत॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्तु॒ घ्नंतं॑ वृ॒त्राण॑ सं॒जितं॒  ॑
> धनानां ॥ ५ ॥

> *śunaṃ huvenu maghavānamiṃdramasminphare nṛtamaṃ vājasāt |*  
> *śṛṇvaṃtamugramūtaye samattu ghnaṃtaṃ vṛtrāṇa saṃjitaṃ*  
> *dhanānāṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुनं । हुवेम । मघवानं । इंद्रं । आस्मिन् । भरे । नृतमं । वाजसात् ।  
> शृण्वंतं । उग्रं । ऊतये । समत्सु । घ्नंतं । वृत्राणि । संजितं । धनानां ॥

> *śunaṃ | huvema | maghavānaṃ | iṃdraṃ | āsmin | bhare | nṛtamaṃ | vājasāt |*  
> *śṛṇvaṃtaṃ | ugraṃ | ūtaye | samatsu | ghnaṃtaṃ | vṛtrāṇi | saṃjitaṃ | dhanānāṃ ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः।
> अस्मिन्भरे । बिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्धार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन् संग्रामे
> शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृद्धं । यद्वा शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखकरं शुघवानं
> धनवंतं अत एवेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोऽतिशयेन
> नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा शृण्वंतमस्माभिः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: "O Indra, वाजसात् (*vājasāt*): that in which there is साति (*sāti*), gain, of वाज (*vāja*), food, is वाजसाति (*vājasāti*). भरे (*bhare*): since warriors bear (बिभ्रति (*bibhrati*)) the fortune of victory by it, भर (*bhara*) is battle. In this battle we call you, शुनं (*śunaṃ*), swollen, grown strong through zeal. Or else शुनं (*śunaṃ*) is a name for happiness: one who gives happiness. You are मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*), possessed of wealth, hence Indra, endowed with unsurpassed lordship, and नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*), in the highest degree the leader of the whole world. We, the Kuśikas, would call you for the sacrifice. Likewise, hearing the praise made by us…" (the sentence continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 113

> क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतमुग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि
> वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घ्नंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संजितं
> सम्यग्वेतारं त्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योरित्यस्य निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । हुवेम । ह्ययतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणे कृते
> शपो लुकि कृते च लिङ् रूपं । निघातः । भरे । भृञ् भरणे । घः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । वाजसात् । षणु दाने । भावे क्तिन् । जनसनेत्यादिनानुनासिकस्यात्वं ।
> बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपवस्वरः । समत्तु । अद भक्षणे । संपूर्वात् क्विप् । संभक्षयंति
> योद्धणामायूंषीति समदः संग्रामाः । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । घ्नंतं । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्य शतरि गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । हो हंतेरिति घत्वं । संजितं ।
> जि जये । क्विप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(The sentence continues:) …"fierce, terrible to enemies; समत्तु (*samattu*), in battles, slaying (घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*)) all the demons that are marked by Vṛtra; and a thorough conqueror (संजितं (*saṃjitaṃ*)) of the wealth (धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)) that belongs to enemies: we call you, for protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*))." (The remainder of the block is grammatical. It also explains समत्सु (*samatsu*) as follows: they thoroughly devour the lives of warriors, therefore समदः (*samadaḥ*) are battles.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—which proceeds for the sake of food
- भरे (*bhare*)—in battle
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—one who increases through zeal, or one who produces happiness
- मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*)—wealthy
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—endowed with unsurpassed wealth
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—the leader: you
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call, praying
- शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—one who listens to (our praises)
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—terrible to enemies
- समत्तु (*samattu*)—in battles
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the Asuras beginning with Vṛtra
- घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*)—one who strikes and destroys
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—the wealth (of enemies)
- संचितं (*saṃcitaṃ*)—you who gather it and give it (to us) **NOTE**
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- (हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call, praying)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in the battle that proceeds for the sake of food, you who give happiness, are wealthy, endowed with unsurpassed wealth, are the leader, listen to our praises, are terrible to enemies, strike and destroy in battles the Asuras beginning with Vṛtra, and gather and give us the wealth of the enemies: we call you, praying, for protection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The special topics of this Ṛk have already been explained earlier.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the eleventh sūkta of the fourth anuvāka, of five ṛks. Its seer is Viśvāmitra, its deity Indra, its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā marks it with the words शंसा महां (*śaṃsā mahāṃ*). It is used in the Marutvatīya śastra on the eighth day of the Samūḷha Daśarātra sacrifice, as the sūtra shows: शंसा महां महश्चित्त्वमिंद्र (*śaṃsā mahāṃ mahaścittvamiṃdra*) (Ā. Sū. 8-7). The block also gives the particulars: Maṇḍala 3, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 49, Aṣṭaka 3, Adhyāya 3, Varga 13, five ṛks.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Hotṛ, praise the great Indra with the śastras. Under the protection of this Indra, all men, having performed the sacrifice and become Soma-drinkers, obtain their desire." Kāma is what is desired, heaven and the like; Sāyaṇa glosses the verb as "they obtain it fully". The two धिषणे (*dhiṣaṇe*) are the two sustainers of gods, men and others. Or else they are bold and capable of protecting those who depend on them, that is, heaven and earth. The gods too (beget Indra). सुक्रतुं (*sukratuṃ*): kratu is work, such as the protection of the world; he whose work is excellent is sukratu. विभ्वतष्टं (*vibhvataṣṭaṃ*): established by Vibhu, that is Brahmā, in the sovereignty of the world. He is great, the घनं (*ghanaṃ*), the slayer of the Vṛtras, who are of the nature of sin. This Indra they begot.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in whose (Indra's) protection (O Hotṛ)
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- कृष्टयः (*kṛṣṭayaḥ*)—men
- सोमपा (*somapā*)—having drunk Soma (at the close of the sacrifice)
- कामं (*kāmaṃ*)—their desired object
- अव्यन् (*avyan*)—obtain fully; (and)
- धिषणे (*dhiṣaṇe*)—heaven and earth, which sustain all
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the gods as well
- सुक्रतुं (*sukratuṃ*)—the excellent doer of deeds
- विभ्वतष्टं (*vibhvataṣṭaṃ*)—one established by Vibhu for the sovereignty of the world
- वृत्राणां (*vṛtrāṇāṃ*)—of Vṛtra and the other Asuras
- घनं (*ghanaṃ*)—the destroyer
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whom, that Indra
- जनयंत (*janayaṃta*)—caused to be born, such a one
- महां (*mahāṃ*)—of great nature
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- शंस (*śaṃsa*)—praise by reciting the śastras

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Hotṛ, praise with the recitation of the śastra-mantras that Indra of great nature, in whose protection all men, after performing the sacrifice and drinking Soma, obtain their desired object; whom heaven and earth, which sustain all, and all the gods also caused to be born: the excellent doer of deeds, established by Vibhu for the sovereignty of the world, the destroyer of Vṛtra and the other Asuras.

### Printed p. 116

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I glorify the mighty Indra, in whom all men, drinking the Soma juice, obtain their wishes ; whom the powerful (heaven and earth) and the gods begot, the doer of great deeds, the slayer of the Vritras, who was fashioned by Vibhu (the creator)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शंस महां इंद्रं (*śaṃsa mahāṃ iṃdraṃ*)—"O Hotṛ, praise in this sacrifice the greatly glorious Indra with śastra-mantras and the like": thus the sacrificer addresses the priest called Hotṛ. What the glory of Indra is, which is meant by the epithet महां (*mahāṃ*) ("greatly glorious"), the seer describes in the following sentences.
यस्मिन् विश्वाः आ कृष्टयः सोमपाः कामं अव्यन् (*yasmin viśvāḥ ā kṛṣṭayaḥ somapāḥ kāmaṃ avyan*)—इंद्रे रक्षतरि सति सर्वे मनुष्याः यज्ञमनुष्ठाय सोमपाः संतः स्वर्गादिकामं सर्वतः प्राप्नुवंति (*iṃdre rakṣatari sati sarve manuṣyāḥ yajñamanuṣṭhāya somapāḥ saṃtaḥ svargādikāmaṃ sarvataḥ prāpnuvaṃti*). While the all-powerful Indra protects, all men perform sacrifices and other good rites, drink the Soma prescribed in those sacrifices, and as the fruit of it obtain the joys of heaven and the like. This is possible only through the glory of Indra.
धीषणे देवाः सुक्रतुं विभ्वतष्टं वृत्राणां हंतारं यं जनयंत (*dhīṣaṇe devāḥ sukratuṃ vibhvataṣṭaṃ vṛtrāṇāṃ haṃtāraṃ yaṃ janayaṃta*)—Since the word धि (*dhi*) is read among the names of rites, the word धीषणे (*dhīṣaṇe*) may be explained as heaven and earth, which are capable in the rites that protect people, or all the creatures on the earth. It is said here that such heaven and earth, and the gods, produced Indra. That Indra, being capable of performing rites such as the protection of the world, is praised by the epithet सुक्रतुं (*sukratuṃ*); being established by Brahmā in the sovereignty of the world, by विभ्वतष्टं (*vibhvataṣṭaṃ*); and being the destroyer of sins, by घनं वृत्राणां (*ghanaṃ vṛtrāṇāṃ*). It is said here that heaven and earth and the gods produced such a greatly glorious Indra. The matter of heaven and earth producing Indra we have already mentioned earlier.

> आतो लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Pṛtanās are battles, where warriors engage. In them Indra is स्वराजं (*svarājaṃ*), self-ruling; हरिष्ठां (*hariṣṭhāṃ*) is हरिस्थां (*haristhāṃ*), standing in a chariot yoked with bay horses; नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*) is the best leader of strength in battle; द्विता (*dvitā*) means that, having come to battle, he proceeds dividing the enemy army in two. No one at all surpasses (तरति (*tarati*)) this Indra; the sense is that no one equals him. नु (*nu*) is a particle of well-known fact. That Indra, इनतमः (*inatamaḥ*), the greatest lord of the army, goes with the Maruts, the सत्वभिः (*satvabhiḥ*), who sit round about him. With his शूषैः (*śūṣaiḥ*), strengths that dry up (shoṣayanti) the forces of the foe, and being पृथुज्रयाः (*pṛthujrayāḥ*), of intense speed toward battle, he destroys the life, or the food, of the Dasyu, the enemy; ह (*ha*) is a particle of well-known fact. Sāyaṇa cites the Nirukta here, which explains पृथुज्रयाः (*pṛthujrayāḥ*) as पृथुजवः (*pṛthujavaḥ*) and then quotes the pāda of the ṛk, with a further word that is not clear (Ni. 5-9). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कृतनासु (*kṛtanāsu*)—in battles
- स्वराजं (*svarājaṃ*)—shining by his own radiance
- हरिष्ठां (*hariṣṭhāṃ*)—seated in a chariot yoked with horses
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—the most excellent leader
- द्विता (*dvitā*)—dividing the enemy army into two
- यं (*yaṃ*)—that same Indra
- नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—no one at all
- तरति (*tarati*)—can surpass him
- इनतमः (*inatamaḥ*)—as the most excellent commander
- सत्वभिः (*satvabhiḥ*)—moving about with his companions the Maruts
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- शूषैः (*śūṣaiḥ*)—with strength that dries up enemies
- प्रथुज्रयाः (*prathujrayāḥ*)—running swiftly toward the battle
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—the life of the enemy
- अविनात् (*avināt*)—destroys

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That same Indra, who shines in battles by his own radiance, is seated in a chariot yoked with horses, is the most excellent leader, and divides the enemy army in two, no one can surpass. As the most excellent commander, moving about with his companions the Maruts, running swiftly toward the battle with his enemy-withering strength, Indra destroys the lives of the enemies.

### Printed p. 118

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Whom, when borne by his steeds, foremost and eminent in battles, breaking in two the (hostile host), no one ever surpasses : supreme in sway, attended by his faithful Maruts, and hastening to combat, he has destroyed with foe-withering (energies) the existence of the Dasyu.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—Yāska says that the word नकिः (*nakiḥ*) is used in the sense of the nine "all-words" collection (sarvapada-samāmnāya), हिकं नुकं (*hikaṃ nukaṃ*) and the others (Ni. 3-13). In the present ṛk the meaning न कश्चिदसि (*na kaścidasi*), "no one is able", is stated for this word. **NOTE**
नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—नेतृतमं (*netṛtamaṃ*): the best among leaders or chiefs.
हरिष्ठां (*hariṣṭhāṃ*)—हरियुक्तेरथे वर्तमानं (*hariyukterathe vartamānaṃ*). The two horses of Indra are called Hari (Ni. 2-28). The sense is: Indra seated in a chariot to which such horses are yoked.
इनतमः (*inatamaḥ*)—The word इन (*ina*) means lord. इनतमः (*inatamaḥ*) means one who is lord in an eminent or the highest degree.
पृथुज्रयाः (*pṛthujrayāḥ*)—Yāska, taking this very ṛk as the example, gives the explanation पृथुज्रयाः पृथुजवः (*pṛthujrayāḥ pṛthujavaḥ*), "of extended speed", that is, one of great speed (Ni. 5-9).
आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—Since the word आयुः (*āyuḥ*) means food (Ni. 3-9) and also life-breath or lifespan (Ni. 10-34), both meanings can be given here.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इंद्रः सहपा बलवान्पृत्सु संग्रामेषु तरणिः । शत्रूनुत्तीर्य वर्तत
> इति तरणिः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अर्वा न । यथार्वा बलवानश्वः शत्रुबलं तरति तथा
> रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ व्यानतिर्वा पृत्सुन्मेहनावान् ! मिह्यते सिच्यते दीयतेऽर्थिभ्य
> इति मेहनं धनं । तद्वान्भवति । तादृश इंद्रः कारे । क्रियत इति कारो यज्ञादिः ।
> तस्मिन्यज्ञॆ भगो न पूषा देव इव हव्यो हवनीयो मतीनां स्तोत्यणां स्तुतीनां
> वा पितेव पालयिता चारुः कमनीयः सुहवः सुष्ठाह्वानोपेतो वयोधा
> अन्नस्य दाता भवति ॥ सहावा । सहोऽस्यास्तीति मतुबर्थे छंदसीवनिपाविति वनिप् ।
> अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायां दीर्घः । पृत्सु । पृतनाशब्दस्य सौ परतः मांस्पृत्सूनामुपसंख्यानमिति पृदादेशः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । व्यानशिः ।
> अशू व्याप्तावित्यस्माच्छंदसि सदादित्वाक्तिप्रत्ययः । तस्य लिड्वद्भावः । अत आदेरित्यभ्यासस्य दीर्घे कृतेऽशोतेश्वेति नुडागमः । प्रादिसमासः । कारे । करोतेः कर्मणि
> घञ् । कर्षात्वतो घञ्नोंत उदात्त इत्यंतोदात्तत्वं । हव्यः । जुहोतेरचो
> यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । सुहवः । हैयतेर्भानेनुपसर्गस्य । पा-
> ३-३-७५ । इत्यप्प्रत्ययः । संप्रसारणं । प्रत्ययस्य पित्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ।
> आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छंदसीति बहुह्रावुत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra is mighty, and in the pṛtanās, the battles, he is तरणिः (*taraṇiḥ*): he moves on having crossed over his enemies. The illustration is अर्वा न (*arvā na*): as a strong horse crosses the force of the enemy, so he pervades (व्यानशिः (*vyānaśiḥ*)) heaven and earth, the two रोदसी (*rodasī*). He is मेहनावान् (*mehanāvān*): mehana is wealth, which is poured out and given to those who ask, and he possesses it. Such an Indra, in the कारे (*kāre*), that is the sacrifice and the like (what is done, kriyate), is like Bhaga, the god Pūṣan, to be invoked (हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)); he is the protector of the praisers or of the praises (मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)), like a father; lovely (चारुः (*cāruḥ*)); possessed of a good invocation (सुहवः (*suhavaḥ*)); and giver of food (वयोधा (*vayodhā*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहावा (*sahāvā*)—Indra, endowed with might
- अर्वा न (*arvā na*)—like a swiftly running horse
- पृत्सु (*pṛtsu*)—in battles
- तरणिः (*taraṇiḥ*)—crossing over the enemy armies
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- व्यानशिः (*vyānaśiḥ*)—pervading
- मेहनावान् (*mehanāvān*)—he is the distributor of wealth in the form of rain
- कारे (*kāre*)—in the sacrifice
- भगो न (*bhago na*)—like Bhaga
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—fit to receive the oblation
- मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)—to the praisers
- पितेव (*piteva*)—like a protector, a father
- चारुः (*cāruḥ*)—of lovely form
- सुहवः (*suhavaḥ*)—possessed of an excellent invocation
- वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)—the giver of food

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, endowed with might, like a swiftly running horse, crosses over the enemy armies in battles, pervades heaven and earth, and distributes wealth in the form of rain. In the sacrifice, like Bhaga

### Printed p. 120

*Bhāvārtha (continued)*
He is worthy to receive the oblation, a protector of the praisers, of lovely form, one who is invoked with excellent invocation, and a giver of food.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Vigorous, rushing through (hostile), like a warhorse, he has pervaded heaven and earth, sending down rain : he is to be worshipped with oblations at the solemn (rite) like Bhaga : he is as the father of those who adore (him); he is beautiful, worthy of invocation, the bestower of food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

- सहावा (*sahāvā*)—The word सहः (*sahaḥ*) is read among the names for strength (Ni. 3-9). The meaning is "one who has strength".
- तरणिः (*taraṇiḥ*)—शत्रूनुत्तीर्य वर्तत इति तरणिः । (*śatrūnuttīrya vartata iti taraṇiḥ |*) Because he overcomes the enemies, that is, defeats them and stays steadfast, Indra is called taraṇi.
- मेहनावान् (*mehanāvān*)—मिह सेचने । (*miha secane |*) मिह्यते सिच्यते दीयतेऽर्थिभ्य इति मेहनं धनं तद्वान् । (*mihyate sicyate dīyate 'rthibhya iti mehanaṃ dhanaṃ tadvān |*) What is given to those who ask is wealth. The meaning is "one who possesses such wealth".
- मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)—The word मति (*mati*) is read among the names for the wise (Ni. 3-19). Here the commentator has explained मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*) as "of the hymns" or "of those who praise".
- कारे (*kāre*)—क्रियत इति कारो यज्ञादिः । (*kriyata iti kāro yajñādiḥ |*) The rite that is done or carried out, that is, the sacrificial rite.
- सुहवः (*suhavaḥ*)—सुष्ठाह्वानोपेतः । (*suṣṭhāhvānopetaḥ |*) One who is invoked well, that is, with faith: one who is called, with mantras, by the priests such as the Hotṛ to come to the sacrificial altar.
- अन्नस्य दाता । (*annasya dātā |*) वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)—The word वयः (*vayaḥ*) is read among the names for food (Ni. 3-9). He bears food, that is, he gives food to those who ask.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स इंद्रो दिवो द्युलोकस्य रजसोंतरिक्षस्य च धर्ता धारकः पृष्टः सर्वत्र
> वर्तमानो रथो न तदियो रथ इवोर्धो वायुरूर्ध्वं गंता वसुभिः सहायतया निवसद्भिमरुद्धिर्नियुत्पान्सहायवान् । यद्वा नेत्ययमुत्तरेणापि
> संबध्यते । यथा वायुर्नियुत्वान्नियुन्नामकवडवाभिस्तद्वानेवमिंद्रो वसुभिर्मरुद्धिः सहायवान् । तथा क्षपां वस्ता रात्रिमाच्छादयनूर्यस्य जगत्पकाशकस्यादित्यस्य जनिता जनयिता भागं भजनीयं वाजं कर्मफलरूपमन्नं विभक्ता साधु
> विभागकर्ता भवति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । धिषणेव । यथाड्यानां वागस्येदमिति विभागं
> करोति तद्वत् ॥ रजसः । रंज राग इत्यस्माद्भरंजिभ्यां कित् । उ. ४-२१६ । इत्यसुन् ।
> कित्वान्नलोपः । रज्यते प्रकाशेनेति रजोंतरिक्षं । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । वस्ता । वस
> आच्छादन इत्यस्य तृचि रूपं । जनिता ! जनयतेस्तृचि जनिता मंत्र इति निपातनाण्णिलोपः । चित्वादंतोदात्तः विभक्ता । भज सेवायामित्यस्य साधुकारिण्यर्थे तृन् ।
> एकाच उपदेश इतीट् प्रतिषेधः । तादौ च निति कृत्यतानिति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra is the upholder of heaven, the world of light, and of the रजसः (*rajasaḥ*), the atmosphere. पृष्टः (*pṛṣṭaḥ*) means present everywhere. Like his own chariot he is ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*), one who goes upward; he is वायुः (*vāyuḥ*), the wind. He is नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*), possessed of helpers, through the Vasus, the Maruts who dwell with him as helpers. Or else, the word न (*na*) is connected also with what follows: as the wind is नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*), possessed of the mares called Niyut, so Indra is accompanied by the Vasus, the Maruts. Likewise he covers the night; he is the begetter of the sun, the illuminer of the world; he is the apportioner of the portion, the worshipful food (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)) that is the fruit of rites, a good divider. The example is धिषणेव (*dhiṣaṇeva*): as speech divides among the wealthy, "this is his", so he divides.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of heaven
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- धर्ता (*dhartā*)—the upholder
- पृष्टः (*pṛṣṭaḥ*)—present everywhere
- रथो न (*ratho na*)—like his chariot
- ऊर्ध्वः वायुः (*ūrdhvaḥ vāyuḥ*)—going upward
- वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*)—with the Vasus
- नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*)—joined (with them)
- क्षपां (*kṣapāṃ*)—the night
- वस्ता (*vastā*)—who covers (with darkness)
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- जनिता (*janitā*)—the begetter
- धिषणा इव (*dhiṣaṇā iva*)—like the speech that has a rich man's wealth divided
- भागं (*bhāgaṃ*)—worshipful
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- विभक्ता (*vibhaktā*)—the divider

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra is the upholder of heaven and the atmosphere, present everywhere, going upward like his chariot, joined with the Vasus. He covers the night with darkness, is the begetter of the sun, and divides the worshipful food, like the speech that has a rich man's wealth divided.

### Printed p. 122

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The upholder of heaven and of the firmament, the wind, like a chariot traversing the upper (region) accompanied by the Vasus; the clother of the night (with gloom). the parent of the sun, the distributor of the portion (allotted to the pious), like the words (of the wealthy appropriating to all) the food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धर्ता दिवो रजसः (*dhartā divo rajasaḥ*)—For the word रजः (*rajaḥ*) Yāska gave the etymology: रजो रजतेर्ज्योती रज उच्यते । (*rajo rajaterjyotī raja ucyate |*) उदकं रज उच्यते । (*udakaṃ raja ucyate |*) लोका रजांस्युच्यंते (*lokā rajāṃsyucyaṃte*) (Ni. 4-19). रज्यते प्रकाशेनेति रजोंतरिक्षं (*rajyate prakāśeneti rajoṃtarikṣaṃ*)—Indra is the regulator of heaven and the atmosphere; that is the meaning.

पृष्टः ऊर्ध्वः रथः न वायुः (*pṛṣṭaḥ ūrdhvaḥ rathaḥ na vāyuḥ*)—Just as Indra's chariot moves everywhere, that is, in all places and in the upper region, so Indra too goes to the worlds above, heaven and the rest. Or, if only the words पृष्टः ऊर्ध्व रथः (*pṛṣṭaḥ ūrdhva rathaḥ*) are explained, the meaning is: he has a chariot able to travel in the upper region, in heaven and so on. In that case the word of comparison न (*na*) has to be joined with the word वायुः (*vāyuḥ*) in explaining. Then:

वायुः न वसुभिः नियुत्वान् (*vāyuḥ na vasubhiḥ niyutvān*)—The sense can be given: Indra, helped by the Marut deities, like the wind that has the vehicle called Niyuta. Or वसुभिर्नियुत्वान्—निवसद्भिमरुद्भिर्नियुत्वान् सहायवान् (*vasubhirniyutvān—nivasadbhimarudbhirniyutvān sahāyavān*)—the meaning can also be given as: one who has obtained help from the Maruts who are always with Indra.

क्षपां (*kṣapāṃ*)—Since the word क्षपा (*kṣapā*) is read among the names of night (Ni. 22-8), क्षपां (*kṣapāṃ*) means the night together with its darkness.

जनिता सूर्यस्य (*janitā sūryasya*)—It has been explained earlier that the sun rises and shines by Indra's power.

विभक्ता भागं धिषणेव वाजं (*vibhaktā bhāgaṃ dhiṣaṇeva vājaṃ*)—यथाड्यानां वागस्येदमिति करोति तद्वत् कर्मफलरूपमन्नं साधु विभागकर्ता भवति । (*yathāḍyānāṃ vāgasyedamiti karoti tadvat karmaphalarūpamannaṃ sādhu vibhāgakartā bhavati |*) The sense of this sentence is: as the wealthy divide, saying "this is for you, this is for him", so Indra distributes food and the like, the fruit in accordance with their rites, to those who have performed sacrifices and other rites.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः।
> अस्मिन्भरे । बिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्धार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन् संग्रामे
> शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृद्धं । यद्वा शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखकरं मघवानं
> धनवंतं अत एवेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोऽतिशयेन
> नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा शृण्वंतमस्माभिः
> क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतमुग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि
> वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घ्नंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संजितं
> सम्यग्जेतारं त्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योरित्यस्य निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । हुवेम । हैयतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणे कृते
> शपो लुकि कृते च लिजि रूपं । निघातः । भरे । भृञ् भरणे । घः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । वाजसात् । षणु दार् । भावे क्तिन् । जनसनेत्यादिनानुनासिकस्यात्वं ।
> बहुप्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । समत्तु । अद भक्षणे । संपूर्वात् क्विप् । संभक्षयंति
> योद्धृणामायूंषीति समदः संग्रामाः । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । घ्नंतं । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्य शतरि गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । हो हंतेरिति घत्वं । संजितं ।
> जि जये । क्विप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, वाजसात् (*vājasāt*): he in whom there is the winning (सातिः (*sātiḥ*)) of food (वाज (*vāja*)), is वाजसातिः (*vājasātiḥ*). भरे (*bhare*): because by it the warriors bear the fortune of victory, भरः (*bharaḥ*) is battle; in this battle. शुनं (*śunaṃ*) means swollen, grown by zeal; or else शुनं (*śunaṃ*) is a name for happiness, so "giver of happiness". मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*) is the wealthy one, and therefore इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*), endowed with unsurpassed lordship; नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*), the supreme leader of the whole world: you we, the Kuśikas, invoke for the sacrifice. Likewise, hearing the praise made by us, शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*); उग्रं (*ugraṃ*), terrible to the enemies; समत्सु (*samatsu*), in battles, slaying all the demons denoted by Vṛtra (वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)); संजितं (*saṃjitaṃ*), the full conqueror of the enemies' wealth: you we invoke for protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—proceeding for the sake of food
- भरे (*bhare*)—in the battle
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—one who grows through zeal, or who produces happiness
- मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*)—wealthy
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—endowed with unsurpassed lordship
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—who is the leader
- (you) हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call, praying
- शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—who listens (to our praises)
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—who is terrible to enemies
- समत्सु (*samatsu*)—in battles
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the demons beginning with Vṛtra
- घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*)—who destroys, slaying
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—the wealth (of the enemies)
- संजितं (*saṃjitaṃ*)—who gathers (for us)
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection

### Printed p. 124

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in the battle that is fought for the sake of food, you who give happiness, are wealthy, endowed with unsurpassed lordship, a leader, who listen to our praises, are terrible to enemies, slay and destroy the demons beginning with Vṛtra in battles, and gather the enemies' wealth for us—you we call, praying, for protection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terri- ble in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The special topics of this ṛk have been explained earlier. This is the fiftieth sūkta.**NOTE**

## Sūkta 50 (Maṇḍala 3)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रः स्वाहेति पंचर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं ॥ दशरात्रॆ नवमेऽहनि मरुत्वतीयशस्त्र इदं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । तृतीयस्येंद्रः स्वाहा
> गायत्साम । आ. ८-७ । इति ॥
> अनुवादवु—इंद्रः स्वाहा ऎंब ई सूक्तवु नाल्कनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि हन्नॆरडनॆय
> सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि ऐदु ऋक्कुगळिरुवुवु ई सूक्तक्कॆ विश्वामित्रनु ऋषियु ; इंद्रनु देवतॆयु
> त्रिष्टुप्छंदस्सु. दशरात्रवॆंब यागद ऒंभत्तनॆय दिनदल्लि मरुत्वतीयशस्त्रमंत्रगळन्नु पठिसुवाग
> ई सूक्तद विनियोगविरुवुदॆंदु आश्वलायनशौतसूत्रद-तृतीयस्येंद्रः स्वाहा गायत्साम
> ऎंब सूत्रदिंद विवृतवागिरुवुदु. (अ. ८-७)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The twelfth sūkta, इंद्रः स्वाहा (*iṃdraḥ svāhā*), of five ṛks, is by Viśvāmitra, in the triṣṭubh metre, addressed to Indra. On the ninth day of the Daśarātra this sūkta is used in the Marutvatīya Śastra. The Sūtra says: तृतीयस्येंद्रः स्वाहा गायत्साम (*tṛtīyasyeṃdraḥ svāhā gāyatsāma*) (Ā. 8-7). The Kannada Anuvāda repeats this: the sūkta is the twelfth in the fourth anuvāka, with five ṛks, seer Viśvāmitra, deity Indra, metre Triṣṭubh, used when the Marutvatīya Śastra mantras are recited on the ninth day of the Daśarātra sacrifice, as set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः॒ स्वाहा॑ पिबतु॒ यस्य॒ सोम॑ आ॒गत्या॒ तुम्रो॑ वृष॒भो  ॒॑
> मरुत्वान् ।  
> ओरु॒व्यचाः॑ पृणतामे॒भिरन्नै॒रास्य॑ ह॒विस्त॒न्व१॒ः॑काम॑मृध्याः ॥१॥

> *iṃdraḥ svāhā pibatu yasya soma āgatyā tumro vṛṣabho*  
> *marutvān |*  
> *oruvyacāḥ pṛṇatāmebhirannairāsya havistanvaḥkāmamṛdhyāḥ ‖1‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । स्वाहा । पिबतु । यस्य । सोमः । आगत्य । तुम्रः । वृषभः । मरुत्वान् ।  
> आ । उरुव्यचाः । पृणतां । एभिः । अन्नैः । आ । अस्य । हविः । तन्नः । कामं । यध्याः॥

> *iṃdraḥ | svāhā | pibatu | yasya | somaḥ | āgatya | tumraḥ | vṛṣabhaḥ | marutvān |*  
> *ā | uruvyacāḥ | pṛṇatāṃ | ebhiḥ | annaiḥ | ā | asya | haviḥ | tannaḥ | kāmaṃ | yadhyāḥ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमिंद्रः स्वाहा स्वाहाकृतमिमं सोमं पिबतु । यस्येंद्रस्यायं सोमः
> स इंद्रो यज्ञं प्रत्यागत्य तुम्रः कर्मविघ्नकारिणां हिंसको वृषभो यष्टणामभिमतफलवर्षको मरुत्वान्मरुद्धिस्तद्वान् उरुव्यचाः प्रभूतव्याप्तिः सन् एभिरस्माभिर्दत्तैरन्नैः सोमादिलक्षणैर्हविर्भिरा पृणतां । समंतात्पूरयतु । ततोऽस्येंद्रस्य संबंधिनस्तन्वः शरीरस्य कामं पुष्पादिलक्षणविषयमभिलाषं हविरस्माभिर्दत्तमा ऋध्याः । सर्वतः पूरयतु ॥ तुम्रः । तुमिराहननार्थः । उरुव्यचाः ।
> व्यचेरसुन् । व्यचेः कुटादित्वमनसीति वक्तव्यमित्यत्रानसीति पर्युदासात् जिताभावः । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । ऋध्याः । ऋध्योतेराशीर्लिज रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May this Indra drink this soma offered with स्वाहा (*svāhā*) (the svāhā-call). The Indra whose soma this is, having come to the sacrifice, is तुम्रः (*tumraḥ*), the destroyer of those who obstruct the rite; वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*), the one who showers the desired fruit on the sacrificers; मरुत्वान् (*marutvān*), accompanied by the Maruts; उरुव्यचाः (*uruvyacāḥ*), of wide extent. Let him fill himself fully with these foods given by us, the oblations beginning with soma. Then let him fulfil on all sides the desire of this Indra's body, whose object is flowers and the like, the oblation given by us.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra drink the Soma offered with the cry svāhā. The Indra for whom this Soma is intended, having come to the sacrifice, being a destroyer of those who cause obstacles to the sacrifice, a showerer of desired fruit, accompanied by the Maruts and widely pervading, may attain full satisfaction with these Soma-oblations given by us. May this oblation given by us bring full nourishment to Indra's body.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May Indra drink the libation ; he of whom is the Soma, having come to the sacrifice ; he who is the repeller (of adversaries), the showerer (of benefits), the lord of the Maruts ; may he, the wide-pervading, be pleased with these (sacrificial) viands ; may the oblation be adequate to the wants of his body.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव जवसे यज्ञं प्रत्यागमनाय सपर्यू परिचारकौ ९ री आ
> युनज्मॆ । रथे योजयामि । प्रदिवः पुरातनस्त्वं ययोरश्वयोः श्रुष्टिं वेगं ।

> हरयो रथे योजतास्तेऽश्वा इह कर्मणि त्वां त्वां धेयुः । यज्ञं प्रति धारयंतु । तत आगतस्त्वं सुषुतस्य सुष्वभिषुतं चारोः कमनीयमस्यॆमं सोमं
> तु क्षिप्रं पिब ॥ सपर्यू । सपरशब्दः कंड्वादिः । तदंतादौणादिकः कुप्रत्ययः । आवः।
> अव रक्षणादिषु । छांदसे लजि रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । धेयुः । दधातेराशीर्लिजि किदाशिषीति यासुट् । एर्लिजि । पा. ६-४-६७ । इत्येकारादेशः । निघातः ।
> पिब । पादादित्पादनिघातः । सुषुतस्य । सुञ् अभिषवे । कर्मणि क्तः । गतिरनंतर इति
> गतिस्वरः । उपसर्गात्सुनोतीत्यादिना संहितायां षत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, for your speed, that is, for your coming to the sacrifice, I yoke to the chariot the two attendants (the two horses)." You, the ancient one, follow the speed (श्रुष्टिं (*śruṣṭiṃ*)) of which two horses; Yāska says "श्रुष्टीति क्षिप्रनामेति (*śruṣṭīti kṣipranāmeti*)" (śruṣṭi is a name for "quick"), and you go along with that speed. O Sushipra, Indra of fair jaws, may the bay horses yoked to the chariot bear you here in this rite, may they hold you toward the sacrifice. Having come thence, quickly drink this well-pressed, lovely Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रदिवः (*pradivaḥ*)—(O Indra) you, the ancient one
- ययोः (*yayoḥ*)—of which horses
- श्रुष्टिं (*śruṣṭiṃ*)—the speed
- आनु आवः (*ānu āvaḥ*)—you follow, of such
- सपर्यू (*saparyū*)—the horses that serve you
- ते (*te*)—your
- जवसे (*javase*)—for swift going (to come to the sacrifice)
- आ युनज्मि (*ā yunajmi*)—I join and bind to the chariot
- सुशिप्र (*suśipra*)—O Indra of excellent cheeks
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—your horses
- इह (*iha*)—in this rite
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- धेयुः (*dheyuḥ*)—may they bear and bring
- सुष्टुतस्य (*suṣṭutasya*)—of what is excellently pressed **NOTE**
- चारोः (*cāroḥ*)—and lovely
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Soma
- तु (*tu*)—quickly
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you, the ancient one, follow the speed of certain horses; I join to your chariot those horses that serve you, so that they bring you quickly to this sacrifice. O Indra of excellent cheeks, may your horses bear you here in this rite. Drink quickly this Soma, well pressed and lovely.
