##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विविक्वान्वेकवानिंद्रोग्निर्वा मे मम मनीषां देवताविषयां स्तुतिं
> प्राविदत् । प्रकर्षण जानातु । तत्र दृष्टांतः । चरंतीं यवस इतस्ततो गच्छंतीं
> प्रयुतां पृथग्भूतामेकाकिनीमगोपां गोप्तृरहितां यथाकामं चरंतीं
> धेनुं नवसूतिकां गामिव देवतानां प्रीणयित्रीं स्तुतिमविददित्यन्वयः । या
> स्तुतिरूपा धेनुः सद्यश्चित्तदानीमेव धासेः । धारयति प्राणान् धीयते दीयतेर्थिभ्य इति वा धासिरन्नं । कर्मणि षष्ठी । भूरि बह्वन्नमपेक्षितं फलं दुदुहे दुग्धे
> इंद्रोग्निरन्ये च देवा अस्याः स्तुतिरूपाया धेनोस्तत्तस्यान्नभूतस्य पयसः
> पनितारः स्तोतारो भवंति । यद्वा । इंद्राग्नी स्तोतारो वयं चास्या धेनोस्तत्पयः प्राप्नुमः ॥ विविक्वान् ! विचिर् पृथग्भाव इत्यस्य क्वसौ रूपं । अविदत् । विद
> ज्ञान इत्यस्य लजि बहुलं छंदसीति शः । दुदुहे । दुह प्रपूरण इत्यस्य लिटि रूपं ।
> यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । पनितारः । पन स्तुतावित्यस्य तृचि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vivikvān, that is Indra or Agni, मे (*me*) "my" मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*) praise directed to the deities, let him know well (प्राविदत् (*prāvidat*)). The illustration: as one knows a cow that is चरंतीं (*caraṃtīṃ*) wandering hither and thither for fodder, प्रयुतां (*prayutāṃ*) separated, alone, अगोपां (*agopāṃ*) without a herdsman, roaming at will, a धेनुं (*dhenuṃ*) newly calved cow—so (let him know) the praise that gratifies the gods; this is the construction. The praise in the form of a cow that सद्यश्चित् (*sadyaścit*) at that very moment milks abundant धासेः (*dhāseḥ*): dhāsi is food, either because it sustains the life-breaths or because it is given to those who seek it; the genitive is in the sense of the object. भूरि (*bhūri*) abundant food, the desired fruit, it milks. Indra, Agni and the other gods are पनितारः (*panitāraḥ*), praisers, of the milk, that is of the food-like milk, of this cow in the form of praise. Or else: Indra and Agni are the praisers, and we obtain that milk of this cow. (The remainder of the block gives the grammar of vivikvān, avidat, duduhe and panitāraḥ.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- या (*yā*)—which cow in the form of praise
- सद्यश्चित् (*sadyaścit*)—immediately
- धासेः (*dhāseḥ*)—food
- भूरि (*bhūri*)—abundantly
- दुदुहे (*duduhe*)—milks (such a one)
- मे (*me*)—my
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—the cow in the form of praise
- विविक्वान् (*vivikvān*)—Indra the discerning
- चरंतीं (*caraṃtīṃ*)—running while eating grass
- प्रयुतां (*prayutāṃ*)—solitary
- अगोपां (*agopāṃ*)—roaming freely without a cowherd
- धेनुं (*dhenuṃ*)—as one knows a cow
- प्र अविदत् (*pra avidat*)—may he know
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni (and the other gods also)
- अस्याः (*asyāḥ*)—of this cow in the form of praise
- पनितारः (*panitāraḥ*)—are the praisers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As one knows a cow that runs about for grass and roams alone at will without a cowherd, let the discerning Indra know my praise, which is like a cow and which yields abundant food. Indra, Agni and the other deities also are praisers of this cow in the form of praise.

### Printed p. 381

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May the discriminating Indra apprehend my glorification (of the gods), which is (free) as a milch cow, grazing alone, without a cowherd, one who is readily milked, yielding abundant nourishment, and of whom Agni and Indra (and we), are the commenders.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this mantra praise is compared to a cow, and the quality common to the two is shown. Just as the protection of a cow that yields milk in plenty and satisfies its owner is necessary, so the same protection is necessary in the matter of praise; thus praise is extolled. The epithets used here to extol praise should be examined, and afterwards the power and the fruitfulness of praise should be considered.

In the present verse it is prayed that Indra and the others may know the cow in the form of praise. The word मनीषा (*manīṣā*) is used as a synonym of praise. This manīṣā is described as the giver of food. The word धासि (*dhāsi*) means food. There is a little distinctiveness in the use of this word.

धासेः (*dhāseḥ*)—this word is read among the names of food, धासिः इरा (*dhāsiḥ irā*) and so on (Ni. 2-7). It is derived from the root थेट् (*theṭ*) meaning "to drink"**NOTE**, and gives the meaning of food in the form of oblation. Or it may also mean "that which sustains life"; the import is "that which makes one stand firm". To understand its import in detail, some examples should be examined.

कविं केतुं धासिं भानुमद्रेर्हिन्वंति शं राज्यं रोदस्योः । (*kaviṃ ketuṃ dhāsiṃ bhānumadrerhinvaṃti śaṃ rājyaṃ rodasyoḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-6-2)

Here the word is an epithet of Vaiśvānara Agni. The epithet धासिं (*dhāsiṃ*) is in the sense of one who lifts up and protects the praiser. Sāyaṇa has given the import: धासिं (*dhāsiṃ*)—धर्तारं (*dhartāraṃ*).

प्राक्तुभ्य इंद्रः प्र वृधो अहभ्यः प्रांतरिक्षात्प्र समुद्रस्य धासेः । प्र वातस्य प्रथसः प्र ज्यो अंतात्प्र सिंधुभ्यो रिरिचे प्र क्षितिभ्यः ॥ (*prāktubhya iṃdraḥ pra vṛdho ahabhyaḥ prāṃtarikṣātpra samudrasya dhāseḥ | pra vātasya prathasaḥ pra jyo aṃtātpra siṃdhubhyo ririce pra kṣitibhyaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-89-11)

Here this epithet is used to describe the growth of Indra. Indra is described as grown beyond heaven and earth. And since he is said to be grown beyond even the place that holds the sea, the greatness of Indra is understood. The word dhāsi means "that which holds". The place that holds the sea is utterly firm; the import is that Indra has grown beyond even that. In this manner the word is used in the sense of "holder".

### Printed p. 382
The word *dhāsi* also occurs in passages such as महीं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धासिं पृथुज्रयसे रीरधा सुवृक्तिं । (*mahīṃ mitrasya varuṇasya dhāsiṃ pṛthujrayase rīradhā suvṛktiṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-30-1). Although *dhāsi* means "food" in such places, food sustains life and strength, and for that reason "food" has *dhāsi* as a synonym. In the same way, in the present Ṛk the praise addressed to Indra and the others sustains the sacrificer's life, or gives him food. This is the purport.

*Manīṣām*: this word is commonly used as a synonym of "praise". The Nirukta reads it among the names of the wise (*manīṣī*). Some places in Sāyaṇa's commentary say that the explanation of *manīṣā* as *manasa īṣā* is acceptable. It can mean a distinguished talent or a power of imagination. This power, filled with devotion and moved by feeling, ripens in praise that takes the form of poetry. That is why the word is used as a synonym of praise. Its full sense is contained in the word used in the mantra quoted below:

मनीषिणः प्र भरध्वं मनीषां यथायथा मतयः संति नृणां । इंद्रं सत्यैरेरयामा कृतेभिः स हि वीरो गिर्वणस्युर्विदानः ॥ (*manīṣiṇaḥ pra bharadhvaṃ manīṣāṃ yathāyathā matayaḥ saṃti nṛṇāṃ | iṃdraṃ satyairerayāmā kṛtebhiḥ sa hi vīro girvaṇasyurvidānaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-111-1).

Here it says that the wise should compose a *manīṣā* addressed to Indra, and there is a coherence in this. According to whatever intellectual power and whatever capacity of imagination the human sacrificers have, they should compose their praise. The first word *manīṣiṇaḥ* means poets with such capacity; the second word *manīṣām* means the work of such poets, inspired by feeling. A work composed in address to the deities is known as praise. Thus:

पतंगो वाचं मनसा बिभर्ति तां गंधर्वोऽवदद्गर्भे अंतः । तां द्योतमानां स्वर्यं मनीषामृतस्य पदे कवयो निपांति ॥ (*pataṃgo vācaṃ manasā bibharti tāṃ gaṃdharvo 'vadadgarbhe aṃtaḥ | tāṃ dyotamānāṃ svaryaṃ manīṣāmṛtasya pade kavayo nipāṃti ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-77-2).

Here the word *manīṣām* has a very deep meaning. It is not merely mental talent. The principle of speech is indicated here: that which lies within the sun, which has the form of the three Vedas, which is of the nature of the Word-Brahman. *Manīṣām* is explained as मनसः ईशित्रिं (*manasaḥ īśitriṃ*). That is, the meaning may be given as that which has an independent movement of mind, free of dependence on another, and so on. In passages such as मनीषिणो मनसा पृच्छत (*manīṣiṇo manasā pṛcchata*) (10-85-4), "let the wise examine with inner vision", the word

### Printed p. 383
*manīṣi* does not mean a principle grasped by the intellect alone, but the power of mind able to realise the supreme truth by inner vision. This power is inspired by a feeling of the nature of *samādhi*. A mere intellectual power without *samādhi* cannot grasp this truth.

कामस्तदग्रे समवर्तताधि मनसो रेतः प्रथमं यदासीत् । सतो बंधुमसति निरविंदन् हृदि प्रतीष्या कवयो मनीषा ॥ (*kāmastadagre samavartatādhi manaso retaḥ prathamaṃ yadāsīt | sato baṃdhumasati niraviṃdan hṛdi pratīṣyā kavayo manīṣā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-4).

In such mantras too, the word *manīṣā* indicates the power of the self able to grasp the laws of the world, such as the creation by the Lord. हृदि निरुद्दया बुद्ध्या (*hṛdi niruddayā buddhyā*): this world-principle can be reached only by the intellect concentrated in the heart in the form of *samādhi*. This is the purport. In the same way, in the contexts that give this word the meaning "praise", it must be understood as praise capable of knowing the principle of the Lord. Since this praise bestows every prosperity, its nature is described by धासेः दुदुहे (*dhāseḥ duduhe*): praise able to draw forth the wealth of food. The prayer is that Indra and the others may take note of our praise, so excellent and so able to know the supreme truth.

कस्ते मद इंद्र रंत्यो भूद्दुरो गिरो अभ्यु १ ग्रो वि धाव । कद्वाहो अर्वागुप मा मनीषा आ त्वा शक्यामुपमं राधो अन्नैः ॥ (*kaste mada iṃdra raṃtyo bhūdduro giro abhyu 1 gro vi dhāva | kadvāho arvāgupa mā manīṣā ā tvā śakyāmupamaṃ rādho annaiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-29-3).

In this Ṛk also Sāyaṇa has said that the same view is indicated. He explains मनीषा सर्वार्थदर्शिनी प्रज्ञा, सर्वगुणग्राहिणी स्तुतिर्वा (*manīṣā sarvārthadarśinī prajñā, sarvaguṇagrāhiṇī stutirvā*) as a supernatural insight that shows the secret of all things, or praise that grasps all qualities.

This *manīṣā* is compared to a cow without a herdsman. The epithet *agopām* allows two meanings. First, "without rule", that is, independent. Independence here does not mean unrestrained. As the *Kāvyaprakāśa* describes the poet's independence, नियतिकृतिनियमरहितां ह्लादैकमयीमनस्य परतंत्रां (*niyatikṛtiniyamarahitāṃ hlādaikamayīmanasya parataṃtrāṃ*), one meaning is that the poet's talent that makes this praise is not bound by external rules; it is praise full of independent feeling and of the nature of *samādhi*. Or else, because of the epithet *agopām*, the need for protection may be shown. Just as a cow without a herdsman needs protection, the praises at hand also need the grace of the Lord. This is the purport. However much milk a cow without a herdsman may be able to give,

### Printed p. 384
that ability is wasted; in the same way any power of a man who has not won the Lord's grace is useless. Another purport may therefore be given: that Indra and Agni should know the distinction of this praise and show favour.

*Prayutām*: just as two meanings can be given to the epithet *agopām*, the same is possible with the epithet *prayutām*. The root *yu* is used in both senses, "mixed" and "unmixed". *Prayuta* may mean "joined together", or "not joined to anything, solitary".

गावो यवं प्रयुता अर्यो अक्षन् ता अपश्यं सहगोपाश्चरंतीः । हवा इदर्यो अभितः समायन्कियदासु स्वपतिष्छंदयाते ॥ (*gāvo yavaṃ prayutā aryo akṣan tā apaśyaṃ sahagopāścaraṃtīḥ | havā idaryo abhitaḥ samāyankiyadāsu svapatiṣchaṃdayāte ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-27-8).

Here the scene of cows gathered together is described. For *prayutāḥ* the gloss is प्रकर्षण मिश्रिताः परस्परेण सह भूताः । (*prakarṣaṇa miśritāḥ paraspareṇa saha bhūtāḥ |*); the purport is that they have mingled with one another and are all crowded together. But in the present Ṛk this word stands together with the epithet *agopām*, so the purport is that the cow is solitary, not mixed with other cows, without a protector, and seeking the protection of the gods.

*Panitāraḥ*: this word is formed from the root *pan*, "to praise". The Nirukta authors read *panasyati* and *panāyate* among the names of the act of honouring. The word is used in the senses "worship", "extol", "show devotion". For example:

रथे तिष्ठन्नयति वाजिनः पुरो यत्रयत्र कामयते सुषारथिः । अभीशूनां महिमानं पनायत मनः पश्चादनु यच्छंति रश्मयः ॥ (*rathe tiṣṭhannayati vājinaḥ puro yatrayatra kāmayate suṣārathiḥ | abhīśūnāṃ mahimānaṃ panāyata manaḥ paścādanu yacchaṃti raśmayaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-75-6).

Citing this Ṛk, they explain the context: the reins tied to the chariot, which hold the horses, are praised as most excellent, and then it is said, "O people, honour such reins." The Nirukta authors explain: हे जनाः अभीशूनां महिमानं पूजयत (*he janāḥ abhīśūnāṃ mahimānaṃ pūjayata*); the purport is "O men, worship these *abhīśu* (rein or rope)" (Ni. 9-6).

यदेव पनाय्क्यं कर्म तदेतदभिवदति । (*yadeva panāykyaṃ karma tadetadabhivadati |*) (Ai. Brā. 6-15). This sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa is explained as: the mantra recites that very act of Soma-drinking which is worthy of honour.

### Printed p. 385
प्रवो धियो मंद्रयुवो विपन्युवः पनस्युवः संवसनेष्वक्रमुः । (*pravo dhiyo maṃdrayuvo vipanyuvaḥ panasyuvaḥ saṃvasaneṣvakramuḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-86-17).

The use of the word here shows its exact meaning. The two words *vipanyuvaḥ* and *panasyuvaḥ* are used together, and both are formed from the root *pan*. *Panasyuvaḥ* is explained as those who desire praise, and *vipanyuvaḥ* as praisers. In the present Ṛk, although *panitāraḥ* means praisers, one must note the special point here. This is not a scene of man praising and worshipping the gods; it is a scene of Indra and the others applauding man's praise. Hence *panitāraḥ* here means those who applaud, those who commend. This is the purport.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः॒ सु पू॒षा वृष॑णा सु॒हस्ता॑ दि॒वो न प्री॒ताः श॑श॒यं  ॑
> दु॑दुह्रे ।  
> विश्वे॒ यद॑स्यां र॒णयं॑त दे॒वाः प्र वोऽत्र॑ वसवः सु॒म्नम॑श्यां ॥ २ ॥

> *iṃdraḥ su pūṣā vṛṣaṇā suhastā divo na prītāḥ śaśayaṃ*  
> *duduhre |*  
> *viśve yadasyāṃ raṇayaṃta devāḥ pra vo 'tra vasavaḥ sumnamaśyāṃ ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । सु । पूषा । वृषणा । सुहस्ता । दिवः । न । प्रीताः । शशयं । दुदुह्रे ।  
> विश्वे । यत् । अस्यां । रणयंत । देवाः । प्र । वः । अत्र । वसवः । सुम्नं अश्यां॥२॥

> *iṃdraḥ | su | pūṣā | vṛṣaṇā | suhastā | divaḥ | na | prītāḥ | śaśayaṃ | duduhre |*  
> *viśve | yat | asyāṃ | raṇayaṃta | devāḥ | pra | vaḥ | atra | vasavaḥ | sumnaṃ aśyāṃ‖2‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वसवः सर्वस्य वासयितारो हे देवा इंद्रः पूषा च वृषणाभिमतफलस्य
> सेक्तारौ सुहस्ता कल्याणपाणी नासत्यौ मित्रावरुणौ वा । राजाना मित्रावरुणा
> सुपाणी इत्यादिषु दृष्टत्वात् । एते सर्वे देवाः । नेति संप्रत्यर्थे । इदानीं
> प्रीताः संतः शशयं नभसि शयानं मेघं दिवो नभसः सकाशात्सु दुदुहे । वृष्टिद्वारापेक्षितं फलं सुष्टु दुहंति । यद्यस्माद्विश्वे सर्वे देवा अस्यां वेद्यां
> रणयंत रमयंते वो युष्माकं संबंधिन्यत्रलोके सुम्मं सुखकरमपेक्षितं
> फलं प्राश्यां । प्राप्णुयां ॥ सुहस्ता । हसेरसिहसीत्यादिना तन्नृत्ययः । नित्तादा-
> Vol. 17

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Vasus, causers of dwelling for all, O gods! Indra and Pūṣan are *vṛṣaṇā*, showerers of the desired fruit, and *suhastā*, fair-handed: either the Nāsatyas or Mitra and Varuṇa, since the epithet is seen in passages such as राजाना मित्रावरुणा सुपाणी (*rājānā mitrāvaruṇā supāṇī*). All these are the gods. *Na* is in the sense of "now". Being pleased now, they have well milked the cloud lying in the sky, *śaśayam*, from heaven, from the sky; that is, they well draw out the fruit needed by way of rain. Since all the gods delight on this altar, may I here, in this world belonging to you, fully obtain the desired fruit that brings happiness." He then begins the grammar: the formation of *suhastā*, with its affix and its accent.**NOTE**

### Printed p. 386

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्युदात्तः । बहुव्रीहावाद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छंदसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । दुदुहे ।
> दुह प्रपूरण इत्यस्य लिटीरयो रे । रणयंत । रमु क्रीडायां । ण्यंतस्य लजं
> रूपं । वर्णव्यापत्तिः । अश्यां । अशू व्याप्तावित्यस्य लिजि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य
> लुक् । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This part is only grammatical: the accent of *suhastā* (initial acute of the compound by the rule on compounds), the form *dudūhe* from the root *duh*, *raṇayanta* from the root *ramu* in the sense of play with the causative, and *aśyām* from the root *aśū* in the sense of pervading, with elision of the stem-vowel and a change of voice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—O Vasus, givers of dwelling
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—givers of what is desired
- सुहस्ता (*suhastā*)—Mitra and Varuṇa, possessed of excellent hands (or the Aśvin deities also)
- न (*na*)—now
- प्रीताः (*prītāḥ*)—being satisfied
- शशयं (*śaśayaṃ*)—the cloud abiding in the sky
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the sky
- सु दुदुहे (*su duduhe*)—have milked, for the sake of rain
- यत् (*yat*)—for that very reason
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods also
- अस्यां (*asyāṃ*)—on this sacrificial altar
- रणयंत (*raṇayaṃta*)—are delighting
- वः (*vaḥ*)—belonging to you
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this place
- सुम्मं (*summaṃ*)—the fruit that brings happiness
- प्र अश्यां (*pra aśyāṃ*)—may I obtain fully

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the givers of dwelling, the god Pūṣan, and Mitra and Varuṇa, givers of what is desired and possessed of excellent hands, being satisfied now, have milked the cloud abiding in the sky from the sky for the sake of rain. For that very reason all the gods too are delighting on this sacrificial altar. May I obtain the fruit that brings happiness in this sacrificial place that belongs to you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra and Pushan, the showerers (of benefits), and the happy-handed Ashwins, well affected towards us, have milked the (cloud) reposing in heaven ; wherefore, Vasus, universal deities, sporting on this (altar), may I here obtain the happiness derived from you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This mantra is recited addressed to the deities who accomplish the sacrifice and, by causing rain, support it. At the beginning stands the praise of deities such as the Vasus, Indra and Pūṣan. The deities named Vasu are addressed with वसवः— सर्वस्य वासयितारः हे देवाः (*vasavaḥ— sarvasya vāsayitāraḥ he devāḥ*). Commonly this word may be an epithet of other deities too. All the deities who bestow grace on man's dwelling may be denoted by the word *vasu*. But from Sāyaṇa's explanation it is understood that in the present Ṛk a separate group of deities with the name Vasu is indicated

### Printed p. 387
. Who are these Vasus? What is their nature? Why do they have this name? For these questions one must look at Yājñavalkya's answer.

अथ हैनं विदग्धः शाकल्यः पप्रच्छ । कति देवा याज्ञवल्केति । .... .... ....त्रयस्त्रिंशत्त्वेव देवा इति । कतमे ते त्रयस्त्रिंशदिति । अष्टौ वसवः, एकादशरुद्राः, द्वादशादित्याः, ते एकत्रिंशत् । इंद्रश्चैव प्रजापतिश्च. (*atha hainaṃ vidagdhaḥ śākalyaḥ papraccha | kati devā yājñavalketi | .... .... ....trayastriṃśattveva devā iti | katame te trayastriṃśaditi | aṣṭau vasavaḥ, ekādaśarudrāḥ, dvādaśādityāḥ, te ekatriṃśat | iṃdraścaiva prajāpatiśca.*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-1-2).

Vidagdha, son of Śakala, asked Yājñavalkya: "How many gods are there?" When Yājñavalkya said "thirty-three", he asked again, "Who are they?" In reply Yājñavalkya explained the number of the gods: "Eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve Ādityas: these make thirty-one gods. Together with Indra and Prajāpati they become thirty-three." As to who these Vasus are:

अग्निश्च पृथिवी च वायुश्चांतरिक्षं चादित्यश्च द्यौश्च चंद्रमाश्च नक्षत्राणि चैते वसवः । एतेषु हीदं सर्वं हितमिति तस्माद्वसव इति ॥ (*agniśca pṛthivī ca vāyuścāṃtarikṣaṃ cādityaśca dyauśca caṃdramāśca nakṣatrāṇi caite vasavaḥ | eteṣu hīdaṃ sarvaṃ hitamiti tasmādvasava iti ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-3).

Agni, the earth, the wind, the atmosphere, the sun, the sky, the moon, the stars: these are the Vasus. Because all beings are placed in them, they are famed by the name Vasus. The explanation of Śaṅkara's commentary is: प्राणिनां कर्मफलाश्रयत्वेन कार्यकारणसंघातरूपेण तन्नि वासत्वेन च विपरिणमंतः जगदिदं सर्वं वासयंति च (*prāṇināṃ karmaphalāśrayatvena kāryakāraṇasaṃghātarūpeṇa tanni vāsatvena ca vipariṇamaṃtaḥ jagadidaṃ sarvaṃ vāsayaṃti ca*). According to the fruit of the actions of living beings they bring about changes in their bodies and limbs, enter into them themselves, provide the conveniences for all of them to dwell, and themselves dwell in all of them; hence the name Vasus.

स मनसा वाचं मिथुनग्ं समभवत् । सोऽष्टौ द्रप्सान्गर्भ्यभवत्तेऽष्टौ वसवोऽसृज्यंत तानस्यामुपादधात् । (*sa manasā vācaṃ mithunagṃ samabhavat | so 'ṣṭau drapsāngarbhyabhavatte 'ṣṭau vasavo 'sṛjyaṃta tānasyāmupādadhāt |*) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-2-6).

Prajāpati united with Speech by mental meditation. Then eight *drapsas* issued forth. They became the eight Vasus. He placed them on the earth. For that reason they are the deities residing on the earth; the Rudras were established in the atmosphere, and the Ādityas in the heavenly world. Since the Vasus are described as the presiding deities of the earth, what is the meaning of the many places where the Vasus are described as dwelling in the atmosphere, as in हग्ंसश्युचिषद्वसुरंतरिक्षसत् (*hagṃsaśyuciṣadvasuraṃtarikṣasat*)? This will be examined further on.

### Printed p. 388
By the mantra अग्निश्च पृथिवी च (*agniśca pṛthivī ca*) it is stated that Agni is one of the Vasus. In some other places the Vasus are said to receive an oblation together with Agni at the morning pressing. So there is room for the questions whether Agni and the Vasus are identical or different deities, and likewise whether Indra and the Vasus are identical or different deities. Even though they are described together with different deities, it becomes clear that the luminous nature of the Vasus is described in the same way everywhere. In the statement that the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas are the deities of the earth, the atmosphere and the heavenly world there are many hidden meanings. For the present, leaving that explanation aside, we may look in a general way at what the Vasus are in the present context.

Prayers such as इंद्रं नो अग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः (*iṃdraṃ no agne vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-10-4) show the relation between the Vasus and Agni. The Chāndogya Upaniṣad describes this same thing: तद्यत्पथमममृतं तद्वसव उपजीवंत्यग्निना मुखेन न वै देवा अश्नंति न पिबंत्येतदेवामृतं दृष्ट्वा तृप्यंति । त एतदेव रूपमभिसंविशंत्येतस्माद्रूपादुद्यंति । स य एतदेवममृतं वेद वसूनामेवैको भूत्वाग्निनैव मुखेनैतदेवामृतं दृष्ट्वा तृप्यंति स एतदेव रूपमभि संवि शत्येतस्माद्रूपादुदेति । स यावदादित्यः पुरस्तादुदेता पश्चादस्तमेता वसूनामेव तावदाधिपत्यं स्वाराज्यं पर्येता ॥ (*tadyatpathamamamṛtaṃ tadvasava upajīvaṃtyagninā mukhena na vai devā aśnaṃti na pibaṃtyetadevāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyaṃti | ta etadeva rūpamabhisaṃviśaṃtyetasmādrūpādudyaṃti | sa ya etadevamamṛtaṃ veda vasūnāmevaiko bhūtvāgninaiva mukhenaitadevāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyaṃti sa etadeva rūpamabhi saṃvi śatyetasmādrūpādudeti | sa yāvadādityaḥ purastādudetā paścādastametā vasūnāmeva tāvadādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ‖*) (Bhā U. 3-6) **NOTE**

The Vasus, with Agni as their mouth, drink the first nectar, which is of the form of the Ṛg-veda. That is: the gods neither eat nor drink; the meaning is that they are satisfied merely by seeing the nectar with the eye. The Vasus, satisfied by this same nectar, enter the red form of the Āditya (the sun) and issue forth from there. The meaning is that the nectar itself, transformed into the form of the Vasus, enters the Āditya. One who knows this principle also enters this same form of the Āditya and issues forth from there as radiance. For as long as the Āditya rises in the east and sets in the west, for so long this knower of the principle enjoys the lordship, the sovereignty and the self-rule of the Vasus; thus the greatness of the Vasus is described. From the statement that they issue forth again from the Āditya, it is said that the Āditya's rays spreading toward the earth and the Vasus are identical. These rays of the Āditya are the cause of the influence of the seasons, and they are the cause of food and the like suited to each season; so the Vasus who exist in the form of these rays are the cause of this food. For this very reason they are praised for the sake of food.

### Printed p. 389
तां वो देवाः सुमतिमूर्जयंतीमिषमश्याम वसवः शसा गोः । सा न सुदानुर्मृळयंती देवी प्रति द्रवंती सुविताय गम्याः ॥ (*tāṃ vo devāḥ sumatimūrjayaṃtīmiṣamaśyāma vasavaḥ śasā goḥ | sā na sudānurmṛḷayaṃtī devī prati dravaṃtī suvitāya gamyāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-4) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-41-18) **NOTE**

"O divine Vasus, grant us to obtain, with the help of the sun's rays, the food that is a means for meditating with a pure mind and that increases strength. May that food produce every kind of happiness for us": the above view is indicated in this prayer. Moreover, when the course of the Āditya in the atmosphere is described, the point is made that the nature of the Vasus also helps the Āditya's revolution. For example—

यमेन दत्तं त्रित एनमायुनगिंद्र एणं प्रथमो अध्यतिष्ठत् । गंधर्वो अस्य रशनामगृभ्यात्सूरादश्वं वसवो निरतष्ट ॥ (*yamena dattaṃ trita enamāyunagiṃdra eṇaṃ prathamo adhyatiṣṭhat | gaṃdharvo asya raśanāmagṛbhyātsūrādaśvaṃ vasavo nirataṣṭa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-163-2) **NOTE**

"This horse given by Yama was yoked to the chariot by Vāyu, who moves in the three places beginning with the earth. Indra, the foremost, mounted this horse. King Soma took the reins of this horse. The Vasus (the sun's rays) obtained this horse from the Āditya." Here Sāyaṇa has shown two kinds of meaning for वसवः (*vasavaḥ*): first the sun's rays, and second, as वसुशब्देनोक्ता (*vasuśabdenoktā*) ... यमादयः (*yamādayaḥ*) (Yama and the others, spoken of by the word "Vasu") **NOTE**. It is understood that these Vasus are not only occupants of the earth-place, as said above, but occupants of the places of the three worlds. The etymology of the Nirukta-kāra also supports this.

वसवो यद्विवसते सर्वमग्निर्वसुभिर्वासन इति समाख्या तस्मात्पृथिवीस्थानाः । इंद्रो वसुभिर्वासन इति समाख्या तस्मान्मध्यस्थासाः । वसव आदित्यरश्मयो विवासनात्तस्याद्दुस्थानाः ॥ (*vasavo yadvivasate sarvamagnirvasubhirvāsana iti samākhyā tasmātpṛthivīsthānāḥ | iṃdro vasubhirvāsana iti samākhyā tasmānmadhyasthāsāḥ | vasava ādityaraśmayo vivāsanāttasyāddusthānāḥ ‖*) (Ni. 12-41)

Agni pervades everything, covering it like a garment; therefore he is called Vāsana. This indicates the earth-place. Because Indra also has this property of pervasion, he too is called Vāsana; hence he is a deity of the middle place, the atmosphere. The radiant rays of the Āditya are likewise all-pervading, so they too are called Vasus; hence they may be deities of the heavenly place. After explaining thus, he cites the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence विश्वस्मै धत्त वसवो वसूनि (*viśvasmai dhatta vasavo vasūni*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-4-44-2) and shows the extended meaning of the word "vasu". In the Ṛk 1-163-2 cited above, the Vasus help the Āditya, who is in the heavenly world;

### Printed p. 390
and since the Ṛk-saṃhitā itself also describes them as helping the atmospheric Maruts and the terrestrial Agni, it is understood that they pervade all three worlds.

ज्मया अत्र वसवो रंत देवा उरावंतरिक्षे मर्जयंत शुभ्राः । आर्वाक्पथ उरुज्रयः कृणुध्वं श्रोता दूतस्य जग्मुषो नो अस्य ॥ (*jmayā atra vasavo raṃta devā urāvaṃtarikṣe marjayaṃta śubhrāḥ | ārvākpatha urujrayaḥ kṛṇudhvaṃ śrotā dūtasya jagmuṣo no asya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-3)

"May the deities called Vasus delight here in this sacrifice together with the terrestrial Agni, and may they also serve the Maruts who are in the wide atmosphere. O Maruts of abundant motion, and O Vasus their friends, join together, come facing us and follow us": so they are praised. Therefore it cannot be said that they are merely terrestrial deities. As the radiance of the Āditya in the heavenly world, they increase their power with the atmospheric Maruts, and then cause the form of the terrestrial Agni to shine more.

त्वे असुर्यं १ वसवो न्यृण्वन्कतुं हि ते मित्रमहो जुषंत । त्वं दस्योरोकसो अग्न आज उरु ज्योतिर्जनयन्नाराय ॥ (*tve asuryaṃ 1 vasavo nyṛṇvankatuṃ hi te mitramaho juṣaṃta | tvaṃ dasyorokaso agna āja uru jyotirjanayannārāya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-5-6)

"O Agni, worthy of worship by all friends, the deities called Vasus have increased radiance in you and made your strength greater. They have also served the rite dear to you. With the brilliance increased by their help, be a benefactor of the sacrificers and destroy the enemies."

क्रतुं ह्यस्य वसवो जुषंताथा देवा दधिरे हव्यवाहं (*kratuṃ hyasya vasavo juṣaṃtāthā devā dadhire havyavāhaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-11.-) **NOTE**

"The deities accepted and honoured as Havyavāha the Agni, lord of the whole sacrifice, whom the Vasus serve, so helped": thus companionship with Agni is described. It is also made known that their influence is the cause of Agni's strength.

In the Upaniṣad sentence cited above, they are called the eight Vasus and their number is stated. In the Śabdakalpadruma their names are given as Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Viṣṇu, Anila, Anala and Prabhāsa. Pointing to the same, the Viṣṇu Purāṇa gives eight names: Āpa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhava, Anila, Anala or Pāvaka, Pratyūṣa (Uṣas) and Prabhāsa. It is also said that all of these are various forms of the world-pervading radiance.

### Printed p. 391
Just as, because it pervades the physical worlds, the particular influence of the Āditya and the rest bears the name "Vasu", so too, when a spiritual principle is taught, the principle of life-breath (prāṇa), which pervades the whole body, bears the name "Vasu".

पुरुषो वाव यज्ञस्तस्य यानि चतुर्विंशति वर्षाणि तत्पातःसवनं । चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरा गायत्री गायत्रं प्रातःसवनं तदस्य वसवोऽन्वायत्ताः प्राणा वाव वसवः एते हीदग्ं सर्वं वासयंति ॥ (*puruṣo vāva yajñastasya yāni caturviṃśati varṣāṇi tatpātaḥsavanaṃ | caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ tadasya vasavo 'nvāyattāḥ prāṇā vāva vasavaḥ ete hīdagṃ sarvaṃ vāsayaṃti ‖*) (Chā. U. 3-16-1)

The Puruṣa himself is of the form of the sacrifice. His first twenty-four years are the morning pressing. By a mantra in the Gāyatrī metre the oblation of the morning pressing is offered. Because it pervades all the limbs, lodged within his body so that the Puruṣa can dwell, prāṇa is well known by the name "Vasu". Therefore the particular principles that pervade the three worlds, beginning with the earth, of the infinite physical universe, both within the body of the Puruṣa and beyond the body, are those that bear the name "Vasu".

सुहस्ता (*suhastā*)—कल्याणपाणी नासत्यौ मित्रावरुणौ वा (*kalyāṇapāṇī nāsatyau mitrāvaruṇau vā*). Sāyaṇa has given two meanings: the Aśvins, having auspicious-acting hands, or else Mitra and Varuṇa. Having attractive hands is an ornament of Mitra and Varuṇa just as it is of the Aśvins.

अथ बाहू उद्गृष्णाति । हिरण्यरूपा उषसो विरोक उभाविंद्रो उदिथः सूर्यश्च । आरोहतं वरुण मित्र गर्तं ततश्चक्षाथामदितिं दितिं चेति बाहू वै मित्रावरुणौ ॥ (*atha bāhū udgṛṣṇāti | hiraṇyarūpā uṣaso viroka ubhāviṃdro udithaḥ sūryaśca | ārohataṃ varuṇa mitra gartaṃ tataścakṣāthāmaditiṃ ditiṃ ceti bāhū vai mitrāvaruṇau ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 5-4-1-15)

At the time of the consecration the king raises both arms, recites the mantra हिरण्य रूपा (*hiraṇya rūpā*) and prays to Mitra and Varuṇa: "O Mitra and Varuṇa, of form attractive like gold, mount as the Āditya mounts his chariot; and look upon Diti and Aditi." It is described that in praying so, those very arms are in the form of Mitra and Varuṇa. It can also be understood that in many contexts excellent hands reflect Mitra and Varuṇa. Moreover, mantras such as अश्विनोर्भाहुब्यां पूष्टो हस्ताभ्यां (*aśvinorbhāhubyāṃ pūṣṭo hastābhyāṃ*) praise the distinction of the arms of the Aśvins. Since this epithet can thus fit both, either meaning may be given here.

### Printed p. 392
शशयं (*śaśayaṃ*)—Formed from the root शी (*śī*), this word is used to describe a thing that lies asleep. The meaning is that they called the sleeping cloud for the sake of rain.

रणयंत (*raṇayaṃta*)—रमयंति, शब्दयंत्येव (*ramayaṃti, śabdayaṃtyeva*). The word is used in the senses "rejoice" and "make sound". On the basis of the original meaning "delightful", the word raṇa is also a synonym of battle. Words such as रराणता (*rarāṇatā*) and रणंत (*raṇaṃta*) are used both in describing a sound expressing joy, "victory is assured", while fighting, and when Sāmans such as the Rathantara are chanted at the time of the sacrifice.

सुम्मं (*summaṃ*)—The word summa is read among the words for happiness (Ni. 3-6). In some places of the Ṛk-saṃhitā it is also used in the sense of favour. But use in the sense of happiness is the more frequent.

> अच्छा॑ पु॒त्रं धे॒नवो॑ वावशा॒ना म॒हश्व॑रंति॒ बिभ्र॑तं॒ वपूं॑षि॥

> *yā jāmayo vṛṣṇa icchaṃti śaktiṃ namasyaṃtīrjānate garbhamasmin |*

> अच्छ । पुत्रं । धेनवः । वावशानाः । महः । चरंति । बिभ्रतं । वपूंषि ॥ ३ ॥

> *yāḥ | jāmayaḥ | vṛṣṇe | icchaṃti | śaktiṃ | namasyaṃtīḥ | jānate | garbhaṃ | asmin |*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> या जामयः । जमंति वर्षाकाले प्रादुर्भवंतीति जामय ओषधयः ।
> वृष्णेऽपां वर्षकायेंद्राय शक्तिं सेचनसावर्थमिच्छंति । नमस्यंतीः प्रह्नेभूतास्ता ओषधयोऽस्मिन्निंद्रे गर्भं वृष्टिद्वारा पुष्पफलादिलक्षणगर्भादानादिसामर्थ्यं जानते । जानंति । वावशानाः फलं कामयमाना धेनवः सर्वस्य प्रीणयित्र्य ओषधयो महो महांति नानाप्रकाराणि वपूंषि रूपाणि बिभ्रतं व्रीहियवनीवारादिफललक्षणं पुत्रं तनयमच्छाभिमुखेन चरंति । प्राप्नुवंति । लोके

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

या जामयः (*yā jāmayaḥ*): the jāmayaḥ are the plants, because they spring up (जमंति (*jamaṃti*)) in the rainy season. They desire power (śakti), the capacity of pouring out, for the showerer (वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)), Indra, who sends down the waters. नमस्यंतीः (*namasyaṃtīḥ*): those plants, bowed down, know in this Indra the capacity of impregnation through rain, the embryo in the form of flowers, fruits and the like (जानते (*jānate*) = they know). वावशानाः (*vāvaśānāḥ*): desiring fruit; धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*): the plants, which gratify everyone; महः (*mahaḥ*): great, of many kinds; वपूंषि (*vapūṃṣi*): forms. They go facing, that is, reach, the son (पुत्रं (*putraṃ*)) who bears (बिभ्रतं (*bibhrataṃ*)) these forms, namely the fruit in the form of rice, barley, wild rice and the like. (The sentence continues on the next page.)

> हि हंभारवं कुर्वाणा धेनवो वत्समभिलक्ष्य गच्छंति । तद्वत् । यद्वा । जामयः ।
> जमंति सर्वत्र प्रसरंतीति जामयः सूर्यदीप्तयः । वृष्णेऽपां वर्षकाय ।
> स्वरश्मिभिर्भौमान्रसानादाय पुनर्वर्षतीति वर्षकः सूर्यः । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिरिति
> स्मृतेश्व । तस्मै वर्षणशक्तिमिच्छंति । ता दीप्तयोऽस्मिन्नादित्ये गर्भमब्रूपगर्भाधानसःमर्थ्यं जानंति ॥ जामयः । जमतेर्गतिकर्मणो जनिघसिभ्यामिण्णिति विधीयमानो बहुलवचनादस्मादपि भवति । नमस्यंतीः । नवः8रब्दान्नमोवरिवश्चित्रजः क्यजिति
> क्यच् । तदंताच्छतरि रूपं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । जानते । ज्ञा अवबोधन इत्यस्य लट
> रूपं । अच्च । निपातस्य चेति संहितायां दीर्घः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As in the world cows, lowing, go toward the calf, so here. Or else: जामयः (*jāmayaḥ*) are the sun's rays, since they spread (जमंति (*jamaṃti*)) everywhere. वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*): for the rain-maker; the sun is the rain-maker, because with his rays he takes up the earthly juices and rains again; and the smṛti says "from the Āditya rain is born". They desire the power of raining for him. Those rays know in this Āditya the capacity of impregnation, the embryo in the form of water.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- या जामय (*yā jāmaya*)—the plants
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—to Indra, the maker of rain
- शक्तिं (*śaktiṃ*)—the capacity of pouring out
- इच्छति (*icchati*)—wish for
- नमस्यंतीः (*namasyaṃtīḥ*)—the plants that have attained humility
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—in this Indra
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the capacity to produce the embryo in the form of flowers and the like
- जानते (*jānate*)—have known
- वावशानाः (*vāvaśānāḥ*)—those that desire fruits
- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—the plants, gratifiers of the world
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of many kinds
- वपूंषि (*vapūṃṣi*)—forms such as grain
- बिभ्रतं (*bibhrataṃ*)—possessing
- पुत्रं (*putraṃ*)—the fruits in the form of sons
- चरंति (*caraṃti*)—obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

All the plants desire from Indra, the maker of creation **NOTE**, the capacity of pouring out. These plants, having attained humility, have known that Indra has the capacity of producing the embryo in the form of flowers and the like. The plants, which desire fruits and gratify the world, obtain the fruits in the form of sons, which possess many kinds of forms such as grain.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The plants that desire for the showerer (Indra) the power (of sending rain) appreciate, when manifest, the embryo (blossom) deposited in him : the cows desirous of reward come to the presence of the calf, invested with many forms

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this Ṛk Sāyaṇa has shown that two kinds of meaning are possible. For जामयः (*jāmayaḥ*) he first gives the meaning plants and trees. If this meaning is right, वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*) is a word equivalent to Indra. धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*) too must be an epithet of the plants. Or else जामयः (*jāmayaḥ*)

### Printed p. 394

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

If jāmayaḥ is taken to mean the sun's rays, then vṛṣṇe must be a synonym of Āditya (the sun), and dhenavaḥ too must be an epithet of the sun's rays. Both kinds of purport are appropriate, yet there is more room for the second, the one concerning Āditya. First:

jāmayaḥ—जमंति वर्षाकाले प्रादुर्भवंतीति जामयः ओषधयः । (*jamaṃti varṣākāle prādurbhavaṃtīti jāmayaḥ oṣadhayaḥ |*) Because plants spring up in the rainy season, they are called jāmis. The word is formed from the root jam in the sense of motion. The Nirukta-writers have given two explanations of it: जामिरन्ने 5- स्यां जनयंति जामपत्यं । जमतीर्वा स्याद्दतिकर्मणो निर्गमनप्राया भवति (*jāmiranne 5- syāṃ janayaṃti jāmapatyaṃ | jamatīrvā syāddatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyā bhavati*) (Ni. 3-9) One derivation: it is formed from the root jan, "to be born", the thought being that another man causes children to be born in her; jāmi is then she who goes to her husband's house. The other: it is formed from the root jam, "to move", and gives the same sense. In the rainy season the sprouts move, that is, appear. Thus one derivation lets us state a purport in which jāmayaḥ is a synonym for plants. By the other derivation the word means kinsfolk. In many contexts it is used in this sense. But "kinsfolk" may be a sister, a wife, a mother, a friend, or any male belonging to a person's side. For example:

अंबयो यंत्यध्वभिर्जामयो अध्वरीयतां । पृंचतीर्मधुना पयः । (*aṃbayo yaṃtyadhvabhirjāmayo adhvarīyatāṃ | pṛṃcatīrmadhunā payaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-16)
The waters, like mothers, flow beneficially as mothers do.

आ घा ता गच्छानुत्तरा युगानि यत्र जामयः कृणवन्नजामि ॥ (*ā ghā tā gacchānuttarā yugāni yatra jāmayaḥ kṛṇavannajāmi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-12-13)
The jāmi chooses one who is not a jāmi; that is, a sister chooses one who is not a brother.

ते मायिनो ममिरे सुप्रचेतनो जामी सयोनी मिथुना समोकसा ॥ (*te māyino mamire supracetano jāmī sayonī mithunā samokasā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-129-4)
Heaven and earth, being jāmis, held the ray under control; here heaven and earth mean "sisters". In the same sense jāmayaḥ means svasāraḥ, the fingers. To denote the mutual relation of the fingers, which serve the sacrifice and help one another, in "हिन्वंति स्वसारो जामयः (*hinvaṃti svasāro jāmayaḥ*)

### Printed p. 395
पतिं (*patiṃ*)" (9-65-1) jāmayaḥ is used in the sense of "wives" of Soma.
"जहि शूर शत्रून् जामिमजामिं मघवन् अमित्रान् (*jahi śūra śatrūn jāmimajāmiṃ maghavan amitrān*)" (6-44-17): "Kill the enemy, whether kinsman or non-kinsman". In this mantra the word is used in a broad sense, without showing a definite kinship. Since the sense must be stated according to context, what relationship is meant here between Indra and the plants? Husband and wife? Father and daughter? Or helper and helped? The question is natural. All these relationships can be shown in this context. It is well known that the creation and growth of plants come through rain, and that rain is possible only by Indra's favour; so the relation of helper belongs to Indra. The essence of the plants is the rain-water, and the essence of the rain-water is the plant:
आपो ह ना ओषधिनाग्ं सारः .... .... ओषधय उ अपाग्ंरसः । (*āpo ha nā oṣadhināgṃ sāraḥ .... .... oṣadhaya u apāgṃrasaḥ |*) (Śa. Brā. 3-6-1-7)
Since the inner essence of water and the sap of the plants are one, Indra, the cause of the standing of the rain-water, is also the cause of the nourishing of the plants' sap. And by killing Vṛtra, the common enemy of both, he became helper to the growth of both.

अथ दर्भस्तंभ मुपदधाति । एतद्वै देवा ओषधीरुपादधत तथैवैतद्यजमान ओषधीरुपधत्ते । जायत एष .... .... आपश्च हैता ओषधयश्च या वै वृत्राद्बीभत्समाना आपः ... .... तेनौषधय उभयेन्नैवैनमेतदन्नेन प्रीणाति ॥ (*atha darbhastaṃbha mupadadhāti | etadvai devā oṣadhīrupādadhata tathaivaitadyajamāna oṣadhīrupadhatte | jāyata eṣa .... .... āpaśca haitā oṣadhayaśca yā vai vṛtrādbībhatsamānā āpaḥ ... .... tenauṣadhaya ubhayennaivainametadannena prīṇāti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-2-3 to 1-3)
The sacrificer's setting up of the darbha is a reflection of the gods' setting up of the plants and the rest. This darbha is the representative of the food the sacrificer desires. The essence of both water and plants, the causes of the sap of food, is contained in this darbha. The water, frightened of Vṛtra, appeared on the dry earth as darbha and as bushes; hence the essence of water and of plants is contained in it. By slaying Vṛtra, enemy of both, Indra became their helper. Therefore the plants became jāmis to him, that is, kinsfolk: one purport can be stated thus.
युष्मा इंद्रोऽवृणीत वृत्रतूर्य इति (*yuṣmā iṃdro 'vṛṇīta vṛtratūrya iti*) (Śa. Brā. 1-1-3-8): Indra won victory with the help of the waters when fighting Vṛtra. All such descriptions show the jāmi-relationship between Indra, the waters, and the plants, their essence.

### Printed p. 396
Since the power of pouring rain and the power of producing plants are contained in Indra, the epithet vṛṣṇe is fitting for him. "यश्चंदसामृषभो विश्वरूपः .... .... समेंद्रो मेधया स्पृणोतु (*yaścaṃdasāmṛṣabho viśvarūpaḥ .... .... sameṃdro medhayā spṛṇotu*)" (Tai. U. 1-4): this Indra, by his power of lordship, has the universe as his form, and is described as ṛṣabha (vṛṣabha) and so on. Since the whole universe comes about from Indra, who has such a supreme nature, he is as a womb to the plants and to their flowers and fruits. Thus the sense referring to Indra is natural.

If jāmayaḥ is taken as the sun's rays and vṛṣṇe as an epithet of the sun, how is it consistent? Sāyaṇa: यद्वा जामयः । जमंति सर्वत्र प्रसरंतीति जामयः सूरदीप्तयः । वृष्णेऽपां वर्षकाय । स्वरशिभिर्भौमान् रसानादाय पुनर्वर्षतीति वर्षकः सूरः (*yadvā jāmayaḥ | jamaṃti sarvatra prasaraṃtīti jāmayaḥ sūradīptayaḥ | vṛṣṇe 'pāṃ varṣakāya | svaraśibhirbhaumān rasānādāya punarvarṣatīti varṣakaḥ sūraḥ*). The word jāmi, from the root jam in the sense of motion, means "spreading everywhere"; here the sun's rays, spreading to all regions, are meant. Because the sun draws up water with his rays and again pours rain on the earth, he is marked by the epithet vṛṣṇe. Even if jāmi is taken as "kinsman", there is no room to ask what kinship holds between the sun and his rays; the relation of part and whole is what the word jāmi conveys here.

If jāmi is taken as the sun's rays, their nature of spreading through the universe is shown. Earlier, in explaining Ṛk 1-156-2, on the words "वर्षिष्ठमुप गाव आगुः (*varṣiṣṭhamupa gāva āguḥ*)", the form of the rays' spreading through the universe was described with examples from the Śruti. Here these same rays bear the epithet dhenavaḥ. What nature does it show? The word dhenu conveys satisfying and helping: धेनुर्धयतीर्वा, धिनोतीर्वा, धयतेऽसौ वत्सेनेति । तर्पयत्यसौ पयसा। (*dhenurdhayatīrvā, dhinotīrvā, dhayate 'sau vatseneti | tarpayatyasau payasā|*) (Ni. 11-42) The chief sense, "satisfies by giving milk", shows the chief mark of the dhenu. Not only the cow: in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā, in many contexts that bring satisfaction, there is a dhenu-metaphor, as the cow satisfies her calf with her milk. For example, in mantras such as उपह्वये सुदघां धेनु (*upahvaye sudaghāṃ dhenu*) there is a description of the cloud-cow that gives the world satisfaction through rain (1-164-26). The one who milks this cloud-cow is Āditya; hence he is vṛṣan. Wherever the sun's rays or the radiant Dawn are described, the quality of the dhenu is present. Though it is a matter of common experience that Dawn and the sun's rays give joy to the world,

### Printed p. 397
in the eyes of the Ṛṣis, the authors of the Ṛk-Saṃhitā, the principle called dhenu holds a venerable place; hence such descriptions are very many. If only a few examples are examined, the fitness of this metaphor becomes clear.

अबोध्यग्निः समिधा जनानां प्रति धेनुमिवायतीमुषासं । यह्वा इव प्र वयामुज्जि हानाः प्र भानवः सिस्रते नाकमच्छ ॥ (*abodhyagniḥ samidhā janānāṃ prati dhenumivāyatīmuṣāsaṃ | yahvā iva pra vayāmujji hānāḥ pra bhānavaḥ sisrate nākamaccha ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-1-1)
Dawn, who gladdens the whole world, appears in the sky and comes like a cow rich in milk. The flames of Agni, like calves, or like birds flying up to settle on a branch, spread upward from Agni and run towards Dawn: a wonderful description.

एता धियं कृणवामा सखायोप या माता ऋणुत व्रजं गोः । (*etā dhiyaṃ kṛṇavāmā sakhāyopa yā mātā ṛṇuta vrajaṃ goḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-45-6)
In such places Dawn is shown as mother-like to the sun's rays.

आ धेनवो धुनयंतामशिश्वीः सबर्दुघाः शशया अप्रदुग्धाः । नव्यानव्या युवतयो भवंतीर्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥ (*ā dhenavo dhunayaṃtāmaśiśvīḥ sabardughāḥ śaśayā apradugdhāḥ | navyānavyā yuvatayo bhavaṃtīrmahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-55-16)
The cow-clouds, dear to the world, though without calves, come towards the earth and pour the nectar of rain. Whether the cloud or the sun's rays are described, since they cause the rain that brings satisfaction, there is the dhenu-metaphor. Where these metaphors occur the particular purport is also noteworthy: the same idea is not repeated everywhere, and the constant variety of idea adorns the description of each setting.

त्रिरस्मै सप्त धेनवो दुदुहे सत्यामाशिरं पूर्व्य व्योमनि । चत्वार्न्या भुवनानि निर्णिजे चारूणि चक्रे यदृतैरवर्धत ॥ (*trirasmai sapta dhenavo duduhe satyāmāśiraṃ pūrvya vyomani | catvārnyā bhuvanāni nirṇije cārūṇi cakre yadṛtairavardhata ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-70-1)
In such places the dhenu-metaphor gives a very profound meaning. Since such contexts are many, the charm of such metaphors is explained in each. Here dhenavaḥ, as a synonym of jāmayaḥ, indicates the principle of the sun's rays: that they bring joy to the world.

### Printed p. 398
jānate garbham asmin—If the sense refers to Indra, the purport is that the womb contains the flowers and fruits of the plants. If it refers to Āditya, a wider purport must be stated. Since all the gods, Indra, Agni and the rest, are united in Āditya, or are particular manifestations of him, whatever powers of the womb each of these gods has individually are all contained in Āditya. When the lightning-fire or the sun is described, the sense of the word garbha is common. Or it would not be wrong to say that Agni, Sūrya, Viṣṇu, Āditya, garbha are words denoting identity. As "womb of the waters" is a synonym for Agni, so it is for Āditya; one may also say that the world is contained in their womb. A few examples may be examined of how, when Viṣṇu, Agni, and Āditya are praised, they are called by synonyms of garbha. In some places Agni is said to lie in the womb of all things; elsewhere the whole world is said to lie in Agni's womb. Of Agni:

बह्वे नां गर्भो अपसामुपस्थान्महान्नविर्निश्वरति स्वधावान् । (*bahve nāṃ garbho apasāmupasthānmahānnavirniśvarati svadhāvān |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-95-3)
गर्भो यो अपां गर्भो वनानां गर्भश्च स्थातां गर्भश्च रथां । (*garbho yo apāṃ garbho vanānāṃ garbhaśca sthātāṃ garbhaśca rathāṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-70-2)
These show that Agni lies in all things as a womb, and that his nature cannot be known by ordinary effort. Moreover, this Agni, like a son in the waters of the cloud in the form of lightning, afterwards receives the sacrificial offering and causes the rain-waters, his mothers, to be born. Hidden in the lightning-form among the cloud-waters, he comes out from the middle of the sea as the submarine fire. This same Agni is the womb of the waters, the womb of plants; or the waters and plants are his womb: so it is described. Of Viṣṇu:

तमु स्तोतारः पूर्व्यं यथा विद ऋतस्य गर्भं जनुषा पिपर्तन । (*tamu stotāraḥ pūrvyaṃ yathā vida ṛtasya garbhaṃ januṣā pipartana |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-156-3)
Viṣṇu is eternal, perfect, the womb of the sacrifice, born as the sacrifice; or the womb of the water. This epithet is given because water is the origin of creation and Viṣṇu in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha is its support. Of Āditya:

उत्तानयोश्च व्वो३र्योनिरंतरत्रा पिता दुहितुर्गर्भमाधत् । (*uttānayośca vvo3ryoniraṃtaratrā pitā duhiturgarbhamādhat |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-16 = 13**NOTE**

### Printed p. 399
In the middle of these heaven and earth, which are stretched upward and serve for enjoyment like cups, in the atmosphere, the place of the maker of all beings, Āditya holds in his womb the water, the womb of his daughter, the earth.

दिव्यं सुपर्णं नायसं बृहंतमपां गर्भं दर्शतमोषधीनां । (*divyaṃ suparṇaṃ nāyasaṃ bṛhaṃtamapāṃ garbhaṃ darśatamoṣadhīnāṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-52)
Āditya dwells in heaven, has an excellent means of descent, is a mover, is the womb of the waters and of the plants. Thus these deities are denoted by words for garbha. Moreover, in many contexts it is explained that the names Agni, Viṣṇu, Āditya are words for different forms of one principle and do not denote different deities. The description of Agni as "अपां गर्भः (*apāṃ garbhaḥ*)", "आसुर गर्भः (*āsura garbhaḥ*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29-11) applies also to Āditya. As Āditya is called the womb of heaven and earth, so Agni is called "रोदस्योः गर्भं (*rodasyoḥ garbhaṃ*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-1-2). In Ṛk 1-164-52 cited above, that same Agni is designated "दिव्यं सुपर्णं (*divyaṃ suparṇaṃ*)", a description showing a solar nature. Therefore, if garbham in the present Ṛk is taken to refer to Āditya, the purport is that the jāmi-rays knew Āditya, who bore in his own womb the whole universe in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha, that is, they knew his pervasion of the universe. To show his pervasion, one may say that he lies in the womb of the universe, or that he has hidden the whole universe in his own womb. Sāyaṇa states the purport referring to Āditya thus: अब्रूपगर्भाधानसामर्थ्यं वहंति (*abrūpagarbhādhānasāmarthyaṃ vahaṃti*).

mahaḥ vapūṃṣi bibhratam—they know the womb-form that bears bodies of many forms. If jāmayaḥ is taken as plants, the forms are the many kinds: rice, barley, nīvāra and so on. If taken as the sun's rays: काळी कराळी च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा । स्पुलिंगिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्तजिह्वाः (*kāḷī karāḷī ca manojavā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā | spuliṃginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti saptajihvāḥ*) (Mu. U. 1-2-4**NOTE**). As the flames of fire in the form of the Supreme Brahman are described in such sentences, so the many forms of the sun's rays are to be understood.

अमी ये सप्त रश्मयस्तत्रा मे नाभिरातता । (*amī ye sapta raśmayastatrā me nābhirātatā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-9)
The many forms of the sun's rays described in such Ṛks were explained earlier.

> अध्वरे यज्ञॆ ग्राज्ञः सोमाभिषवार्थमुपलान् युजानः प्रयुंजानेऽहं सुमेके सुरूपे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ मनीषा मनस ईषया स्तुतिलक्षणया
> वाचाच्छ विवक्कि । अभिमुख्येन सौमि । हे अग्ने ते तव भूरिवारा यजमानैर्बहुवारं वरणीया दर्शताः कमनीयतया दर्शनीया यजत्रा: पूज्या इमा दीप्तयो

> चकारस्य कुत्वं व्यत्ययेन । युजानः । युजिबुधिदृशः किच्चेत्यानच् । कित्तादगुणः।
> चित्तादंतोदात्तः । मनीषा । सुपो डादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, who am employing the pressing-stones for the pressing of Soma at the sacrifice (अध्वरे (*adhvare*)), address (विवक्कि (*vivakki*)) the beautiful heaven and earth (सुमेके (*sumeke*) रोदसी (*rodasī*)), facing them, with speech in the form of praise. मनीषा (*manīṣā*) is explained as "by the impulse of the mind", that is, by speech of the nature of praise. Then, to Agni: these flames of yours, much chosen by the sacrificers (भूरिवारा (*bhūrivārā*)), lovely to see through their desirability (दर्शताः (*darśatāḥ*)), and worthy of worship (यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*)), turn upward (ऊर्ध्वा (*ūrdhvā*)) for the sake of Manu, that is, for the business of men.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- ग्राव्यः (*grāvyaḥ*)—the stones that press the Soma
- युजानः (*yujānaḥ*)—I, who hold them for the pressing
- सुमेके (*sumeke*)—of excellent form
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- मनीषा (*manīṣā*)—with speech in the form of praise
- अच्छ विवक्कि (*accha vivakki*)—standing facing them, I recite (O Agni)
- भूरिवाराः (*bhūrivārāḥ*)—much desired by the sacrificers
- दर्शताः (*darśatāḥ*)—of attractive form
- यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*)—worthy of worship
- ते इमाः (*te imāḥ*)—these rays of yours
- मनवे (*manave*)—for the business of men
- ऊर्ध्वाः (*ūrdhvāḥ*)—turned upward
- भवंति (*bhavaṃti*)—spread out

### Printed p. 401

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the sacrifice I stand ready, holding the stones in order to crush and press out the Soma juice, and I recite to heaven and earth, which are of excellent juice, standing facing them, with speech in the form of praise. O Agni, these rays of yours, which are desired by the sacrificers, of attractive form and worthy of worship, spread upward for the business of men.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I glorify with praise the beautiful heaven and earth, taking in hand the stones (to express the libation) at the sacrifice, as these your graceful, adorable, and many-blessing rays (Agni) mount up for the good of man.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—ध्वरतिः हिंसाकर्म (*dhvaratiḥ hiṃsākarma*) (Ni. 1-8). The word is formed from the root ध्व (*dhva*), which gives the sense "to cause injury". अध्वरे (*adhvare*) means "in the sacrifice that is free from injury".

ग्रावः (*grāvaḥ*)—सोमाभिषवार्थमुपलान् (*somābhiṣavārthamupalān*). It means the stones held for crushing and pressing the Soma juice. Although the two words ग्राव (*grāva*) and अद्रि (*adri*) both have in common usage the general sense "stone", it can be said, from their descriptions and epithets, that the ग्राव (*grāva*) and the अद्रि (*adri*) that serve to press out the Soma juice must have differed in their very form. Generally, where the word ग्राव (*grāva*) is used the bhāṣya gives it the meaning "stone", and where the word अद्रि (*adri*) stands it gives the meaning ग्राव (*grāva*). But this difference of meaning is not the basis for showing how they differ. From the epithets and comparisons that describe their form, and from the words that denote the sound they make while the Soma is pressed, it is understood that these two implements are different. बृहाण (*bṛhāṇa*) (5-41-12); पर्वत (*parvata*) (10-94-1); अश्रमण (*aśramaṇa*), अश्वथित (*aśvathita*), अमृत्यु (*amṛtyu*), अनातुर (*anātura*), अजर (*ajara*), आमविष्णु (*āmaviṣṇu*) (10-94-11), क्षेमकाम (*kṣemakāma*) (10-94-12): all of these are epithets showing the distinctive character of the अद्रि (*adri*); epithets such as पृथु (*pṛthu*) and पृथुबुध (*pṛthubudha*) show the distinctive character of the ग्राव (*grāva*) alone. The ग्राव (*grāva*) is generally compared to a bull, and the अद्रि (*adri*) to a horse.

Some portions of the Grāva-stotra make known the greatness of this ग्राव (*grāva*). According to the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, this praise comprises the sūkta 10-94, which praises the ग्राव (*grāva*) directly, preceded by the mantras Ṛ. Saṃ. 1, 24, 3; 5, 81, 1; 8, 41, 1; 8, 1, 1. At the end the sūkta 10-175 is recited.

### Printed p. 402
Of these, the mantras 1, 24, 3; 5, 81, 1 and 10, 175 are addressed to the deity Savitṛ. Since he is the impeller of all, he is prayed to impel the pressing of the juice. For example:

प्र वो ग्रावाणः सविता देवः सुवतु धर्मणा । धूर्षु युज्यध्वं सुनुत ॥ (*pra vo grāvāṇaḥ savitā devaḥ suvatu dharmaṇā | dhūrṣu yujyadhvaṃ sunuta ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 18-175-1) **NOTE**
O pressing-stones, may the god Savitṛ, the impeller of all, impel you to the pressing of Soma. At the places of pressing, join together with faith and with eagerness for the work, and press. In the same way the stones are praised by mantras such as ग्रावाणः अप दुच्चुनामप सेधत दुर्मतिं (*grāvāṇaḥ apa duccunāmapa sedhata durmatiṃ*). Besides these, we may examine just a few of the mantras that are recited describing the beneficial and purifying sound the stones make at the time of pressing, and praising the stones.

प्रैते वदंतु प्र वयं वदाम ग्रावभ्यो वाचं वदता वदद्भ्यः । यदद्रयः पर्वताः साकमाशवः श्लोकं घोषं भरथेंद्राय सोमिनः ॥ (*praite vadaṃtu pra vayaṃ vadāma grāvabhyo vācaṃ vadatā vadadbhyaḥ | yadadrayaḥ parvatāḥ sākamāśavaḥ ślokaṃ ghoṣaṃ bharatheṃdrāya sominaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-1)
Let these stones raise a praise in the form of sound. Let us too offer a fitting counter-praise to this praise. O stones, heavy and swift-moving, as soon as you recite your praise in the form of sound addressed to Indra, the Soma juice will surely be pressed by you.

एते वदंति शतवत्सहस्रवदभि क्रंदंति हरितेभिरासभीः । विष्ट्वी ग्रावाणः सुकृतः सुकृत्यया होतुश्चित्पूर्वे हविरद्यमाशत ॥ (*ete vadaṃti śatavatsahasravadabhi kraṃdaṃti haritebhirāsabhīḥ | viṣṭvī grāvāṇaḥ sukṛtaḥ sukṛtyayā hotuścitpūrve haviradyamāśata ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-2)
These stones make a deep sound from their green-coloured mouths, like the deep sound that arises when thousands of people gather and shout. Keeping the sacrifice under their own control, they receive the oblation even before Agni, the divine hotṛ.

सुपर्णा वाचमक्रतोप द्यव्याखरे कृष्णा इषीरा अनर्तिषुः । न्य १ ज्ञयंत्युपरस्य निष्कृतं पुरू रेतो दधिरे सूर्यश्वितः ॥ (*suparṇā vācamakratopa dyavyākhare kṛṣṇā iṣīrā anartiṣuḥ | nya 1 jñayaṃtyuparasya niṣkṛtaṃ purū reto dadhire sūryaśvitaḥ ‖*)
(10-94-5)
These stones, moving softly, make a sound in the atmosphere. They rejoice in the courtyard as a black antelope dances. They press out a juice that shines like the sun.

### Printed p. 403
ध्रुवा एव वः पितरो युगेयुगे क्षेमकामासः सदसो न युंजते । अजुर्यासो हरिषाचो हरिद्रव आ द्यां रवेण पृथिवीमशुश्रवुः ॥ (*dhruvā eva vaḥ pitaro yugeyuge kṣemakāmāsaḥ sadaso na yuṃjate | ajuryāso hariṣāco haridrava ā dyāṃ raveṇa pṛthivīmaśuśravuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-12)
O stones, your fathers the mountains, desiring peace for themselves, used to remain apart (विवक्त (*vivakta*)), taking no share in the assembly. Ageless, and satisfied by obtaining Soma, they used to spread their soft sounds through all of heaven and earth and make them echo.

तदिद्वदंत्यद्रयो विमोचने यामन्नंजस्पा इव फेदुपब्बिभिः । वसंतो बीजमिव धान्याकृतः पृंचंति सोमं न मिनंति बप्सतः ॥ (*tadidvadaṃtyadrayo vimocane yāmannaṃjaspā iva phedupabbibhiḥ | vasaṃto bījamiva dhānyākṛtaḥ pṛṃcaṃti somaṃ na minaṃti bapsataḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-13)
At the time of pressing these stones, like chariots moving swiftly on the road, and like farmers sowing seed who raise a cry of joy, press out the Soma juice sounding deeply and attractively. And they do no harm at all. In this way the praise of the ग्राव (*grāva*) runs. This praise also takes the form of a description of the ग्राव (*grāva*). And before reciting the last mantra, सुते अध्वरे (*sute adhvare*), the priest called Grāvastut recites the sūkta 10-76, which begins with the mantra आ व ऋंजस ऊर्जां (*ā va ṛṃjasa ūrjāṃ*), and the sūkta 10-175, which begins with the mantra प्र वो ग्रावाणः (*pra vo grāvāṇaḥ*) quoted above. And at the beginning or in the middle, as the occasion suits, he recites the Pāvamānī mantras until the pressing is finished. On all these occasions there is praise and description of the ग्राव (*grāva*). Although the present mantra is addressed to heaven and earth, the ग्राव (*grāva*) held ready for pressing the Soma at the time of their prayer is also praised.

सुमेके (*sumeke*)—This word is an epithet of heaven and earth. Sāyaṇa has explained it as "of good form". In many contexts it comes to mean "of good state" or "of unshakable nature". In some places it is understood as "of excellent action", or "skilled in service". When this word is an epithet of heaven and earth, it becomes स्वकीयाभिः प्रकाशयुक्ते (*svakīyābhiḥ prakāśayukte*), that is, "self-luminous with their own radiance", as Sāyaṇa has explained in mantras such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-15-5.

मनीषा (*manīṣā*)—It means "by speech in the form of praise". Its further meanings have been given in the special topics of the first ṛk of this same sūkta.

रोदसी (*rodasī*)—The further meanings of this word have been given in the special topics of the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-56-7.

### Printed p. 404
The words भूरिवाराः (*bhūrivārāḥ*), दर्शताः (*darśatāḥ*), यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*) are epithets of the flames of Agni and describe the divine nature of those flames. The greatness of Agni's flame will be given in the special topics of the next mantra.

##### Grammar

- विवक्कि — वच परिभाषणे । लटि बहुलं छंदसीति शपः श्लुः । अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च बहुलं छंदसीत्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । चकारस्य कुत्वं व्यत्ययेन ।
- युजानः — युजिबुधिदृशः किच्चेत्यानच् । कित्तादगुणः । चित्तादंतोदात्तः ।
- मनीषा — सुपो डादेशः ।

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या ते॑ जि॒ह्वा मधु॑मती सुमे॒धा अग्ने॑ दे॒वेषू॒च्यत॑  ॒
> उरूची ।  
> तये॒ह विश्वां॒ अव॑से॒ यज॑त्रा॒ना सा॑दय पा॒यया॑ चा॒  ॑
> मधूनि ॥ ५ ॥

> *yā te jihvā madhumatī sumedhā agne deveṣūcyata*  
> *urūcī |*  
> *tayeha viśvāṃ avase yajatrānā sādaya pāyayā cā*  
> *madhūni ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> या । ते । जिह्वा । मधुमती । सुमेधाः । अग्ने । देवेषु । उच्यते । उरूची ।  
> तया । इह । विश्वान् । अवसे । यजत्रान् । आ । सादय । पायय । च । मधूनि ॥

> *yā | te | jihvā | madhumatī | sumedhāḥ | agne | deveṣu | ucyate | urūcī |*  
> *tayā | iha | viśvān | avase | yajatrān | ā | sādaya | pāyaya | ca | madhūni ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने ते तव मधुमत्युदकवती सुमेधाः । शोभना मेधा प्रज्ञा
> यॆस्स्याः सा । सर्वस्य ज्ञापयित्रि या जिह्वा ज्वालोरूची बहुव्याप्तिः सती देवेषु
> मध्य आह्वानार्थमुच्यते प्रेर्यते तया जिह्वया यजत्रान्यजनीयान्विश्वान्देवानिह
> कर्मण्यस्माकमवसे रक्षणाया सादय । उपवेशय । किंच तान्विश्वानेवान्मधूनि
> मदकरान् सोमान्पायय ॥ सुमेधाः । नित्यमसिच् प्रजामेधयोरित्यसिच् ।
> उच्यते । वच परिभाषणे । कर्मणि यकि रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । उरूची
> अंचतेः क्विन् । अंचतेश्चोपसंख्यानमिति जीप् । अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोप
> इति जीप उदात्तत्वं । पायय । पा पान इत्यस्य णौ परतः शाच्छासाह्वान्नावेषां
> युगिति युक् । तिजि उत्तरत्वादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, your tongue is honeyed (मधुमती (*madhumatī*)), that is, watery, and of good wisdom (सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)): she who has good insight, who makes all know. That tongue, the flame, being widely pervading (उरूची (*urūcī*)), is sent forth (उच्यते (*ucyate*)) among the gods to summon them. With that tongue seat (आ सादय (*ā sādaya*)) here, in our rite, for our protection, all the gods who are worthy of worship (यजत्रान् (*yajatrān*)). And further, make those same gods drink the Soma juices (मधूनि (*madhūni*)), the intoxicating ones.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ते (*te*)—your
- मधुमती (*madhumatī*)—watery (sweet)
- सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)—that which gives to all the knowledge (of duty)
- या जिह्वा (*yā jihvā*)—the tongue that there is

- उरूची (*urūcī*)—having the power to pervade widely
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods
- उच्यते (*ucyate*)—is renowned
- तया (*tayā*)—with the help of that tongue

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, your tongue, which is watery and makes known to all the knowledge of duty, is renowned among the gods as having the power to pervade widely. With the help of that tongue, seat all the gods who are worthy of the sacrifice, in this rite, for our protection, and make them drink the sweet Soma juice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
With your wide-spreading tongue, Agni, sweet and intelligent, which is renowned amongst the gods, bring hither all the adorable deities for our protection, and give them to drink of the sweet (libation).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This mantra contains praise of the flame of Agni. मधुमती (*madhumatī*) and सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*) are epithets of जिह्वा (*jihvā*). उरुची (*urucī*) also makes known the greatness of the flame.

मधुमती (*madhumatī*)—a flame accompanied by मधु (*madhu*). What is मधु (*madhu*)? Here it is explained as "water". The word मधु (*madhu*) is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-12). मधुमती (*madhumatī*) means "that which is accompanied by water". The description of Agni as born of water is well known from epithets such as अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) and अपांगर्भः (*apāṃgarbhaḥ*). The praise of the water-filled flame of Agni at times of sacrifice carries a special meaning in the Brāhmaṇas and elsewhere. The distinctive character of this description is understood from some examples.

समिधं प्रास्याभिजुहोत्यग्नेरनीकमप आ विवेशापां नपात्पतिरक्षन्नसुर्यं । (*samidhaṃ prāsyābhijuhotyagneranīkamapa ā viveśāpāṃ napātpatirakṣannasuryaṃ |*)
(Vā. Saṃ. 8-24)
O Agni, in the form of Apāṃnapāt, the waters are your face. To escape the onslaught of the Rākṣasas I have entered the waters, which are your face. Be gracious. Thus an identity between the face of Agni and the waters is stated. In some places, when the relation between Agni and the waters is shown, only the physical relation is shown. A more hidden relation is also indicated. At the time of building the fire-altar the priests, absorbed in meditation, grasp the nature of the waters and describe it in this way.

##### Grammar

- सुमेधाः — नित्यमसिच् प्रजामेधयोरित्यसिच् ।
- उच्यते — वच परिभाषणे । कर्मणि यकि रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ।
- उरूची — अंचतेः क्विन् । अंचतेश्चोपसंख्यानमिति जीप् । अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोप इति जीप उदात्तत्वं ।
- पायय — पा पान इत्यस्य णौ परतः शाच्छासाह्वान्नावेषां युगिति युक् । तिजि उत्तरत्वादनिघातः ।

ते चेतयमानाः । एतदपश्यन्नप एवैनदभ्यवहरामापो वा अस्य सर्वस्य प्रतिष्ठा तद्यत्रास्य सर्वस्य प्रतिष्ठा तदेनत्प्रतिष्ठाप्य यदत्राग्नेयं तदद्व्योधि जनयिष्याम इति तदपोऽभ्यवाहरन् । (*te cetayamānāḥ | etadapaśyannapa evainadabhyavaharāmāpo vā asya sarvasya pratiṣṭhā tadyatrāsya sarvasya pratiṣṭhā tadenatpratiṣṭhāpya yadatrāgneyaṃ tadadvyodhi janayiṣyāma iti tadapo 'bhyavāharan |*) (Śa. Brā. 6-8-22)

The waters (water) are the support of this whole world. Therefore let us carry this brick-pile to the presence of the waters. Then, having established it in the waters, the support of the universe, let us take from there only the fiery part. So the priests carry the fire-altar to the presence of the waters, which are the mouth of Agni. Then, reciting the mantra

अप्सग्ने सधिष्टव सौषधीरनु रुध्यसे । गर्भे संजायसे पुनः । (*apsagne sadhiṣṭava sauṣadhīranu rudhyase | garbhe saṃjāyase punaḥ |*) (Mai. Saṃ. 8-43-9)

they praise Agni, who is filled by the waters and has spread those water-principles into the plants and the rest, and they glorify in another way the matter described in the Ṛk at hand.

Next, the flame spreading toward the Sun, and this flame, filled by the waters, joining the water that stands in the atmosphere and is of the nature of the Sun's rays, is described thus:

अग्ने दिवो अर्णमच्छा जिगासीति । आपो वा अस्य दिवोर्णस्ता एष धूमेनाभैत्यच्छा देवाग्ं ऊचिषे धिष्ण्या य इति प्राणा वै देवा धिष्ण्यास्ते हि सर्वाधिय इष्टंति या रोचने परस्तात्सूरस्य याश्चावस्तादुपतिष्यंत आप इति रोचनो ह नामैष लोको यत्रैष एतत्तपति तद्याश्चृतं परेणापो याश्चावरेण ता एतदाह ॥ (*agne divo arṇamacchā jigāsīti | āpo vā asya divorṇastā eṣa dhūmenābhaityacchā devāgṃ ūciṣe dhiṣṇyā ya iti prāṇā vai devā dhiṣṇyāste hi sarvādhiya iṣṭaṃti yā rocane parastātsūrasya yāścāvastādupatiṣyaṃta āpa iti rocano ha nāmaiṣa loko yatraiṣa etattapati tadyāścṛtaṃ pareṇāpo yāścāvareṇa tā etadāha ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-1-1-24)

The whole atmosphere is a flowing stream of water. O Agni, your attractive flames go and join that stream of water. O Agni, as soon as you, in the form of flame, join the stream of the atmosphere, impel the gods, the representatives of the vital principle, to favour us. May the water-principle that is pervasive beyond even the radiance of heaven, that extends over earth and the other places, and that is all-pervading, become one with you: so it is prayed. Therefore it is described by the epithet madhumatī; it should be understood what nature the epithet sumedhāḥ shows for this same tongue.

अग्ने नय सुसथा राये अस्मान् विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् ॥ (*agne naya susathā rāye asmān viśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān ‖*) (Ī. Ka. 15)

### Printed p. 407
In this mantra the nature of Agni described by the epithet sumedhāḥ is what is praised. Because Agni is omniscient, knows the principle of sacrifice fully and is famed as Jātaveda, he is prayed to be the guide along the good path.

उरूची (*urūcī*)—Because he pervades the three forms (Agni, Vāyu, Āditya) and the three worlds, the epithet urūcī shows the property of pervasiveness.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining Agni! Your wisdom (pramati), of many forms and not consorting with anyone other than us, nourishes us by giving the desired fruit. The illustration: like the stream of a mountain, that is, as the water-stream of a cloud, joining the plants, trees and so on, makes them grow. O Vasu, who causes all to dwell, O Jātaveda, of born wisdom, Agni, give us that wisdom, able to do good to others; and likewise give a good wisdom (sumati), beneficial to all people. असश्चंती (*asaścaṃtī*): the root saśc means movement; पीपयत् (*pīpayat*) from the root pā (to drink); रास्व (*rāsva*) from rā (to give), a middle-voice form by vyatyaya. (The accent remarks are omitted.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव अग्ने (*deva agne*)—O shining Agni!
- चित्रा (*citrā*)—of many forms
- असश्चंती (*asaścaṃtī*)—not moving elsewhere (leaving us)
- या ते (*yā te*)—your wisdom of favour, which
- पर्वतस्य (*parvatasya*)—of the cloud
- धारा इव (*dhārā iva*)—as the stream in the form of rain makes plants and the rest grow
- पीपयत् (*pīpayat*)—nourishes us and makes us grow
- वसो (*vaso*)—O causer of dwelling for all
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni of born wisdom
