##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, shining, causer of dwelling, of born wisdom! Your wisdom of favour, of many forms and moving nowhere else away from us, nourishes us and makes us grow, as the rain-stream of the cloud makes plants and the rest grow. Set that wisdom, which brings good to all, on our side.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Divine Agni, giver of dwellings, knower of all that exists. extend to us that bencvolence which, unshared by others, cherishes us like the showers of the rain-cloud ; that kindness which is beneficent for all mankind.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*)—Having cited the Nirukta explanation जातानि वेद, जातानि वैनं विदुः (*jātāni veda, jātāni vainaṃ viduḥ*) and so on, it was explained earlier how the name Jātavedas suits Agni (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 8, p. 161-1).

सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—प्रमतिं (*pramatiṃ*): two kinds of distinction are shown in wisdom. The word pramati is explained as excellent wisdom and sumati as good wisdom,

वसो (*vaso*)—Sāyaṇa takes the word as meaning one called vasu because he causes all to dwell. It was shown in the special topics of the 2nd Ṛk of this same sūkta that, being all-pervading, he may also be denoted by the word vasu. Where Agni is said to be joined with the Vasus, they are indicated as different deities; but since in many places the all-pervading Agni, Āditya and the Vasus are said to be identical, the epithet vasu for Agni is fitting.

### Printed p. 409
it may be said that the word pramati indicates the power of knowledge useful for grasping the meaning of principles, and sumati the moral power of action needed for excellent conduct of rites.

पर्वतस्य धारा इव (*parvatasya dhārā iva*)—In this simile the word parvata is explained as cloud. How the meaning "cloud" suits parvata is a matter to be considered. In the Ṛk Saṃhitā the word parvata is used mostly in sūktas addressed to Indra and to the Maruts. The current meaning is famous as "mountain"; the question is what is the basis for explaining it as cloud. Yāska's explanation is:

पर्ववान् पर्वतः ; पर्व पुनः प्रणातेः प्रीणातीर्वा (*parvavān parvataḥ ; parva punaḥ praṇāteḥ prīṇātīrvā*) (Ni. 1-20)

Parvata is that which has joints (parva). The word parva is formed from the root pṛ, meaning "fill", or from the root prī, meaning "satisfy". The etymologists' explanation is that what has such a parva is parvata. According to this, there is no objection to a cloud being named parvata, either because clouds fill the empty sky or because through rain they satisfy the world. The same word is used in many places as an epithet of giri.

आश्मानं चित्सर्वं १ पर्वतं गिरिं प्र च्यावयंति यामभिः । (*āśmānaṃ citsarvaṃ 1 parvataṃ giriṃ pra cyāvayaṃti yāmabhiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-56-4)
त्यं चित्पर्वतं गिरिं शतवंतं सहस्रिणं । वि स्तोतृभ्यो रुरोजिथ ॥ (*tyaṃ citparvataṃ giriṃ śatavaṃtaṃ sahasriṇaṃ | vi stotṛbhyo rurojitha ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-64-5)

In these places parvata is an epithet of giri. Of these, in the first it is explained as उदकवान् मेघः (*udakavān meghaḥ*), a cloud able to fill the world with water, and in the second as पर्ववान् गिरिः (*parvavān giriḥ*), a cloud having joints.

In the Nighaṇṭu parvata, adri and giri are all read among the names of cloud (Ni. 1-10). Sāyaṇa, on Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-56-4, says the word giri is formed from the root gṛ, निगिरत्युदकमिति गिरिः (*nigiratyudakamiti giriḥ*): the cloud is called giri because it pours out water; and that the word adri is formed from the root ad (2-165-4). Since Indra is described as splitting all these with his thunderbolt and releasing water, cloud must be the well-known meaning of all of them in the Ṛk Saṃhitā. But that the original meaning of all the words is the common "mountain" is also known from many sources.

### Printed p. 410
वि वृत्रं पर्वशो ययुर्वि पर्वता अराजिनः । चक्राणा वृष्टि पौंस्यं ॥ (*vi vṛtraṃ parvaśo yayurvi parvatā arājinaḥ | cakrāṇā vṛṣṭi pauṃsyaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-23)

Here Indra struck with his thunderbolt and split these mountains, lightless and full of darkness; so it is understood that the word parvata denoted the mass of darkness. This mass of darkness is the cloud.

But to explain the word parvata everywhere simply as cloud would not be proper either. For after Indra's victory there are four kinds of attainment: 1) release of the cows; 2) unobstructed flow of the waters; 3) appearance of the dawn; 4) sunrise. These four are what occurs after Indra's victory. Therefore explaining parvata merely as cloud is possible only in some contexts.

स मातरा सूर्येणा कवीनामवासयद्रुजदद्रिं गृणानः ॥ (*sa mātarā sūryeṇā kavīnāmavāsayadrujadadriṃ gṛṇānaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-32-2)

In such places it says that having split the adri he caused the sunlight and spread it over heaven and earth. Here the word adri is explained as parvata, but not the mountain commonly so called; so it must be explained as a mass of darkness resembling a mountain. Similarly:

महांतमिंद्र पर्वतं वि यद्वः सृजो सि धारा अव धानवं हन् ॥ (*mahāṃtamiṃdra parvataṃ vi yadvaḥ sṛjo si dhārā ava dhānavaṃ han ‖*) (Saṃ. 5-32-1)

The mountain that holds back the water must be explained as the dark cloud. The sense fits if it is the deep cloud standing in the atmosphere, as in:

शिशुं नदीनाग्ं हरिमदिबुध्नमिति गिरिर्वा अद्रिगिरिबुध्ना उ वा आपः ॥ (*śiśuṃ nadīnāgṃ harimadibudhnamiti girirvā adrigiribudhnā u vā āpaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-5-2-18)

This supports the idea stated in the Brāhmaṇa passage that the water, the embryo of that Varuṇa's horse which was earlier called the Sun's rays (वारुणो ना अश्वः (*vāruṇo nā aśvaḥ*)), rests at the base of the adri. This darkness, dense like a mountain and pervasive, holds back the water and the sun's rays (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16 6; 8). Its use in this very sense of "full of darkness" is seen in many other places. For example,

त्वमपापसिधानावृणोरपाधारयः पर्वते दानुमद्वसु । (*tvamapāpasidhānāvṛṇorapādhārayaḥ parvate dānumadvasu |*) (Pa. Saṃ. 102-4) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 411
Many places describe how Indra (Indra in the form of the Sun), with his shining rays, set all the mountains in motion and made the hidden Sun shine; in them the meaning must be taken as stated above. Passages such as "शिशुं नदीनां हरिमद्रिबुद्धं (*śiśuṃ nadīnāṃ harimadribuddhaṃ*)" (Vā. Saṃ. 13-82) also support this meaning.

Just as the word parvata is used to denote a mass of darkness and its density, so it is used also to denote a mass of light, the opposite of darkness. For example,

प्राक्तादपाक्तादधरादुदक्तादभि जहि रक्षसः पर्वतेन । (*prāktādapāktādadharādudaktādabhi jahi rakṣasaḥ parvatena |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104-9)

In such places the explanation पर्ववान् पर्वतः (*parvavān parvataḥ*) is given. Here "thunderbolt" is the meaning, that is, a mass of light. If the word parvata is formed from the root prī, as in the etymologists' second explanation, it may also have been used in the sense of friends who give pleasure. For example,

अस्मे रुद्रा मेहना पर्वतासो वृत्रहत्ये भरहूत् सजोषाः ॥ (*asme rudrā mehanā parvatāso vṛtrahatye bharahūt sajoṣāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-63-12)

Here the Maruts are Indra's friends. Because they helped Indra in battle and in slaying Vṛtra, they became dear to him. Therefore they are denoted by the word parvata. Sāyaṇa explains the sense of this word: पर्वतसद्वशाः पूरणवंतः प्रीणनवंतो वा मरुतः । (*parvatasadvaśāḥ pūraṇavaṃtaḥ prīṇanavaṃto vā marutaḥ |*)

There are contexts where parvata is understood as a particular luminous deity. For example,

प्रोतये वरुणं मित्रमिंद्रं मरुतः कृष्वावसे नो अद्य । प्र पूषणं विष्णुमग्निं पुरंधिं सवितारमोषधीः पर्वतांश्च ॥ (*protaye varuṇaṃ mitramiṃdraṃ marutaḥ kṛṣvāvase no adya | pra pūṣaṇaṃ viṣṇumagniṃ puraṃdhiṃ savitāramoṣadhīḥ parvatāṃśca ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-21-9)
शं नः पर्वता ध्रुवयो भवंतु शं नः सिंधवः शमु सन्त्वापः ॥ (*śaṃ naḥ parvatā dhruvayo bhavaṃtu śaṃ naḥ siṃdhavaḥ śamu santvāpaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-35-8)

In all such places the parvatas too are prayed to for favour along with deities such as Indra and Mitra; it is prayed that the mountains be pleasant to us. In such contexts Sāyaṇa explains: पर्वतान् अद्रीन् इत्येतान् देवान् । (*parvatān adrīn ityetān devān |*) the deities called parvata are joined with Indra and the other deities and prayed to for our protection. But in places such as न पर्वता न नद्यः (*na parvatā na nadyaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-55-7) he explains it as the earthly mountain. In contexts such as ध्रुवा ह पर्वता इमे (*dhruvā ha parvatā ime*) (Tai. Brā. 2-4-28) and पर्वत इवाविचाचलिः (*parvata ivāvicācaliḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-173-2), too, the simile is of the earthly mountain, firmly established.

### Printed p. 412
In the verse under discussion, the comparisons beginning with धारा इव (*dhārā iva*) support the meaning "cloud" itself.

विश्वजन्या (*viśvajanyā*)—beneficial to all people. It is an adjective of the word सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*), "excellent understanding": an understanding that brings welfare to everyone. The word जन्य (*janya*) is used in three senses. First, formed from the root जन् (*jan*), it means "fit for birth"; this is the conventional sense. In passages such as पात्पतिर्जन्यादंहसो नो मित्रः (*pātpatirjanyādaṃhaso no mitraḥ*) (4-55-5) the word जन्य (*janya*) denotes what is connected with people; the prayer there is "free us from the sin connected with people". Besides this, जन्य (*janya*) denotes what is beneficial to people. In contexts such as जनंजनं जन्यो नातिमन्यते (*janaṃjanaṃ janyo nātimanyate*) (10-91-2), जन्य (*janya*) means "beneficial to people". The same meaning must be stated for विश्वजन्यां (*viśvajanyāṃ*).

स आ यजस्व नृवतीरनु क्षाः स्वार्हा इषः क्षुमतीर्विश्वदन्याः ॥ (*sa ā yajasva nṛvatīranu kṣāḥ svārhā iṣaḥ kṣumatīrviśvadanyāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-2-6)

The sense is: offer to the gods food that is a means to the welfare of all people. In the same way, in the present verse too the purport of the word विश्वजन्य (*viśvajanya*) must be stated as "what brings welfare to all people".

विश्वजन्यां सुमतिं (*viśvajanyāṃ sumatiṃ*)—in the prayer "grant a good understanding that brings welfare to all", a vision of the welfare of the world is indicated: not looking only to one's own selfish good, but that the whole world may find well-being.

## Sūkta 58 (Maṇḍala 3)

> धेनुः प्रत्नस्येति नवर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं त्रिष्टुभमाश्विनं । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । धेनुर्नवाश्विनमिति ॥ प्रातरनुवाक आश्विनक्रत् त्रिष्टुभे छंदस्याश्विन
> शस्त्रे चास्य सूक्तस्य विनियोगः । सूत्रितं च । धेनु: प्रत्नस्य क उ श्रवदिति सूक्ते ।
> आ. ४-१५ । इति ॥ व्यूक्षे दशरात्रे द्वितीये छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रेयमाश्विनश्च
> तुर्थस्तृचः । द्वितीयस्याग्निं व इति खंडे सूत्रितं । धेनुः प्रत्नस्य काम्यं दुहाना
> ब्रह्माण इंद्रोप याहि विद्वान् । आ. ८-१० । इति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning धेनुः प्रत्नस्य (*dhenuḥ pratnasya*) is the fifth sūkta, of nine verses. Its seer is Viśvāmitra, its deity the Aśvins, its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says धेनुर्नवाश्विनमिति (*dhenurnavāśvinamiti*). The sūkta is applied in the Prātaranuvāka, in the Āśvina-kratu, to the Āśvina-śastra in the Triṣṭubh metre. The sūtra says: धेनु: प्रत्नस्य क उ श्रवदिति सूक्ते (*dhenu: pratnasya ka u śravaditi sūkte*) (Ā. Sū. 4-15). Further, in the Vyūḍha Daśarātra, in the second Chandoma, in the Prauga-śastra, the fourth tṛca (set of three verses) is the Āśvina one; the sūtra in the khaṇḍa beginning द्वितीयस्याग्निं व (*dvitīyasyāgniṃ va*) reads धेनुः प्रत्नस्य काम्यं दुहाना ब्रह्माण इंद्रोप याहि विद्वान् (*dhenuḥ pratnasya kāmyaṃ duhānā brahmāṇa iṃdropa yāhi vidvān*) (Ā. Sū. 8-10).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning धेनुः प्रत्नस्य (*dhenuḥ pratnasya*) is the fifth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. Viśvāmitra is its seer; the Aśvins are its deity; Triṣṭubh is its metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is described as धेनुर्नवाश्विनं (*dhenurnavāśvinaṃ*). At the time of reciting the mantras of the Prātaranuvāka, this sūkta is applied to the Āśvina-śastra mantras in the Triṣṭubh metre belonging to the Āśvina-kratu; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra धेनुः प्रत्नस्य क उ श्रवदिति सूक्ते (*dhenuḥ pratnasya ka u śravaditi sūkte*) (Ā. 4-15). And in the Daśarātra sacrifice called Vyūḍha, in the second Chandoma, among the Prauga-śastra mantras, the first three ṛks of this sūkta are applied to the fourth tṛca (tṛca means three ṛks), which has the Aśvins as deity; this is set out in the khaṇḍa द्वितीयस्याग्निं व (*dvitīyasyāgniṃ va*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra धेनुः प्रत्नस्य काम्यं दुहाना ब्रह्माण इंद्रोप याहि विद्वान् (*dhenuḥ pratnasya kāmyaṃ duhānā brahmāṇa iṃdropa yāhi vidvān*) (Ā. 8-10).

Sūkta 58
Maṇḍala 3 · Anuvāka 5 · Sūkta 58
Aṣṭaka 3 · Adhyāya 4 · Varga 3, 4
Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 9
Seer: Viśvāmitra
Deity: the Aśvins
Metre: Triṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> धे॒नुः प्र॒त्नस्य॒ काम्यं॒ दुहा॑नां॒तः पु॒त्रश्च॑रति॒ दक्षि॑णायाः ।  
> आ द्यो॑त॒निं व॑हति शु॒भ्रया॑मो॒षसः॒ स्तोमो॑ अ॒श्विना॑वजीगः॥

> *dhenuḥ pratnasya kāmyaṃ duhānāṃtaḥ putraścarati dakṣiṇāyāḥ |*  
> *ā dyotaniṃ vahati śubhrayāmoṣasaḥ stomo aśvināvajīgaḥ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> धेनुः । प्रत्नस्य । काम्यं । दुहाना । अंतरिति । पुत्रः । च र ति । दक्षिणायाः ।

### Printed p. 414

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धेनुः प्रीणयित्रुषाः प्रत्नस्य पुरातनस्याग्नेः काम्यं कमनीयं पयो
> दुहाना । दोग्द्रि भवति । दक्षिणाया उषसः पुत्रः सूरस्तस्या अंतश्चरति ! उषसोऽनंतरं शुभ्रयामा । सूर्यकिरणसंपर्काच्छुभ्रतया गमनं यस्यासौ शुभ्रयामा दिवसः । द्योतनिं सर्वस्य प्रकाशकं सूर्यमा वहति । बिभर्ति । अत उषसः
> पुराश्विन् स्तोतुं स्तोमः स्तोत्रकारी होत्रादिरजीगः । जागर्ति । उत्तिष्ठति ॥
> शुभ्रयामा । या प्रापणे । आतो मनिन् । बहुप्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । अजीग ।
> जागृ निद्राक्षये । लजतिष्यदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । आकारस्येकारश्चांदसः । गुणे कृते
> हल्ब्यादिना तिपो लोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

धेनुः (*dhenuḥ*) is the one who gratifies, Uṣas. She yields (दुहाना (*duhānā*), a milker) the desirable milk of ancient Agni. The son of the southern Uṣas, the sun, moves within her. After Uṣas comes the "bright-coursed" one (शुभ्रयामा (*śubhrayāmā*)), the day, whose going is bright through contact with the sun's rays. It bears (वहति (*vahati*), "carries") the illuminator of all, the sun. Therefore the praiser (स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)), the hotṛ and others, wakes (अजीगः (*ajīgaḥ*), "is awake, rises") in order to praise the Aśvins before Uṣas.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धेनुः (*dhenuḥ*)—Uṣas, the goddess who gives joy to the world
- प्रत्नस्य (*pratnasya*)—for the ancient Agni
- काम्यं (*kāmyaṃ*)—the desired age (vayas)**NOTE**
- दुहाना (*duhānā*)—she milks
- दक्षिणायाः (*dakṣiṇāyāḥ*)—of Uṣas
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—the son, the sun
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the atmosphere
- चरति (*carati*)—he moves
- शुभ्रयामा (*śubhrayāmā*)—the day lit up by the sun's rays
- द्योतनिं (*dyotaniṃ*)—the sun, the illuminator of all
- आ वहति (*ā vahati*)—it bears
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—before the appearance of Uṣas
- अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*)—to praise the Aśvins
- स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)—the praiser
- अजीगः (*ajīgaḥ*)—wakes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Uṣas, who gives joy to the world, milks the desired age for ancient Agni. The sun, son of Uṣas, moves in the atmosphere. The day, lit up by the sun's rays, bears the sun, the illuminator of all. Before the appearance of Uṣas the praiser wakes in order to praise the Aśvins.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The milch-cow (the dawn) yields the desired milk to the ancient (Agni); the son of the south passes within (the firmament) ; the bright-houred (day) brings the illuminative (sun) : the praiser awakes to (glory) the Ashwins preceding the dawn.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This mantra describes the relation of Uṣas to the sacrificial fire, how the world is lit by the sun's radiance as soon as Uṣas appears, and also the companionship of Uṣas with the Aśvins. Because Uṣas gives joy to the world, she is denoted by the word धेनु (*dhenu*)

### Printed p. 415
(cow). The special meaning suggested by the word धेनु (*dhenu*) has been stated earlier. Here the word is used to show the relation between Agni and Uṣas. Or it may be said that just as she is a cause of growth for Agni, so through Agni she is a cause of growth for the world. There is no doubt that the world gets still greater joy from the sight of Uṣas than the calf gets from the sight of the cow. Darkness is destroyed, and not only physical darkness: the darkness of ignorance too is destroyed. Along with the delight that comes from seeing with the eye, delight of the self is also gained. Since she gives satisfaction in many ways, it is quite proper that she is denoted by the word धेनु (*dhenu*). She is also described by the word दक्षिणायाः (*dakṣiṇāyāḥ*). And it is stated here that Āditya is her son; in the same way Agni too can be called her son. How the relation of mother and son holds between Uṣas and Āditya and Agni is also explained in many places.

ऋतवस्तेऽथ यः स भूतानां पतिः संवत्सरः सोऽथ या सोषाः पत्न्यौषसी सा तानीमानि भूतानि च भूतानां च पतिः संवत्सर उषसि रेतोऽसिंचन्त न संवत्सरे कुमारोऽजायत ॥ (*ṛtavaste 'tha yaḥ sa bhūtānāṃ patiḥ saṃvatsaraḥ so 'tha yā soṣāḥ patnyauṣasī sā tānīmāni bhūtāni ca bhūtānāṃ ca patiḥ saṃvatsara uṣasi reto 'siṃcanta na saṃvatsare kumāro 'jāyata ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-3-8)

The beings created by Prajāpati are the seasons. The lord of beings is the year. Uṣas is his wife. At first this year, lord of beings, and the seasons cast seed in Uṣas. Then a son was born. This boy is the one marked by the name Agni. Varieties of names suited to their natures became known for him. The relation of mother and son between Uṣas and Agni is suggested also in the present verse. In passages such as नक्तोषासा वर्णमामेम्याने धापयेते शिशुमेकं समाची (*naktoṣāsā varṇamāmemyāne dhāpayete śiśumekaṃ samācī*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-4), where Night and Uṣas together nourish one son common to both, this son may be either Agni or the sun. Through these sons she possesses the power to protect the world and the power to bestow wealth on the world. Therefore she is described by the epithet दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*).

उदु श्रिय उषसो रोचमाना अस्तुरपां नोर्मयो रुशंतः कृणोति विश्वा सुपथा सुगान्यभूदु वस्वी दक्षिणा मघोनी ॥ (*udu śriya uṣaso rocamānā asturapāṃ normayo ruśaṃtaḥ kṛṇoti viśvā supathā sugānyabhūdu vasvī dakṣiṇā maghonī ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-64-1)

As soon as the rays of the radiant Uṣas spread over the universe like a flow of water, the world gets new vitality and becomes a bestower of wealth. For this very reason she is described by the epithets मघोनी (*maghonī*) and दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*). All these points are suggested in the present verse.

### Printed p. 416
सोमः (*somaḥ*)—this word means "praise". **NOTE**. In some contexts it is also used of the praiser.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒युग्व॑हंति॒ प्रति॑ नामृ॒तेनो॒र्ध्वा भ॑वंति पि॒तरे॑व॒ मेधाः॑।  
> जरे॑थाम॒स्मद्वि प॒णेर्म॑नी॒षां यु॒वोरव॑श्चकृ॒मा या॑तम॒र्वाक् ॥ २ ॥

> *suyugvahaṃti prati nāmṛtenordhvā bhavaṃti pitareva medhāḥ|*  
> *jarethāmasmadvi paṇermanīṣāṃ yuvoravaścakṛmā yātamarvāk ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुयुक् । वहंति । प्रति । वां । ऋतेन । ऊर्ध्वाः । भवंति । पितरा इव । मेधाः ।  
> जरेथां । अस्मत् । वि । पणेः । मनीषां । युवोः । अवः । चकृम । आ । यातं ।  
> अर्वाक् ॥ २ ॥

> *suyuk | vahaṃti | prati | vāṃ | ṛtena | ūrdhvāḥ | bhavaṃti | pitarā iva | medhāḥ |*  
> *jarethāṃ | asmat | vi | paṇeḥ | manīṣāṃ | yuvoḥ | avaḥ | cakṛma | ā | yātaṃ |*  
> *arvāk ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ सुयुक् सुष्टु रथे योजिता अश्वा ऋतेन सत्यभूतेन रथेन वां
> युवां प्रति वहंति । यज्ञं प्रत्यागमनाय धारयंति । मेधा यज्ञाश्चोर्ध्वा
> युष्मदभिमुखमूर्ध्वा भवंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । पितरेव ' यथा पुत्राः पितर मातापितरावभिलक्ष्य गच्छंति तद्वत् । अस्मदस्मत्तः सकाशात्पणेर्मनीषामासुरीं बुद्धिं वि
> जरेथां । विशेषेण नाशयतं । वयं तु युवोर्युवयोरवो हनिर्लक्षणमन्नं
> चक्रम । कुर्मः । युवामर्वागस्मादाभिमुख्येना यातं ॥ सुयुक् । युजे
> क्विप् । सुपां सुलुगिति सुपो लुक् । पितरेव । पिता मात्रेति पितुः शेषः । सुपो
> डादेशः । जरेथां । ज्ञष वयोहान् । ण्यंतस्य जनीज्यष्ट सुरंजोऽमंताश्वेति
> मित्त्वाद्वृद्ध्यभावः । छंदस्युभयथेत्याधाम आर्धधातुकत्याणिलोपतः । शपः पिता ;
> दनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, the horses well yoked (सुयुक् (*suyuk*)) to the chariot carry you both (प्रति वहंति (*prati vahaṃti*)) by the chariot that is true (ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), "of the nature of truth"), that is, they bear you to come to the sacrifice. The sacrifices (मेधाः (*medhāḥ*)) turn upward (ऊर्ध्वाः (*ūrdhvāḥ*)) towards you. The illustration: पितरेव (*pitareva*), as sons go towards their parents, mother and father. Utterly destroy (वि जरेथां (*vi jarethāṃ*)) from us the Asura mind (मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)) of the niggard (पणेः (*paṇeḥ*)). We, for our part, have made for you both (युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)) food (अवः (*avaḥ*)) in the form of oblation. Come to us, facing us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*)—O Aśvins)
- सुयुक् (*suyuk*)—horses yoked to a fine chariot
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—in the chariot of the nature of truth
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you both
- प्रति वहंति (*prati vahaṃti*)—bring, for coming to the sacrifice
- मेधाः (*medhāḥ*)—the sacrifices
- ऊर्ध्वाः (*ūrdhvāḥ*)—facing you

### Printed p. 417
- पितरेव (*pitareva*)—as children go facing their father
- भवंति (*bhavaṃti*)—they look to you
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us
- पणेः मनीषां (*paṇeḥ manīṣāṃ*)—the understanding connected with the wicked
- वि जरेथां (*vi jarethāṃ*)—destroy completely
- युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—addressing you both
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—food in the form of oblation
- चक्रम (*cakrama*)—we have prepared
- आर्वाक् (*ārvāk*)—facing us
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—be gracious and come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, horses yoked to a fine chariot bring you both, in the chariot of the nature of truth, to come to the sacrifice. As children stand facing their father, the sacrifices face you. Destroy from us the understanding connected with the wicked. Addressing you both, we have prepared food in the form of oblation. Be gracious and come facing us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The well-yoked (horses) bear you both in your truth (preserving car): the offerings proceed towards you as (children to their parents): discard from us the disposition of the niggard : we have made ready for you our offering : come to our presence.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the previous mantra the relation of Uṣas to the Aśvins was stated; in the present one the prayer is that the Aśvins come towards the sacrifice. Stating the manner in which they are to come to the sacrifice, the mantra indicates the route of their coming with सुयुक् ऋतेन तां प्रतिवहंति (*suyuk ṛtena tāṃ prativahaṃti*).

Here the word ऋत (*ṛta*) has been explained as "chariot". But that is not its direct meaning: the word ऋत (*ṛta*) is first taken as "truth", and then it is explained as "of the nature of truth", with the construction with "in the chariot" or "on the chariot-way". As described in mantras such as

नृवद्दस्रा मनोयुजा रथेन पृथुपाजसा । सचेथे अश्विनोषसं ॥ (*nṛvaddasrā manoyujā rathena pṛthupājasā | sacethe aśvinoṣasaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-5-2)

the manner of coming to the sacrifice in a splendid chariot, following Uṣas as soon as she appears, is described. The word ऋत (*ṛta*) is used in the senses of truth, sacrifice, water, conduct of the nature of truth, and so on. If here it is taken as "path of the nature of truth", it may suit the context.

Even if ऋत (*ṛta*) is taken as "truth", it means that which has an eternal state. The sun and the other planets all move regularly, eternal and radiant, and (the text breaks off at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 418
The path of the sun and the other planets, which move regularly and well, is permanent and radiant; it is established usage in the Ṛgveda to call this course ṛta. What the path of ṛta is, as described in the words वर्वर्ति चक्रं परि द्यामृतस्य (*varvarti cakraṃ pari dyāmṛtasya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-11), has been explained in full earlier. This same path of ṛta is described in passages such as
अग्निर्गांधर्वीं पथ्यामृतस्याग्नेर्गव्यूतिर्घृत आ निषत्ता (*agnirgāṃdharvīṃ pathyāmṛtasyāgnergavyūtirghṛta ā niṣattā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-6)
as the lofty and spacious path of the Gandharva. It has likewise been explained that the path of the Ādityas and others is described by epithets such as ऋतस्य योना (*ṛtasya yonā*) and ऋतस्य पदे (*ṛtasya pade*). In the present verse the sense of ऋतेन (*ṛtena*) is that the Aśvins' excellent horses bring them along this permanent and radiant Gandharva path.

मेधाः (*medhāḥ*)—the word मेध (*medha*) means sacrifice. In some places it also means the oblation fit for the sacrifice. At मेधं जुषंत वह्नयः (*medhaṃ juṣaṃta vahnayaḥ*) (1-3-9) Sāyaṇa explains: मेध्यते देवैः सह, संगम्यते इति मेधं हविः (*medhyate devaiḥ saha, saṃgamyate iti medhaṃ haviḥ*) — since the oblation joins and becomes one with the gods, the word मेध (*medha*) applies to it. Or, if मेध (*medha*) is taken to mean wisdom, the act of a wise man is also मेध (*medha*). Some hold that because worship of the gods and the like is the act of the wise, the sacrifice has the name मेध (*medha*). This sense too is not without support:
यदेव विद्यया करोति श्रद्धयोपनिषदा तदेव वीर्यवत्तरं भवति (*yadeva vidyayā karoti śraddhayopaniṣadā tadeva vīryavattaraṃ bhavati*) (Bhā. U. 1-1-10)
The Chāndogya and others say that the rite performed with knowledge and with faith is the one that becomes vigorous; since the need of knowledge at the time of performing rites is thus stated, the word मेध (*medha*) may be so applicable. But in giving this sense, the etymology मेध्यते देवैः सह (*medhyate devaiḥ saha*) must still be applied to the sacrifice.
इतः प्रदानादि देवा उपजीवंति (*itaḥ pradānādi devā upajīvaṃti*) (Śa. Brā. 1-2-4-5)
The offering made from here reaches the gods, and they live because they are thereby satisfied; this shows the relation of cause and effect between the gods' existence and the sacrifice. So this etymology also fits. Or तन्नेध्यमभूत् (*tannedhyamabhūt*) (Śa. Brā. 10-6-5-7): "it became pure"; because it became pure, the word मेध (*medha*) applies — the etymology can be given thus too.

पितरेव ऊर्ध्वा भवंति (*pitareva ūrdhvā bhavaṃti*)—there is a special point in the description that the sacrifice goes to face the Aśvins and receives them, as children go to meet a father. Of the

### Printed p. 419
other gods, all take part in the sacrifice, whereas the Aśvins alone have no share in it; this is known to all. The Vedic sentence अन्यत्रैवाश्विभ्यां (*anyatraivāśvibhyāṃ*) (Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-1), that Indra and the other gods took part, excluding the Aśvins, states this exactly. Yet how is a father–son relation possible? There is a story that explains the circumstance showing the close connection between the Aśvins and the sacrifice.
तावेदद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रत्यधत्तां तददस्तद्विवाकीर्त्यानां ब्राह्मणे व्याख्यानये यथा तद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिदधतुः तस्मात् .... ....॥ (*tāvedadyajñasya śiraḥ pratyadhattāṃ tadadastadvivākīrtyānāṃ brāhmaṇe vyākhyānaye yathā tadyajñasya śiraḥ pratidadhatuḥ tasmāt .... ....‖*) (Śa. Brā. 4-1-5-15)
In this story the Aśvins repaired the headless sacrifice so that the sacrificial work was completed; it is also said that the story is told in the Brāhmaṇa called Divākīrtya (Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-9). The same matter is recited in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as well (Ai. Brā. 4-9). Thus, when the sacrifice lacked its principal part, they set it right and made the sacrifice indebted to them; as if to show gratitude for this, the sacrifice receives the Aśvins — so the present mantra describes.

पणिं मनीषां (*paṇiṃ manīṣāṃ*)—here पणि (*paṇi*) is taken to mean unbelievers who have no faith in the sacrifice. मनीषा (*manīṣā*) means understanding. The prayer is: may we not have such an unbelieving mind, or if we have it, destroy it and make a believing mind arise in the performance of the sacrifice.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ सुयुग्भिः सुष्टु योजितैरश्वैः सुवृता । पुनःपुनरावर्तत इति
> वृच्चक्रं । शोभनचक्रोपेतेन रथेनागत्य दसौ शत्रूणामुपक्षपयितारौ युवामद्रॆः । आद्रियते सर्वैरित्यद्रिः स्तोता । तस्येमं श्लोकं स्तोत्रं शृणुतं । अंग
> हे अश्विनौ विप्रासो मेधाविनः पुराजाः पुरातना ऋषयो वां युवामवर्ति
> मस्माकं वृत्तिहानिं प्रति गमिष्ठा अतिशयेन गंताराविति किमाहुः किं कथयंतीति ।
> न कथयंतीत्यर्थः । प्रथमाष्टकेष्टमेध्याये सुवृता रथेनेत्यादि गतं ॥
> गमिष्ठा । गंतृशब्दादिष्टनि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, with well-yoked horses (सुयुग्भिः (*suyugbhiḥ*)) and a car (सुवृता (*suvṛtā*): वृत् (*vṛt*) is the wheel, which turns again and again — a car with fine wheels), come, दसौ (*dasau*), destroyers of enemies, and hear this praise (श्लोकं (*ślokaṃ*) = स्तोत्रं (*stotraṃ*)) of the worshipper अद्रेः (*adreḥ*) — one who is honoured (आद्रियते (*ādriyate*)) by all is अद्रि (*adri*), the praiser. अंग (*aṃga*): O Aśvins, do the wise, ancient seers (विप्रासो (*viprāso*) पुराजाः (*purājāḥ*)) not say of you that you are most ready to go (गमिष्ठा (*gamiṣṭhā*)) to our अवर्तिं (*avartiṃ*), loss of livelihood? That is, they do say it. "सुवृता रथेन (*suvṛtā rathena*)" and the rest has been treated in the first Aṣṭaka, eighth Adhyāya. गमिष्ठा (*gamiṣṭhā*) is the iṣṭhan form from the word गंतृ (*gaṃtṛ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुयुग्भिः (*suyugbhiḥ*)—well yoked to the car
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—joined with horses
- सुवृता (*suvṛtā*)—having excellent wheels
- रथेन (*rathena*)—coming in the car
- दसौ (*dasau*)—you, destroyers of enemies
- अद्रेः (*adreḥ*)—of the praiser
- इमं श्लोकं (*imaṃ ślokaṃ*)—this praise
- शृणुतं (*śṛṇutaṃ*)—hear
- अंग (*aṃga*)—O Aśvins
- विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)—wise
- पुराजाः (*purājāḥ*)—ancient seers
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- अवर्तिं प्रति (*avartiṃ prati*)—towards those afflicted by sorrow
- गमिष्ठा (*gamiṣṭhā*)—as those who go
- किं आहुः (*kiṃ āhuḥ*)—have they not said?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, coming in a car with excellent wheels, drawn by horses yoked in the best manner, you who destroy enemies, hear this praise of the worshipper. O Aśvins, have the wise and ancient seers not said of you that you go towards those afflicted by sorrow?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Dasras, with well-yoked horses and well-constructed car, hear this praise of the worshipper, for have not the ancient sages declared you, Ashwins, to be most ready to come to the aid of the destitute ?

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दस्रा—दसु-उपक्षयेः-शत्रुणां उपक्षपयितारौ । यद्वा । देववैद्यतेन रोगाणां उपक्षपयितारौ । (*dasrā—dasu-upakṣayeḥ-śatruṇāṃ upakṣapayitārau | yadvā | devavaidyatena rogāṇāṃ upakṣapayitārau |*) It means destroyers of enemies, or, being divine physicians, destroyers of diseases. दस्रा (*dasrā*) may also mean दर्शनीयौ (*darśanīyau*), those of beautiful form. In the present verse the commentator takes it as destroyers of enemies. Of the Aśvins, sons of Saraṇyū, one is named Dasra and the other Nāsatya, yet it is customary to speak of both together as दस्रा (*dasrā*).

### Printed p. 421
अद्रेः (*adreḥ*)—the word अद्रि (*adri*) is used in the senses of the soma-pressing stone, mountain and so on, and its special senses have been given earlier. Here it is taken to mean the praiser. आद्रियते सर्वैरित्यद्रि (*ādriyate sarvairityadri*): because he is honoured by all, the praiser is designated by the epithet अद्रि (*adri*); this is understood from Sāyaṇa's explanation.
सुवृता (*suvṛtā*)—पुनःपुनरावर्तत इति वृत् चक्रं (*punaḥpunarāvartata iti vṛt cakraṃ*): since the wheel turns repeatedly, the word वृत् (*vṛt*) is used for it. The qualified word सुवृता (*suvṛtā*) shows an excellent wheel. The epithets त्रिवंधुरः (*trivaṃdhuraḥ*) and त्रिचक्रः (*tricakraḥ*) of the Aśvins' car and their distinction have been given earlier.
श्लोकं (*ślokaṃ*)—स्तुतिं (*stutiṃ*): here it is explained as praise. In the Saṃhitā the meaning of this word has to be stated according to context. Where the word is used in Brāhmaṇa sentences, the sense given is, as is current here, a metrically bound composition. But in the Ṛgveda there is no rule that it must be taken as such a composition. For instance:
यदद्रयः पर्वताः साकमाशवः श्लोकं घोषं भरथेंद्राय सोमिनः॥ (*yadadrayaḥ parvatāḥ sākamāśavaḥ ślokaṃ ghoṣaṃ bharatheṃdrāya sominaḥ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-1)
In this verse the nature of the sound made by the stones at the time of soma-pressing is described. Here the word घोष (*ghoṣa*) has the epithet श्लोक (*śloka*): श्लोकं श्रोतव्यं घोषं (*ślokaṃ śrotavyaṃ ghoṣaṃ*) — an audible sound, that is, a sound pleasing to hear. Similarly,
युजे नां ब्रह्म पूर्व्यं नमोभिर्वि श्लोक एतु पथ्येव सूरेः । (*yuje nāṃ brahma pūrvyaṃ namobhirvi śloka etu pathyeva sūreḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-13-1)
here the carts that hold the oblation are described; the prayer is that their श्लोक (*śloka*), their sound, go to the gods from all sides and satisfy them. Thus, though in some places the word is used in the sense of sound, in many contexts the sense of praise is well established. On this basis the English commentators have taken the word as "noise" even in the Śatapatha and elsewhere. For example:
श्लोकाय स्वाहेति वीर्यं वै श्लोको विरेणैवैनं....। (*ślokāya svāheti vīryaṃ vai śloko vireṇaivainaṃ....|*) (Śa. Brā. 5-3-5-9)
They render it: "To the noise, hail. " noise means vigour ; with vigour he thus sprinkles him. According to this explanation श्लोक (*śloka*) means vigorous sound. But in explaining the sense of Brāhmaṇa sentences, Sāyaṇa and others have given it as a composition in verse-quarters (पाद (*pāda*)).

### Printed p. 422
For example, in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, at तदप्येषश्लोकोऽभिगीतः (*tadapyeṣaśloko 'bhigītaḥ*) — "on this matter this śloka is recited" — Sāyaṇa explains श्लोकः पादबद्धः मंत्रः (*ślokaḥ pādabaddhaḥ maṃtraḥ*), a mantra bound in verse-quarters. This śloka stands bound in quarters in the form मरुतः परिवेष्टारः मरुतस्यावसन् गृहे (*marutaḥ pariveṣṭāraḥ marutasyāvasan gṛhe*) and so on. But though the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa has the quarter-bound order, the same sentence in the Śatapatha (Śa. Brā. 13-5-4-6) is not subject to this rule. This rule can be seen in the Upaniṣads and the like.
यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्वांगिरस इतिहासः पुराणं विद्या उपनिषदः श्लोकाः (*yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvāṃgirasa itihāsaḥ purāṇaṃ vidyā upaniṣadaḥ ślokāḥ*) (Bṛ. U. 2-4-10)
Here the श्लोक (*śloka*) is said to be distinct from the four Vedas, the Upaniṣads, Itihāsa and Purāṇa. श्लोका ब्राह्मणप्रभवा मंत्राः तदेते श्लोकाः (*ślokā brāhmaṇaprabhavā maṃtrāḥ tadete ślokāḥ*)—Śaṅkarācārya explains in his commentary that श्लोक (*śloka*) means the mantras cited in the Brāhmaṇas. Examples can be seen in many places.
स्वप्नेन शारीरमभिप्रहत्यासुप्तः सुप्तानभिचाकशीति । शुक्रमादाय पुनरैति स्थानं हिरण्मयः पुरुष एकहंसः ॥ (*svapnena śārīramabhiprahatyāsuptaḥ suptānabhicākaśīti | śukramādāya punaraiti sthānaṃ hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣa ekahaṃsaḥ ‖*)
These and the like are specimens of श्लोक (*śloka*) in the Chāndogya and other Upaniṣads. Further, the Taittirīya Upaniṣad uses this word in two senses.
इदं पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति (*idaṃ pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā | tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati*) (Tai. U. 2-1)
Here श्लोक (*śloka*) means a mantra. Having first stated the greatness of some principle, another mantra is cited to support it; in such a context it is the practice in the Upaniṣads and the like to say तदप्येष श्लोको भवति (*tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati*). Besides,
अहमन्न महमन्न महमन्नं । अहमन्नादोs २ हमन्नादोs २ हमन्नादः । अहग् श्लोकतृदहग् श्लोककृदहग् श्लोककृत् ॥ (*ahamanna mahamanna mahamannaṃ | ahamannādos 2 hamannādos 2 hamannādaḥ | ahag ślokatṛdahag ślokakṛdahag ślokakṛt ‖*) (Tai. U. 3-10)
"I am food; I am the eater of food; I am the combination of food and eater of food" — here श्लोक (*śloka*) is taken to mean combination. श्लोको नाम अन्नान्नादयोः संघातः (*śloko nāma annānnādayoḥ saṃghātaḥ*): Śaṅkarācārya explains that श्लोक (*śloka*) means the combined form of food and the eater of food. The sense current here is also derived from this same root. श्लोक (*śloka*)

### Printed p. 423
is derived from the root श्लोक् (*ślok*), meaning combination (संघाते (*saṃghāte*)). To string pleasing words together in metre means to bring words together according to rule, in the way of the grammarians. Śaṅkarācārya gives this same meaning for the word in the cited Upaniṣad sentence. It is the context in which the Self describes its own Brahman nature: "the aggregate of food and the eater of food is also I."
Since such usages exist, in the present verse श्लोक (*śloka*) is taken as praise. It may be a combination of mantras praising the gods, or, as Sāyaṇa says in explaining the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence, a praise bound in quarters, of the nature of a mantra and a combination of words.
अंग (*aṃga*) is an address to the Aśvins; it may mean "those with attractive limbs". Epithets such as युवाना (*yuvānā*), वल्गू (*valgū*), मधुवर्णा (*madhuvarṇā*), शुभस्पती (*śubhaspatī*) describe the attractive limbs of the Aśvins.
पुराजाः नां आहुः (*purājāḥ nāṃ āhuḥ*)**NOTE**—the sentence "the ancient seers have said that you go towards those afflicted by sorrow" points to occasions when many seers in the past praised the Aśvins' generosity and power. It is well known that Kutsa Āṅgirasa and others praised them, describing how the Aśvins protected sufferers such as Rebha and Vandana, in sentences like याभी रेभं निवृतं सितं (*yābhī rebhaṃ nivṛtaṃ sitaṃ*). The same point is stated here.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> क्वचिदिति प्रश्नॆ । हे अश्विनौ आ मन्येथां । इमां मदीयां स्तुतिं जानीतं ।
> किंच एवैर्गमनसाधनैरश्वैरा गतं । यज्ञं प्रत्यागच्छतं । विश्वे सर्वॆ जनासः
> स्तोतारोऽश्विनाश्विन् वां युवां हवंते । स्तुतिलक्षणाभिर्वाग्निराह्वयंति । किंच
> गोऋजीका गवां पयसा मिश्रणोपेतानि मधूनि मदकराणि सोमरसरूपाणीमेमानि हवींषि युवाभ्यां प्र ददुः । अध्वर्यादयः प्रयच्छंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> मित्रासो न । यथा मित्राणि मित्रेभ्योऽपेक्षितं ददति तद्वत् । उस्रः । वसति नभसीत्युस्रः सूरः । अग्र उषसोऽग्र उदेति । तस्मादागच्छतमिति भावः ॥ ददुः । दाण्
> दान इत्यस्य लिट्युसि रूपं । हियोगादनिघातः । उस्रः । वस निवासे । स्थायितंबीत्यादिना रक् । कित्वात्संप्रसारणं । शासिवसिघसीनां चेति षत्वाभावश्चांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa takes कच्चित् (*kaccit*) as marking a question. "O Aśvins, आ मन्येथां (*ā manyethāṃ*): know this praise of mine." He adds: "come also with एवैः (*evaiḥ*), that is, with horses, the means of travel; come to the sacrifice." विश्वे जनासः (*viśve janāsaḥ*) are all the singers, who call you, Aśvins, with praises. Further, गोऋजीका (*goṛjīkā*) means "mixed with the milk of cows." मधूनि (*madhūni*) means "intoxicating," that is, these oblations in the form of Soma juice. The Adhvaryu and the others offer (प्र ददुः (*pra daduḥ*)) them to you. The simile is मित्रासो न (*mitrāso na*): as friends give their friends what they need. उस्रः (*usraḥ*) is the sun, who dwells in the sky. He rises ahead of the dawn. The sense is therefore: "come."
**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कच्चित् आ मन्येथाः (*kaccit ā manyethāḥ*)—if you regard our praise as good
- एवैः (*evaiḥ*)—with horses, the means of travel
- आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—come to our sacrifice
- विश्वे जनासः (*viśve janāsaḥ*)—all the singers too
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- हवंते (*havaṃte*)—call, praying
- गोऋजीका (*goṛjīkā*)—mixed with milk
- मधूनि (*madhūni*)—sweet, in the form of Soma juice
- इमा (*imā*)—these oblations
- मित्रासो न (*mitrāso na*)—as one gives lovingly to friends
- प्र ददुः (*pra daduḥ*)—offer to you
- उस्रः (*usraḥ*)—the sun
- अग्रे (*agre*)—has risen in front

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, if you regard our praise as good, come to our sacrifice with horses, the means of travel. All the singers too call you with prayer. They offer to you these oblations, mixed with milk and sweet, in the form of Soma juice, as one gives lovingly to friends. The sun has risen in front. Therefore be gracious to this sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
If you regard (my prayer), come with your quick steeds : all men, Ashwins, invoke you : to you they offer the sweet (Soma) juice mixed with milk, as friends (give gifts to friends) : the sun is in advance, (therefore come to the rite).

### Printed p. 425

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

एवैः (*evaiḥ*)—गमनसाधनैः (*gamanasādhanaiḥ*): "with horses that help in moving about." Ordinarily this epithet denotes the Maruts, the companions of Indra. Words such as एवासः (*evāsaḥ*) and एवयामरुत् (*evayāmarut*) describe the Maruts. But in a few places it is used as an epithet of horses, the means of travel. Moreover, in
सनाद्दिवं परि भूमा विरूपे पुनर्भुवा युवती स्वेभिरेवैः । (*sanāddivaṃ pari bhūmā virūpe punarbhuvā yuvatī svebhirevaiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62-8),
in the description that Night and Dawn move alternately by their own attractive, revolving comings and goings, the word means simply "going." Where the word is an epithet of the Maruts, its special sense has been explained earlier.

उस्रः (*usraḥ*)—वसति नभसीत्युस्रः सूर्यः (*vasati nabhasītyusraḥ sūryaḥ*): it is explained that the sun is named Usra because he dwells in the sky. In general it is hard to give a definite meaning for the words उस्रः (*usraḥ*), उस्रा (*usrā*), उस्रिया (*usriyā*) and उस्रिक (*usrika*); one must state it according to each context. In
द्रन्नो वन्वन् क्रत्वा नार्वोस्रः पितेव जारयायि यज्ञैः । (*dranno vanvan kratvā nārvosraḥ piteva jārayāyi yajñaiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-12-4)
the word usra is used as a synonym of "bull." Usra can also mean a sun-ray. The words उस्रा (*usrā*) and उस्प्रिया (*uspriyā*) also occur as synonyms of "milk."

> एवांगूषः । प्रज्ञादित्वात्स्वार्थिकोऽण् । प्रत्यॆयस्वरः । एह यातमित्यर्धर्चोगतः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Aśvins, eclipsing (तिरः (*tiraḥ*)) by your own splendour many (पुरू चित् (*purū cit*)) realms, that is, places, come here to this rite by the paths (पथिभिः (*pathibhiḥ*)) on which the gods travel. O opulent ones (मघवाना (*maghavānā*)), among the people, that is, among the singers, there is a praise (आंगूषः (*āṃgūṣaḥ*)) of you, to be recited all round. O Dasras, removers of enemies, these निधयः (*nidhayaḥ*) of yours are filled with intoxicating Soma." The निधयः (*nidhayaḥ*) are special vessels, so called because the Soma is deposited in them. Hence the sense: "come." Sāyaṇa derives अंगूषः (*aṃgūṣaḥ*) in two ways. By the second, the praise is so called because it goes (अंगति (*aṃgati*)) to the gods. He closes by saying that the half-verse एह यातं (*eha yātaṃ*) is complete.

- इह (*iha*)—to be in this rite
- देवयानैः (*devayānaiḥ*)—on which the gods travel
- पथिभिः (*pathibhiḥ*)—by paths
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—come
- मॆघवाना (*mèghavānā*)—O wealthy Aśvin deities
- जनेषु (*janeṣu*)—among the singers
- वां (*vāṃ*)—on your behalf
- अंगूषः (*aṃgūṣaḥ*)—the singer (is abundant)
- दसौ (*dasau*)—O Aśvin deities, destroyers of enemies
- वां (*vāṃ*)—meant for you
- मधूनां (*madhūnāṃ*)—filled with Soma
- इमे निधयः (*ime nidhayaḥ*)—these vessels are ready

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, you who pervade even many worlds with your splendour, come by the paths on which the gods travel, to take part in this rite. O wealthy Aśvins, among the singers the praise on your behalf is abundant. O Aśvins, destroyers of enemies, these vessels, meant for you and filled with Soma, are ready.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Eclipsing (by your splendour) many regions, Ashwins, (come hither); loud praise awaits you opulent (Ashwins) amongst men : come to this rite by the paths traversed by. the gods: here, Dasras, are ample stores of the exhilarating juices

### Printed p. 427

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The pervasive power of the Aśvins' splendour and the nature of the path on which they travel are described in this Ṛk. The nature of that path is described by देवयानैः पथिभिः (*devayānaiḥ pathibhiḥ*).

देवयानैः पथिभिः (*devayānaiḥ pathibhiḥ*)—The natures of the two paths, devayāna and pitṛyāna, were briefly explained earlier (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, Part 12, pp. 563-564). But since the two courses of the individual soul, bound to its actions, were there indicated only briefly and as the context required, some points not explained there are given here. The path by which gods travel from heaven to earth and from earth to heaven has been called devayāna from the time of the Vedic Saṃhitās. In the Brāhmaṇas and other Śruti and Smṛti texts, and in the works of the ancient and later poets who illumined secular literature, this word has a technical meaning. In the beginning, however, its real nature was not described so precisely, and only a gross picture was suggested by the technical word itself. In some Smṛti and other works this word is a synonym for the chariot, the vehicle of the gods. But this meaning is very secondary and does not show the established sense. That devayāna and pitṛyāna are, from the spiritual point of view, the higher and the lower path is a matter that can be learned exactly from the Upaniṣads and the like. It also suggests the belief that the soul which travels by devayāna to the excellent world of the Ādityas receives the full help of the gods. By descriptions such as परं मृत्यो अनु परे हि पंथां (*paraṃ mṛtyo anu pare hi paṃthāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-18-1), it is said to be a path free from death.

In the Ṛk Saṃhitā this path is described as connected with Agni, who creates the relation between gods and men. It is an established matter that he carries the sacrificial oblation to the gods and offers it, and also brings the gods themselves to the place of sacrifice and honours them. But for these tasks there is a definite path, and it is known to Agni alone.
अस्मे वत्सं परि षंतं न विंदन्निच्छंतो विश्वे अमृता अमूराः । श्रमयुवः पदव्यो धियंधास्तस्थुः पदे परमे चार्वग्नेः । (*asme vatsaṃ pari ṣaṃtaṃ na viṃdannicchaṃto viśve amṛtā amūrāḥ | śramayuvaḥ padavyo dhiyaṃdhāstasthuḥ pade parame cārvagneḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-2)
"O Agni, you know the path on which the gods travel, and you are their messenger. To carry their oblation, the gods and the others, desiring your help, knew the highest place in which you are and the path to your world; yet they did not see you alone, and they stood in your world."

### Printed p. 428

In the beginning, the path on which Agni, carrying the oblation, travels became known in the end as the path on which the sacrificer, the performer of the sacrifice, also travels.
स एष देवयानो वा पितृयाणो वा पंथाः । तदुभयतोऽग्निशिखे समोषंत्यौ तिष्ठतः प्रति तमोषतो यः प्रत्युष्योऽत्युतग्ं सृजेते योऽतिसृज्यः शांतिरापस्तदेतमवैतत्पंथानग्ं शमयति ॥ (*sa eṣa devayāno vā pitṛyāṇo vā paṃthāḥ | tadubhayato 'gniśikhe samoṣaṃtyau tiṣṭhataḥ prati tamoṣato yaḥ pratyuṣyo 'tyutagṃ sṛjete yo 'tisṛjyaḥ śāṃtirāpastadetamavaitatpaṃthānagṃ śamayati ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 1-9-3-2)
The path that carries either to the world of the gods or to the world of the fathers is one. On both sides of this common path two flames burn steadily. They do not harm the doer of good but make room for his passage; the doer of evil they burn. Therefore
यत्रासते सुकृतो यत्र ते ययुस्तत्र त्वा देवःस विता दधातु (*yatrāsate sukṛto yatra te yayustatra tvā devaḥsa vitā dadhātu*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 18-17-4).
**NOTE**
Since Savitṛ is the god who leads the doers of good on the good path, he is prayed to lead the sacrificers, the doers of good, on that same pure path, free from dust and free from death.

Thus one description is that a single path leads to both the world of the gods and the world of the fathers, and that the easy way on it accords with each person's actions. Another kind is the description in which the two paths are given separately: one the path of the doers of good, the other the path of those without that. But there is one main point to be noticed here: in the Ṛk Saṃhitā passage सुकृतो यत्र ते (*sukṛto yatra te*) good action is praised. What is that good action? Is it only the performance of sacrifice, or is there something else? The answer is: if a man is without knowledge and merely a performer of sacrifice, he has no entry to devayāna; the man of knowledge has entry. But the rule that he must also be a performer of sacrifice is not clearly stated. Then who has the right to enter devayāna? For now, the question of that right and its answer are not relevant to us. Who is such a person, and what the nature of his action should be, will be explained later as the context permits. In the present context only the description of the path is relevant. So one must understand what is the nature of the path on which the gods travel or which the doer of good follows, and what is the nature of the path on which the one without it travels. One must also understand whether the devayāna on which the Aśvins are to travel in this Ṛk is described in the Upaniṣads and the like just as it is in the Ṛk Saṃhitā and the like.

Earlier, when explaining the path of Ṛta, the nature of the paths well known in the Ṛk Saṃhitā, the path of the Ādityas, the path of the Gandharvas and the path of the gods, was explained with examples. That is described as an eternal

### Printed p. 429

and steady path. Although some points show that the account of the path in the Upaniṣads and the like differs from it in many ways, it can be said that the reality described in both settings is the same. This path of the gods is described thus in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad:
ये चेमेऽरण्ये श्रद्धा तप इत्युपासते तेऽर्चिषमभिसंभवंत्यर्चिषाहरह्न आपूर‍्यमाणपक्षमापूर‍्यमाणपक्षाद्यान्नडुदजेति मासांस्तान् । मासेभ्यः संवत्सरं संवत्सरादादित्यमादित्याच्चंद्रमसं चंद्रमसो विद्युतं तत्पुरुषोऽमानवः स एनान्ब्रह्म गमयत्येष देवयानः पंथा इति ॥ (*ye ceme 'raṇye śraddhā tapa ityupāsate te 'rciṣamabhisaṃbhavaṃtyarciṣāharahna āpūryamāṇapakṣamāpūryamāṇapakṣādyānnaḍudajeti māsāṃstān | māsebhyaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ saṃvatsarādādityamādityāccaṃdramasaṃ caṃdramaso vidyutaṃ tatpuruṣo 'mānavaḥ sa enānbrahma gamayatyeṣa devayānaḥ paṃthā iti ‖*)
(Bhā. U. 5-10-1, 2)
**NOTE**
Those who, knowing the fire-knowledge, practise austerity joined with faith enter the flame. (This is the sun's ray in the form of fire, in the flame of the funeral pyre.) From this flame, which is of the nature of light, they enter the day; from the day, the bright fortnight; from the bright fortnight, the uttarāyaṇa, the northern course of the sun; from there, the year; from the year, the world of the Ādityas; from there, the moon-world, other than it; from there, the world of lightning. This is devayāna.
अथ य इमे ग्राम इष्टापूर्ते दत्तमित्युपासते ते धूममभिसंभवंति धूमाद्रात्रिं रात्रेरपरपक्षमपरपक्षाद्यान्नड्डक्षिणैतिमासांस्तान्नैते संवत्सरमभिप्राप्रुवंति मासेभ्यः पितृलोकं पितृलोकादाकाशं .... .... तं देवा भक्षयंति । (*atha ya ime grāma iṣṭāpūrte dattamityupāsate te dhūmamabhisaṃbhavaṃti dhūmādrātriṃ rātreraparapakṣamaparapakṣādyānnaḍḍakṣiṇaitimāsāṃstānnaite saṃvatsaramabhiprāpruvaṃti māsebhyaḥ pitṛlokaṃ pitṛlokādākāśaṃ .... .... taṃ devā bhakṣayaṃti |*)
(Bhā. U. 5-10-3, 4)
Those who live in villages and, placing faith in sacrificial action done for desire, perform the action, enter the smoke. From the smoke they enter the night, full of darkness; from the night, the dark fortnight; from the dark fortnight, the dakṣiṇāyana; from the dakṣiṇāyana, the year; from there, the world of the fathers; from there, the sky; and through it, the world of the Moon (Soma). Since Soma is food for the gods, they eat it. The same description, slightly varied, is given in the same way in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad also (6-2-15). In the account of pitṛyāna the sky is not included. Moreover,
अणुः पंथा विततः पुराणो मां स्पषोऽनुवित्तो मय्येव । तेन धीरा अपियंति ब्रह्मविदः स्वर्ग० लोकमित ऊर्ध्वं विमुक्ताः ॥ (*aṇuḥ paṃthā vitataḥ purāṇo māṃ spaṣo 'nuvitto mayyeva | tena dhīrā apiyaṃti brahmavidaḥ svarga0 lokamita ūrdhvaṃ vimuktāḥ ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 4-4-8)

### Printed p. 430
This subtle path is eternal and ancient. By this path the knowers of the Veda, becoming liberated, enter the world of heaven. And further,

तस्मिञ्चुक्लमुत नीलमाहुः पिंगलं हरितं लोहितं च । एष पंथा ब्रह्मणा हानुवित्तस्तेनैति ब्रह्मवित्पुण्यकृत्यैजसश्च ॥ (*tasmiñcuklamuta nīlamāhuḥ piṃgalaṃ haritaṃ lohitaṃ ca | eṣa paṃthā brahmaṇā hānuvittastenaiti brahmavitpuṇyakṛtyaijasaśca ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 4-4-9)

This path is famed for a mixture of colours and is highly attractive. White, blue, tawny, green and red all combine to make a delightful path. The description of its nature says that the knower of Brahman and the one who does meritorious deeds travel by this radiant path alone.

Another point must be noted in this context. Earlier, in explaining the phrase तिस्रो महीरुपरास्तस्थुः (*tisro mahīruparāstasthuḥ*) in the second Ṛk of Sūkta 56 of this same chapter, it was explained that the Saṃhitā passages themselves make known that there is no world other than the world of Āditya, which is the highest and best of the worlds. But in the Chāndogya, here cited, the description runs: the world of Āditya, beyond it the world of the Moon, and beyond that the world of lightning. The Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad has one more distinctive feature:

स एवं देवयानं पंथानमापद्याग्निलोकमागच्छति स वायुलोकं स आदित्यलोकं स वरुणलोकं स इंद्रलोकं स प्रजापतिलोकं स ब्रह्मलोकं ॥ (*sa evaṃ devayānaṃ paṃthānamāpadyāgnilokamāgacchati sa vāyulokaṃ sa ādityalokaṃ sa varuṇalokaṃ sa iṃdralokaṃ sa prajāpatilokaṃ sa brahmalokaṃ ‖*) (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 1-3)

The doer of good, having thus entered the path of the gods, comes from there in order to the world of Vāyu, then the world of Āditya, the world of Varuṇa, the world of Indra, the world of Prajāpati, and finally the world of Brahman; so he reaches the world of Brahman, the supreme principle. No scriptural basis can be named for this kind of division. There are many differing points between it and the description of the worlds in the Ṛk Saṃhitā.

सूर्यद्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयांति यत्रामृतः स पुरुषो ह्यव्ययात्मा । (*sūryadvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayāṃti yatrāmṛtaḥ sa puruṣo hyavyayātmā |*) (Mu. U. 1-1)

This description of the door of the sun agrees with the description of the Ṛk Saṃhitā. The path called the Gandharva path, spoken of in the Ṛk अग्निर्गांधर्विं पथ्यां (*agnirgāṃdharviṃ pathyāṃ*) (10-80-6), is to be understood here as the path of the gods, the Devayāna, on which the Aśvins travel. Among the worlds indicated in the present Ṛk, this path of the Devayāna is only one part. Therefore

### Printed p. 431
the other, still more extensive worlds are also indicated by पुरू चित् रजांसि (*purū cit rajāṃsi*). What the nature of those worlds may be according to the Ṛk Saṃhitā has been stated earlier.

रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)—Uses of this word in many senses, such as the delightful heaven, light, water and the atmosphere, were stated earlier (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 2, pp. 57-59).

आंगूषः (*āṃgūṣaḥ*)—आंगूषस्तोम आघोषः (*āṃgūṣastoma āghoṣaḥ*) (Ni. 5-11): a hymn to be recited aloud is called āṅgūṣa.

> *purāṇaṃ | okaḥ | sakhyaṃ | śivaṃ | vāṃ | yuvoḥ | narā | draviṇaṃ | jahnāvyāṃ |*

> विकल्पेन याज्याः । सूत्रितं च । यदि नाधीयात्पुराणमोकः सख्यं शिवं वामिति
> चतस्रो याज्याः ! आ. ९-११ । इति ॥
> हे अश्विनौ वां युवयोः पुराणं पुरातनं सख्यमोकः सेव्यं शिवं कल्याणकरं भवति । किंच हे नरा नरावस्मदीय कर्मणो नेतारौ युवोर्युवयोर्द्रविणं धनं जह्नाव्यां जह्नु कुलजायां भवति। शिवानि सुखकराणि युवयोः सख्यानि

> संतो वयं मध्वा मदकरेण सोमेन युवां सह युगपत् नु क्षिप्रं मदेम ।
> हर्षयेम ॥ सख्यं । सख्युर्भाव इत्यर्थे सख्युर्य इति यत्पत्ययः । जह्नाव्यां ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Aptoryāma sacrifice, in the Acchāvāka's śastra of the atirikta-ukthya, the four Ṛks beginning पुराणमोकः (*purāṇamokaḥ*) are alternatively yājyā verses. It is also given in a sūtra: यदि नाधीयात्पुराणमोकः सख्यं शिवं वामिति चतस्रो याज्याः (*yadi nādhīyātpurāṇamokaḥ sakhyaṃ śivaṃ vāmiti catasro yājyāḥ*) (Ā. 9-11).
O Aśvins, your ancient friendship is an abode, to be resorted to, and auspicious, bringing welfare. And further, O leaders, guides of our rite, your wealth is in the woman of Jahnu's family (Jahnāvī). Renewing your friendly bonds, which bring happiness, we, being alike, made friends and one through the benefit of offering oblations, shall delight you both together, quickly, with the intoxicating Soma. [The block goes on with the grammar of सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*) and the beginning of जह्नाव्यां (*jahnāvyāṃ*); it is omitted here.]

### Printed p. 432

> जह्नोः संबंधिनीत्यर्थे तस्येदमित्यण् । ओर्गुणः । ह्रस्वदीर्घयोर्व्यत्ययः ।
> मदेनु । मदी हर्ष इत्यस्याशीर्लिज् लिज्याशिष्यज् प्रत्ययः । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

जह्नाव्यां (*jahnāvyāṃ*) means "belonging to Jahnu", and मदेम (*madema*) is from the root मदी (*madī*) in the sense of rejoicing. The rest is grammatical and is left to the Grammar section.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Aśvins) वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- पुराणं (*purāṇaṃ*)—ancient
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—friendship
- ओकः (*okaḥ*)—worthy to be resorted to
- शिवं (*śivaṃ*)—bringing welfare
- नरा (*narā*)—leaders of the rite
- युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—your
- द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)—wealth
- जह्नाव्यां (*jahnāvyāṃ*)—is filled in the Jahnu family
- शिवानि (*śivāni*)—bringing happiness
- सख्या (*sakhyā*)—your friendship
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- कृष्णानाः (*kṛṣṇānāḥ*)—doing
- समानाः (*samānāḥ*)—we who are one with you (through friendship)
- मध्वा (*madhvā*)—with the sweet Soma juice
- सह (*saha*)—together
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- मदेम (*madema*)—we shall gladden (you)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, your ancient friendship is worthy to be resorted to and brings welfare. Your wealth, O leaders of the rite, is filled in the Jahnu family. We, who renew your happiness-bringing friendship and are one with you, shall quickly delight you both together with the sweet Soma juice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Your ancient friendship is desirable and auspicious; your wealth, leaders (of rites), is in the family of Jahnu : renewing that auspicious friend- ship, may we, your associates, delight you with the sweet (Soma juice).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

These four Ṛks of this sūkta beginning पुराणमोकः (*purāṇamokaḥ*) (Ṛks 6, 7, 8, 9 of this sūkta), at the time of reciting the atirikta-ukthya mantras of the sacrifice called Aptoryāma, when the priest called Acchāvāka recites the śastra mantras, may alternatively be recited as yājyā mantras. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra यदि नाधीयात्पुराणमोकः सख्यं शिवं वामिति चतस्रो याज्याः (*yadi nādhīyātpurāṇamokaḥ sakhyaṃ śivaṃ vāmiti catasro yājyāḥ*) (Ā. 9-11).
ओकः (*okaḥ*)—सेव्यं (*sevyaṃ*): worthy of being resorted to. This is a word describing the friendship of the Aśvins. Ordinarily the word ओकः (*okaḥ*) means a comfortable dwelling-place. The Nirukta says: ओक इति निवासनामोच्यते । (*oka iti nivāsanāmocyate |*) (Ni. 3-3). The author of the Nirukta explains with an example that this word also indicates the extreme affection attached to that dwelling. (Ni. 3-3)

### Printed p. 433
अथ स ओकः पुनरेव तदेति यत आगतो भवति । (*atha sa okaḥ punareva tadeti yata āgato bhavati |*) Because an adopted son feels attachment to his own home and returns there again, ओकः (*okaḥ*) is a synonym for one's own home.
The Nirukta author cites the Ṛk Saṃhitā passage

अधा चिदोकः पुनरित्स एत्या नो वाज्यभीषाळेतु नव्यः । (*adhā cidokaḥ punaritsa etyā no vājyabhīṣāḷetu navyaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-4-8)

and shows that the above meaning is made plain in this passage. The sense is that the comfort found in one's own home is found also in friendship with the Aśvins. The epithet शिव (*śiva*) is there to show that this same friendship is also auspicious.
जह्नाव्यां (*jahnāvyāṃ*)—जह्नु कुलजायां (*jahnu kulajāyāṃ*). The sense is that all the wealth of the Aśvins is filled in the Jahnu family. This word, indicating a lineage, is used in two places in the Ṛk Saṃhitā. Earlier, in

आ जह्नावीं समनसोप वाजैस्त्रिरहो भागं दधतीमयातं । (*ā jahnāvīṃ samanasopa vājaistriraho bhāgaṃ dadhatīmayātaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-19)

too the prayer is addressed to the Aśvins: it prays that the Aśvins favour the people born in the Jahnu family. In the present Ṛk also Viśvāmitra, born in the Jahnu family, praises the Aśvins. The power of this same Viśvāmitra is described in many places. The Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa praises him: Viśvāmitra of the Jahnu line, by his own strength and by performing the sattra called Jātūrātra and so increasing his power, helped the Jāhnavas who were fighting the Vṛjīvants and won the kingdom for them. (Pa. Brā. 21-12) **NOTE**

अधीयत देवरातो रिक्षयोरुभयोर्यषिः । जह्नूनां चाधिपत्ये दैवे वेदे च गाथिनां ॥ (*adhīyata devarāto rikṣayorubhayoryaṣiḥ | jahnūnāṃ cādhipatye daive vede ca gāthināṃ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 33-18)

The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa names this lineage thus: Śunaḥśepa, famed as Devarāta, became lord of the kingdom of the Jahnus and the Gādhis. It is the view of scholars that these names cannot denote different lineages. Some scholars hold that the Gādhi line also belongs to, and is included in, the Jāhnavī descent; this may be called a sound view. Here it is natural that Viśvāmitra, born in the Jahnu line, should praise the power of his own line.

#### Ṛk 7

> अश्वि॑ना वा॒युना॑ यु॒वं सु॑दक्षा नि॒युद्धि॑श्च स॒जोष॑सा  
> युवाना ।  
> नास॑त्या ति॒रोअ॑ह्न्यं जुषा॒णा सोमं॑ पिबतम॒स्रिधा॑  
> सुदानू ॥ ७ ॥

> *aśvinā vāyunā yuvaṃ sudakṣā niyuddhiśca sajoṣasā*  
> *yuvānā |*  
> *nāsatyā tiroahnyaṃ juṣāṇā somaṃ pibatamasridhā*  
> *sudānū ‖ 7 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अश्विना । वायुना । युवं । सुदक्षा । नियुद्धिः । च । सजोषसा । युवाना ।  
> नासत्या । तिरोअह्न्यं । जुषाणा । सोमं । पिबतं । अस्त्रिधा । सुदानू इति  
> सुदानू ॥ ७ ॥

> *aśvinā | vāyunā | yuvaṃ | sudakṣā | niyuddhiḥ | ca | sajoṣasā | yuvānā |*  
> *nāsatyā | tiroahnyaṃ | juṣāṇā | somaṃ | pibataṃ | astridhā | sudānū iti*  
> *sudānū ‖ 7 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुदक्षा शोभनसामर्थ्योपेत् युवाना नित्यतरुण् नासत्या । न विद्यतेऽसत्यं ययोस्त् । सुदानू शोभनफलस्य दातारौ हे अश्विनौ वायुना नियुद्धिरश्चैश्च सजोषसा संगतौ जुषाणा सोमविषयप्रीतियुक्तावस्त्रिधानुपक्षीणौ युवं
> युवां तिरोअह्न्यमहि तिरोहिते हूयमानमिमं सोमं पिबतं ॥ नियुद्धिः ।
> यौतेः क्विप् । तिरोअह्न्यं । अह्नि भवमह्न्यं । भवे छंदसीति यत् । तिरो भूतमह्न्यं यस्मिन्काले स तिरोअह्न्यः । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, सुदक्षा (*sudakṣā*) endowed with fine capacity, युवाना (*yuvānā*) ever young, नासत्या (*nāsatyā*) those in whom there is no untruth (न विद्यतेऽसत्यं (*na vidyate 'satyaṃ*) yayoḥ), सुदानू (*sudānū*) givers of good reward: united with Vāyu and with the Niyut horses, सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*) in company, जुषाणा (*juṣāṇā*) joyful about the Soma, अस्त्रिधा (*astridhā*) undiminished, you both drink this Soma that is offered at the तिरोअह्न्यं (*tiroahnyaṃ*) time, when the day has passed. [Grammar of नियुद्धिः (*niyuddhiḥ*) and तिरोअह्न्यं (*tiroahnyaṃ*) follows in the block and is left to the Grammar section.] **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुदक्षा (*sudakṣā*)—endowed with excellent capacity
- युवाना (*yuvānā*)—ever young
- नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—of true nature
- सुदानू (*sudānū*)—excellent givers, O Aśvins
- वायुना (*vāyunā*)—with Vāyu
- नियुद्धिः च (*niyuddhiḥ ca*)—and with their horses
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—united
- आस्प्रिधा (*āspridhā*)—undiminished
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- तिरोअह्न्यं (*tiroahnyaṃ*)—pressed at the end of the day
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—this Soma juice
- पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, endowed with excellent capacity, ever young, of true nature, excellent givers: you two, united with Vāyu and with the horses, and undiminished, drink this Soma juice pressed at the end of the day.

### Printed p. 435

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Ashwins, endowed with power, ever young, in whom is no untruth, unwearied, munificent, accepters (of libations), drink with Vayu and your steeds, rejoicing together, of the Soma libation offered at the close of day.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—The authors of the Nirukta gave an etymology of this word, and the meaning was explained earlier. The view of Aurṇavābha, who says it means "free from untruth", was also given. But according to some others another etymology is possible: नाक-सत्या (*nāka-satyā*), that is, those who are in heaven. Just as the word भास्कर (*bhāskara*), meaning light, becomes बाकुर (*bākura*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-1-8), and the word कर्मकार (*karmakāra*) becomes कर्मार (*karmāra*) (10-72-2), so नाक-सत्या (*nāka-satyā*) may become नासत्या (*nāsatyā*). Moreover, this view points out that the etymology agrees with the description of the Aśvins as sons of the heavenly world in Ṛks such as दिवो नपाताश्विना हुवे वां (*divo napātāśvinā huve vāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-61-4).
अस्त्रिधा (*astridhā*)—The root स्त्रिध् (*stridh*) is used in the two senses "to err" and "to perish". Hence अस्त्रिधा (*astridhā*) may mean "always going the right way", or "free from destruction". As said in many places, such as उदूहथुरणसो अस्त्रिधानैः (*udūhathuraṇaso astridhānaiḥ*), it is proper to give the meaning "free from destruction" in the present Ṛk also.

> सद्यस्तदानीमेव परि याति ह । सर्वतः प्राप्नोति खलु । अश्विनो रथस्य वेगवत्त्वे
> मंत्रवर्णः । यो वामश्विना मनसा जवीयान्रथः स्वश्वो विश आजिगाति । ऋग्वे.
> १-११७-२ । इति । अतः कारणादस्मदीयं यज्ञं प्रत्यागच्छतमिति भावः ॥ ईयुः । इण्
> गतावित्यस्य लिटि दीर्घ इणः कितीत्यभ्यासस्य दीर्घः । पादादित्पादनिघातः । यतमानाः ।
> यती प्रयत्न इत्यस्य शानचि रूपं । शपः पित्वादनुदात्तत्वे शानचो लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । ऋतजाः । जनेर्विट् । विड्वनोरित्यात्वं । अद्रिजूतः ।
> जू इति सौत्रो धातुः । कर्मणि क्तः । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Ashvins! The many (पुरूचीः (*purūcīḥ*), those that go forward) इषः (*iṣaḥ*), foods in the form of oblations, move round about you. So too the worshippers, unrebuked by anyone (अमृध्राः (*amṛdhrāḥ*)) and striving (यतमानाः (*yatamānāḥ*)) in the rite, attend you with their praise-words (गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)). ऋतजा (*ṛtajā*) is the begetter of ṛta, that is, of water; or it is that which comes into being in the ṛta, the sacrifice. अद्रिजूतः (*adrijūtaḥ*) means drawn by the worshippers. Your chariot goes round heaven and earth at once, instantly; it reaches everywhere." For the speed of the Ashvins' chariot he cites a mantra: "Ashvins, the chariot of yours that is swifter than thought, with good horses, comes to the peoples" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-2). Therefore, he says, the sense is: come to our sacrifice.

The rest of the block is grammar (īyuḥ, yatamānāḥ, ṛtajāḥ, adrijūtaḥ), which the Grammar section carries.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरूचीः (*purūcīḥ*)—very abundant
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods in the form of oblations
- वां परि (*vāṃ pari*)—towards you
- ईयुः (*īyuḥ*)—approach
- अमृध्राः (*amṛdhrāḥ*)—the blameless
- यतमानाः (*yatamānāḥ*)—those engaged in the rite, the worshippers
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with their praises (they serve)
- ऋतजाः (*ṛtajāḥ*)—that which sheds water in the form of rain
- अद्रिजूतः (*adrijūtaḥ*)—that which is drawn by praises
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- रथः (*rathaḥ*)—chariot
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at once
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- परि याति ह (*pari yāti ha*)—pervades, does it not

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ashvins, very abundant foods in the form of oblations are offered towards you. The blameless worshippers, engaged in the rite, serve you with their praises. Your chariot, which sheds water in the form of rain and is drawn by the worshippers, at once pervades heaven and earth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Ashwins, abundant (sacrificial) viands are presented to you, and blameless worshippers (salute you) with praises : your water-shedding car, attracted by the sacrificers, quickly compasses earth and heaven.

### Printed p. 437

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Purūcī: this word is formed from the root añc, of the sense of going, joined with the word puru. It is used to express a very great quantity or a multitude in number. Here it is an adjective of इषः (*iṣaḥ*).

Amṛdhrāḥ: the word mṛdhra means contempt; amṛdhra is that which lacks it. It is an adjective of the worshippers; the purport is "those who are scorned by no one".

Ṛtajāḥ: if ṛta is taken here to mean water, the word means "that which produces water". This word is an adjective of the chariot of the Ashvins. That the chariot of the Ashvins is a cause of the creation of water is perhaps nowhere to be found; yet what Sāyaṇa has explained is not without basis. Since there is the description "your chariot at once pervades heaven and earth" (नां रथः सद्यः द्यावा पृथिवी परि याति (*nāṃ rathaḥ sadyaḥ dyāvā pṛthivī pari yāti*)), and since there is also one view that the Ashvins are themselves heaven and earth, on that basis their chariot may be called a means of rain. It was said earlier, in the form of a story, that the union of heaven and earth is the cause of rain. Or one may infer that when rain falls, these two are united. The sentence कौ वैतां नावर्षं (*kau vaitāṃ nāvarṣaṃ*) (Ai. Brā. 4-27) was cited earlier: if they are separated there is no fall of rain at all. Hence it may be said that the chariot of the Ashvins, who are themselves of the form of heaven and earth, became also the cause of the fall of rain. Sāyaṇa has explained ऋतस्य उदकस्य जनयिता (*ṛtasya udakasya janayitā*). Or, as another explanation, ऋते यज्ञॆ प्रादुर्भवतीति वा (*ṛte yajñè prādurbhavatīti vā*), "that which is born in the sacrifice". What the basis of this explanation is cannot be said.

Adrijūtaḥ: स्तोतृभिराकृष्टः (*stotṛbhirākṛṣṭaḥ*), meaning "drawn by the worshippers". For this word the scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit-English Dictionary, gives "Excited by the friction of Stones", that is, impelled by the rubbing of stones, meaning pressed out, and cites this very Ṛk. This meaning too cannot be called unsound. If the two words ṛtajāḥ and adrijūtaḥ are taken as synonyms of the Soma juice, the sense is that the Soma juice is produced for the sacrifice and is crushed and pressed out with stones. To state the purport thus is more fitting to the context than Sāyaṇa's explanation. To fit the purport to this Ṛk as Sāyaṇa explains it is rather laborious work.

> इत्यर्थः । तमिमं सोमं पातं । पिबतं । दुरोणेऽस्माकं गृह आ गतं । आगच्छतं।

> निरित्येष समित्येतस्य स्थाने । नि. १२-७ । इति यास्कः । संस्कारि । यद्वा । संस्कृतं गृहमागमिष्ठोऽतिशयेनागच्छन् भवति ॥ युवाकुः । यातेः कटिकुषिभ्यां काकुरिति
> बाहुलकादस्मादपि भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण मध्योदात्तः । करिक्रत् । करोतेर्यज्लुकि
> शतरि दाधर्ति दर्धर्ति दर्धर्षित्यादिना चुत्वाभावे यणादेशे कृतेऽंगस्यानृकारांतत्पादभ्यासस्य रिगागमो न प्राप्नोतीति सोऽपि निपात्यते ॥ अभ्यस्तस्वरः । निष्कृतं ।
> करोतेरादिकर्मणि क्तः । संस्कर्तुं प्रवृक्त इत्यर्थः । थाथादिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Ashvins! The Soma that is मधुषुत्तमो (*madhuṣuttamo*), sending forth sweet juice to the utmost, is युवाकुः (*yuvākuḥ*), desiring you; or else युवाकुः (*yuvākuḥ*) means mixed with vasatīvarī waters and the like. Drink (पातं (*pātaṃ*)) this Soma and come (आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)) to our house (दुरोणे (*duroṇe*)). भूरि (*bhūri*) is abundant; वर्पः (*varpaḥ*) is protecting brilliance, or form, or wealth to be chosen by all. Your chariot, करिक्रत् (*karikrat*), producing this again and again, is आगमिष्ठः (*āgamiṣṭhaḥ*), most coming, to the निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*) of the offerer who has pressed the Soma." Here निः (*niḥ*) stands in place of सम् (*sam*), according to Yāska (Ni. 12-7); निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*) is thus the prepared, refined place. Or: the chariot comes most surely to the house that has been prepared. The remainder (युवाकुः (*yuvākuḥ*), करिक्रत् (*karikrat*), निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*): formation and accent) is grammar. **NOTE**

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Ashvins
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—this Soma
- मधषुत्तमः (*madhaṣuttamaḥ*)—full of sweet juice **NOTE**
- युवाकुः (*yuvākuḥ*)—desiring you
- तं (*taṃ*)—this Soma
- पातं (*pātaṃ*)—drink
- दुरोणे (*duroṇe*)—to our house
- आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—come
- भूरि (*bhūri*)—abundant
- वर्पः (*varpaḥ*)—brilliance
- करिक्रत् (*karikrat*)—making it spread again and again
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- रथः (*rathaḥ*)—chariot
- सुतवर्तः (*sutavartaḥ*)—of the sacrificer who has pressed the Soma juice **NOTE**
- निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*)—to the sacrificial house
- आगमिष्ठः (*āgamiṣṭhaḥ*)—may it come

### Printed p. 439

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ashvins, this Soma is full of sweet juice and desires you. Drink this Soma. Come to our house. May your chariot, which is abundant and makes its brilliance spread again and again, come to the sacrificial house of the sacrificer who has pressed the Soma juice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Ashwins, this most sweet Soma is mixed ; drink it : come to (our) dwelling: your car, repeatedly bestowing wealth, is coming to the appointed place of the offerer of the libation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Duroṇe: this word is read among the names of houses (Ni. 3-13). It means a dwelling-house. But in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā it is generally used in the sense of the sacrificial house.

Varpaḥ: this word is read among the names of form (Ni. 3-7). In this word beauty and radiance are suggested together. The word is used when describing a form that is full of lustre and attractive.

In the present Ṛk two or three explanations of the meaning of this word are given: वर्षः वारकं तेजः, रूपं वा, सर्वै: वरणीयं धनं वा (*varṣaḥ vārakaṃ tejaḥ, rūpaṃ vā, sarvai: varaṇīyaṃ dhanaṃ vā*). It is indicated that it may mean brilliance, or form, or wealth desired by all.

The sentence भूरि वर्षः करिक्रत् (*bhūri varṣaḥ karikrat*) shows that two kinds of meaning are possible for the word varṣa. Karikrat means making something spread again and again; bhūri means very abundant. If the meaning given is that the chariot of the Ashvins makes brilliance spread again and again, taking varṣa as brilliance, then, since the chariot of the Ashvins is itself full of brilliance, its brilliance spreads whenever that chariot comes to the sacrificial house: this is one kind of purport. Secondly, since however many times their chariot comes the sacrificer's prosperity increases, भूरि वर्षः करिक्रत् (*bhūri varṣaḥ karikrat*) also fits when the meaning is given in terms of wealth. But to say that it means the radiant form, which is the established sense of the word varṣa, is proper in the present context. [Karikrata is also the name of the seer of the mantra 10-136-5.]

Niṣkṛta: this word is used in the sense of a house. As to how this purport is obtained, the author of the Nirukta has given its explanation and illustrated it with an example.

### Printed p. 440
निरित्येष समित्येतस्य स्थाने (*nirityeṣa samityetasya sthāne*) (Ni. 12-2). The prefix niḥ is used in the sense of sam. Saṃskṛta means a place that has been refined. But "refined" here may be an arrangement made so that a dwelling-place is a place of assignation and secret. The author of the Nirukta, citing the Ṛk यदादीध्ये न दविषाण्येभिः परायध्योऽव हीये सखिभ्यः । न्युप्ताश्च बभ्रवो वाचमक्रत्र एमीदेषां निष्कृतं जारिणीव ॥ (*yadādīdhye na daviṣāṇyebhiḥ parāyadhyo 'va hīye sakhibhyaḥ | nyuptāśca babhravo vācamakratra emīdeṣāṃ niṣkṛtaṃ jāriṇīva ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-34-) **NOTE**, has shown that there the word niṣkṛta means a place of tryst. A woman of loose conduct going to the niṣkṛta and joining him means going to a secret place and meeting him.

But this purport is not found everywhere. A refined house may also mean the preparations made for sacrifices and the like. In the present context it means the sacrificial house of the sacrificer.

## Sūkta 59 (Maṇḍala 3)
The fifty-ninth sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मित्रो जनानिति नवर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं त्रैष्टुभं मैत्रं । मित्रो
> मैत्रं चतुर्गायत्र्यंतमित्यनुक्रमणिका । आदितः पंच त्रिष्टुभः शिष्टाश्चतस्रो
> गायत्र्यः । मित्रो देवता ॥ अग्निहोत्रार्थे पयसि वर्षविंदुपतने मित्रो जनानित्यनया समिधमादध्यात् । सूत्रितं च । मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाण इति समिदाधानं । आ. ३-११ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning मित्रो जनान् (*mitro janān*) has nine ṛks and is the sixth sūkta; its seer is Viśvāmitra, its metre is triṣṭubh, and it is addressed to Mitra. The Anukramaṇikā says: मित्रो मैत्रं चतुर्गायत्र्यंतं (*mitro maitraṃ caturgāyatryaṃtaṃ*). The first five ṛks are triṣṭubh, the remaining four gāyatrī; the deity is Mitra. Use: when, in the milk drawn for the agnihotra, drops of rain fall, one should place a fuel-stick (samidh) on the fire with this ṛk मित्रो जनान् (*mitro janān*). It is also laid down in the sūtra: मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाण इति समिदाधानं (*mitro janānyātayati bruvāṇa iti samidādhānaṃ*) (Ā. 3-11). **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, "Mitro janān", is the sixth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It contains nine ṛks. Viśvāmitra is the seer of this sūkta; Mitra is the deity; the metre is triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: मित्रो मैत्रं चतुर्गायत्र्यंतं (*mitro maitraṃ caturgāyatryaṃtaṃ*). In this sūkta the first five ṛks are in the triṣṭubh metre; the remaining four ṛks are in the gāyatrī metre; Mitra is the deity. It is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाण इति समिदाधानं (*mitro janānyātayati bruvāṇa iti samidādhānaṃ*) (Ā. 3-21), that when, while milking for the agnihotra, drops of rain fall in the milk, a samidh-offering should be made in the fire with the ṛk "Mitro janān".
