> शोभनेन कर्मणा च विष्ट्वी व्याप्यामृतत्वमेरिरे । देवत्वं प्रापुः । तथा च

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Ṛbhus, "grandsons of Manu" (manor napātaḥ), are the sons of the man Aṅgiras, and are apasaḥ, that is, possessed of work such as sacrifice. They fully attained (समानशुः (*samānaśuḥ*), "rightly obtained") Indra's friendship, that is, equal renown. Having attained Indra's friendship, those Ṛbhus दधन्विरे (*dadhanvire*) (dadhanvire): though formerly, being human, liable to die, they now sustain their lives through Indra's friendship. So a mantra: आधारयंत वह्नयः (*ādhārayaṃta vahnayaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-20-8). The Saudhanvanas, the Ṛbhus, sons of the seer named Sudhanvan, being doers of good works, by abundant works that are the means of removing the obstacles to the attainment of godhood, and by good work, pervading (the world), attained immortality, that is, godhood. And so

### Printed p. 497

> मंत्रांतरमाव्नायते । मर्तासः संतो अमृतत्वमानशुः । ऋग्वे. १-११०-४ । इति॥
> नपातः । नभ्राण्नपादित्यादिना नञ्ञः प्रकृतिभावः । दधन्विरे । धनिर्गत्यर्थः । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । लिटि रूपं । ईरिरे । ईर गत् । मंत्रत्वादाम्न भवति । निघातः ।
> सुकृत्यया । करोतेर्भावे कृञ्ञः श चेति क्यप् । प्रत्ययस्य व्यत्ययेनांतोदात्तत्वं । समासे कृदुत्तरस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Another mantra is handed down: मर्तासः संतो अमृतत्वमानशुः (*martāsaḥ saṃto amṛtatvamānaśuḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-110-4). The rest of the block treats the accent and formation of napātaḥ, dadhanvire, īrire and sukṛtyayā.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनोः (*manoḥ*)—of the human Aṅgiras
- नपातः (*napātaḥ*)—sons
- अपसः (*apasaḥ*)—performers of sacrifice and other works
- ऋभवः (*ṛbhavaḥ*)—the Ṛbhus
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—friendship
- समानशुः (*samānaśuḥ*)—obtained, and
- दधन्विरे (*dadhanvire*)—also attained freedom from death
- सौधन्वनासः (*saudhanvanāsaḥ*)—the Ṛbhus, sons of Sudhanvan
- सुकृतः (*sukṛtaḥ*)—as excellent doers of works
- शमीभिः (*śamībhiḥ*)—by excellent works
- सुकृत्यया (*sukṛtyayā*)—by good conduct
- विष्ट्वी (*viṣṭvī*)—pervading everywhere
- अमृतत्वं (*amṛtatvaṃ*)—freedom from death
- एरिरे (*erire*)—obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Ṛbhus, sons of the human Aṅgiras and doers of sacrifice and other works, obtained the friendship of Indra. And by that help they also attained freedom from death. The Ṛbhus, sons of Sudhanvan, as excellent doers of works, pervading everywhere through excellent knowledge of duty and through their dealings, obtained freedom from death.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The Ribhus, the performers of (good) works, the grandsons of a man, have attained the friendship of Indra : they have perpetuated (existence): the sons of Sudhanvan have attained immortality : performers of pious acts influencing (the result), through their devotion (they have attained divinity) by their works

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The present Ṛk says that the Ṛbhus, sons of Aṅgiras, obtained Indra's friendship. It is also stated that the word manoḥ is a synonym for the human Aṅgiras. If manoḥ means Aṅgiras, then, to understand the relation between the Ṛbhus of the form of the Āditya's rays, described in the preceding Ṛk, and Aṅgiras, one must know the relation between the Āditya and Aṅgiras. Then, knowing the relation between Aṅgiras and Indra, one can understand the purport of the Ṛbhus' having cultivated the friendship of Indra, who has such a close relation.

### Printed p. 498
The very form of the Āditya whom the Chāndogya and other texts praise as the udgītha is also Aṅgiras. How is this?

अथाधिदैवतं य एवासौ तपति तमद्गीथमुपासीतोद्यन्वा एष प्रजाभ्य उद्दायति । उद्यन्‌स्तमो भयमपहन्त्यपहंता ह वै भयस्य तमसो भवति य एवं वेद ॥ (*athādhidaivataṃ ya evāsau tapati tamadgīthamupāsītodyanvā eṣa prajābhya uddāyati | udyanstamo bhayamapahantyapahaṃtā ha vai bhayasya tamaso bhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Bhā. U. 1-3-1)**NOTE**

One should worship the luminous Āditya himself as the udgītha. As soon as he rises he sings for the creatures in a manner that gives them joy. He destroys darkness and fear. Therefore this Āditya is the essence of the life of living beings and the giver of their contentment. Because he is thus the essence of life, the udgītha in the form of the Āditya is itself called Aṅgiras. How?

तं हांगिरा उद्दीथमुपासां चक्र एतमु एवांगिरसं मन्यंतेऽंगानां यद्रसः ॥ (*taṃ hāṃgirā uddīthamupāsāṃ cakra etamu evāṃgirasaṃ manyaṃte 'ṃgānāṃ yadrasaḥ ‖*) (Bhā. U. 1-2-10)**NOTE**

The Aṅgirases worshipped the udgītha. If one asks the reason for their worshipping, it is that they themselves are of the nature of the udgītha. How? The udgītha is the essence (rasa) of the limbs. Therefore udgītha means Aṅgiras. The rays of the Āditya give essence to the limbs of living beings. Therefore the udgītha is of the nature of the Āditya and of the nature of Aṅgiras; so by this explanation non-difference between the Āditya and Aṅgiras has been stated. Then what is the relation between such an Aṅgiras and Indra? It was explained earlier, in the Special Topics on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-4, how the epithet अंगिरोभिः अंगिरस्तमः (*aṃgirobhiḥ aṃgirastamaḥ*) shows Indra's Aṅgiras-nature. The meaning of the statement that Indra in the form of Aṅgiras caused the cows to be released is that Indra in the form of the Āditya split the mountain of the form of darkness and freed the cows of the form of rays.

अगच्छदु विप्रतमः सखीयन्नसूदयत्सु कृते गर्भमद्रिः । (*agacchadu vipratamaḥ sakhīyannasūdayatsu kṛte garbhamadriḥ |*)
ससान मर्यो युवभिर्मखस्यन्नथाभवदंगिराः सद्यो अर्चन् ॥ (*sasāna maryo yuvabhirmakhasyannathābhavadaṃgirāḥ sadyo arcan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-7)

In Ṛks of this kind this point is stated clearly.

शमीभिः (*śamībhiḥ*)—This word is read among the names of works (Ni. 3-1). It means the various kinds of skilled works and sacrificial works described earlier.

विष्ट्वे (*viṣṭve*)—This word too is read among the names of works (Ni. 3-1). Sāyaṇa, explaining this word elsewhere, has said as follows. There too the two, viṣṭvī, śamī,

### Printed p. 499
The Kannada commentary continues: because the two words are used in one and the same place, if the word शमी (*śamī*) means "action", the same meaning cannot be given to the word विष्ट्वि (*viṣṭvi*); another meaning must be given. So Sāyaṇa explains as follows:

विष्ट्वितृत्र न कर्मनाम । शमीत्यनेन पौनरुक्तप्रसंगात् । किं तर्हि । विषेर्वाप्त्यर्थस्य क्रियाशब्दोऽयं विष्ट्विति । विष्ट्वा व्याप्ता ॥ (*viṣṭvitṛtra na karmanāma | śamītyanena paunaruktaprasaṃgāt | kiṃ tarhi | viṣervāptyarthasya kriyāśabdo 'yaṃ viṣṭviti | viṣṭvā vyāptā ‖*)

Although the word is read among the names of actions, the word शमी (*śamī*) already denotes action, so there would be repetition. He therefore states that this word, formed from the root विष् (*viṣ*) in the sense of pervading, means "all-pervading".

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋभवो यूयमिंद्रेण सचा सह सरथं समानमेकं रथमारुह्य
> सुतेऽभिषुतसोमवति यज्ञे याथ । गच्छथ । अथो अनंतरमिंद्रेण सहैकरथमारूढा यूयं वशानां । उश्यते काम्यते यजमानेन स्वर्गादिलक्षणं फलमेभिरिति वशा मनुष्याः । तेषां श्रिया स्तुतिहविरादिरूपया सह भवथ । हे सौधन्वनाः
> सुधन्वनः पुत्रा वाघतोऽमृतत्वादिलक्षणफलस्य वोढारो मेधाविनो वेति यास्कः।
> तादृशा हे ऋभवो वो युष्माकं सुकृतानि देवत्वस्य प्रापकाणि शोभनानि
> कर्माणि न प्रतिमै । प्रतिमातुमियत्तया परिच्छेत्तुं न केनापि शक्यानि । तथा
> वीर्याणि युष्माकं सामर्थ्यानि च नैव प्रतिमातुं शक्यानि ॥ वशानां । वश कांतौ ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Ṛbhus, mounting one common chariot together with Indra, you go to the sacrifice in which Soma has been pressed. Then, having mounted the same chariot as Indra, you are together with the वशानां (*vaśānāṃ*). The वशाः (*vaśāḥ*) are men: the sacrificer desires (उश्यते (*uśyate*)) through them the fruit marked by heaven and the like. You are together with their "splendour" (श्रिया (*śriyā*)), in the form of praise, oblations and the like. O Sudhanvan's sons, वाघतः (*vāghataḥ*) means, according to Yāska, bearers of the fruit marked by immortality, or the wise. Of such you, O Ṛbhus, the good deeds that bring godhood, the well-done actions, cannot be measured, that is, delimited as "so much", by anyone. Likewise your powers cannot be measured. The grammatical remarks on वशानां (*vaśānāṃ*) begin here and continue on the next page.

### Printed p. 500

> वशिरण्योरुपसंख्यानमिति करणेऽप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । वशाशब्दो बंध्यावचनश्चेदंतोदात्तो भवति । वशा मेषा अवसृष्टास
> आहुताः । ऋग्वे. १०-९१-१४ । इति । वः । युष्मच्छब्दस्य षष्ठीबहुवचने वसादेशः ।
> निघातः । प्रतिमै । माज् माने । विच् । प्रतिमाः प्रतिमानं । तस्य चतुर्थैकवचन
> आतो लोपश्चांदसः । एकादेशस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The remaining remarks are grammatical, on वशानां (*vaśānāṃ*), वः (*vaḥ*) and प्रतिमै (*pratimai*). Sāyaṇa also notes that when the word वशा (*vaśā*) means a barren cow it is accented on the last syllable, and he cites Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-91-14 for it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Ṛbhus) इंद्रेण सचा (*iṃdreṇa sacā*)—with Indra
- सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)—mounting one and the same chariot
- सुते (*sute*)—to the sacrifice in which Soma has been pressed
- याथ (*yātha*)—come
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- वशानां (*vaśānāṃ*)—belonging to men
- श्रिया सह (*śriyā saha*)—with the wealth of praise and the like
- भवथ (*bhavatha*)—join together
- सौधन्वनाः (*saudhanvanāḥ*)—sons of Sudhanvan
- वाघतः (*vāghataḥ*)—wise ones
- ऋभवः (*ṛbhavaḥ*)—O Ṛbhus
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- सुकृतानि (*sukṛtāni*)—auspicious deeds
- वीर्याणि च (*vīryāṇi ca*)—and heroic acts
- न प्रतिमै (*na pratimai*)—no one is able to measure

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ṛbhus, mounting one and the same chariot with Indra, come to the sacrifice in which Soma has been pressed. Then join together with the wealth of praise and the like that belongs to men. O Ṛbhus, sons of Sudhanvan and wise ones, no one is able to measure your auspicious deeds or your heroic acts.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Go with Indra in his chariot when the libation is poured out, and be (welcomed) with honour by the (worshipper) desiring (your favour): Ribhus, sons of Sudhanwan, bestowers (of the rewards of pious acts), your virtuons deeds, your great faculties, are not to be measured.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वशानां (*vaśānāṃ*)—उश्यते काम्यते यजमानेन स्वर्गादिलक्षणं फलं एभिः इति वशाः मनुष्याः । (*uśyate kāmyate yajamānena svargādilakṣaṇaṃ phalaṃ ebhiḥ iti vaśāḥ manuṣyāḥ |*) Since fruits such as heaven are desired through sacrificial rites, men who show such a desire are well known by the name वशाः (*vaśāḥ*). The expressions वशा निवित् (*vaśā nivit*) and the like, specified in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka and other works, also indicate the same meaning. (Ai. Ā. 1-5-2)

> विकरणस्य लुक् । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the fifth day of the Ābhiplavika, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, the three verses beginning इंद्र ऋभुभिः (*iṃdra ṛbhubhiḥ*) form the Ṛbhu tṛca. This is stated in the sūtra: धृतवती भुवनानामभिश्रियेंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्भिरिति तृचौ (*dhṛtavatī bhuvanānāmabhiśriyeṃdra ṛbhubhirvājavadbhiriti tṛcau*) (Ā. 7-7). The first verse is also the prasthita-yājyā of the hotṛ at the third pressing, as the sūtra says: इंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्भिः समुक्षितमिंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं (*iṃdra ṛbhubhirvājavadbhiḥ samukṣitamiṃdrāvaruṇā sutapāvimaṃ sutaṃ*) (Ā. 5-5).

O Indra, accompanied by the वाजवद्धिः (*vājavaddhiḥ*) Ṛbhus. Vāja is the name of the brother of the Ṛbhus. Or else vāja is food, and the Ṛbhus are those who have it. Drink the Soma that has been sprinkled with water and pressed with the stones. गभस्तोः (*gabhastoḥ*): the two arms are called गभस्ती (*gabhastī*), either because with them people take (गृह्णंति (*gṛhṇaṃti*)) food after chewing, or because they take hold of objects. आ वृषस्व (*ā vṛṣasva*) means "pour in". The sense is: take the cup with both arms and drink the Soma. O Maghavan, O Indra, urged by the act of praise, rejoice in the house of the sacrificer who has given the oblation, together with the Ṛbhus, the sons of Sudhanvan, the men; become gladdened by drinking Soma. The rest is grammatical, on समुक्षितं (*samukṣitaṃ*), गभस्तोः (*gabhastoḥ*) and मत्त्व (*mattva*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वाजवद्भिः (*vājavadbhiḥ*)—possessed of food
- ऋभुभिः (*ṛbhubhiḥ*)—together with the Ṛbhus
- समुक्षितं (*samukṣitaṃ*)—mixed with water
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed with the pressing stones
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- गभस्त्योः (*gabhastyoḥ*)—lifting it with both arms
- आ वृषस्व (*ā vṛṣasva*)—drink
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—by the act in the form of praise
- इषितः (*iṣitaḥ*)—you who are urged
- दाशुषः (*dāśuṣaḥ*)—of the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- गृहे (*gṛhe*)—in the house
- सौधन्वनेभिः (*saudhanvanebhiḥ*)—sons of Sudhanvan
- नृभिः सह (*nṛbhiḥ saha*)—with the Ṛbhus who have the form of men
- मत्स्य (*matsya*)—drink Soma and become satisfied

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, together with the Ṛbhus who are possessed of food, lift with both arms the Soma that has been soaked in water and crushed and pressed with stones, and drink it. O wealthy Indra, urged by the act in the form of praise, drink Soma in the house of the sacrificer who offers the oblation, together with the Ṛbhus, sons of Sudhanvan, who have the form of men, and become satisfied.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, along with the food-bestowing Ribhus, accept with both hands the (cup of the) effused Soma libation ; excited Maghavan, by worship, rejoice with the human sons of Sudhanwan in the dwelling of the donor (of the offering).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the fifth day of the sacrifice called Abhiplava, when the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited, the three verses of this sūkta beginning इंद्र ऋभुभिः (*iṃdra ṛbhubhiḥ*) are to be recited as a tṛca addressed to the Ṛbhus. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra धृतवती भुवनानामभिश्रियेंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्भिरिति तृचौ (*dhṛtavatī bhuvanānāmabhiśriyeṃdra ṛbhubhirvājavadbhiriti tṛcau*) (Ā. 7-7). And the first verse of this sūkta is to be recited by the hotṛ at the third pressing as the prasthita-yājyā mantra; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana sūtra इंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्भिः समुक्षितमिंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं (*iṃdra ṛbhubhirvājavadbhiḥ samukṣitamiṃdrāvaruṇā sutapāvimaṃ sutaṃ*) (Ā. 5-5).

The injunction is stated that the present mantra and the one after it are to be recited in the form of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra. In both these mantras Indra is prayed to drink Soma together with the Ṛbhus; they are also in the form of the Ārbhava-pavamāna stotra. How it got the name Ārbhava-pavamāna is explained at length in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 15, in the account of the third pressing.

### Printed p. 503
**Special Topics** (continued)
गभस्तोः (*gabhastoḥ*)—The word गभस्ति (*gabhasti*) is read among the names of rays. In many places it is also used in the sense of "hand". In places where this word occurs, Sāyaṇa himself has explained it in some as "ray" and in some as "hand". For example, in वाचस्पतये पवस्वेति वृष्णोऽग्ंशुभ्यां गभस्ति पूत इति (*vācaspataye pavasveti vṛṣṇo 'gṃśubhyāṃ gabhasti pūta iti*) (Śa. Brā. 4-9-1-9), गभस्तिपूतः (*gabhastipūtaḥ*) is explained as हस्ताभ्यां पूतः (*hastābhyāṃ pūtaḥ*). But when the same sentence occurs in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, he explains it as "purified by the rays of the sun" (Tai. Saṃ. 1-4-2). Again, in the same Taittirīya Saṃhitā, in the sentence at 6-4-5, गभस्तिना हि एनं पावयति (*gabhastinā hi enaṃ pāvayati*), he explains it as "hand". Although by usage the meaning "ray of the sun" predominates for the word गभस्ति (*gabhasti*), in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā too it is explained as "hand" in many places.

गभस्तिपूतं भरत श्रुतायेंद्राय सोमं यज्यवो जुहोत । (*gabhastipūtaṃ bharata śrutāyeṃdrāya somaṃ yajyavo juhota |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-8): here गभस्तिपूत (*gabhastipūta*) means "purified by the hands": offer the Soma to Indra. And in गभस्तिपूतो नृभिरद्रिभिः सुतो महे वाजाय धन्याय धन्वसि । (*gabhastipūto nṛbhiradribhiḥ suto mahe vājāya dhanyāya dhanvasi |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-86-34) also, the meaning "hand" is established. In the present verse Indra is prayed to lift the Soma with both गभस्ति (*gabhasti*), that is, with both arms, and drink it.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुरुष्टुत बहुभिः स्तुत हे इंद्र ऋभुमान् ऋभुणा तद्वान् वाजवान्
> वाजेन ऋभोर्भ्रात्रा युक्तः शच्येंद्राण्या कर्मणा वा सहितः सन् नोऽस्माकमिह
> कर्मण्यस्मिन् तृतीयसवने मत्स्य । हृष्टो भव । हे इंद्र शुभ्यं त्वदर्थमिमानि
> स्वसराण्यहानि येमिरे । तव सोमपानार्थं त्रिषु सवनेषु नियतान्यासते । किंच
> देवानामग्न्यादीनां व्रता व्रतानि कर्माणि च मनुषो मनुष्यस्य धर्मभिः कर्मभिः
> साकं त्वदर्थं नियतान्यासते॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, praised by many (पुरुष्टुत (*puruṣṭuta*)), ऋभुमान् (*ṛbhumān*) is one having the Ṛbhu; वाजवान् (*vājavān*) is one joined with Vāja, the brother of Ṛbhu. Accompanied by शच्या (*śacyā*), that is, Indrāṇī or the act, be gladdened at this third pressing of ours in this rite. O Indra, these स्वसराणि (*svasarāṇi*), the days, are fixed (येमिरे (*yemire*)) for you; they remain appointed for your Soma-drinking in the three pressings. Moreover the व्रता (*vratā*), the rites and actions, of the gods Agni and the rest, together with the धर्मभिः (*dharmabhiḥ*), the actions, of man (मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)), remain appointed for you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुष्टुत (*puruṣṭuta*)—praised by many
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ऋभुमान् (*ṛbhumān*)—joined with Ṛbhu
- वाजवान् (*vājavān*)—joined with Vāja
- शच्या (*śacyā*)—joined with Indrāṇī
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- इह (*iha*)—in this, a part of the rite
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—in the third pressing
- मत्स्य (*matsya*)—obtain satisfaction
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for your satisfaction
- इमानि स्वसराणि (*imāni svasarāṇi*)—these days
- येमिरे (*yemire*)—move in a fixed course and recur **NOTE**
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the other gods
- व्रता च (*vratā ca*)—the rites also
- मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)—of man
- धर्मभिः (*dharmabhiḥ*)—together with the actions (are performed for your satisfaction)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, praised by many, being joined with Ṛbhu, with Vāja and with Śacī, be satisfied at this third pressing, which is a part of our rite. For your satisfaction these days move in a fixed course and recur. The rites of the other gods too, joined with the actions of man, are performed for your satisfaction.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, the praised of many associated with Ribhu, and with Vaja, exult with Shachi, at this our sacrifice: these self-revolving (days) are devoted to you, as well as the ceremonies (addressed) to the gods, and the virtuous acts of man.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शच्या—इंद्राण्या कर्मणा वा । (*śacyā—iṃdrāṇyā karmaṇā vā |*) It is explained as "with Indrāṇī or with action". In the Nighaṇṭu the word शची (*śacī*) is read among the names of speech (Ni. 1-11), among the names of actions (Ni. 2-1) and among the names of intelligence (3-9). In general it is used mostly in the sense of action. The meaning "wife of Indra" for the word शची (*śacī*) is not supported in the Ṛgveda—

### Printed p. 505

*(continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 6)*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In passages such as तुभ्यं श्चोतंत्यध्रिगो शचीव स्तोकासो अग्ने (*tubhyaṃ ścotaṃtyadhrigo śacīva stokāso agne*) (Ai. Brā. 2-12), the word शचीवः (*śacīvaḥ*) is explained as "possessed of power" (śaktimān). Addressing Agni, "O powerful Agni", the word शची (*śacī*) is taken to mean power. In the present Ṛk, whichever of the meanings power, action or intelligence is given, it is suitable. Since Indra is the doer of deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra, since he has obtained manifold powers, and since he is endowed with intelligence, any of these meanings can be given to this word, which is an epithet of Indra.

स्वसराणि (*svasarāṇi*)—the word स्वर (*svara*) is read among the names for "worthy" (Ni. 1-9) and among the names for "house" (Ni. 3-4). In Ṛks such as आ हंसासो न स्वसराणि गंतन मधोर्मदाय मरुतः समन्यवः । (*ā haṃsāso na svasarāṇi gaṃtana madhormadāya marutaḥ samanyavaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-5) it is explained as "house". In the present Ṛk it means "days".

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑ ऋ॒भुभि॑र्वा॒जिभि॑र्वा॒जय॑न्नि॒ह स्तोमं॑ जरि॒तुरुप॑  ॒॑
> याहि यज्ञियं ।  
> श॒तं केते॑भिरिषि॒रेभि॑रा॒यवे॑ स॒हस्र॑णीथो अध्व॒रस्य॒ होम॑नि ॥

> *iṃdra ṛbhubhirvājibhirvājayanniha stomaṃ jariturupa*  
> *yāhi yajñiyaṃ |*  
> *śataṃ ketebhiriṣirebhirāyave sahasraṇītho adhvarasya homani ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्र । ऋभुभिः । वाजिभिः । वाजयन् । इह । स्तोमं । जरितुः । उप । याहि ।  
> यज्ञियं ।  
> शतं । केतेभिः । इषिरेभिः । आयवे । सहस्रणीथः । अध्वरस्य । होमनि ॥ ७ ॥

> *iṃdra | ṛbhubhiḥ | vājibhiḥ | vājayan | iha | stomaṃ | jarituḥ | upa | yāhi |*  
> *yajñiyaṃ |*  
> *śataṃ | ketebhiḥ | iṣirebhiḥ | āyave | sahasraṇīthaḥ | adhvarasya | homani ‖ 7 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वाजिभिर्वाजयुक्तैर्य्यभुभिः सहितस्त्वं वाजयन् स्तोतुर्वाजमन्नं कुर्वाण इह यज्ञे यज्ञियं यज्ञार्हं जरितु: स्तोमं स्तोत्रमुप

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, accompanied by the Ribhus, who are possessed of food (वाज (*vāja*)), making food for the singer, come here to this sacrifice, to the praise (stoma) of the singer, which is worthy of the sacrifice. (The sentence continues on the next page.)

### Printed p. 506

> याहि । आगच्छ । पुनः किंविशिष्टः । केतेभिः । केत्यते ज्ञायते सर्वमेभिरिति केताः
> प्राज्ञा मरुतः । तैः शतं शतसंख्याकैरिषिरेभिरिषिरैर्गमनकुशलैरश्वैः सहित आयवे
> मनुष्याय यजमानाय सहस्रनीथो बहुप्रकारनयनोपेतोऽध्वरस्य । न विद्यते
> द्वरो हिंसा यस्य तादृशस्य सोमस्य होमनि होम आगच्छेति शेषः ॥ वाजयन् ।
> वाजं करोतीति णिच् । णाविष्ठवदितीष्टवद्भावात्तुरिष्ठेमेयःस्थिति टिलोपः ।
> केतेभिः । कित ज्ञाने । घञ् । इंताद्वाद्युदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Come." And how is he accompanied? केतेभिः (*ketebhiḥ*): those by whom everything is known (केत्यते ज्ञायते (*ketyate jñāyate*)) are केताः (*ketāḥ*), the wise Maruts. With them, and with a hundred swift horses skilled in going (इषिरेभिः (*iṣirebhiḥ*)), Indra, "leader of a thousand" (सहस्रनीथः (*sahasranīthaḥ*)), that is, bringing many kinds of guidance, is to come for the man, the sacrificer (आयवे (*āyave*)), to the oblation of the Soma that is अध्वर (*adhvara*), to which no harm (dvara) belongs. "Come" is the word to be supplied. Then follow the derivations of वाजयन् (*vājayan*) and केतेभिः (*ketebhiḥ*) (grammar not given here).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वाजिभिः (*vājibhiḥ*)—endowed with food
- ऋभुभिः (*ṛbhubhiḥ*)—together with the Ribhus
- वाजयन् (*vājayan*)—producing the food needed by the praiser
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- जरितुः (*jarituḥ*)—of the praiser
- यज्जियं (*yajjiyaṃ*)—worthy of sacrifice
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—towards the praise
- उप याहि (*upa yāhi*)—become one who comes
- केतेभिः (*ketebhiḥ*)—with the wise Maruts
- शतं इषिरेभिः (*śataṃ iṣirebhiḥ*)—and with a hundred horses, being joined with them
- आयती (*āyatī*)—for man (the sacrificer) **NOTE**
- सहस्रनीथः (*sahasranīthaḥ*)—taking food of many kinds
- अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—of the Soma free of harm
- होमनि (*homani*)—be present at the oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, together with the Ribhus who are possessed of fire **NOTE**, producing the food needed by the praiser, come in this sacrifice towards the praiser's praise, which is worthy of sacrifice. Joined with the wise Maruts and with a hundred horses, taking food of many kinds for the sacrificer, the man, be present at the oblation of the harmless Soma.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, with the food-bestowing Ribhus rewarding (worship) with food, come hither to (receive) the reverential praise of the adorer, with a hundred quick-going steeds, the indications (of the Maruts): come to the burnt offering of the sacrifice, yielding a thousand blessings to the sacrificer.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The present mantra tells of the relation between Indra and the Ribhus and of their nature as givers of food. On the relation of Indra and the Ribhus, on the doubt that arose concerning the oblation offered to them, and on what the Ārbhava-pavamāna is, details are given in the description of the third pressing (tṛtīya-savana) in Ṛ. Saṃ., Part 15.

### Printed p. 507

वाजयन् (*vājayan*)—स्तोतुः अन्नं कुर्वाणः (*stotuḥ annaṃ kurvāṇaḥ*), that is, procuring and giving food to the praiser. The word वाजिभिः (*vājibhiḥ*) too is explained as "endowed with food" (said of the Ribhus). वाजयतीत्यर्चतिकर्मा (*vājayatītyarcatikarmā*) (Ni. 3-19): in some contexts वाजयति (*vājayati*) must mean "one who worships". Moreover the word वाज (*vāja*) is read among the names for food (Ni. 3-9), among the names for battle and among the names for strength. It is also used in the sense of praise. In मां नरः स्वश्वा वाजयंतो मां वृताः समरणे हवंते । (*māṃ naraḥ svaśvā vājayaṃto māṃ vṛtāḥ samaraṇe havaṃte |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-42-5) the word वाजयंतः (*vājayaṃtaḥ*) is an epithet of नरः (*naraḥ*) and अश्वाः (*aśvāḥ*); it is explained as men and horses desiring battle. In passages such as स मातरा विचरन्वाजयन्नपः प्र मेधिरः स्वधया पिन्वते पदं । (*sa mātarā vicaranvājayannapaḥ pra medhiraḥ svadhayā pinvate padaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-68-4) it also means "impelling". But the word वाज (*vāja*) is mostly used in the senses of food and strength. In the present Ṛk it is explained as "producing food".

That when Indra joins the Ribhus the abundance of वाज (*vāja*) becomes greater is well known from the Śruti. That the Ribhus are makers of fire is also described in many places. A fixed association of food with them is stated. For example, in विदानासो जन्मनो वाजरत्ना उत ऋतुभिर्यभवो मादयःध्वं । (*vidānāso janmano vājaratnā uta ṛtubhiryabhavo mādayaḥdhvaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-34-2) the word वाजरत्नाः (*vājaratnāḥ*) is explained अन्नेन राजमानाः (*annena rājamānāḥ*), "the Ribhus shining with food", showing that the Ribhus are constantly endowed with food. The same point is made in the present Ṛk, and food is asked of them and of their friend Indra.

केतेभिः (*ketebhiḥ*)—केत्यते ज्ञायते सर्वमेभिरिति केताः प्राज्ञाः मरुतः (*ketyate jñāyate sarvamebhiriti ketāḥ prājñāḥ marutaḥ*). Because everything is known through them, the Maruts, having such a quality, are called केताः (*ketāḥ*). The meaning is: joined with such Maruts.

## Sūkta 61 (Maṇḍala 3)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उषो वाजेनेति सप्तर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रमुषोदेवताकं । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । उष उषस्यमिति ॥ प्रातरनुवाक उषस्यॆ क्रतावाश्विनशस्त्रे च त्रैष्टुभे
> छंदस्येतस्य सूक्तस्य विनियोगः । सूत्रितं च । उषो वाजेनेदमु त्यत । आ. ४-१४ ।
> इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta उषो वाजेन (*uṣo vājena*) has seven Ṛks; it is the eighth sūkta (of the anuvāka) of Viśvāmitra, with Uṣas as deity. So the Anukramaṇī: उष उषस्यमिति (*uṣa uṣasyamiti*). Its use: in the Prātaranuvāka, in the Uṣasya kratu and in the Āśvina-śastra, for the Ṛks in the Triṣṭubh metre. It is stated in the sūtra उषो वाजेनेदमु त्यत (*uṣo vājenedamu tyata*) (Ā. 4-14).

Anuvāda: This sūkta उषो वाजेन (*uṣo vājena*) is the eighth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. Its seer is Viśvāmitra; the deity is Uṣas; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said उष उषस्यं (*uṣa uṣasyaṃ*). At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, this sūkta is applied to the Triṣṭubh Ṛks of the Āśvina-śastra mantras connected with the Uṣasya kratu, as explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra उषो वाजेनेदमु तृत (*uṣo vājenedamu tṛta*) **NOTE** (Ā. 4-14).

Sūkta 61. Maṇḍala 3. Anuvāka 5. Sūkta 61. Aṣṭaka 3. Adhyāya 4. Varga 8. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Seer: Viśvāmitra. Deity: Uṣas. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

> मघोनि ।

> *uṣo vājena vājini pracetāḥ stomaṃ juṣasva gṛṇato*

> पुराणी । देवि । युवतिः । पुरंठधिः । अनु । व्रतं । चरसि । विश्ववारे ॥ १ ॥

> *uṣaḥ | vājena | vājini | pracetāḥ | stomaṃ | juṣasva | gṛṇataḥ | maghoni |*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाजेन वाजिन्यन्नेनान्नवति । तथा च मंत्रः । सं वाजैर्वाजिनीवति । ऋग्वे.
> १-४८-१६ । इति । मघोनि धनवति हे उषः प्रचेताः प्रकृष्टज्ञानवती सती गृणतः
> तव स्तोत्रं कुर्वतः स्तोतुः स्तोमं स्तोत्रं जुषस्व । सेवस्व । यद्वा ।
> वाजेन हनिर्लक्षणेनान्नेन सह स्तोमं जुषस्विति संबंधः । विश्ववारे विश्वैः
> सर्वैर्वर्णनीये हे उषो देवि पुराणी पुरातनी युवतिरित्युपमा तद्वच्छोभमाना । सुसंकाशा मात्सम्यष्टेव योषा । ऋग्वे १-१२३-११ । इतिवत् । पुरंधिः ।
> पुरु बहु धीः स्तोत्रलक्षणं कर्म यस्याः सा । बहुस्तोत्रवती । पुरंधिर्बहुधीरिति यास्कः । पुरंधिः शोभमाना ना । एवंविधगुणोपेता त्वमनु व्रतं यज्ञकर्माभिलक्ष्य चरसि। यष्टव्यतया वर्तसे ॥ मघोनि । मघशब्दान्मतुबर्थे छंदसीवनिपाविति वनिप् । स्त्रियामृन्नेभ्यो जीप् । श्वयुवमघोनामतद्धित इति संप्रसारणे कृते गुणः । संबुद्धावंबार्थनद्योर्ह्रस्वः । निघातः । पुराणी । पुराणशब्दः
> पुराणप्रोक्तेष्टित्यंतोदात्तत्वेन निपातितः । टिड्डाणइंति जीप् । अनुदात्तस्य च
> यत्रोदात्तलोप इत्यंतोदात्तत्वं । पुरंधिः । पृषोदरादित्वादुकारस्यामादेश
> ईकारस्य ह्रस्वश्च । आद्युदात्तप्रकरणे दिवोदासादीनां छंदस्युपसंख्यानमित्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वाजेन (*vājena*) means "with food"; वाजिनी (*vājinī*) means "possessing food". So the mantra सं वाजैर्वाजिनीवति (*saṃ vājairvājinīvati*) (Ṛgve. 1-48-16). मघोनि (*maghoni*): O wealthy Uṣas, being प्रचेताः (*pracetāḥ*), one of excellent knowledge, enjoy (जुषस्व (*juṣasva*), "serve") the praise of the praiser who praises you. Or else: enjoy the praise together with the food that has the oblation as its mark (havir-lakṣaṇa). विश्ववारे (*viśvavāre*): O Uṣas, to be extolled by all; पुराणी (*purāṇī*), ancient; युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*) is a simile: shining like a young woman, as in सुसंकाशा मात्सम्यष्टेव योषा । (*susaṃkāśā mātsamyaṣṭeva yoṣā |*) (Ṛgve. 1-123-11) **NOTE**. पुरंधिः (*puraṃdhiḥ*): she whose work, consisting of praise, is much (पुरु बहु धीः (*puru bahu dhīḥ*)), one with many praises; Yāska: पुरंधिर्बहुधीरिति (*puraṃdhirbahudhīriti*). Possessed of such qualities, you go about (चरसि (*carasi*)) in regard to the rite (व्रतं (*vrataṃ*)), the sacrificial action, that is, you are present as one to be worshipped. The remainder gives derivations and accent rules (not rendered here).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजेन वाजिनि (*vājena vājini*)—endowed with abundance of food
- मघोनि (*maghoni*)—and wealthy
- उषः (*uṣaḥ*)—O Uṣas
- प्रचेताः (*pracetāḥ*)—having excellent intelligence
- गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)—of him who praises you
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—the praise
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept
- विश्ववारे (*viśvavāre*)—honoured by all
- देवि (*devi*)—of divine nature
- पुराणी (*purāṇī*)—ancient
- युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*)—ever young
- पुरंधिः (*puraṃdhiḥ*)—you who are worthy of many praises
- अनुव्रतं (*anuvrataṃ*)—showing favour to the sacrificial rite
- चरसि (*carasi*)—you act

### Printed p. 510

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Uṣas, possessed of abundance of food and wealthy, you who have excellent intelligence, accept the praise of the praiser who praises you. Honoured by all, of divine nature, ancient, ever young, worthy of many praises, you go about showing favour to the sacrificial rite.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Affluent Ushas, giver of sustenance, possessed of intelligence, be propitiated by the praise of him who lauds you, (and worships) with (sacrificial) food : divine Ushas, adored by all, you (though) ancient are (still) young ; the object of manifold worship, you are present at the recurring (morning) rite.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

All the Ṛks that praise Uṣas have the form of supreme poetry. Epithets such as पुराणी (*purāṇī*) and युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*), which ordinarily show opposite qualities, describe those same qualities in Uṣas at one and the same time. Among all such epithets, the epithet पुरंधि (*puraṃdhi*) shows the all-pervading qualities of Uṣas.

पुरंधिर्बहुधीस्तत्कः पुरंधिर्भगः पुरस्तात्तस्यान्वादेश इत्येकं। इंद्र इत्यपरं स बहुकर्मतः पुरां च दारयितृतमः । वरुण इत्यपरं तं प्रज्ञया स्तौति ॥ (*puraṃdhirbahudhīstatkaḥ puraṃdhirbhagaḥ purastāttasyānvādeśa ityekaṃ| iṃdra ityaparaṃ sa bahukarmataḥ purāṃ ca dārayitṛtamaḥ | varuṇa ityaparaṃ taṃ prajñayā stauti ‖*) (Ni. 6-13).

This explanation the Nirukta-kāra gave when citing the Ṛk भगं नासत्या पुरंधिं (*bhagaṃ nāsatyā puraṃdhiṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-4). The Nirukta-kāra explains this word as "one possessed of abundant understanding (धी (*dhī*))". That is, other examples too show that the word is used when conveying the senses of abundance, fullness, prosperity and the like. In the Nirukta again the Ṛk
आदाय श्वेनो अभरत्सोमं सहस्रं सवा अयुतं च साकं । अत्रा पुरंधिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः । (*ādāya śveno abharatsomaṃ sahasraṃ savā ayutaṃ ca sākaṃ | atrā puraṃdhirajahādarātīrmade somasya mūrā amūraḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-26 7) **NOTE**
is cited (Ni. 11-2). For this word Sāyaṇa says बहुकर्म (*bahukarma*), the abundance of action, and Durgācārya in the Nirukta says बहु नः धनस्य दाता (*bahu naḥ dhanasya dātā*), one who gives wealth in great abundance. Again the Nirukta-kāra … (the window ends here; the sentence continues in the next).

### Printed p. 511
The Ṛk
पावीरवी तन्यतुरेकपादजो दिवो धर्ता सिंधुरापः समुद्रियः । विश्वे देवासः शृणवन् वचांसि मे सरस्वती सह धीभिः पुरंध्या ॥ (*pāvīravī tanyaturekapādajo divo dhartā siṃdhurāpaḥ samudriyaḥ | viśve devāsaḥ śṛṇavan vacāṃsi me sarasvatī saha dhībhiḥ puraṃdhyā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-13)
is also quoted (Ni. 12-30). Here the word *purandhi* is explained as "made use of by praise": words accompanied by manifold praises. Commenting on this same mantra, Sāyaṇa says बहुविधया प्रज्ञया सहिता सरस्वती (*bahuvidhayā prajñayā sahitā sarasvatī*), that is, "Sarasvatī endowed with manifold wisdom", and he treats it as an epithet of Sarasvatī. But from Durgācārya's explanation (Ni. 12-30), बहुधात्रा माध्यमिकया वाचा (*bahudhātrā mādhyamikayā vācā*), it is understood that Purandhi is a particular deity resembling Sarasvatī. Likewise, in
शं नो भगः शमु नः शंसो अस्तु शं नः पुरंधिः शमु संतु रायः । शं नः सत्यस्य सुयमस्य शंसः शं नो अरमा पुरुजातो अस्तु ॥ (*śaṃ no bhagaḥ śamu naḥ śaṃso astu śaṃ naḥ puraṃdhiḥ śamu saṃtu rāyaḥ | śaṃ naḥ satyasya suyamasya śaṃsaḥ śaṃ no aramā purujāto astu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-35-2)
and similar Ṛks, just as deities such as Bhaga and Aramā are prayed to, Purandhi too is prayed to for protective and auspicious favour. Sāyaṇa also, in his bhāṣya, says that Purandhi is a separate deity.

In many places this word is used of the wife or of woman in general, and gives the sense of women who are not barren, who are fit to obtain wealth of offspring and are well-nourished. For example, in
अग्निः सप्तिं वाजंभरं ददात्यग्निर्वीरं श्रुत्यं कर्मनिष्ठां । अग्नी रोदसी वि चरत्समंजन्नग्निर्नारीं वीरकुक्षिं पुरंधिं ॥ (*agniḥ saptiṃ vājaṃbharaṃ dadātyagnirvīraṃ śrutyaṃ karmaniṣṭhāṃ | agnī rodasī vi caratsamaṃjannagnirnārīṃ vīrakukṣiṃ puraṃdhiṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-1)
and similar Ṛks it is understood as a wife capable of bearing children, and in
प्र बोधया पुरंधिं जार आ ससतीमिव । (*pra bodhayā puraṃdhiṃ jāra ā sasatīmiva |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-134-3)
and similar Ṛks, as a woman fit for enjoyment. Thus this epithet, which has the capacity to convey manifold qualities, in the present Ṛk conveys the many qualities of Ushas.

Sāyaṇa here explains the word *dhī* as praise, and states one purport as "having much praise" and another as "or shining much". Since it conveys abundant and plentiful quality, all the above-mentioned qualities are fully present in Ushas.

### Printed p. 512
Whether one says she has abundant intelligence, or has ritual action, or has praise, or is a giver of wealth, or is capable of bringing forth because she is the giver of food to the world and the giver of vitality, any sense one states fits.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उषो॑ दे॒व्यम॑र्त्या॒ वि भा॑हि चं॒द्रर॑था सू॒न्यता॑ ई॒रयं॑ती ।  
> आ त्वा॑ वहंतु सु॒यमा॑सो॒ अश्वा॒ हिर॑ण्यवर्णां पृथु॒पाज॑सो॒ ये ॥ २ ॥

> *uṣo devyamartyā vi bhāhi caṃdrarathā sūnyatā īrayaṃtī |*  
> *ā tvā vahaṃtu suyamāso aśvā hiraṇyavarṇāṃ pṛthupājaso ye ‖ 2 ‖*

> उषः । देवि । अमर्त्या । वि । भाहि । चंद्ररथा । सूनृताः । ईरयंती ।

> *uṣaḥ | devi | amartyā | vi | bhāhi | caṃdrarathā | sūnṛtāḥ | īrayaṃtī |*  
> *ā | tvā | vahaṃtu | suyamāsaḥ | āśvāḥ | hiraṇyavarṇāṃ | pṛthupājasaḥ | ye ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उषो देव्यमर्त्या मरणधर्मरहिता चंद्ररथा सुवर्णमयरथोपेता
> सूनृताः प्रियसत्यरूपा वाच ईरयंत्युच्चारयंती । तथा च मंत्रवर्णः । सुम्मावरी सूनृता ईरयंती । ऋग्वे. १-११३-१२ । इति । तादृशी त्वं वि भाहि । सूर्यकिरणसंबंधाद्विशेषेण दीप्यस्व : पृथुपाजसः प्रभूतबलयुक्ता अरुणवर्णा यः ५श्वा
> विद्यंते सुयमासः सुष्टु नियंतुं शक्या रथे योजितास्तेऽश्वा हिरण्यवर्णां त्वा
> श्वामा वहंतु ॥ सुयमासः । यमेरकृच्छार्थे खल् । लित्स्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Ushas, divine, immortal (free from the nature of death), possessed of a golden chariot, uttering (*īrayantī*) the *sūnṛtā*, speech of pleasant truth. The mantra text says so: सुम्मावरी सूनृता ईरयंती (*summāvarī sūnṛtā īrayaṃtī*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-12). Such as you are, shine forth: blaze in a special way through connection with the sun's rays. The horses that are of great strength (*pṛthupājasaḥ*) and ruddy in colour, easy to restrain (*suyamāsaḥ*) and yoked to the chariot—may those horses bring you, golden-hued.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवि (*devi*)—divine in nature
- उषः (*uṣaḥ*)—O goddess Ushas
- अमर्त्या (*amartyā*)—free from the nature of death
- चंद्ररथा (*caṃdrarathā*)—possessing a golden chariot
- सूनृताः (*sūnṛtāḥ*)—pleasant words
- ईरयंती (*īrayaṃtī*)—uttering
- विभाहि (*vibhāhi*)—shine
- पृथुपाजसः (*pṛthupājasaḥ*)—of abundant strength
- ये अश्वाः (*ye aśvāḥ*)—whichever horses
- सुयमास (*suyamāsa*)—those that are yoked to the chariot
- हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*)—golden in form
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आ वहंतु (*ā vahaṃtu*)—may they carry (hither)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Ushas, shine, immortal, possessed of a golden chariot, uttering pleasant words. May the horses of abundant strength, yoked to the chariot, bear you, golden in form, hither.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Ushas, who are divine and immortal, mounted in a golden chariot, shine radiant, causing to be heard the sounds of truth; may your vigorous and well-trained horses bring you who are golden-haired, (hither),

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

*Candrarathā*: the word *candra* is read among the names of gold (Ni. 2-10). *Candrarathā* means one having a golden chariot. Or, following the Nirukta's explanation चंद्रश्चंदतेः कांतिकर्मणः । (*caṃdraścaṃdateḥ kāṃtikarmaṇaḥ |*) (Ni. 11-5), that the word *candra* may be formed from the root *cand*, giving the sense "radiant, delightful", Sāyaṇa, in
वि तद्ययुररुणयुग्निरश्वैश्चित्रं भांत्युषसश्चंद्ररथाः । अग्रं यज्ञस्य बृहतो नयंतीर्वि ता बाधंते तम ऊर्मायाः ॥ (*vi tadyayuraruṇayugniraśvaiścitraṃ bhāṃtyuṣasaścaṃdrarathāḥ | agraṃ yajñasya bṛhato nayaṃtīrvi tā bādhaṃte tama ūrmāyāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-65-2)
explains *candrarathāḥ*, an epithet of the Ushases, as "having radiant chariots". Likewise, in
चंद्रमग्निं चंद्ररथं हरिव्रतं वैश्वानरमप्सुषदं स्वर्विदं । विगाहं तूर्णिं तविषीभिरावृतं भूर्णिं देवास इह सुश्रियं दधुः ॥ (*caṃdramagniṃ caṃdrarathaṃ harivrataṃ vaiśvānaramapsuṣadaṃ svarvidaṃ | vigāhaṃ tūrṇiṃ taviṣībhirāvṛtaṃ bhūrṇiṃ devāsa iha suśriyaṃ dadhuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-5)
Sāyaṇa explains *candrarathaṃ*, an epithet of Vaiśvānara Agni, as आह्लादकः रथः यस्य । (*āhlādakaḥ rathaḥ yasya |*), "one whose chariot is gladdening", that is, having a chariot that causes joy. Hence in the present Ṛk too the sense may be stated either as a golden chariot or as a chariot that produces joy.

*Sūnṛtāḥ īrayantī*: *sūnṛtā*, *sūnṛtāvatī*, *sūnṛtāvarī* and the like are all epithets or synonyms of Ushas (Ni. 2-19): सूनृतेति वाज्‌नाम । (*sūnṛteti vājnāma |*) *Netrī*: producer. उषसः प्रादुर्भवानंतरं हि पशुपक्षिमृगादयः सर्वे शब्दं कुर्वंति । अतस्मैव तासां वाचां प्रवर्तयिता इत्युच्यते । (*uṣasaḥ prādurbhavānaṃtaraṃ hi paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥ sarve śabdaṃ kurvaṃti | atasmaiva tāsāṃ vācāṃ pravartayitā ityucyate |*) The word *sūnṛta* applies to all

### Printed p. 514
manner of speech-activity. Since, after the rising of Ushas, the speech-activity of all animals, birds and the rest begins, the meaning is that Ushas herself is the producer of all of it. Kutsa and Vasiṣṭha have used this epithet abundantly. In
एषा गेत्री राधसः सूनृतानामुषा उच्छंती रिभ्यते वसिष्ठैः । (*eṣā getrī rādhasaḥ sūnṛtānāmuṣā ucchaṃtī ribhyate vasiṣṭhaiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-76-7)
and a few similar places only, Sāyaṇa explains *sūnṛtānām* as "leader of praises". In the present Ṛk it reads *sūnṛtāḥ īrayantī*; the meaning is either "uttering pleasant words" or "impelling".

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O goddess Ushas, you are *pratīcī* to all the worlds: she who "turns towards and reaches" them. You, as the *ketu*, the making-known, of the immortal sun (free from the nature of death), stand aloft in the sky. O *navyasī*, newer, being born again and again, O Ushas: *artha* means a road, that by which one goes (*aryate*). Wishing to travel the one same road, of the time preceding sunrise, you turn back (*ā vavṛtsva*): become again returned to that road. An example: like a wheel (*cakram iva*): as the wheel of the chariot of the sun moving in the sky revolves again and again.

> रूपं । ईकारलोपश्छांदसः । ववृत्स्व । वृतु वर्तने । बहुलं छंधसीति विकरणस्य
> श्लुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The remainder of the block is purely grammatical (the formation of *artham*, *navyasi*, *vavṛtsva*); it is left to the Grammar section.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उषः (*uṣaḥ*)—O goddess Ushas
- विश्वा भुवनानि (*viśvā bhuvanāni*)—all the worlds
- प्रतीची (*pratīcī*)—pervading
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—of the deathless sun
- केतुः (*ketuḥ*)—as the one who makes known
- ऊर्ध्व (*ūrdhva*)—in the sky
- तिष्ठसि (*tiṣṭhasi*)—you stand
- नव्यसि (*navyasi*)—O Ushas, who appear new every day
- समानं अर्थं (*samānaṃ arthaṃ*)—the one same road
- चरणीयमाना (*caraṇīyamānā*)—wishing to travel
- चक्रमिव (*cakramiva*)—as a wheel turns
- आ ववृत्स्व (*ā vavṛtsva*)—you are one whose motion recurs every day

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Ushas, pervading all the worlds, as the one who makes known the deathless sun, you stand in the sky. O Ushas, who appear new every day, wishing to travel the one same road, you are one whose motion recurs every day, as a wheel turns.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Ushas, who spread over all the regions, you abide on high, the ensign of the immortal (sun), purposing to travel the same road, repeatedly turn back ever new, (revolving) like a wheel.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The idea suggested by words such as *navyasi*, *cakram iva ā vavṛtsva* is explained in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. There it is described that the thirty forms of Ushas revolve in a circle, that those thirty forms propound one and the same principle, and that there is an inseparable relation between the path of Ṛta and the revolving of Ushas. Although she appears anew again and again, her beginninglessness is described by sentences such as "ever and again being born, ancient". The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa too says this:
इमा एव ता उषसो याः प्रथमा व्यौच्छन् । ता देव्यः कुर्वते पंचरूपा । शश्वतीर्नावपृज्यंति । न गमंत्यंतं ॥ (*imā eva tā uṣaso yāḥ prathamā vyaucchan | tā devyaḥ kurvate paṃcarūpā | śaśvatīrnāvapṛjyaṃti | na gamaṃtyaṃtaṃ ‖*) (Tā. Brā. 2-5-6-5)
**NOTE**

### Printed p. 516
"*Viśvā bhuvanāni pratīcī*": the form of Ushas described in the present Ṛk as having pervaded and shone over all the worlds is that same first form of Ushas, as it was at the time of creation. There is no difference in it. "Those same Ushases are present every day": the very form of that Ushas continues even now, uninterruptedly and infinitely (Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara). Though she takes five forms, beginning with spring, the basic principle is one. It is unbroken. Though it recurs like a wheel, it follows one path of Ṛta.
आदर्शि गातुरुरवे वरीयसी पंथा ऋतस्य समयंस्त रश्मिभिश्च क्षुर्भगस्य रश्मिभिः। (*ādarśi gātururave varīyasī paṃthā ṛtasya samayaṃsta raśmibhiśca kṣurbhagasya raśmibhiḥ|*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-136-2)
In this description, that for the sun of wide extent the still wider path of Ṛta was marked out with the help of his rays, the broad path of Ṛta in the sky that is indicated is the eternal course of Ushas.

> अव॒ स्यूमे॑व चिन्व॒ती म॒घोन्न्यु॒षा या॑ति॒ स्वस॑रस्य॒ पत्नि ॑।  
> स्व१॒॑र्जनं॑ती सु॒भगा॑ सु॒दंसा॒ अंता॑द्दि॒नः प॑प्रथ॒ आ पृ॑थि॒व्याः ॥

> *ava syūmeva cinvatī maghonnyuṣā yāti svasarasya patni |*  
> *svarjanaṃtī subhagā sudaṃsā aṃtāddinaḥ papratha ā pṛthivyāḥ ‖*

> अव । स्यूम इव । चिन्वती । मघोनी । उषाः । याति । स्वसरस्य । पत्नि ।  
> स्वः । जनंती । सुभगा । सुदंसाः । आ । अंतात् । दिवः । पप्रथे । आ । पृथिव्याः ॥४॥

> *ava | syūma iva | cinvatī | maghonī | uṣāḥ | yāti | svasarasya | patni |*  
> *svaḥ | janaṃtī | subhagā | sudaṃsāḥ | ā | aṃtāt | divaḥ | paprathe | ā | pṛthivyāḥ ‖4‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> येयमुषाः स्यूमेव वस्त्रमिव विस्तृतं तमोऽवचिन्वत्यवचयमपक्षयं
> प्रापयंती मघोनी धनवती स्वसरस्य । सुष्पृष्यति क्षिपति तम इति स्वसरः सूरो
> वासरो वा । तस्य पत्नि सती याति गच्छति । स्वः स्वकीयं तेजो जनंती जनयंती
> सुभगा सुधना सौभाग्ययुक्ता ना सुदंसाः शोभनाग्नि होत्रकर्मा सेयमुषा

> स्यूमेव । षुवु तंतुसंताने । अविषिविशुषिभ्यः किदिति मन्प्रत्ययः । ध्योः शूडनु-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ushas, like a stitched garment (*syūma*), i.e. like a spread-out cloth, bringing the extended darkness to diminution (*avacaya*, decay); she is *maghonī*, wealthy; the wife of *svasara*. He who well casts away (*suṣpṛṣyati*, *kṣipati*) darkness is *svasara*, the sun or the day. Being his wife, she goes. *Svaḥ*: her own light, generating; *subhagā*, of good wealth, endowed with good fortune; *sudaṃsāḥ*, of good agnihotra-ritual action. She, Ushas, spreads (*paprathe*), shines, from the end of heaven to the end of the earth. The remainder is grammar (*syūma*, root *syu*, and so on), the next page continues it.

### Printed p. 517

> नासिके चेत्यूट् । यणादेशः । सुपां सुलुगिति सोर्लुक् । नित्ताद्युदात्तः ।
> चिन्वती । शतुरनुम इति जीप उदात्तत्वं । जनंती । जन जनन इत्यस्य ण्यंतस्य शतरि
> रूपं । छंदस्युभयथेति शप आर्धधातुकत्वेन णिलोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Grammar only (*cinvatī*, *janantī*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघोनी (*maghonī*)—wealthy
- स्वसरस्य (*svasarasya*)—of the sun
- पत्नि (*patni*)—the wife
- उषाः (*uṣāḥ*)—goddess Ushas
- स्यूम इव (*syūma iva*)—the darkness that spreads like a cloth
- अव चिन्तती (*ava cintatī*)—destroying
- याति (*yāti*)—she goes
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—her own light
- जनंती (*janaṃtī*)—creating (spreading)
- सुभगा (*subhagā*)—endowed with good fortune
- सुदंसाः (*sudaṃsāḥ*)—helper of excellent ritual action
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of heaven
- आ अंतात् (*ā aṃtāt*)—from the end
- पृथिव्याः आ (*pṛthivyāḥ ā*)—to the end of the earth
- पप्रथे (*paprathe*)—shines, famous

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wealthy goddess Ushas, wife of the sun, goes about destroying the darkness spread like a cloth. Spreading her own light, endowed with good fortune and a helper of excellent ritual action, she shines renowned from the end of heaven to the end of the earth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The opulent Ushas, the bride of the far-darting (sun), throwing off (darkness) like a garment, proceeds : diffusing her own (lustre), auspicious, promoting sacred acts, she is renowned to the ends of the heaven and of the earth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

*Svasara*: सुष्टु अस्यति क्षिपति तम इति स्वसरः सूरो वासरो वा । (*suṣṭu asyati kṣipati tama iti svasaraḥ sūro vāsaro vā |*) Because it completely scatters and destroys darkness, the word *svasara* means either the sun or the day. Further on, the word *svaḥ* is explained as light.
विश्वाः पिन्वथः स्वसरस्य धेना अनु वामेकः पविरा ववर्त । (*viśvāḥ pinvathaḥ svasarasya dhenā anu vāmekaḥ pavirā vavarta |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-62-2)
In such places the precise meaning of *svasara* is stated to be the sun.
*Svaḥ*: this word is read among the common names, *svaḥ*, *pṛśni*, *nāka* and so on. The Nirukta says that all these are synonyms of heaven and of the sun. The sun too, being of the nature of light, is designated by the word *svaḥ*. And,

### Printed p. 518

(Special Topics, continued) The nirvacana of this word, स्वतो भासं ज्योतिषां । स्वतो भासेति वा ॥ (*svato bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāṃ | svato bhāseti vā ‖*) (Ni. 9-14), and the like, was given earlier together with the special senses of the word. In the present Ṛk the word is used to describe the radiance of Uṣas.

"Wife of Svasara" (स्वसरस्य पत्नि (*svasarasya patni*)) may mean either the wife of the Sun or the wife of the day (ahas). The relation between the Sun and Uṣas is described in one way in one place and in another way elsewhere. In passages such as योषा जारस्य चक्षसा विभाति (*yoṣā jārasya cakṣasā vibhāti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-11) it is established that she is the wife of Āditya.

कदा नो देवीरमृतस्य पत्निः सूरो वर्णेन शतनन्नु पासः । (*kadā no devīramṛtasya patniḥ sūro varṇena śatanannu pāsaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-5-13)

The description that the Uṣases, wives of the Sun, who give life to the world and protect it, spread out their light, is just as in the present Ṛk. But in

एता उ त्याः प्रत्यदृश्रन् पुरस्ताज्योतिर्यच्छंतीरुषसो विभातीः । अजीजनन्तूर्यं यज्ञमग्निपपाचीनं तमो आगादबुष्टं ॥ (*etā u tyāḥ pratyadṛśran purastājyotiryacchaṃtīruṣaso vibhātīḥ | ajījanantūryaṃ yajñamagnipapācīnaṃ tamo āgādabuṣṭaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-78-3)

it is said that the shining Uṣases, who spread radiance over the world, brought the Sun into being; so in some places a relation of mother and begotten is also stated.

स्यूम इव (*syūma iva*)—the word syūma is explained as "cloth". Because cloth is woven of warp and woof, it has the synonym syūma. In the same way dense darkness, like warp and woof, is here compared with syūma. In some places the same synonym stands for radiance having this quality. For example, in

सूम्यमगभस्तिमृतयुग्भि रश्वैराश्विना वसुमंतं वहेथां ॥ (*sūmyamagabhastimṛtayugbhi raśvairāśvinā vasumaṃtaṃ vahethāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-21-3)

and similar places, स्यूमगभस्ति (*syūmagabhasti*) is said to mean either "having pleasant rays" or "having rays [of the kind called] sūta".

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the praisers: turning towards you, offer to the shining goddess Uṣas, with your homage (namas), a fine hymn of praise (suvṛkti). Madhudhā: she "holds" sweet words that have the character of praise; or madhu is Soma, and she bears it; or madhudhā is "nurse of Āditya"; or, since there is no avagraha, this is an indivisible word, a name of Uṣas, with no analysable parts. This Uṣas in the sky has taken upward-directed radiance (pājas); aśret means "resorts to". Likewise, radiant and lovely to see, Uṣas shines forth greatly. Or else rocanā means "the worlds", which she lights up with her own radiance. Sāyaṇa cites the mantra text व्युच्छंती हि रश्मिभिर्विश्वमाभासि रोचनं (*vyucchaṃtī hi raśmibhirviśvamābhāsi rocanaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-49-4).

- विभातीं (*vibhātīṃ*)—shining
- उषसं देवीं (*uṣasaṃ devīṃ*)—addressing the goddess Uṣas
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- नमसा (*namasā*)—accompanied by homage
- सुवृक्तिं (*suvṛktiṃ*)—excellent praise
- प्र भरध्वं (*pra bharadhvaṃ*)—compose and offer
- मधुधा (*madhudhā*)—Uṣas, the repository of sweetness
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the sky
- ऊर्ध्वं (*ūrdhvaṃ*)—directed upward
- पाजः (*pājaḥ*)—radiance (continued on the next page)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Given on p. 520.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Offer, with your prostrations, due praise to the divine Ushas, shining upon you: the repository of sweetness manifests her brightness aloft in the sky, and, radiant and lovely, lights the regions.

- तेजस्सन्नु (*tejassannu*) (radiance, completing पाजः (*pājaḥ*))
- अश्रेत् (*aśret*)—has obtained
- रोचना (*rocanā*)—radiant

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praisers, compose and offer your excellent praise, accompanied by homage, to the goddess Uṣas who shines turned towards you. Uṣas, the repository of sweetness, has obtained in the sky radiance directed upward. Radiant and of lovely appearance, she shines exceedingly.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सुवृक्तिं (*suvṛktiṃ*)—it is explained as formed from the root वृंच् (*vṛṃc*). This nirvacana shows that the praise composed after being separated out and refined is what the word vṛkti denotes. Or सुप्रवृत्ता स्तुतिः (*supravṛttā stutiḥ*): it may also mean praise composed under a most excellent impulse of the mind.

मधुधा (*madhudhā*)—two or three kinds of nirvacana are shown for this word: मधुराणि स्तुतिलक्षणानि वाक्यानि दधातीति (*madhurāṇi stutilakṣaṇāni vākyāni dadhātīti*); मधु सोमः (*madhu somaḥ*), तं धारयतीति वा (*taṃ dhārayatīti vā*); यद्वा (*yadvā*) मधुधा-आदित्यधात्री (*madhudhā-ādityadhātrī*); यद्वा (*yadvā*) the word is an indivisible name उषोनाम (*uṣonāma*) with no analysable parts because there is no avagraha. Sāyaṇa explains that the epithet madhudhā is fitting for Uṣas because she bears the sweet characteristics suited to praise; or because she bears Soma (madhu meaning Soma); or, if madhu is taken to mean Āditya, because she is his nurse; or because she is denoted by an indivisible word.

रण्वसंदृक् (*raṇvasaṃdṛk*)—raṇva means "lovely" and sandṛk means "form"; the sense is "having a lovely form".

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Ṛtāvarī is "possessed of truth": this Uṣas is known (abodhi) to all from the sky, the world of heaven, by her rays (arkaiḥ, "radiances"). Then she, possessed of wealth (revatī), stands pervading the two worlds, heaven and earth, in such a way that they are variously coloured (citram). O Agni, you who ask (bhikṣamāṇaḥ) for oblations from the shining goddess Uṣas as she comes towards you, obtain (eṣi) the desirable (vāmam) wealth (draviṇam) that consists of the agnihotra and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतावरी (*ṛtāvarī*)—Uṣas, who is possessed of truth
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the world of heaven
- आर्कॆः (*ārkèḥ*)—together with her radiances
- अबोधि (*abodhi*)—is known by all
- रेवती (*revatī*)—Uṣas, possessed of wealth
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—making them to be endowed with many kinds of forms
- आ अस्थात् (*ā asthāt*)—stands pervading
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- आयतीं (*āyatīṃ*)—coming towards you
- विभातीं (*vibhātīṃ*)—and shining
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—Uṣas
- भिक्षमाणः (*bhikṣamāṇaḥ*)—you who ask for oblations
- वामं (*vāmaṃ*)—attractive
- द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)—wealth that has the form of agnihotra and the like
- एषि (*eṣi*)—you obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Uṣas, possessed of truth, is known to all from the world of heaven together with her radiances. Uṣas, possessed of wealth, stands pervading heaven and earth, making them endowed with many kinds of forms. O Agni, you who ask for oblations from the shining goddess Uṣas coming towards you obtain attractive wealth that has the form of agnihotra and the like.

### Printed p. 522

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The possessor of truth is recognized in the sky by her rays : the possessor of wealth has taken a marvellous station in earth and heaven : Agni, soliciting alms of the radiant advancing Ushas, obtain your desired treasure (of oblations).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋतावरी (*ṛtāvarī*)—सत्यवती (*satyavatī*). The word ṛta means "truth". Because Uṣas guards truth, the epithet ṛtāvarī belongs to her.

अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)—तेजोभिः (*tejobhiḥ*), "by radiances". All radiant deities such as Agni are denoted by the word arka. For example, अग्निर्वा अर्कः (*agnirvā arkaḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 1-4-1), "Agni is Arka", and the like, is stated. Abundant radiance is also denoted by arka.

चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—the word citra is used in many senses. In the Ṛk पशून्न चित्रा सुभगा प्रधाना (*paśūnna citrā subhagā pradhānā*) (1-92-12) too, the word citrā is an epithet of Uṣas. There two meanings are given, चायनीया (*cāyanīyā*) and पूजनीया (*pūjanīyā*). The sense "charming, attractive" is the more common in use. चित्रं महनीयं (*citraṃ mahanīyaṃ*), that is, "worthy of reverence", is also a meaning. In the present place, नानाविधरूपयुक्तं (*nānāvidharūpayuktaṃ*) means Uṣas, who has assumed many kinds of forms so as to be attractive.

वामं (*vāmaṃ*)—वननीयं (*vananīyaṃ*), "desired by all". At अस्य वामस्य पलितुः (*asya vāmasya palituḥ*) (1-164-1) two kinds of meaning are given: first वननीयस्य (*vananīyasya*), one who is desired and served by all; second वामस्य विश्वस्य उद्धरितुः (*vāmasya viśvasya uddharituḥ*), one who has extended the world in the form of the universe. In the present place too both meanings can be given. Uṣas is desired by all, so she is to be sought after; moreover she is the one who, in her own manner, causes the world to be spread out. So here both meanings fit.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒तस्य॑ बु॒द्ध उ॒षसा॑मिष॒ण्यन्वषा॑ म॒ही रोद॑सी॒ आ वि॑वेश ।  
> म॒ही मि॒त्रस्य॒ वरु॑णस्य मा॒या चं॒द्रेव॑ भा॒नुं वि द॑धे  ॒
> पुरुत्रा ॥ ७ ॥

> *ṛtasya buddha uṣasāmiṣaṇyanvaṣā mahī rodasī ā viveśa |*  
> *mahī mitrasya varuṇasya māyā caṃdreva bhānuṃ vi dadhe*  
> *purutrā ‖ 7 ‖*

> मही । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । माया । चंद्राइव । भानुं । वि । दधे । पुरुत्का ॥७॥

> *ṛtasya | buddhe | uṣasāṃ | iṣaṇyan | vṛṣā | mahī iti | rodasī iti | ā | viveśa |*  
> *mahī | mitrasya | varuṇasya | māyā | caṃdrāiva | bhānuṃ | vi | dadhe | purutkā ‖7‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषा वृष्टि द्वारा प्रेरक आदित्य ऋतस्याग्नि होत्रादिकर्मकरणे सत्यभूतस्याहो बुद्धे मूल उषसामिषण्यन् प्रेरणं कुर्वनृही महत्यौ रोदसी द्यावाप्रथिव्याना विवेश । स्वतेजोभिः सर्वतः प्रविष्टवान् । यद्वा । वृषा वर्षितेषण्यन्
> सर्वतो गच्छन्नुषसां संबंधी रश्मिसमूहो रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्य विष्टवानिति
> योजनीयं । तत उषा मही महती मित्रस्य वरुणस्य मित्रावरुणयोर्माया
> प्रभारूपा सती चंद्रेव सुवर्णानीव भानुं स्वप्रभां पुरुत्रा बहुषु देशेषु वि
> दधे । विदधाति । सर्वत्र प्रसारयति ॥ मही । अल्लोपश्रांदसः । पुरुत्रा । देवमनुष्येत्यादिनाधिकरणे त्राप्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vṛṣā is Āditya, who impels through rain. At the root (budhne) of ṛta, the day that is true in the performance of agnihotra and other rites, urging on the dawns (uṣasām iṣaṇyan), he has entered the two great worlds, heaven and earth, pervading them everywhere with his own rays. Or else: vṛṣā is the mass of Uṣas's rays, going in all directions, which has entered heaven and earth; this is how the construction is to be made. Then Uṣas, great, being as the radiance (māyā) of Mitra and Varuṇa, like gold (candreva means "like gold"), spreads out her own light (bhānum) in many places (purutrā); vidadhe means "spreads", extends everywhere.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—Āditya, the causer of rain
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the day that is true by nature
- बुद्धे (*buddhe*)—at the root
- उषसां (*uṣasāṃ*)—to the manifestation of the Uṣases
- इषण्यन् (*iṣaṇyan*)—urging
- मही (*mahī*)—great
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- आ विवेश (*ā viveśa*)—has pervaded with his radiance (and Uṣas also)
- मही (*mahī*)—she of great nature
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—of Mitra
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—and of Varuṇa (of Mitra and Varuṇa)
- माया (*māyā*)—being of the form of radiance
- भानुं (*bhānuṃ*)—her own light
- चंद्रेव (*caṃdreva*)—spreading it like golden lustre
- पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)—in many regions
- विदधे (*vidadhe*)—has spread

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Āditya, the causer of rain, at the root of the day that is true by nature, urging the manifestation of the Uṣases, has pervaded. Uṣas too, of great nature and being the radiance of Mitra and Varuṇa, spreads her light like golden lustre in many regions.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The showerer (of rain, the sun), urging on the dawn, at the root of the truthful (day has) pervaded the vast heaven and earth; the mighty Ushas, the golden light, as it were, of Mitra and Varuna, diffuses her lustre in different directions.

### Printed p. 524

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋतस्य बुद्धे (*ṛtasya buddhe*) — अह्नः मूले (*ahnaḥ mūle*): "at the root of the day, which is of the nature of truth" is the meaning. Earlier, when the path of Ushas was described, it was explained in that context what the path of ṛta is. The budhna of such a ṛta, which is of the nature of truth, must be understood to mean its root.
In the Ṛksaṃhitā the word budhna is commonly explained as root, support and so on. In some places it is also used as a synonym of the atmosphere (antarikṣa). But even when it is used in the sense of the atmosphere, the explanation of the Nirukta authors is that the atmosphere is called budhna because it holds and keeps the waters, that is, because it is the support of the water: सहबद्धा अस्मिन्, धृता आपः (*sahabaddhā asmin, dhṛtā āpaḥ*) (Ni. 10-44).
इंद्राय गिरो अनिशितसर्गा अपः प्रेरयं सगरस्य बुध्नात् ॥ (*iṃdrāya giro aniśitasargā apaḥ prerayaṃ sagarasya budhnāt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-89-4)
Here सगरस्य बुध्नात् (*sagarasya budhnāt*) has been explained as: that which is the support of the atmosphere itself, the deep root-region of the atmosphere. The same meaning can be taken in the present ṛk also.
माया (*māyā*) — The special meanings of this word have been given earlier in this same part. Since Ushas belongs to Mitra, Varuṇa and the others, in the present context she may be called a form of radiance that is indicative of their power.
The sixty-second sūkta.

## Sūkta 62 (Maṇḍala 3)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमा उ वामित्यष्टादशर्चं नवमं सूक्तं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । इमा
> उ द्वन्नैंद्रावरुणबार्हस्पत्यपौष्णसावित्रसौम्यमैत्रावरुणास्त्वचा अंत्यो जमदग्न्यार्षो वा चतुर्थाद्या गायत्र्य इति । कृत्सस्य विश्वामित्र ऋषिरंत्यस्य तृचस्य
> जमदग्निर्वा । अद्यास्ति स्रस्त्रिष्टुभः शिष्टाः पंचदश गायत्र्यः । प्रथमस्येंद्रावरुणा
> देवता द्वितीयस्य बृहस्पतिस्तृतीयस्य पूषा चतुर्थस्य सविता पंचमस्य सोमः
> षष्ठस्य मित्रावरुणा ॥ अभिप्लविकेषूक्ष्येषु शृतीयसवने स्तोमवृद्धौ सत्यां
> स्वस्वशस्त्रे होत्रका अंत्यसूक्तमवशेष्य स्तोमाभिशंसनार्थं तृचादिसंख्या ऋच
> आवपेयुः । तत्र मैत्रावरुणस्यावापार्थमाद्यस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च । इमा उ नां
> भ्रमयो मन्यमाना इति तिस्त्रः । आ. ७-९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning इमा उ वां (*imā u vāṃ*) has eighteen ṛks and is the ninth sūkta. Of it the Anukramaṇikā says: इमा उ द्वन्नैंद्रावरुणबार्हस्पत्यपौष्णसावित्रसौम्यमैत्रावरुणास्त्वचा अंत्यो जमदग्न्यार्षो वा चतुर्थाद्या गायत्र्य इति (*imā u dvannaiṃdrāvaruṇabārhaspatyapauṣṇasāvitrasaumyamaitrāvaruṇāstvacā aṃtyo jamadagnyārṣo vā caturthādyā gāyatrya iti*). For the whole sūkta Viśvāmitra is the seer; for the last tṛca the seer is Jamadagni, or else (Viśvāmitra). The first ones are triṣṭubh and the remaining fifteen are gāyatrī.**NOTE** The deities: of the first tṛca Indra and Varuṇa, of the second Bṛhaspati, of the third Pūṣan, of the fourth Savitṛ, of the fifth Soma, of the sixth Mitra and Varuṇa.
Use: in the abhiplava ukthya rites, at the third pressing, when the stoma is to be increased, the hotṛ-priests, each at his own śastra, leave out the last sūkta and insert tṛcas and the like, of the required number of ṛks, to announce the stomas. Of these, for the insertion of the Maitrāvaruṇa, the first tṛca is used. It is also laid down in the sūtra: इमा उ नां भ्रमयो मन्यमाना इति तिस्त्रः (*imā u nāṃ bhramayo manyamānā iti tistraḥ*) (Ā. 7-9).

### Printed p. 525

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta इमा उ वां (*imā u vāṃ*) is the ninth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has eighteen ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated: इमा उ द्वोन्यैंद्रावरुणबार्हस्पत्यपौष्टसावित्रसौम्यमैत्रावरुणास्त्रृचा अंत्यो जमदग्नार्षो वा चतुर्थाद्या गायत्र्यः (*imā u dvonyaiṃdrāvaruṇabārhaspatyapauṣṭasāvitrasaumyamaitrāvaruṇāstrṛcā aṃtyo jamadagnārṣo vā caturthādyā gāyatryaḥ*). For this whole sūkta Viśvāmitra is the seer; for the last three ṛks Viśvāmitra or Jamadagni is the seer. The first three ṛks of this sūkta are in the triṣṭubh metre; the remaining fifteen ṛks are in the gāyatrī metre. For the first tṛca, that is, the three ṛks (ṛks 1–3), Indra and Varuṇa are the deities; for the second tṛca (ṛks 4–6) Bṛhaspati, for the third tṛca (7–9) Pūṣan, for the fourth tṛca (10–12) Savitṛ, for the fifth tṛca (13–15) Soma, for the sixth tṛca (16–18) Mitra and Varuṇa are the deities. In the third pressing connected with the ukthya of the abhiplava sacrifice, when the priests of the hotṛ group recite their respective śastra-mantras, the related tṛcas of this last sūkta are to be recited for the insertion ṛks (āvapana) that are recited for the increase of the stoma; and the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa is to recite the first three ṛks for the insertion mantras (āvāpa). This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra इमा उ वां भ्रमयो मन्यमाना इति तिस्रः (*imā u vāṃ bhramayo manyamānā iti tisraḥ*) (Ā. 7-9).
Sūkta 62.
Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 62.
Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 4; Varga 9, 10, 11.
Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 18.
Ṛṣi: 1–15 Viśvāmitra; 16–18 Viśvāmitra or Jamadagni.
Devatā: 1–3 Indra and Varuṇa; 4–6 Bṛhaspati (dual); 7–9 Pūṣan; 10–12 Savitṛ; 13–15 Soma; 16–18 Mitra and Varuṇa.
Chandas: 1–3 triṣṭubh; 4–18 gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मा उ॑ वां भ्र॒मयो॒ मन्य॑माना यु॒वाव॑ते॒ न तुज्या॑  
> अभूवन् ।

> *imā u vāṃ bhramayo manyamānā yuvāvate na tujyā*  
> *abhūvan |*

### Printed p. 526

> क्वंत्यदिंद्रावरुणा यशो वां येन स्मा सिनं भरथः  
> सखिभ्यः ॥ १ ॥

> *kvaṃtyadiṃdrāvaruṇā yaśo vāṃ yena smā sinaṃ bharathaḥ*  
> *sakhibhyaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमाः । ऊं इति । नां । भ्रमयः । मन्यमानाः । युवावते । न । तुज्याः ।  
> अभूवन् ।  
> क्व । त्यत् । इंद्रावरुणा । यशः । नां । येन । स्म । सिनं । भरथः । सखिभ्यः ॥ १ ॥

> *imāḥ | ūṃ iti | nāṃ | bhramayaḥ | manyamānāḥ | yuvāvate | na | tujyāḥ |*  
> *abhūvan |*  
> *kva | tyat | iṃdrāvaruṇā | yaśaḥ | nāṃ | yena | sma | sinaṃ | bharathaḥ | sakhibhyaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणौ नां युवयोः संबंधिन्यो मन्यमाना बलिभिः शत्रुभिरभिमन्यमाना आत एव भ्रमयो भ्रमणशीला इमाः प्रजाः । उः पूरणः । युवावते । तृतीयार्थे चतुर्थि । यौवनवता बलिना शत्रुणा तुज्या हिंस्या नाभूवन् ।
> न भवंतु । अपि च नां युवयोस्तत्तादृशं यशः क्व कुत्रास्ते । येन यशसा
> सखिभ्योऽस्मभ्यं सिन्नमन्नं भरथः स्म प्रदातुं संपादयथः । तत्कास्त इत्यन्वयः ।
> यद्वा । हे इंद्रावरुणौ नां युवयोः संबंधिन्य इमा अस्माभिः क्रियमाणा
> भ्रमयो युवां प्राप्तुं भ्रमणशीला मन्यमानाः । मन्यतिरर्चतिकर्मा । युवामर्चंत्यस्ताः स्तुतयो युवावते युवाभ्यां सदृशायान्यस्मै देवाय न तुज्याः ।
> तुजतिर्दानकर्मार्थः । प्रदेया मा भूवन् । शिष्टं समानं ॥ भ्रमयः । भ्रमु
> अनवस्थाने । भ्रमेः संप्रसारणं चेतीस्त्ययः संप्रसारणं च । व्यत्ययेनांतोदात्तत्वं । युवावते । युष्मदस्मद्भां छंदसि सादृश्य उपसंख्यानमिति
> वतुप् । अविभक्तावपि युवादेशश्चांदसः । तुज्याः । तुज हिंसादाननिकेतनेषु ।
> अफ्न्यादयश्चति यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । सिनं । पिञ् बंधने ।
> इण्णॆ इङ्जुष्यविभ्यो नगिति नक् । व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, these subjects (prajāḥ) of yours are मन्यमाना (*manyamānā*), that is, are opposed by mighty enemies, and for that very reason are भ्रमयो (*bhramayo*), given to wandering. The word उः (*uḥ*) is a filler. युवावते (*yuvāvate*) has the dative in the sense of the instrumental: by an enemy who is young and mighty may they not become तुज्या (*tujyā*), to be harmed. And where is that fame of yours by which you provide food (सिन्नमन्नं (*sinnamannaṃ*)) to us, your friends, so as to give it? Thus the construction.
Or else: O Indra and Varuṇa, these (praises) of yours, made by us, are भ्रमयो (*bhramayo*), wandering in order to reach you, मन्यमानाः (*manyamānāḥ*); the verb मन्यति (*manyati*) has the sense of worshipping. These praises that worship you are न तुज्याः (*na tujyāḥ*) for another god like you; तुजति (*tujati*) has the sense of giving: let them not be given. The rest is the same.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- नां (*nāṃ*)—those belonging to you
- मन्यमानाः (*manyamānāḥ*)—those opposed by enemies
- भृमयः (*bhṛmayaḥ*)—(therefore) those who wander about bewildered
- इमाः (*imāḥ*)—these people
- युवावते (*yuvāvate*)—by a youthful enemy
- तुज्याः (*tujyāḥ*)—harmed
- न अभूवन् (*na abhūvan*)—let them not become
- येन (*yena*)—by which fame
- सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)—to us, your friends
- सिनं (*sinaṃ*)—food
- भरथः स्म (*bharathaḥ sma*)—you procure and give (such)
- नां (*nāṃ*)—your
- त्यत् यशः (*tyat yaśaḥ*)—that same renown
- क्व (*kva*)—where?

### Printed p. 527

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, may these people, who belong to you, who are opposed by enemies and for that very reason wander about bewildered, not be harmed by a youthful enemy. Where is that renown of yours by which you procure food for us, your friends?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra and Varuna, may these people who are relying upon you, and wandering about (in alarm), sustain no injury from a youthful (adversary); for where is that reputation (you enjoy) on account that you bestow sustenance on your friends.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Two kinds of meaning have been given for this mantra. In the first half, according to the first construction: इमाः वां भ्रमयः तुज्याः न अभूवन् (*imāḥ vāṃ bhramayaḥ tujyāḥ na abhūvan*). There is the prayer that those who belong to you and who wander about harmed by enemies may, by your grace, from now on not be harmed by enemies. The two words मन्यमानाः (*manyamānāḥ*) and भ्रमयः (*bhramayaḥ*) are both adjectives of इमाः (*imāḥ*). मन्यमानाः (*manyamānāḥ*) means those who are confronted by enemies, and भ्रमयः (*bhramayaḥ*) means those who wander about bewildered. Although the word युवावते (*yuvāvate*) ends in the dative case, the instrumental sense must be stated for it: यौवनवता बलिना शतु णा (*yauvanavatā balinā śatu ṇā*), "by an enemy who is young and strong"; the purport is that they should not be न तुज्याः (*na tujyāḥ*), harmed. According to the second construction: युवयोः संबधिन्यः इमाः अस्माभिः क्रियमाणाः भ्रमयः युवां प्राप्तंभ्रमणशीलाः मन्यमानाः अर्चंत्यस्ताः स्तुतयो युवावते युवाभ्यां सदृशायान्यस्मैदेवाय न तुज्याः न प्रदेयाः । (*yuvayoḥ saṃbadhinyaḥ imāḥ asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇāḥ bhramayaḥ yuvāṃ prāptaṃbhramaṇaśīlāḥ manyamānāḥ arcaṃtyastāḥ stutayo yuvāvate yuvābhyāṃ sadṛśāyānyasmaidevāya na tujyāḥ na pradeyāḥ |*). The prayer becomes: may these rites and praises performed by us not go to any other gods like you, but to you alone. According to this, the two words इमाः (*imāḥ*) and भृमयः (*bhṛmayaḥ*) are adjectives of मन्यमानाः (*manyamānāḥ*); the meaning is the praises and other rites that eagerly strive to reach you. तुज्याः (*tujyāḥ*) has the sense of giving. न तुज्याः न प्रदेयाः (*na tujyāḥ na pradeyāḥ*) is the purport.

### Printed p. 528
भ्रमयः (*bhramayaḥ*) — भ्रमणशीलाः (*bhramaṇaśīlāḥ*). Generally this word is an adjective of a thing that has the action of moving about, or is a synonym for a thing showing such action. For example:
धारावरा मरुतो धृष्णोऽजसो मृगा न भीमास्तविषीभिरर्चिनः । अग्नयो न शुशुचाना ऋजीषिणो भृमिं धमंतो अप गा अवृण्वत ॥ (*dhārāvarā maruto dhṛṣṇo 'jaso mṛgā na bhīmāstaviṣībhirarcinaḥ | agnayo na śuśucānā ṛjīṣiṇo bhṛmiṃ dhamaṃto apa gā avṛṇvata ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-1)
There भ्राम्यंतं मेघं (*bhrāmyaṃtaṃ meghaṃ*) has been given as the meaning: the moving cloud. The Maruts, who make trees and the like all move, who are terrible and brilliant, made the wandering clouds move with still greater speed for the sake of water; here the speed of the motion too is indicated. In explaining the purport of this word in the same context, the scholar Max Müller has given his opinion in this way:
भृमि (*bhṛmi*) Seems to me a name of the cloud, driven about by the wind. The Taithiriyas read भृमिं (*bhṛmiṃ*) and Sayana explains it by मेघं धमंतश्चालयंतः (*meghaṃ dhamaṃtaścālayaṃtaḥ*). In most passages, no doubt, भृमि (*bhṛmi*) means quick, fresh and is opposed to रध्र (*radhra*), (4-32-2 ; 7-56-20) In I. 31-17, as applied to अग्नि (*agni*) it may mean quick. But in our passage, that meaning is impossible, and I prefer the tradional meaning of the cloud. Sayana's explanation according to which भृमि (*bhṛmi*) is a musical instrument, may rest on some traditional authority. [Sacred Books of the East. Vol. 32. P. 288]
In this mantra (2-31 4)**NOTE** भ्रमि (*bhrami*) must be understood to mean a cloud, and moreover a cloud scattered by the Maruts. Sāyaṇa too has indicated this same opinion. In many contexts it also indicates speed of motion, or the sense "new" may also be proper. For example,
इमे रद्रं चिन्मरुतो जनंति चिद्यथा वसवो जुषंत ॥ (*ime radraṃ cinmaruto janaṃti cidyathā vasavo juṣaṃta ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-20)
Here the word भृमि (*bhṛmi*) indicates a meaning opposed to the meaning of the word रध्र (*radhra*). रध्र (*radhra*) means a prosperous man, and भृमि (*bhṛmi*) a man in the opposite condition. That is, the रध्र (*radhra*) is well settled; the poor man must wander about. Since constant wandering is an assured activity, the poor man with such a quality is indeed denoted by the word भृमि (*bhṛmi*). In some places Sāyaṇa

### Printed p. 529
has explained this word as a special musical instrument, an aid to song; it is also a synonym for horses and the like that have swift motion. In this and similar ways the scholar Max-Müller has given his opinion. Even when two meanings are taken for the word भृमि (*bhṛmi*) in the present ṛk, a devout man or a praise (stuti)**NOTE**, motion shows itself to be the chief quality. If it is taken as a man, he is one driven away by the enemy and wandering about bewildered; if it is taken as praise, it is something wandering eagerly in order to go swiftly and reach the deity.
मन्यमानाः (*manyamānāḥ*) — The Nirukta authors have read the word मन्यते (*manyate*) both among the names of the sense of radiance (Ni. 2-6) and among the names of the sense of worshipping (Ni. 3-14). In the present context, if it is taken as praise, it means either a radiant praise or a praise worthy of worship. According to the first construction, अभिमन्यमानाः (*abhimanyamānāḥ*) means those who are struck and driven away by enemies.
सिनं (*sinaṃ*) — The word sina is read among the names of food (Ni. 2-7). As is said in places such as सुमंगलं सिनवदस्तु सातं (*sumaṃgalaṃ sinavadastu sātaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-102-11), here too the meaning is food. In some contexts it can also mean reward. But in the four or five contexts in the Ṛksaṃhitā, this word is used in the sense of food.

> हे इंद्रावरुणौ रयीयन् रयिमात्मन इच्छन्नयमु पुरुतमो वैदिककर्मप्रवृत्ततयातिशयेन पुरुर्महान्यजमानोऽवसे रक्षणायान्नाय वा वां युवां

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, this sacrificer, रयीयन् (*rayīyan*), desiring wealth for himself, is पुरुतमः (*purutamaḥ*), exceedingly great (puru) through being engaged in Vedic rites, for protection or for food, (the text breaks off here, in the middle of the sentence).

### Printed p. 530

> शश्वत्तमं सर्वदा जोहवीति । भृशमाह्वयति । मरुद्धिर्देवविशेषैर्दिना पृथिव्या च
> सजोषौ संगच्छंतौ युवां मे मम हवं युष्मदीयमाह्वानं शृणुतं ॥
> पुरुतमः । तमपो व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वं । जोहवीति । ह्वयतेर्यज्लुक्यभ्यस्तस्य चेति संप्रसारणे रूपं । दिवा । ऊडिदमिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । पृथिव्या ।
> उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादित्युदात्तत्वं । हवं । ह्वयतेर्भावेनुपसर्गस्येत्यप् ।
> प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes his explanation of the verse. The worshipper जोहवीति (*johavīti*) calls you "constantly" (शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*): at all times), that is, he summons you vehemently. Associated (सजोषौ (*sajoṣau*)) with the Maruts, who are a special class of gods, and with heaven and earth, you two, Indra and Varuṇa, are to hear my invocation addressed to you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- रयियॆन् (*rayiyèn*)—desiring wealth
- अयमु पुरुतमः (*ayamu purutamaḥ*)—this sacrificer, eminent through the performance of rites
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you two
- शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*)—always
- जोहवीति (*johavīti*)—calls
- मरुद्भिः (*marudbhiḥ*)—with the Maruts
- दिवा (*divā*)—with the presiding deity of the heavenly world
- शृथिव्या च (*śṛthivyā ca*)—and with the earth
- सजोषा (*sajoṣā*)—you who are united
- मे (*me*)—my
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—invocation in the form of praise
- शृणुतं (*śṛṇutaṃ*)—hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, this sacrificer, eminent through the performance of rites, calls you always, desiring wealth and seeking protection. You who are united with the Maruts, with the presiding deity of the heavenly world and with the earth, hear my invocation in the form of praise.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Most diligent (in pious rites) this your worshipper), Indra and Varuna, desirous of wealth, incessantly invokes you for protection: associated with the Maruts, with heaven and earth, hear my invocation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

रयीयन् (*rayīyan*)—रयिं आत्मन इच्छन् (*rayiṃ ātmana icchan*): desiring wealth for himself. This states the sacrificer's wish.

पुरुतमः (*purutamaḥ*)—वैदिककर्मप्रवृत्ततॆया अतिशयेन पुरुः महान् (*vaidikakarmapravṛttatèyā atiśayena puruḥ mahān*): exceedingly great (पुरुः (*puruḥ*)) through being engaged in Vedic rites. Because the sacrificer acquires greatness by performing the sacrifices and other rites prescribed by rule, the epithet पुरुतमः (*purutamaḥ*) is used. The meaning is either "one possessed of the utmost greatness" or "one possessed of abundant ritual action".
