The sūtra छंदोभिधानान्नेति चेन्न (*chaṃdobhidhānānneti cenna*) (1-1-26) was likewise explained above, showing that the Gāyatrī as metre is not merely of eight syllables, but that the Supreme Brahman itself is indicated by this metre.

गायत्राख्यच्छंदोद्वारेण तदनुगते ब्रह्मणि चेतसोऽर्पणं चित्तसमाधानमनेन ब्राह्मणवाक्येन निगद्यते । (*gāyatrākhyacchaṃdodvāreṇa tadanugate brahmaṇi cetaso 'rpaṇaṃ cittasamādhānamanena brāhmaṇavākyena nigadyate |*) (Bra. Sū. 80. 1-1-25)**NOTE**

It is understood that through the metre called Gāyatra one should wholly offer the mind to Brahman, who pervades it, and practise meditation of that nature. In the present prayer भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि (*bhargo devasya dhīmahi*) the word धीमहि (*dhīmahi*) conveys both knowledge and meditation. Sāyaṇa has given the purport of the word धीमहि (*dhīmahi*) as परब्रह्मात्मकं तेजः धैयतया मनसा धारयामः (*parabrahmātmakaṃ tejaḥ dhaiyatayā manasā dhārayāmaḥ*). In places such as शाधि यां देवतामुपास्ये (*śādhi yāṃ devatāmupāsye*)**NOTE** and तं पश्यते निष्कलं ध्यायमानः (*taṃ paśyate niṣkalaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ*) (Mu. U. 3-1-8)**NOTE**, the three roots उपास् (*upās*), विद् (*vid*) and धै (*dhai*) are all used in the sense of knowledge consisting of meditation. In the same way, when it says भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि (*bhargo devasya dhīmahi*), the purport is likewise meditation consisting of knowledge. But one must also understand how this meditation consisting of knowledge is possible through the Gāyatrī, and what its manner is.

युंजते मन उत युंजते धियो विप्रा विप्रस्य बृहतो विपश्चितः । वि होत्रा दधे वयुनाविदेक इन्मही देवस्य सवितुः परिष्टुतिः ॥ (*yuṃjate mana uta yuṃjate dhiyo viprā viprasya bṛhato vipaścitaḥ | vi hotrā dadhe vayunāvideka inmahī devasya savituḥ pariṣṭutiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-1)**NOTE**

### Printed p. 615

In this meditation, which describes how the wise ṛṣis concentrate their minds and perform meditation on Savitṛ, everything that man is to meditate on is indicated. But what should the manner of this meditation be? What is its object? How is the Gāyatrī the chief means for this meditation directed to Brahman? Or how does realisation of Brahman, called Gāyatra, come from meditation in the form of the Gāyatrī?

**25. The nature of the Praṇava, which is the means of meditation and consists of the Vyāhṛtis.**

तज्योतिर्यज्योतिः स आदित्यः स वा एष ओमित्येतदात्माभवत् स त्रेधात्मानं व्यकुरुता ओमिति तिस्रो मात्रा एताभिः सर्वमिदमोतं प्रोतं चैवास्मीत्येवं ह्याहृतद्वा आदित्य ओमित्येवं ध्यायत आत्मानं युंजीतेति॥ (*tajyotiryajyotiḥ sa ādityaḥ sa vā eṣa omityetadātmābhavat sa tredhātmānaṃ vyakurutā omiti tisro mātrā etābhiḥ sarvamidamotaṃ protaṃ caivāsmītyevaṃ hyāhṛtadvā āditya omityevaṃ dhyāyata ātmānaṃ yuṃjīteti‖*) (Mai. U. 6-3)

The light of Āditya described above evolved in the form of Oṃ. It became threefold. It was also stated above that the whole world is woven together, as warp and woof, by this Oṃkāra, which consists of the three Vyāhṛtis. Therefore realisation of this light of Āditya is possible only through the Praṇava, which consists of the Vyāhṛtis and of Oṃkāra and indicates the whole world beginning with Bhūḥ. By meditation of the nature of the Praṇava, the unity of all the worlds, though they are diverse, is also directly realised.

एतत्तेजो यदसावादित्य ओमित्येतदक्षरस्य चैतत् तस्मादोमित्यनेनैतदुपासीताजस्रं इत्येकोऽस्य संबोधयिता ॥ (*etattejo yadasāvāditya omityetadakṣarasya caitat tasmādomityanenaitadupāsītājasraṃ ityeko 'sya saṃbodhayitā ‖*) (Mai. U. 6-4)

Āditya, who is the one awakener (illuminator) of the whole universe and of the nature of the Praṇava, is to be known only through meditation in the form of Oṃkāra. But the relation between the Gāyatrī and the Praṇava, when they serve as the means of meditation, has been stated above. The nature of both is of the form of the Vyāhṛtis beginning with Bhū. Moreover the Praṇava is itself a part of the Gāyatrī.

नवाक्षराणि गायत्र्यष्टौ तानि यान्यन्वाह प्रणवो नवमः ॥ (*navākṣarāṇi gāyatryaṣṭau tāni yānyanvāha praṇavo navamaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-4-1-15)

### Printed p. 616

The Gāyatrī consists of nine syllables. The Praṇava, which is the syllable Oṃ, is the ninth. The Praṇava is a part of the mantra that is to be recited as eight-syllabled. The passage thus shows that the Praṇava, which must always be recited together with the Gāyatrī (itself a means of meditation), is also of the nature of the Gāyatrī. In the same way as the Gāyatrī is praised, in the words गायत्रि वा इदग्ं सर्व० भूतं (*gāyatri vā idagṃ sarva0 bhūtaṃ*) and so on, as the all-pervading form of the Supreme Brahman, it is shown that no mantra is higher than the Praṇava, since it expounds the Brahman-principle that lies beyond the three times: न हि प्रणवादधिकं किंचिन्मंत्रजात्रमस्ति त्रिकालातीतस्य ब्रह्मणः प्रतिपादकत्वात्. (*na hi praṇavādadhikaṃ kiṃcinmaṃtrajātramasti trikālātītasya brahmaṇaḥ pratipādakatvāt.*). The greatness of this Praṇava is described thus:

ओमित्येतदक्षरमिदग्ं सर्वं तस्योपव्याख्यानं भूतं भवद्भविष्यदिति सर्वमोंकार एव । यच्चान्यत्रिकालातीतं तदप्योंकार एव ॥ (*omityetadakṣaramidagṃ sarvaṃ tasyopavyākhyānaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavadbhaviṣyaditi sarvamoṃkāra eva | yaccānyatrikālātītaṃ tadapyoṃkāra eva ‖*) (Mā. U. 1) **NOTE**

The whole universe consists of Oṃkāra. Therefore the Praṇava in the form of Oṃkāra is the Supreme Brahman. Commenting on this sentence, Śrī Śaṅkarācārya says:

यदिदं अर्थजातं अभिधेयभूतं तस्य अभिधानाव्यतिरेकात् अभिधानस्य च ओंकाराव्यतिरेकात् ओंकार एवेदं सर्वं परं च ब्रह्म अभिधानाभिधेयोपायपूर्वकमेव गम्यत इति ओंकार एव । तस्य एतस्य परापरब्रह्मरूपस्य अक्षरस्य ओं इत्येतस्य उपव्याख्यानं ॥ (*yadidaṃ arthajātaṃ abhidheyabhūtaṃ tasya abhidhānāvyatirekāt abhidhānasya ca oṃkārāvyatirekāt oṃkāra evedaṃ sarvaṃ paraṃ ca brahma abhidhānābhidheyopāyapūrvakameva gamyata iti oṃkāra eva | tasya etasya parāparabrahmarūpasya akṣarasya oṃ ityetasya upavyākhyānaṃ ‖*) (Mā. U. Śaṅkara-bhāṣya 1) **NOTE**

All the things in the world that are denoted by name and form, and are thus objects of denotation, consist of Oṃkāra. The denotation itself (the manner of denoting) is also Oṃkāra. Since the Supreme Brahman too is known only by way of the means called denotation and the denoted, it too is Oṃkāra. The explanation of this syllable Oṃ, which is of the form of the higher and the lower Brahman, is a means to the understanding of Brahman and therefore stands close to Brahman; thus he has shown the identity of the Praṇava with Brahman. Here only the significance of the Praṇava at the time of reciting the Gāyatrī, which is a means to the realisation of Brahman, is examined. Just as the Upaniṣad texts describe the Gāyatrī, which is of the form of Brahman, as the direct means to the knowledge of Brahman, so too the Praṇava, which is a part of the Gāyatrī and of the form of Brahman, is a chief limb of the meditation in the form of the Gāyatrī, and is a direct means to the realisation of Brahman, which is one with it; this is also stated clearly.

एतद्वाव तत्स्वरूपं नभसः खेंतर्भूतस्य यत् परं तेजस्तत्रेधाभिहितमग्नावादित्ये प्राण एतद्वाव तत् स्वरूपं नभसः खेंतर्भूतस्य यदो- मित्येतदक्षरमनेनैव तदुद्भुद्यत्युदयत्युच्छूसत्यजस्रं ब्रह्मधीयालंबं .... .... .... .... ॥ (*etadvāva tatsvarūpaṃ nabhasaḥ kheṃtarbhūtasya yat paraṃ tejastatredhābhihitamagnāvāditye prāṇa etadvāva tat svarūpaṃ nabhasaḥ kheṃtarbhūtasya yado- mityetadakṣaramanenaiva tadudbhudyatyudayatyucchūsatyajasraṃ brahmadhīyālaṃbaṃ .... .... .... .... ‖*) (Maitrī Upaniṣad 7-11) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 617

The space in the lotus of the heart is the supreme light. It has become transformed into the forms of Āditya, Vāyu and Agni (this has been explained earlier). The Brahman-principle that is of the nature of space in the lotus of the heart is itself the Praṇava in the form of Oṃkāra. From this Praṇava alone the supreme light arises, rises, and spreads to the whole universe. This light is the support of the universe. The Gāyatrī form, which is the mother of the metres and the essence of the Vedas, is of the nature of this Praṇava. (एतद्वाव तत्स्वरूपं (*etadvāva tatsvarūpaṃ*)) In the time of meditation, contemplating this is contemplating Brahman. Through this complete contemplation one can know that the goal and the means are one. That this Praṇava is Brahman is shown thus:

ओमिति ब्रह्म । ओमितीदग्ं सर्वं । ओमित्येतदनुकृति ह स्म वा अप्यो श्रावयेत्याश्रावयंति । ओमिति सामानि गायंति । ओग्ं शोमिति शस्त्राणि शग्ंसंति । ओमित्यध्वर्युः प्रतिगरं प्रतिगृणाति । ओमिति ब्रह्मा प्रसौति । ओमित्यग्निहोत्रमनुजानाति । ओमिति ब्राह्मणः प्रवक्ष्यन्नाह ब्रह्मोपाप्नवानीति । ब्रह्मैवोपाप्णोति ॥ (*omiti brahma | omitīdagṃ sarvaṃ | omityetadanukṛti ha sma vā apyo śrāvayetyāśrāvayaṃti | omiti sāmāni gāyaṃti | ogṃ śomiti śastrāṇi śagṃsaṃti | omityadhvaryuḥ pratigaraṃ pratigṛṇāti | omiti brahmā prasauti | omityagnihotramanujānāti | omiti brāhmaṇaḥ pravakṣyannāha brahmopāpnavānīti | brahmaivopāpṇoti ‖*) (Trai. U. 1-8) **NOTE**

Oṃ (the Praṇava) is Brahman. The whole universe is Oṃ. That is the imitation. Those who sing the Sāman, and the Adhvaryu and others, utter the response (pratigara) with it. One who studies the Veda, before beginning study, with the thought "Let me obtain Brahman", obtains Brahman itself by uttering Oṃkāra. Oṃ means the Supreme Self; by uttering it the Supreme Self is attained.

स य एतदेवं विद्वानक्षरं प्रणत्येतदेवाक्षरं स्वरममृतमभयं प्रविशति तत्प्रविश्य यदमृता देवास्त्रदमृतो भवति ॥ (*sa ya etadevaṃ vidvānakṣaraṃ praṇatyetadevākṣaraṃ svaramamṛtamabhayaṃ praviśati tatpraviśya yadamṛtā devāstradamṛto bhavati ‖*) (Chā. U. 1-4-5)

This Praṇava in the form of Oṃkāra is immortal and of the nature of fearlessness. The gods too took refuge in it and obtained immortality and fearlessness. Those who know this truth and take refuge in this sound in the form of Oṃkāra become immortal and obtain fearlessness. How is it possible that the state of mind indicated by the mantra beginning युंजते मन उत युंजते (*yuṃjate mana uta yuṃjate*), and the meditative search for knowledge in it, accomplish the goal through the power of the Praṇava?—

### Printed p. 618

प्रणवो धनुः शरो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते । अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत्तन्मयो भवेत् ॥ (*praṇavo dhanuḥ śaro hyātmā brahma tallakṣyamucyate | apramattena veddhavyaṃ śaravattanmayo bhavet ‖*) (Mu. U. 2-2-4) **NOTE**

The Praṇava is the bow. The Self is the arrow. Brahman is the target. It must be pierced without heedlessness. One must become one with it, like the arrow. Just as the bow is the cause of the arrow's going and reaching the target, so the Praṇava must be the means by which the arrow called the Self reaches the target called the Imperishable. Thus the nature of the Praṇava as a means of meditation is shown. And further:

यः पुनरेतं त्रिमात्रेणोमित्येतेनैवाक्षरेण परं पुरुषमभिध्यायीत स तेजसि सूर्ये संपन्नः । यथा पादोदरस्त्वचा विनिर्मुच्यत एवं ह वै स पाप्मना विनिर्मुक्तः स सामभिरुन्नीयते ब्रह्मलोकं स एतस्माज्जीवघनात्परात्परं पुरिशयं पुरुषमीक्षते ॥ (*yaḥ punaretaṃ trimātreṇomityetenaivākṣareṇa paraṃ puruṣamabhidhyāyīta sa tejasi sūrye saṃpannaḥ | yathā pādodarastvacā vinirmucyata evaṃ ha vai sa pāpmanā vinirmuktaḥ sa sāmabhirunnīyate brahmalokaṃ sa etasmājjīvaghanātparātparaṃ puriśayaṃ puruṣamīkṣate ‖*) (Praśna. U. 5-5) **NOTE**

The man who meditates on the Supreme Person with the help of the three mātrās a, u, m — which are the parts of the Praṇava and which also denote the three worlds Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, the parts of the Gāyatrī — attains union with the radiance of Āditya. As a serpent casts off its slough and becomes clean, such a worshipper too wholly casts off his sin and becomes pure. He is carried to the world of Brahman by means of the Sāman chant. He obtains the vision of the Supreme Self, who is higher than the whole mass of conscious living beings and dwells within the heart. And the fruit of this meditation is:

तिस्रो मात्रा मृत्युमत्यः प्रयुक्ता अन्नोन्यसक्ता अनविप्रयुक्ताः । क्रियासु बाह्याभ्यंतरमध्यमासु सम्यक्प्रयुक्तासु न कंपते ज्ञः ॥ (*tisro mātrā mṛtyumatyaḥ prayuktā annonyasaktā anaviprayuktāḥ | kriyāsu bāhyābhyaṃtaramadhyamāsu samyakprayuktāsu na kaṃpate jñaḥ ‖*) (Pra. U. 5-6) **NOTE**

If these three mātrās are separated and used without relation of one to another, they become destructive. If, in all the bodily actions of man — external, internal and intermediate — one worships by joining them all together so as to bring them into harmony, and obtains their power for all one's dealings, then the man, fearing nothing in any circumstance, remains unshaken.

ऋग्भिरेतं यजुर्भिरंतरिक्षं सामभिर्यत्तत्कवयो वेदयंते । तमोंकारेणैवायतनेनान्वेति विद्वान्यत्तच्छांतमजरममृतभयं परं चेति॥ (*ṛgbhiretaṃ yajurbhiraṃtarikṣaṃ sāmabhiryattatkavayo vedayaṃte | tamoṃkāreṇaivāyatanenānveti vidvānyattacchāṃtamajaramamṛtabhayaṃ paraṃ ceti‖*) (Pra. U. 5-7)

### Printed p. 619

The man who worships in this manner obtains this world by the Ṛks, the atmosphere by the Yajus, and by the Sāmans the world of Āditya which the seers perceive. And further, with the help of Oṃkāra, which is the synthesis of all these, he realises the principle that is tranquil, free from old age, free from death, free from fear and higher than the highest.

By these descriptions and explanations above, the common nature of the Gāyatrī and the Praṇava has been indicated. Although the order of utterance in time states that, from the practical standpoint, the Praṇava comes first and the Gāyatrī afterwards, the nature and power of the Praṇava are indeed the nature and power of the Gāyatrī.

**26. The Praṇava and the Gāyatrī are both forms of Brahman; the fruit of worshipping Brahman in the form of the Vyāhṛtis Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Suvaḥ, Mahaḥ.**

If these two, which are direct means to the realisation of Brahman, are said to be forms of Brahman, then it becomes necessary at once to examine such matters as: what are the Vyāhṛtis, which are worldly divisions of the Brahman indicated as Savitṛ and which are parts common to the Praṇava and the Gāyatrī; how many are their divisions; and what is the nature of the Vyāhṛtis as aids to meditation that is of the nature of the Praṇava and of the Gāyatrī. It was stated above that the Maitrī Upaniṣad explains the letters a, u, m of the Praṇava as masculine, feminine and neuter, and in other ways. Similar divisions are given, somewhat differently, in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad also. The divisions in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad have gained great importance from the standpoint of spiritual knowledge and of worship. Śaṅkarācārya too has given these divisions great prominence from the standpoint of worship and explained them at length. The divisions are given thus in the Taittirīya:

अनंतरं व्याहृत्यात्मनो ब्रह्मणः अंतरुपासनं स्वाराज्यफलं प्रस्तुयते (*anaṃtaraṃ vyāhṛtyātmano brahmaṇaḥ aṃtarupāsanaṃ svārājyaphalaṃ prastuyate*) (Tai. U. Śa. Bhā. 1-5) **NOTE**

Having stated that worship concerning the Saṃhitās also is a means to knowledge, Śaṅkarācārya says in his introduction to the worship of Brahman through the Vyāhṛtis that the method is now stated of worshipping inwardly the Brahman in the form of the Vyāhṛtis, which gives the fruit called svārājya. Its order is as follows—

### Printed p. 620

भूर्भुवः सुवरिति वा एतास्तिस्रो व्याहृतयः । तासा मुहस्मै तां चतुर्थीं। माहाचमस्यः प्रवेदयते । मह इति । तत् ब्रह्म । स आत्मा । अंगान्यन्या देवताः । भूरिति वा अयं लोकः । भुव इत्यंतरिक्षं । सुवरित्यसौ लोकः । मह इत्यादित्यः । आदित्येन वाव सर्वॆ लोका महीयंते । भूरिति ना अग्निः । भुव इति वायुः । सुवरित्यादित्यः । मह इति चंद्रमाः । चंद्रमसा वाव सर्वाणि ज्योतिर्गंषि महीयंते । भूरिति वा ऋचः । भुव इति सामानि । सुवरिति यजूगंषि । मह इति ब्रह्म । ब्रह्मणा वाव सर्वे वेदा महीयंते । भूरिति वै प्राणः । भुव इत्यपानः । सुवरिति व्यानः । मह इत्यन्नं । अन्नेन वाव सर्वॆ प्राणा महीयंते । ता वा एताश्चतस्रश्चतुर्धा। चितस्रश्चतस्रो व्याहृतयः । ता यो वेद । स वेद ब्रह्म । सर्वेऽस्मै देवा बलिमावहंति ॥ (*bhūrbhuvaḥ suvariti vā etāstisro vyāhṛtayaḥ | tāsā muhasmai tāṃ caturthīṃ| māhācamasyaḥ pravedayate | maha iti | tat brahma | sa ātmā | aṃgānyanyā devatāḥ | bhūriti vā ayaṃ lokaḥ | bhuva ityaṃtarikṣaṃ | suvarityasau lokaḥ | maha ityādityaḥ | ādityena vāva sarvè lokā mahīyaṃte | bhūriti nā agniḥ | bhuva iti vāyuḥ | suvarityādityaḥ | maha iti caṃdramāḥ | caṃdramasā vāva sarvāṇi jyotirgaṃṣi mahīyaṃte | bhūriti vā ṛcaḥ | bhuva iti sāmāni | suvariti yajūgaṃṣi | maha iti brahma | brahmaṇā vāva sarve vedā mahīyaṃte | bhūriti vai prāṇaḥ | bhuva ityapānaḥ | suvariti vyānaḥ | maha ityannaṃ | annena vāva sarvè prāṇā mahīyaṃte | tā vā etāścatasraścaturdhā| citasraścatasro vyāhṛtayaḥ | tā yo veda | sa veda brahma | sarve 'smai devā balimāvahaṃti ‖*) (Kṛ. U. 1-5) **NOTE**

The three Vyāhṛtis Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Suvaḥ, which are limbs, are the three; the fourth Vyāhṛti, Mahaḥ, was made known by Māhācamasya. (ऋष्यनुस्मरणमपि उपासनांगं (*ṛṣyanusmaraṇamapi upāsanāṃgaṃ*) — remembering the seer's name is also a limb of worship.) This Vyāhṛti, bearing the name Mahaḥ, is the great Brahman. It is the all-pervading Self. All the rest are its limbs.

इतराश्च वाहृतयो लोकाः देवाः वेदाः प्राणाश्च महः इत्यनेन व्याहृत्यात्मना आदित्यचंद्रब्रह्मान्नभूतेन वाप्यंते यतः ॥ (*itarāśca vāhṛtayo lokāḥ devāḥ vedāḥ prāṇāśca mahaḥ ityanena vyāhṛtyātmanā ādityacaṃdrabrahmānnabhūtena vāpyaṃte yataḥ ‖*) (Śa. Bhā.) **NOTE**

All the worlds beginning with Bhūḥ, the gods, the Vedas and the vital airs are pervaded by the Self in the form of the great Vyāhṛti, which has the forms of the sun, the moon, Brahman and food, called Mahaḥ. Therefore all of them are limbs of this Self called Mahaḥ. In the statement अंगान्यन्या देवताः (*aṃgānyanyā devatāḥ*), the word "deities" is used as an indicator; all worldly beings pervaded by the Self are included in it. The order of the division ता वा एताश्च तस्रश्चतुर्धा (*tā vā etāśca tasraścaturdhā*) is as follows—

(1) Bhūḥ is this world. Bhuvaḥ is the atmosphere. Suvaḥ is the world of heaven. Mahaḥ is Āditya. By Āditya all the worlds become great. This is the Supreme Brahman, the inner controller of all.

(2) Bhūḥ is Agni, Bhuvaḥ is Vāyu, Suvaḥ is Āditya. Mahaḥ is the moon. By the moon all the lights become great. (It was stated earlier, in Sūkta 1-164, that this moon-world is beyond the world of Āditya and does not mean the familiar disc of the moon.

### Printed p. 621

(3) Bhūḥ is the Ṛks. Bhuvaḥ is the Sāmans. Suvaḥ is the Yajus texts. Mahaḥ is Brahman; by Brahman all become great.

(4) In the fourth division, Bhūḥ is prāṇa, Bhuvaḥ is apāna, Suvaḥ is vyāna, and Mahaḥ is food. Food is the cause of the greatness of all the vital airs.

Thus each of them is of four kinds. He who knows their nature fully is as one who has known the complete Brahman. All the gods serve him and offer him tribute.

The method of worship, which is the means to the realisation of the Supreme Brahman — of that form of Brahman explained above, in which all the other deities named Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Suvaḥ are limbs of the Brahman known as Mahaḥ — is also stated in the Taittirīya thus:

स य एषोंतर्हृदय आकाशः । तस्मिन्नयं पुरुषो मनोमयः । अमृतो हिरण्मयः । अंतरेण तालुके । य एषस्तन इवावलंबते । सेंद्रयोनिः । यत्रासौ केशांतो विवर्तते । व्यपोह्य शीर्षकपाले । भूरित्यग्नौ प्रतितिष्ठति । भुव इति वायौ । सुवरित्यादित्ये । मह इति ब्रह्मणि । अप्पोति स्वाराज्यं । अप्पोति मनसस्पतिं । वाक्पतिश्चक्षुष्पतिः । श्रोत्रपतिर्विज्ञानपतिः । एतत्ततो भवति । आकाशशरीरं ब्रह्म । सत्यात्मप्राणारावं मन आनंदं शांतिसमृद्धममृतं । इति प्राचीनयोगोपास्त्व ॥ (*sa ya eṣoṃtarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ | tasminnayaṃ puruṣo manomayaḥ | amṛto hiraṇmayaḥ | aṃtareṇa tāluke | ya eṣastana ivāvalaṃbate | seṃdrayoniḥ | yatrāsau keśāṃto vivartate | vyapohya śīrṣakapāle | bhūrityagnau pratitiṣṭhati | bhuva iti vāyau | suvarityāditye | maha iti brahmaṇi | appoti svārājyaṃ | appoti manasaspatiṃ | vākpatiścakṣuṣpatiḥ | śrotrapatirvijñānapatiḥ | etattato bhavati | ākāśaśarīraṃ brahma | satyātmaprāṇārāvaṃ mana ānaṃdaṃ śāṃtisamṛddhamamṛtaṃ | iti prācīnayogopāstva ‖*) (Kṛ. U. 1-6) **NOTE**

In the space within the heart there is a Person, consisting of mind, immortal, golden. What hangs between the two jaws like a breast, where the ends of the hair part in two, is the womb of Indra. The worshipper is established in Agni called Bhūḥ, in Vāyu called Bhuvaḥ, in Āditya called Suvaḥ, in Brahman called Mahaḥ. He obtains svārājya. He becomes lord of the mind. He becomes lord of the speech organs, of the eyes, of the ears, and of the faculties of knowledge. Beyond that, he is established in Brahman, whose body is space, who is the Self of all, who delights in the vital airs, whose mind is bliss, who is rich in peace and immortal, and he becomes of the form of Brahman itself.

तेषु आत्मभावेन स्थित्वा आप्नोति ब्रह्मभूतः स्वाराज्यं स्वराड्भावं । स्वयमेव राजा अधिपतिर्भवति अंगभूतानां देवानां यथाब्रह्म ॥ (*teṣu ātmabhāvena sthitvā āpnoti brahmabhūtaḥ svārājyaṃ svarāḍbhāvaṃ | svayameva rājā adhipatirbhavati aṃgabhūtānāṃ devānāṃ yathābrahma ‖*) (Śa. Bhā.)

### Printed p. 622

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Abiding in all the vyāhṛtis with the feeling of identity with the Self, and becoming Brahman itself, he obtains svārājya, that is, the state of being self-ruling. He himself is the king. Just as Brahman is the overlord of the gods who are its limbs, so he too is the overlord. Just as all the gods offer tribute to Brahman, so they offer it to him. Just as Brahman, being the Self of all, is lord of all minds, so he too becomes. For that reason he becomes one who delights in the Self, one whose nature is bliss, one of tranquil mind, one free from death. From this it is understood that the instruction given to Prācīnayogya, "Worship Brahman who has the vyāhṛtis as its Self," teaches the nature of the worship that takes the form of the vyāhṛtis.

**27. The Gāyatrī and the Praṇava, which praise the divine song of Brahman in the form of the Āditya, are themselves of the nature of song.**

Thus the Śrutis praise the Praṇava and the Gāyatrī, which consist of the vyāhṛtis bhūḥ and the rest, as the direct means of meditating on the Supreme Reality that pervades all the worlds, bhūḥ and the rest, designated by their syllables. The great mantra Gāyatrī has been described as गायति (*gāyati*) and त्रायते च (*trāyate ca*) ("it protects and it sings"), and so its special quality is shown. In the same way the Praṇava, which is of the nature of the syllable Om, is also praised.

ओं इत्येतदक्षरमुद्गीथमुपासीत । ओमिति ह्युद्धायति ॥ (*oṃ ityetadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta | omiti hyuddhāyati ‖*) (Bhā. U. 8-1-1) **NOTE**

The syllable Om is to be worshipped as the udgītha. It praises the reality of Brahman in the form of song. This Brahman-reality, which pervades the universe, abides in the form of the udgītha.

अथ खलु य उद्गीथः स प्रणवो यः प्रणव स उद्गीथ इत्यसौ वा आदित्य उद्गीथ एष प्रणव ओमिति ह्येष स्वरन्नेति ॥ (*atha khalu ya udgīthaḥ sa praṇavo yaḥ praṇava sa udgītha ityasau vā āditya udgītha eṣa praṇava omiti hyeṣa svaranneti ‖*) (Chā. U. 1.-5-8)

The udgītha is the praṇava; the praṇava is the udgītha. The Āditya is the udgītha and is of the nature of the praṇava. The Brahman who is in the form of the Āditya is the one that is called praṇava and udgītha; the Puruṣa who dwells within the heart of a person is also in this very form. How?

अथ य एषोऽंतरक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यते सैवर्काम .... .... यावमुप गोष्णौ गोष्णौ यन्नाम तन्नाम ॥ (*atha ya eṣo 'ṃtarakṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate saivarkāma .... .... yāvamupa goṣṇau goṣṇau yannāma tannāma ‖*) (Śrī. Ṭi. Si. 2-5) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 623

Just as in the world of the Āditya the Supreme Reality moves about in the form of song, so the reality within the person also moves about in the form of song, by the same name and in the same manner. The meaning is that this divine Puruṣa, who is of the nature of song, is to be worshipped with the praṇava, which is of the nature of song and protects the world, and with the great Gāyatrī mantra. By the recitation of this Gāyatrī, which is the direct means to the realisation of Brahman and is itself of the form of Brahman, all the sins of a human being are destroyed.

अग्निरेव मुखं यदि ह वा अपि बह्विवाग्नावभ्यादधति सर्वमेव तत्संदहत्येवं हैवैवं विद्यद्यपि बह्विव पापं कुरुते सर्वमेव तत्संप्स्याय शुद्धः पूतोऽजरोऽमृतः संभवति ॥ (*agnireva mukhaṃ yadi ha vā api bahvivāgnāvabhyādadhati sarvameva tatsaṃdahatyevaṃ haivaivaṃ vidyadyapi bahviva pāpaṃ kurute sarvameva tatsaṃpsyāya śuddhaḥ pūto 'jaro 'mṛtaḥ saṃbhavati ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 5-14-8)

The mouth of the Gāyatrī is Agni. Just as whatever substance, however great in quantity, is placed in fire, the fire consumes it entirely, so for a man who knows the reality of the Gāyatrī, however many sins he may have committed, all his sins are destroyed and he becomes ageless, immortal, pure and of sanctified self. Thus the great power of the Gāyatrī is described. To make known that one who knows the power of this great mantra and worships it attains the nearness of Brahman and becomes Brahman itself, its greatness is described in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka in the form of a story, as follows.

**28. Praise of the Gāyatrī.**

रक्षाग्ंसि ह वा पुरोऽनुवाके तपोऽग्रमतिष्ठंत तान्प्रजापतिर्वरेणोपामंत्रयत तानि वरमवृणीतादित्यो नो योद्रा इति तान्प्रजापतिरब्रवीद्योधयध्वमिति तस्मादुत्तिष्ठंतग्ं ह वा तानि रक्षाग्स्यादित्यं योधयंति यावदस्तमन्वगात्तानि ह वा एतानि रक्षाग्ंसि गायत्रियाभिमंत्रितेनांभसा शाम्यंति तदु ह वा एते ब्रह्मवादिनः पूर्वाभिमुखास्संध्यायां गायत्रियाभिमंत्रिता आप ऊर्ध्व० विक्षिपंति ता एता आपो वज्री भूत्वा तानि रक्षाग्ंसि मंदेहारुणे द्वीपे प्रक्षिपंति यत्पदक्षिणं प्रक्रमंति तेन पाप्नानमवधून्वंत्युद्यंतमस्तंयंतमादित्यमभिध्यायन्कुर्वन् ब्राह्मणो विद्वान्स कलं भद्रमश्नुतेऽसावादित्यो ब्रह्मेति ब्रह्मैव सन् ब्रह्माप्येति य एवं वेद ॥ (*rakṣāgṃsi ha vā puro 'nuvāke tapo 'gramatiṣṭhaṃta tānprajāpatirvareṇopāmaṃtrayata tāni varamavṛṇītādityo no yodrā iti tānprajāpatirabravīdyodhayadhvamiti tasmāduttiṣṭhaṃtagṃ ha vā tāni rakṣāgsyādityaṃ yodhayaṃti yāvadastamanvagāttāni ha vā etāni rakṣāgṃsi gāyatriyābhimaṃtritenāṃbhasā śāmyaṃti tadu ha vā ete brahmavādinaḥ pūrvābhimukhāssaṃdhyāyāṃ gāyatriyābhimaṃtritā āpa ūrdhva0 vikṣipaṃti tā etā āpo vajrī bhūtvā tāni rakṣāgṃsi maṃdehāruṇe dvīpe prakṣipaṃti yatpadakṣiṇaṃ prakramaṃti tena pāpnānamavadhūnvaṃtyudyaṃtamastaṃyaṃtamādityamabhidhyāyankurvan brāhmaṇo vidvānsa kalaṃ bhadramaśnute 'sāvādityo brahmeti brahmaiva san brahmāpyeti ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Trai. Ā. 2-2) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 624

In former times the rākṣasas practised fierce austerity. Then the god Prajāpati appeared before them and asked what boon they wished. They prayed: "Grant us the power and the opportunity to fight with Sūra (the sun)." Prajāpati agreed: "So be it." For that reason the rākṣasas, as soon as the sun rises, begin to fight with him and keep on fighting until his setting. But they can be driven away by water hallowed by the recitation of the Gāyatrī. Therefore the brahmavādins, at the morning twilight (and at the evening twilight too), recite the Gāyatrī and offer arghya with the water so hallowed. These drops of water offered as arghya turn into thunderbolts and hurl the rākṣasas into the island called मंदेहारण (*maṃdehāraṇa*) **NOTE**. Then the brahmavādins, by worship accompanied by circumambulation and obeisance, shake off their sin. A brāhmaṇa who knows this truth (the knower of Brahman), if he recites the Gāyatrī and offers arghya at sunrise and at sunset, and through this worships and meditates on the Āditya, obtains every kind of good (welfare). The Āditya is the Supreme Brahman. The man who knows that the Āditya, the object of worship of the Gāyatrī **NOTE**, is Brahman, and so worships, attains union with Brahman and becomes of the very form of Brahman. Thus the recitation of the Gāyatrī is praised.

**Kannada.**

**The greatness of the Gāyatrī**

The mantra beginning तत्सवितुः (*tatsavituḥ*), famous throughout the world and declaring the spiritual aim of man, is renowned as the Gāyatrī. The inspiration of this mantra has spread over the whole earth and has attracted the minds of all seekers of truth in the world. All alike have extolled it as the great mantra that declares the lofty aim of man.

India will never forget the inspiration which the all-knowing great sages taught in the Vedas and Upaniṣads at the dawn of history. Their keen minds, ceaselessly absorbed in the knowledge of reality, were ever engaged in piercing the darkness of tamas and entering the divine radiance. Neither merely personal worldly happiness nor the otherworldly happiness of heaven was their aim. As the great mantra says, धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् (*dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt*), their whole aim lay in the acquisition of knowledge. No aim better than this can exist for man; in such terms they have praised the greatness of the Gāyatrī.

### Printed p. 625

The matter taught by the Gāyatrī mantra is the pursuit of that human goal by which all the actions of life, without the distinction "this is small, this is great, this is low, this is high," become excellent human goals. The supreme goal of life is contained in the pursuit of the Supreme Reality, called by various names such as Ātman, Paramātman, Brahman. For the personality to shine with the light of this vision of harmony and attain fullness, the divine presence of the Lord must be gained in the solitude of meditation. At the time of this meditation the pure intellect of the person should touch the consciousness of the worlds and the unseen worlds, and he should pray that the radiance of that divine consciousness fill him.

तेजोऽसि तेजो मयि धेहि .... .... ओजोऽसि ओजो मयि धेहि ॥ (*tejo 'si tejo mayi dhehi .... .... ojo 'si ojo mayi dhehi ‖*)

You who are the radiance of radiance, fill me with radiance. You who are the strength of strength, fill me with might. You are the vigour of all vigour; manifest as vigour in me also. You are the peace of all endurance; arise in my self as that peace of endurance. In this way, at the time of meditation, the seeker of truth, whose aspiration blazes up touching Brahman, and the consciousness which desires peace of the Self and through it peace of the world (ओं द्यौः शांतिरंतरिक्षं शांति: (*oṃ dyauḥ śāṃtiraṃtarikṣaṃ śāṃti:*) …), prays through the meditation in the form of the mantra भर्गॊ देवस्य धीमहि (*bhargò devasya dhīmahi*), धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् (*dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt*).

To say it in sum: the nature of the Gāyatrī is that it praises the reality that teaches universal harmony and is the means to that knowledge of reality. सूर आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (*sūra ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1); योऽसौ तपन्नुदेति । स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायोदेति (*yo 'sau tapannudeti | sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇānādāyodeti*) (Tai. Ā. 1-14-1); असावादित्यो ब्रह्म (*asāvādityo brahma*) (Tai. Ā. 2-2-1). The very same light of the Āditya, the reality and radiance of the Āditya, which is praised in these and similar passages, is praised in the present mantra also. This great Gāyatrī mantra is the means, in the form of meditation, to the realisation of Savitṛ, the Self of the universe, by praising him. The Upaniṣads praise this very thing as the reality of Supreme Brahman. The questions arise naturally: How is it that Savitṛ, the Self of the universe, is the deity who teaches the reality of Supreme Brahman? Is the bhargas of Savitṛ the form of the supreme light of the Supreme Person? How is meditation in the form of the Gāyatrī the chief means of knowing this supreme light? And is it proper to call the Gāyatrī, which is merely a metre, the Supreme Reality named Parabrahman? Therefore it is necessary to examine these matters now.

The purpose of the mantra is to worship by meditation on the bhargas of Savitṛ, who is worthy of worship by the whole world. The reality from which the whole world arises, by whose power all the beings so arisen live, and into which, again, at the time of dissolution

### Printed p. 626

the whole world is merged: such Brahman is denoted by the word savitṛ, as stated in the foregoing explanations. It has also been made clear that worship of the Gāyatrī is the chief means for knowing such Brahman-reality. This kind of worship is the very nature of the present mantra तत्सवितुः (*tatsavituḥ*). Sāyaṇa's commentary on this mantra has been quoted above and its purport given. Here the words that are the parts of this mantra are explained on the basis of Śruti passages, and the fruit of meditating on this mantra is also stated. Vidyāraṇya Svāmin has set out the meaning of the Gāyatrī mantra in verse thus:

तदित्यवाङ्मनोगम्यं धैयं यत्तूरमंडले । सवितुः सकलोत्पत्तिस्थितिसंहारकारिणः ॥ वरेण्यमाश्रयणीयं यदाधारमिदं जगत् । भर्गः स्वसाक्षात्कारेणाविद्यातत्कार्यदाहकं ॥ देवस्य द्योतमानस्य ह्यानंदात्क्रीडतोऽपि वा । धीमह्यहं स एवेति तेनैवाभेदसिद्धये ॥ धियोऽंतःकरणवृत्तीश्च प्रत्यक्रवणचारिणीः । य इत्यलिंगधर्मं यत्सत्यज्ञानादिलक्षणं ॥ नोऽस्माकं बहुधाभ्यस्तभिन्नभेददृशां तथा । प्रचोदयात्वेरयतु प्रार्थनेयं विचार्यते ॥ (*tadityavāṅmanogamyaṃ dhaiyaṃ yattūramaṃḍale | savituḥ sakalotpattisthitisaṃhārakāriṇaḥ ‖ vareṇyamāśrayaṇīyaṃ yadādhāramidaṃ jagat | bhargaḥ svasākṣātkāreṇāvidyātatkāryadāhakaṃ ‖ devasya dyotamānasya hyānaṃdātkrīḍato 'pi vā | dhīmahyahaṃ sa eveti tenaivābhedasiddhaye ‖ dhiyo 'ṃtaḥkaraṇavṛttīśca pratyakravaṇacāriṇīḥ | ya ityaliṃgadharmaṃ yatsatyajñānādilakṣaṇaṃ ‖ no 'smākaṃ bahudhābhyastabhinnabhedadṛśāṃ tathā | pracodayātverayatu prārthaneyaṃ vicāryate ‖*)

The Supreme Reality, which cannot be reached by speech or mind (यतो वाचो निवर्तंते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह (*yato vāco nivartaṃte | aprāpya manasā saha*)) and which abides in the orb of the sun, is what the word तत् (*tat*) denotes. Because it is the root cause of the origin, continuance and dissolution of all the worlds, this Brahman is denoted by the word सवितृ (*savitṛ*). This Brahman, the support of the whole world, is the most worshipful and honoured place of refuge. Because this divine light, self-luminous and illuminating the world, burns up and destroys the ignorance of the world and its effects such as sorrow, it has the name भर्ग (*bharga*). Because he is luminous and intent on the sport of bliss, Savitṛ has the epithet देवस्य (*devasya*). The meaning of the word धीमहि (*dhīmahi*) is the meditation of non-difference: "I am this very Brahman who is in the form of Savitṛ." The activities of the inner organ of the individual are what the word धि (*dhi*) denotes. The reality which has the characteristics of truth, knowledge and so on and whose nature is beyond gender is designated by यः (*yaḥ*). The word नः (*naḥ*) points to the individual selves in whom, through the notion of being different from Brahman, the feeling of difference has grown from the beginning. The prayer is that he may impel us, who by the notion of difference appear as different selves, to practise the meditative contemplation that is the means to the realisation of non-difference with Brahman. What scriptural authority there is for the purport stated by Vidyāraṇya must now be examined.

### Printed p. 627

तत् (*tat*)

In the present mantra two kinds of construction are shown for the word तत् (*tat*). Some hold that this word is an epithet of सवितुः (*savituḥ*), others that it is an epithet of भर्गः (*bhargaḥ*). Though there are thus two views in the explanation, in sum the purport of both is the same. How? First: तत् इति षष्ठ्या परिणम्यते तस्येत्यर्थः । (*tat iti ṣaṣṭhyā pariṇamyate tasyetyarthaḥ |*) The meaning तस्य (*tasya*), ending in the sixth case, is reached for the word तत् (*tat*); it means "of that god." Or else तस्य (*tasya*) means ब्रह्मणः (*brahmaṇaḥ*); the word तत् (*tat*) itself denotes Brahman.

ओं तत्सदिति निर्देशः त्रिविधो ब्रह्मणः स्मृतः । (*oṃ tatsaditi nirdeśaḥ trividho brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ |*) (Bha. Gī. 17-23) **NOTE**

The commentators have made this clear when explaining the word तत् (*tat*) there. Rāmānujācārya says तच्छब्दो हि ब्रह्म वाची प्रसिद्धः । (*tacchabdo hi brahma vācī prasiddhaḥ |*) — the word तत् (*tat*) is well known as denoting Brahman — and Śaṅkarācārya, explaining the meaning of the word, says तत् इति ब्रह्माभिधानं उच्चार्य । (*tat iti brahmābhidhānaṃ uccārya |*) — "having uttered तत् (*tat*), the name that refers to Brahman." In the Upaniṣads the word तत् (*tat*) is used in many places as a synonym of Brahman. For example, the expression तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो (*tattvamasi śvetaketo*) is famous throughout the world: तत् (*tat*) means Brahman, त्वं (*tvaṃ*) means the individual self. It is clear that by तत्त्वमसि (*tattvamasi*) the non-difference of the individual self and Brahman is stated. तत्वदं हि सर्वज्ञं सत्यसंकल्पं जगत्कारणं ब्रह्म परामृशति । तदैक्षत बहु स्यां । इत्यादिषु तस्यॆव प्रकृतित्वात् । (*tatvadaṃ hi sarvajñaṃ satyasaṃkalpaṃ jagatkāraṇaṃ brahma parāmṛśati | tadaikṣata bahu syāṃ | ityādiṣu tasyèva prakṛtitvāt |*) The word तत् (*tat*) points to that Brahman who is all-knowing, of true resolve, the cause of the world; the sentence तदैक्षत (*tadaikṣata*) and the like teach the same. Thus it is explained everywhere. In the Chāndogya, the section beginning तज्जलानिति (*tajjalāniti*) (Chā. U. 3-14-1) is renowned as the "tat-tvam" section **NOTE**. The sentences ओं तत्पृह । ओं तद्वायुः । ओं तदात्मा (*oṃ tatpṛha | oṃ tadvāyuḥ | oṃ tadātmā*) and the like teach the same. Therefore, since in the present mantra the word तत् (*tat*) is a synonym of Brahman, it is used as an epithet of Savitṛ, who is of the form of Supreme Brahman. It is one view that the statement that it should be taken to mean तस्य सवितुः (*tasya savituḥ*) is correct.

Secondly, to say that the word तत् (*tat*) is an epithet of भर्गः (*bhargaḥ*) is another view. Bhaṭṭabhāskara, explaining the purport of this mantra in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (Tai. Ā. 1-11), says तत्सवितुः इति । व्याख्यातं सं पश्यामि इत्यत्र । (*tatsavituḥ iti | vyākhyātaṃ saṃ paśyāmi ityatra |*) — informing us that in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, in the section beginning सं पश्यामि (*saṃ paśyāmi*), the explanation of this mantra has been given — and then explains it again. But the explanation given in the Āraṇyaka differs from that given in the Saṃhitā section. In the Āraṇyaka: सवितुः देवस्य प्रेरयितुः तत् तादृशं वरेण्यं भर्गः । (*savituḥ devasya prerayituḥ tat tādṛśaṃ vareṇyaṃ bhargaḥ |*) Of Savitṛ, the impeller of the world

### Printed p. 628
having explained it as "the brilliance of the god, famed in the world and worthy of worship", he has shown that the word तत् (*tat*) is an adjective of the word भर्गः (*bhargaḥ*). He has also stated clearly that the same is explained in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā section. There, however, (it says) आहवनीयमुपतिष्ठते—तत्सवितुरिति गायत्रा । (*āhavanīyamupatiṣṭhate—tatsavituriti gāyatrā |*), and the rule तत्तस्य सुपां सुलुक् (*tattasya supāṃ suluk*) shows that the sixth case ending is elided in the word तत् (*tat*). He has made it plain that the meaning should be taken as तस्य सवितुः (*tasya savituḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. Bhā. 1-5-6). He has further said that, as in सवितुः देवस्य तदन्नादि धीमहि (*savituḥ devasya tadannādi dhīmahi*), the word तत् (*tat*) may also be an adjective of the word भर्ग (*bharga*), which gives the meaning "food and the like". Although the explanations differ in this way, it may be said that, from the point of view of examining the truth, there is no contradiction between the two.

हिरण्मये परे कोशे विरजं ब्रह्म निष्कलं । तच्छभ्रं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिस्तद्यदात्मविदो विदुः ॥ (*hiraṇmaye pare kośe virajaṃ brahma niṣkalaṃ | tacchabhraṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotistadyadātmavido viduḥ ‖*) (Mu. U. 2-2-9). In the supreme golden sheath, which is of the nature of the Supreme and is golden, there is Brahman, free from passion and without parts (without distinctions). It is a light-form shining more brightly than the most radiant lights. Only knowers of the Self can know it.

न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चंद्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भांति कुतोऽयमग्नि । तमेव भांतमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥ (*na tatra sūryo bhāti na caṃdratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhāṃti kuto 'yamagni | tameva bhāṃtamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti ‖*) (Mu U. :-2-18). Before that divine light which is Brahman the sun cannot shine; the light of the moon and the stars cannot shine before it. By its own self-luminosity all radiant lights shine; everything in the world is illumined by that light. In such passages the identity of Brahman and light is stated, showing that one principle is called by two names. Therefore, if the word तत् (*tat*) is an adjective of Savitṛ, it means तस्य जगत्पेरकस्य सवितुः (*tasya jagatperakasya savituḥ*); if it is an adjective of the word भर्ग (*bharga*), it means ब्रह्मरूपस्य सवितुः जगत्पसिद्धं ज्योतिः (*brahmarūpasya savituḥ jagatpasiddhaṃ jyotiḥ*).

सवितुर् (*savitur*)
The derivation of the word Savitṛ, and that the Supreme Brahman itself is what the word Savitṛ denotes, have been stated above. सूते सकलजननिर्वृतिहेतुं वृष्टिं (*sūte sakalajananirvṛtihetuṃ vṛṣṭiṃ*)—one kind of derivation is that the sun is named Savitṛ because he brings forth rain, which gives satisfaction to all the worlds. *sauti sakalaśreyāṃsi

### Printed p. 629
dhātṛṇāṃ savitā*—he is called by this name because he gives all good things to worshippers. उद्यंतमस्तंयन्तमादित्यमभिध्यायन्नुर्वनाह्मणो विद्वान् सकलं भद्रमश्नुते (*udyaṃtamastaṃyantamādityamabhidhyāyannurvanāhmaṇo vidvān sakalaṃ bhadramaśnute*)—by meditation on the sun rising and setting, welfare comes to the whole world. Such Śruti passages support the above derivation.

सविता सर्वभूतानां सर्वभावान् प्रसूयते । सवनात् प्रेरणाच्चैव सविता तेन चोच्यते ॥ (*savitā sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvabhāvān prasūyate | savanāt preraṇāccaiva savitā tena cocyate ‖*) (by the Yogin Yājñavalkya). The derivation, "the name Savitṛ is because he is the cause of the birth of the whole world and the impeller of all worldly activities", is found in the Upaniṣads and other works just as in the Saṃhitā passages quoted earlier. This verse as quoted also gives the same explanation. Moreover, the praises of Savitṛ in the Ṛk Saṃhitā are always accompanied by such derivations, and those same praises also explain the meaning of the present mantra.

विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुंचते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे । वि नाकमख्यत्सविता वरेण्योऽनु प्रयाणमुषसो वि राजति ॥ (*viśvā rūpāṇi prati muṃcate kaviḥ prāsāvīdbhadraṃ dvipade catuṣpade | vi nākamakhyatsavitā vareṇyo 'nu prayāṇamuṣaso vi rājati ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-2). The wise Savitṛ bears all the forms of the world within himself. He brings forth welfare for all creatures of the world, two-footed and four-footed. He is the impeller of all living powers. Therefore he is the most choiceworthy. By this quality he illumines the world. This description praises Savitṛ in the same way as Brahman is praised in the Upaniṣad words quoted above, तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति (*tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti*).

उतेशिषे प्रसवस्य त्वमेक इदुत पूषा भवसि देव यामभिः । उतेदं विश्वं भुवनं वि राजसि श्यावाश्वस्ते सवितः स्तोममानशे ॥ (*uteśiṣe prasavasya tvameka iduta pūṣā bhavasi deva yāmabhiḥ | utedaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vi rājasi śyāvāśvaste savitaḥ stomamānaśe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-5).
तत्सवितुर्वृणीमहे वयं देवस्य भोजनं । श्रेष्ठं सर्वधातमं तुरं भगस्य धीमहि ॥ (*tatsaviturvṛṇīmahe vayaṃ devasya bhojanaṃ | śreṣṭhaṃ sarvadhātamaṃ turaṃ bhagasya dhīmahi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-82-1).
Savitṛ is the lord of all worldly activities, the protector of the whole world. He bears all beings within himself. He is the cause of all creation, preservation and dissolution. "We wish to know the greatness of such Savitṛ, the lord of the world." Since Savitṛ's own nature is thus praised, it is known that Savitṛ is

### Printed p. 630
the Supreme Deity who rules the world. Upaniṣad passages such as देवाय सवित्रे सत्यप्रसवाय (*devāya savitre satyaprasavāya*) (Bṛ. U. 6-5-19) state this nature clearly.

युंजानः प्रथमं मनस्तत्त्वाय सविता धियः । अग्नोर्ज्योतिर्निचाय्य पृथिव्या अध्याभरत् ॥ (*yuṃjānaḥ prathamaṃ manastattvāya savitā dhiyaḥ | agnorjyotirnicāyya pṛthivyā adhyābharat ‖*) (Śve. U. 2-1). Savitṛ, the impeller of consciousness, first with a restrained mind obtained the intellect whose nature is the impulse of truth. Then he made the light in the form of fire spread over the earth. Therefore युंजते मन उत युंजते धियो विप्रा विप्रस्य बृहतो विपश्चितः (*yuṃjate mana uta yuṃjate dhiyo viprā viprasya bṛhato vipaścitaḥ*). The order of worship is thus taught: to realise the divine light of Savitṛ, the cause of the world, one should contemplate it with a restrained mind in the form of meditation. The divine nature of this Savitṛ, the cause of the world, has been explained above.

वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*).
वरेण्यं पुरुषार्थकामिभिर्वर्णीयं । श्रेष्ठं वा । (*vareṇyaṃ puruṣārthakāmibhirvarṇīyaṃ | śreṣṭhaṃ vā |*) Since all human goals are obtained only through Savitṛ's grace, and since he is the most excellent as a form of light, he is highly esteemed by the world. सत्यात्म प्राणारामं मन आनंदं । शांतिसमृद्धममृतं । (*satyātma prāṇārāmaṃ mana ānaṃdaṃ | śāṃtisamṛddhamamṛtaṃ |*) The Supreme Brahman whose Self is truth, whose breath is a place of delight, whose mind is the abode of bliss, and who is rich in peace—such a Supreme Self is esteemed by the world; therefore श्रोतव्यो मंतव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः (*śrotavyo maṃtavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ*): he is to be heard, to be reflected upon, and to be meditated upon; thus he is praised.

भर्गः (*bhargaḥ*).
The choiceworthy light of Savitṛ is what the word Bharga denotes: अविद्यातत्कार्ययोर्भर्जनाद्भर्गः स्वयंज्योतिः परब्रह्मात्मकं तेजः । (*avidyātatkāryayorbharjanādbhargaḥ svayaṃjyotiḥ parabrahmātmakaṃ tejaḥ |*) Because it destroys ignorance and its fruits, sin and sorrow, the supreme light of the Supreme Brahman is known as Bharga. The meaning of this word is given in the Maitrī Upaniṣad as follows.
अथ भर्गा इति यो ह वा अमुष्मिन्नादित्ये निहितस्तारकोऽक्षिणि वैष भर्गाख्यो भाभिर्गतिरस्य हीति भर्गो भर्जयतीति वैष भर्गा इति रुद्रो ब्रह्मवादिनोऽथ भ इति भासयतीमान् लोकान् र इति रंजयतीमानि भूतादि ग इति गच्छंत्यस्मिन्नागच्छंत्यस्मादिमाः प्रजास्तस्माद्भरगत्वाद्भर्गः ॥ शश्वत् सूयमानात् सूर्यः सवनात् सविता .... .... .... .... ॥ (*atha bhargā iti yo ha vā amuṣminnāditye nihitastārako 'kṣiṇi vaiṣa bhargākhyo bhābhirgatirasya hīti bhargo bharjayatīti vaiṣa bhargā iti rudro brahmavādino 'tha bha iti bhāsayatīmān lokān ra iti raṃjayatīmāni bhūtādi ga iti gacchaṃtyasminnāgacchaṃtyasmādimāḥ prajāstasmādbharagatvādbhargaḥ ‖ śaśvat sūyamānāt sūryaḥ savanāt savitā .... .... .... .... ‖*) (Mai. U. 6-2).

### Printed p. 631
What Savitṛ's Bharga is must be examined. अथ य एषोऽंतरक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यते (*atha ya eṣo 'ṃtarakṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate*)—the light that shines within the sun shines also as light in the eye of the person, as praised in the Chāndogya and other texts (Chā. U. 1-7-5); that light is what is called Bharga.

(1) भाभिः किरणैरधिष्ठानधर्मैरस्य गतिर्गमनं विषयव्याप्तिरस्य इति व्युत्पत्तेर्भर्ग इत्येकं निर्वचनं (*bhābhiḥ kiraṇairadhiṣṭhānadharmairasya gatirgamanaṃ viṣayavyāptirasya iti vyutpatterbharga ityekaṃ nirvacanaṃ*)—भाः (*bhāḥ*) means a ray endowed with brilliance. Because there is movement in the form of such rays, and because from this movement there is all-pervasiveness, the sun's radiance is named Bharga: this is one kind of derivation.
(2) Secondly, भर्जयति जगत् संहरतीति रुद्रो भर्ग इति (*bharjayati jagat saṃharatīti rudro bharga iti*)—it is the view of the Brahmavādins that Rudra is named Bharga because he destroys the world.
(3) Thirdly, भकाररेफगकाराणां प्रत्येकनिर्वचनं । (*bhakārarephagakārāṇāṃ pratyekanirvacanaṃ |*) भासयति तेजोमंडलांतर्गतचित्पकाशेन इमान् सर्वानेव लोकान् इति भ इत्युच्यते । (*bhāsayati tejomaṃḍalāṃtargatacitpakāśena imān sarvāneva lokān iti bha ityucyate |*) इमानि भूतानि स्थावरजंगमात्मकानि प्राणानुगतचिदानंदात्मना रंजयति प्रीणयति सुखात्मकं करोति इति र उच्यते । (*imāni bhūtāni sthāvarajaṃgamātmakāni prāṇānugatacidānaṃdātmanā raṃjayati prīṇayati sukhātmakaṃ karoti iti ra ucyate |*) अस्मिन् सर्वकारणात्मनि सुषुप्तिप्रळययोः सर्वा इमा प्रजाः गच्छंति लयं प्राप्पुवंति तथा प्रभोधसृष्टोरस्मादेवागच्छंत्याविर्भवंतीति ग इत्युच्यते ॥ (*asmin sarvakāraṇātmani suṣuptipraḷayayoḥ sarvā imā prajāḥ gacchaṃti layaṃ prāppuvaṃti tathā prabhodhasṛṣṭorasmādevāgacchaṃtyāvirbhavaṃtīti ga ityucyate ‖*)
A separate derivation can be given for each of the three letters bha, ra, ga. Thus: 1) because it makes all the worlds shine by its brilliance, it is called bha. 2) Because it delights all beings, moving and unmoving, with its own nature of consciousness-bliss, and gives them happiness, it is called ra. 3) And because in deep sleep and at dissolution all beings are absorbed in Supreme Brahman, the cause of all, and again at awakening and at creation come forth from Brahman alone, it is called ga. Since the Supreme Brahman is thus the combination and harmony of bha, ra and ga, he is named Bharga; so the derivations of this word are stated.

It has been stated above that the word Bharga is given other meanings such as Savitṛ's brilliance or food. भर्गः, तेजः, अन्नं, धनं (*bhargaḥ, tejaḥ, annaṃ, dhanaṃ*)—the word Bharga has the meaning brilliance, food or wealth; any of these meanings may be taken. The commentary of Bhaṭṭabhāskara on the Taittirīya Saṃhitā has also been quoted above and explained (Tai. Saṃ. Bha. Bhā. 1-5-6).
भृजः साके भवेद्धातुर्यस्मात् पाचयते ह्यसौ । भ्राजते दीप्यते यस्मात् जगदंते हरत्यपि ॥ (*bhṛjaḥ sāke bhaveddhāturyasmāt pācayate hyasau | bhrājate dīpyate yasmāt jagadaṃte haratyapi ‖*)

### Printed p. 632
कालाग्नि रूपमास्थाय सर्पार्चिः सप्तरश्मिभिः । भ्राजते तत्स्वरूपेण तस्माद्भर्गः स उच्यते ॥ (*kālāgni rūpamāsthāya sarpārciḥ saptaraśmibhiḥ | bhrājate tatsvarūpeṇa tasmādbhargaḥ sa ucyate ‖*) (Yogi-Yājñavalkya). Because he ripens the world, and at the end of time destroys it, and, assuming the form of the fire of time, shines with seven rays, the name Bharga is well known. भेति भासयते लोकान् । रेति रंजयते प्रजाः । ग इत्यागच्छतेजस्रं भरगो भर्ग उच्यते (*bheti bhāsayate lokān | reti raṃjayate prajāḥ | ga ityāgacchatejasraṃ bharago bharga ucyate*)—in this explanation too, as in the Maitrī Upaniṣad passage above, the combination and harmony of the powers of Brahman called Savitṛ, indicated by the letters bha, ra, ga, are stated.

देवस्य (*devasya*).
देवो द्युलोकवर्तित्वाद्देवनाद्देवनेन वा । (*devo dyulokavartitvāddevanāddevanena vā |*) Savitṛ is denoted by the word देव (*deva*) because he dwells in the heavenly world, because he is shining, or because his nature is playful.
दीव्यते क्रीडते यस्माद्रोचते द्योतते दिवि । तस्माद्द्देव इति प्रोक्तः स्तूयते सर्वदेवतैः ॥ (*dīvyate krīḍate yasmādrocate dyotate divi | tasmādddeva iti proktaḥ stūyate sarvadevataiḥ ‖*). By the greatness through which this god Savitṛ plays in the world that is his sport, and is a giver of delight to this world by his play, and by which he shines radiant in the heavenly world—by that very greatness the epithet "deva" is established for him. Or: दीव्यति नंदतीति देवः । अखंडानंदैकरस इत्यर्थः । (*dīvyati naṃdatīti devaḥ | akhaṃḍānaṃdaikarasa ityarthaḥ |*) This epithet is because he is always in the bliss that is play, and because he is of the nature of bliss itself. Śaṅkarācārya also says देवस्येति सर्वद्योतनात्मताखंडचिदेकरसं । (*devasyeti sarvadyotanātmatākhaṃḍacidekarasaṃ |*)—it is the designation of the principle that illumines everything, is indivisible, and is of the nature of bliss.
अन्नोऽन्तर आत्मानंदमयः । तेनैष पूर्णः । .... .... .... .... तस्य प्रियमेव शिरः । मोदो दक्षिणः पक्षः । प्रमोद उत्तरं पक्षः । आनंद आत्मा ॥ (*anno 'ntara ātmānaṃdamayaḥ | tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ | .... .... .... .... tasya priyameva śiraḥ | modo dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ | pramoda uttaraṃ pakṣaḥ | ānaṃda ātmā ‖*) (Tai. U. 2-5). The meaning stated is that the special quality of Supreme Brahman, who is described as this blissful Person, endowed with the wings of joy and delight and himself of the nature of bliss, is what the word देव (*deva*) denotes. In ब्रह्मजज्ञं देवमीड्यं विदित्वा (*brahmajajñaṃ devamīḍyaṃ viditvā*) (Ka. U. 1-17) and similar places also this meaning is given to the word देव (*deva*). Passages such as आत्मरतिः आत्मक्रीड (*ātmaratiḥ ātmakrīḍa*) and यस्य विश्व उपासते (*yasya viśva upāsate*) also praise this quality.

### Printed p. 633
धीमहि (*dhīmahi*)
For the word धीमहि (*dhīmahi*) the meanings ध्यायामः (*dhyāyāmaḥ*) and मनसा धारयामः (*manasā dhārayāmaḥ*) are given. Or one may also say ध्येयतया धारयामः (*dhyeyatayā dhārayāmaḥ*). Thus both meanings, meditation and holding, are stated: let us hold him in the mind in the form of meditation. The benefit and necessity of meditation have been stated above. Supreme Brahman, who cannot be reached by speech or mind, is not within the range of speech and mind; therefore realisation must be attained only through worship in the form of meditation. The order of realisation in this meditation is also prescribed: धीमह्यहं स एवेति तेनैवाभेदसिद्धये (*dhīmahyahaṃ sa eveti tenaivābhedasiddhaye*). The word धीमहि (*dhīmahi*) conveys the holding in meditation by which the individual soul, which held the separate idea that it is different from Supreme Brahman, knows itself to be Brahman and attains realisation of unity.
बुध्यादिसर्वदृश्यसाक्षिलक्षणं यन्ने स्वरूपं तत्सर्वाधिष्ठानभूतं परमानंदं निरस्तसमस्तानर्थरूपं स्वप्रकाशचिदात्मकं ब्रह्मेत्येवं धीमहि ध्यायेम । (*budhyādisarvadṛśyasākṣilakṣaṇaṃ yanne svarūpaṃ tatsarvādhiṣṭhānabhūtaṃ paramānaṃdaṃ nirastasamastānartharūpaṃ svaprakāśacidātmakaṃ brahmetyevaṃ dhīmahi dhyāyema |*) Śaṅkarācārya explains the meaning of the word धीमहि (*dhīmahi*) thus: that inner Self of mine which is the witness of the entire visible world beginning with the intellect, and that Self-principle which is the substratum of all the worlds, of the nature of supreme bliss, removing all evil, self-luminous, and called Brahman—by meditating on it as Brahman, there is realisation of Brahman. He has also said that this meditation is of the nature of knowledge of oneness with Brahman. It was said before that Savitṛ's light is named Bharga because it destroys faults such as ignorance; the same is the fruit of the meditation indicated by the word धीमहि (*dhīmahi*).
अहं विश्वं भुवनमभ्यभवां । सुवर्ण ज्योतीः । (*ahaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanamabhyabhavāṃ | suvarṇa jyotīḥ |*) (Tai. U. 3-8). "I have overcome all the worlds, which are diverse, and having attained realisation of Brahman, the supreme light, I have become Brahman itself": the means, in the form of meditation, for the coming of such a feeling of unity is here extolled. As the fruit of this meditation, which is knowledge: मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते (*martyo 'mṛto bhavatyatra brahma samaśnute*)—the mortal man gains immortality and here itself attains realisation of Brahman. As the sun shines in the sky, he too shines with the divine brilliance that is Brahman.

धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)
To obtain knowledge of oneness with Brahman, the knowledge that is its means and the action that brings about that knowledge are absolutely necessary. The prayer is that Savitṛ may impel such a धी (*dhī*). Here two kinds of meaning may be given to the word धी (*dhī*): intellect or insight, or action. Since ignorance must be destroyed, insight is necessary. This insight comes only through action in the form of worship,

### Printed p. 634
…is attainable. Therefore both meanings are appropriate. Moreover, since meditation is itself a form of praise of Savitṛ, it would not be wrong to take the word धी (*dhī*) as "praise." Good works are the means to knowledge of Brahman. Action preceded by special knowledge is itself also a form of praise. This identity, or concomitance, of knowledge and action is stated in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad as follows.

विज्ञानं यज्ञं तनुते । कर्माणि तनुतेऽपि च । विज्ञानं देवास्सर्वे ब्रह्म ज्येष्ठमुपासते । (*vijñānaṃ yajñaṃ tanute | karmāṇi tanute 'pi ca | vijñānaṃ devāssarve brahma jyeṣṭhamupāsate |*) (Tai. U. 2-1)

One who has special knowledge performs the sacrifice. Because the agency consists in such knowledge, there is the understanding that the Self made of knowledge is Brahman. But in order to realise the Brahman made of bliss, who surpasses the Brahman made of knowledge, meditation in the form of action grounded in knowledge is indispensable. So the word धी (*dhī*), comprising knowledge, action and meditation, here denotes meditation that is preceded by knowledge and is of the nature of action. The prayer is that He impel us to such meditation.

**यः (*yaḥ*)**
यः सविता सूरः (*yaḥ savitā sūraḥ*): one meaning is "the Brahman in the form of Savitṛ, who exists, may impel us." Or else यः (*yaḥ*) is a change of gender: यद्भर्गो धियः प्रचोदयात् । तत् ध्यायेम (*yadbhargo dhiyaḥ pracodayāt | tat dhyāyema*) is the construction. That is, "let us meditate on that Bharga, the light of the Sun, which impels our action preceded by knowledge", another meaning expressing the aspiration. Thus Sāyaṇa has shown two constructions. There is also a view that यः (*yaḥ*), by change of gender, may indicate the inner Brahman itself. Mādhava states it thus: य इत्यलिंगदर्मं यत्सत्यज्ञानादिलक्षणं (*ya ityaliṃgadarmaṃ yatsatyajñānādilakṣaṇaṃ*); the purport is that the Supreme Brahman itself should impel our thought. तस्य यच्छब्दनिर्दिष्टस्यात्मनः स्वरूपभूतं परं ब्रह्म तत्सवितुरित्यादिसद्यै: निर्दिष्टते (*tasya yacchabdanirdiṣṭasyātmanaḥ svarūpabhūtaṃ paraṃ brahma tatsaviturityādisadyai: nirdiṣṭate*): the Supreme Brahman that is the very nature of the Self is indicated by "tat savituḥ" and the rest. Thus Śaṅkarācārya gives the word यः (*yaḥ*) a meaning referring to the Supreme Brahman.**NOTE**

**नः (*naḥ*)**
नः (*naḥ*) means "to us." The notion "Brahman is one, we the individual selves are another, we are finite" creates a sense of difference between Brahman and the individual selves. But this sense of difference has grown naturally in man and is not easily removed. In truth there is no difference of any kind between the Supreme Self and the individual selves, yet the sense of difference grows out of the ignorance natural to man.

### Printed p. 635
Therefore, regarding the individual selves as standing apart from Brahman, the prayer is made: "Grant to us, who are different from you, the intellect that impels to good works and is the means of worshipping you."

**प्रचोदयात् (*pracodayāt*)**
प्रचोदयात् । प्रेरयेत् (*pracodayāt | prerayet*): may He impel the good intellect that produces good works. The prayer is that, through action preceded by knowledge, He give the power to know Savitṛ's Bharga. One important point must be noted in this prayer: the main point is that without the grace of God the fruit of knowledge cannot be obtained.

मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युंजन् मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥ (*mayyāsaktamanāḥ pārtha yogaṃ yuṃjan madāśrayaḥ | asaṃśayaṃ samagraṃ māṃ yathā jñāsyasi tacchṛṇu ‖*) (Bha. Gī. 7-1)**NOTE**

ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन ! (*jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana !*) When Arjuna asked, "If knowledge is the highest of all, why do you urge me to action?", Kṛṣṇa explains that knowledge without action has no value. But the action must take this form: one must offer the whole intellect to God, be absorbed in Him, take refuge in Him and so obtain God's grace as its fruit. Otherwise mere knowledge is of no use, he answers. The gist is that even the most learned cannot attain success by himself without God's grace.

मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् । (*mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṃ rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitamātmayogāt |*) (Bha. Gī. 11-47)

"My form, of divine light, became visible to you only through my grace": here it is taught that realisation of God is impossible without God's grace. The same matter is stated clearly in the Upaniṣads and elsewhere.

नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यः न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन ॥ यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्येष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वां ॥ (*nāyamātmā pravacanena labhyaḥ na medhayā na bahunā śrutena ‖ yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyastasyeṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svāṃ ‖*) (Kar. 2-23)**NOTE**

This Supreme Self is not to be obtained by discourse, nor by the power of intellect, nor by much hearing of scripture. He is obtained only by the grace of the Supreme Self on whom one relies and whose grace one wins.

### Printed p. 636
Whoever wins such grace, to him the Supreme Self unveils His own body: thus the necessity of God's grace is taught. As in the Īśa Upaniṣad:

आग्ने नय सुपधा राये अस्मान् विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् । युयोध्यस्यज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नमउक्तिं विधेम ॥ (*āgne naya supadhā rāye asmān viśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān | yuyodhyasyajjuhurāṇameno bhūyiṣṭhāṃ te namauktiṃ vidhema ‖*) (Īśa. 18)

"O Agni, you who know all actions, give us good intellect and lead us on the good path": as God's grace is prayed for there, so in the present Ṛk too the prayer is: make known to us the knowledge that is the means of knowing God's Bharga, and the action that is of its nature and is service of God; and give us the power to practise it and so worship God.

##### Grammar

- सवितुः—षु प्रसवैश्वर्ययोः धातु. अथवा षूज् प्राणिगर्भविमोचने. कर्तृर्थदल्लि तृच् प्रत्यय आर्धधातुकस्येड्वल्वादेः ऎंबुदरिंद अदक्कॆ इडागम. प्रत्यय निमित्तवागि धातुविन उकारक्कॆ गुण, अवादेश. सवितृशब्द. षष्ठि एकवचनांतरूप. प्रत्यय चित्तादुदरिंद चितः ऎंबुदरिंद अंतोदात्तस्वर बरुत्तदॆ.
- वरेण्यं—वृञ् वरणे. धातु- वृञ् एण्यः (उ. सू. ३७८) ऎंबुदरिंद एण्य प्रत्यय. अर्धधातुकवादुदरिंद इदन्नु निमित्तीकरिसि धातुविन ऋकारक्कॆ सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः ऎंबुदरिंद गुण. ऋकारद स्थानक्कॆ बरुवुदरिंद रपरवागि बरुत्तदॆ. द्वितीया एकवचनांतरूप.
- भर्गः—भ्रस्थ पाके. धातु. सर्वधातुभ्य आसन् ऎंबुदरिंद असुन् प्रत्यय. भ्रस्टो रोपधयोरमन्यतरस्यां (पा. सू. ६-४-४७) भस्वधातुसंबंधियाद रेफक्कू उपधॆगू लोपवू समागमवू बरुत्तदॆ ऎंबुदरिंद इल्लि रमागम. इदु मित्तादुदरिंद मिदचोंत्यात्परः ऎंबुदरिंद अंत्याचिन परवागि बरुत्तदॆ. न्यंक्वादिगणदल्लि इदन्नु पाठमाडुवुदरिंद जकारक्कॆ कुत्वदिंद गकारादेश. प्रत्यय नित्तादुदरिंद आद्युदात्तस्वर बरुत्तदॆ.
- देवस्य—दिवु क्रीडादिषु धातु. नंदिग्रहपचादिभ्यः ऎंबुदरिंद पचादिसतितवादुदरिंद अच् प्रत्यय. अदन्नु निमित्तीकरिसि धातुविन लघूपधॆगॆ गुण. चितः ऎंबुदरिंद अंतोदात्तस्वर बरुत्तदॆ. षष्ठी एकवचनांतरूप.

### Printed p. 637
- धीमहि—ध्यॆ चिंतायां धातु. लिज् उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचनदल्लि व्यत्ययदिंद आत्मनेपदद महिज् प्रत्यय. बहुलं छंदसि ऎंबुदरिंद धातुविन यकारक्कॆ संप्रसारण (इकारादेश) संप्रसारणाच्च ऎंबुदरिंद पूर्वरूप. हलः ऎंबुदरिंद संप्रसारणक्कॆ दीर्घ. अथवा धीज् आधारे धातु. चित्तादुदरिंद आत्मनेपदी. हिंदिनंतॆ लिजिनल्लि बहुलं छंधसि ऎंबुदरिंद विकरण प्रत्ययक्कॆ लुक्. अतिजंतद परदल्लि बंदिरुवुदरिंद तिजंतनिघातस्वर बरुत्तदॆ.
- धियः—ध्यॆ चिंतायां धातु. ध्यायतेः संप्रसारणंच (वा. २-५१) ऎंबुदरिंद क्विप् प्रत्यय. अदरॊडनॆ धातुविन यकारक्कॆ संप्रसारण. पूर्वरूप. हलः ऎंबुदरिंद दीर्घ. धी शब्द. धातुस्वर बरुत्तदॆ. द्वितीयाबहुवचनदल्लि शस्‌प्रत्यय. अचिश्रुधातु—ऎंबुदरिंद धातुविन इकारक्कॆ इयजादेश. प्रत्ययसकारक्कॆ रुत्व. विसर्ग.
- प्रचोदयात्— प्र उपसर्ग. चुद प्रेरणे. धातु. लेट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनदल्लि तिप् प्रत्यय. इकारलोप. लेटोडाटौ ऎंबुदरिंद आडागम. चुरादियल्लि पठितवादुदरिंद धातुविगॆ स्वार्थदल्लि णिच्. अदक्कॆ गुण, अयादेश. यः ऎंबुदर संबंधविरुवुदरिंद यद्वृत्तान्नित्यं ऎंबुदरिंद निघातस्वर निषेध बरुत्तदॆ. आगमा अनुदात्ताः ऎंबुदरिंद आडागम अनुदात्तवागुवुदरिंद णिच् प्रत्ययस्वरदिंद दकारोत्तराकारवु उदात्तवागुत्तदॆ. तिजि चोदात्तवति ऎंबुदरिंद उदात्तविशिष्टतिजंतपरवादुदरिंद गतिगॆ (प्र) अनुदात्तस्वर बरुत्तदॆ.

## Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वस्य॑ सवि॒तुर्व॒यं वा॑ज॒यंतः॒ पुरं॑ध्या ।  
> भग॑स्य रा॒तिमी॑महे ॥ ११ ॥

> *devasya saviturvayaṃ vājayaṃtaḥ puraṃdhyā |*  
> *bhagasya rātimīmahe ‖ 11 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवस्य । सवितुः । वयं । वाजयंतः । पुरंध्या ।  
> भगस्य । रातिं । ईमहे ॥ ११ ॥

> *devasya | savituḥ | vayaṃ | vājayaṃtaḥ | puraṃdhyā |*  
> *bhagasya | rātiṃ | īmahe ‖ 11 ‖*

### Printed p. 638

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाजयंतो वाजमन्नमात्मन इच्छंतो वयं देवस्य द्योतमानस्य सवितुः
> पुरंध्या तद्विषयस्तुत्या प्रज्ञया वा भगस्य भजनीयस्य धनस्य रातिं दानमीमहे ।
> याचामहे ॥ रातिं । मंत्रे वृषेत्यादिना क्तन उदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, desiring *vājaṃ*, food for ourselves, ask (ईमहे (*īmahe*), "we beg") the gift (रातिं (*rātiṃ*)) of the wealth worthy to be shared (भगस्य (*bhagasya*)), of the shining (देवस्य (*devasya*)) Savitṛ, by praise (पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*)) addressed to him, or by intelligence.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजयंतः (*vājayaṃtaḥ*)—desirous of obtaining food
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of the shining
- सवितुः (*savituḥ*)—Savitṛ
- पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*)—by intelligence in the form of praise
- भगस्य (*bhagasya*)—of the venerable wealth
- रातिं (*rātiṃ*)—the gift
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We, desirous of food, ask for the gift of venerable wealth from the shining Savitṛ, by intelligence in the form of praise.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Desirous of food, we solicit with praise, of the divine Savitri, the gift of affluence.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*)—तद्विषयस्तुत्या प्रज्ञया वा (*tadviṣayastutyā prajñayā vā*): by praise concerning Savitṛ, or by intelligence. पुरंधिर्बहुधीः (*puraṃdhirbahudhīḥ*): one with abundant intellect may be called Purandhi. The authors of the Nirukta, asking who such a deity is, give the purport together with an etymology of this word (Ni. 6-13). Since the word धी (*dhī*) is listed among the names of action, this epithet may also indicate a special quality of Indra. In places such as पुराणी देवि युवतिः पुरंधि (*purāṇī devi yuvatiḥ puraṃdhi*) (3-60-1) it has been explained earlier as "possessing much praise." It may be said that the word is used here to show the abundance of praise or intelligence in the present mantra. The special meanings and usages of this word were given earlier in this same volume, in the special topics of Ṛk 3-61-1 (Ṛ. Saṃ.).

देवस्य (*devasya*)—द्योतमानस्य (*dyotamānasya*): of the shining Savitṛ.

दीव्यते क्रीडते यस्माद्रोचते द्योतते दिवि । तस्माद्भाव इति प्रोक्तः स्तूयते सर्वदेवतैः ॥ (*dīvyate krīḍate yasmādrocate dyotate divi | tasmādbhāva iti proktaḥ stūyate sarvadevataiḥ ‖*) (Yogiyājña verse 3)**NOTE**

### Printed p. 639
By whatever power he sports in the world through playful resolve and action, and by whatever greatness he shines radiant in the heavenly world, for that reason Savitṛ is denoted by the word "deva": thus the importance of the epithet is explained.

## Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वं नरः॑ सवि॒तारं॒ विप्रा॑ य॒ज्ञैः सु॑वृ॒क्तिभिः॑ ।  
> न॒म॒स्यंति॑ धि॒येषि॒ताः ॥ १२ ॥

> *devaṃ naraḥ savitāraṃ viprā yajñaiḥ suvṛktibhiḥ |*  
> *namasyaṃti dhiyeṣitāḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवं । नरः । सवितारं । विप्राः । यज्ञैः । सुवृक्तिभिः ।  
> नमस्यंति । धिया । इषिताः ॥ १२ ॥

> *devaṃ | naraḥ | savitāraṃ | viprāḥ | yajñaiḥ | suvṛktibhiḥ |*  
> *namasyaṃti | dhiyā | iṣitāḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नरः कर्मणां नेतारो विप्रा मेधाविनोऽध्वय्यादयो धियेषिताः
> कर्मणा बुद्ध्या वा प्रेयमाणाः संतः सवितारं देवं त्वां यज्ञैर्यजनीयैर्हविर्भिः सुवृक्तिभिः शोभनस्तोत्रैश्च नमस्यंति । परिचरंति ॥ नमस्यंति । नमोवरिवश्चित्रजः क्यजिति क्यच् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The नरः (*naraḥ*), leaders of rites, and the विप्राः (*viprāḥ*), the wise adhvaryus and others, धियेषिताः (*dhiyeṣitāḥ*), impelled by action or by intellect, serve (नमस्यंति (*namasyaṃti*), "they attend on") you, the god Savitṛ, with sacrifices, that is, offerings fit for sacrifice, and with good praises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरः (*naraḥ*)—leaders of rites
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the wise adhvaryus and others
- धियेषिताः (*dhiyeṣitāḥ*)—impelled by intelligence
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—who are of divine nature
- सवितारं (*savitāraṃ*)—and of the form of Savitṛ, you
- यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)—with offerings fit for sacrifice
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—with excellent praises
- नमस्यंति (*namasyaṃti*)—they serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Savitṛ, the adhvaryus and others, leaders of rites and wise, impelled by their intelligence, serve you, who are of divine nature and of the form of Savitṛ, with offerings fit for sacrifice and with excellent praises.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Devout and wise men, impelled by intelligence, adore the divine Savitri with sacrifices and sacred hymns.

### Printed p. 640

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Suvṛktibhiḥ—the word सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*) means an excellent hymn of praise. One may say that it is formed from the root वृज् (*vṛj*) preceded by सु (*su*). In places such as नासत्याभ्यां बर्हिरिव प्र वृंजे (*nāsatyābhyāṃ barhiriva pra vṛṃje*) the root (वृज् (*vṛj*), वृंज् (*vṛṃj*)) has the sense "cuts", yet the purport is given as "procure"; in the same way the word सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*) too may be taken to mean something excellently constructed, something procured. Ordinarily the word सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*) is used only as a synonym of "hymn". The sense "purify by cutting" is natural to it. For example, just as in places such as दधिध्वे व्यक्तबर्हिषः (*dadhidhve vyaktabarhiṣaḥ*) (1-38-1) the purport is that the darbha grass is cut properly and purified, so here too the meaning is a hymn constructed with purified words; that is, the purport is a sacred and venerable hymn.

Some scholars show the derivation of this word as सु (*su*) + ऋक्ति (*ṛkti*) and explain it as an excellent hymn. For example, the scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit English Dictionary, explains su-ṛkti as su- + ṛc, ṛc preceded by su, meaning an excellent hymn consisting of ṛks, and states that the derivation should be shown in the way su-ita becomes suvita. But in places such as नमोव्यक्ति (*namovyakti*) the derivation namaḥ + ṛc is not valid.
इहेहैषां कृणुहि भोजनानि ये बर्हिषो नमोवृक्तिं न जग्मुः (*ihehaiṣāṃ kṛṇuhi bhojanāni ye barhiṣo namovṛktiṃ na jagmuḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-131-2)
In such places the word नमस् (*namas*) is explained as food or praise, and the word व्यक्ति (*vyakti*) as avoidance. It is shown to be formed from the root वृज् (*vṛj*) and used in the sense of cutting, and the purport in the quoted ṛk is that a cutting of praise does not occur. On the basis of such examples there is no difficulty in saying that the present word su-vyakti also is formed from the root वृज् (*vṛj*). Hymns made by choosing words suited to the occasion and refining them in poetic praises are what the word सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*) denotes.

That example of नमोव्यक्ति (*namovyakti*) is taken only to show that the word व्यक्ति (*vyakti*) in it is formed from the root वृज् (*vṛj*); the purport of the two words is not the same. Or else, there is room to say that even where this word is used in the sense of avoidance, the meaning is still an excellent hymn. For example—

### Printed p. 641
अग्निः न स्ववृक्तिभिर्होतारु त्वा वृणीमहे (*agniḥ na svavṛktibhirhotāru tvā vṛṇīmahe*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-1-1)
Here, in the word स्वव्यक्ति (*svavyakti*), the word स्व (*sva*) is explained as स्वयंकृताभिः (*svayaṃkṛtābhiḥ*)—made by oneself—and व्यक्तिभिः (*vyaktibhiḥ*) as दोषवर्जिताभिः (*doṣavarjitābhiḥ*)—separated from faults. The purport is "(we choose you) with hymns made by oneself and free of faults, hence excellent"; so in the present case too, सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*) may be explained as "with hymns that are excellent and, being free of faults, superior".

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोमो॑ जिगाति गातु॒विद्दे॒वाना॑मेति निष्कृ॒तं ।  
> ऋ॒तस्य॒ योनि॑मा॒सदं॑ ॥ १३ ॥

> *somo jigāti gātuviddevānāmeti niṣkṛtaṃ |*  
> *ṛtasya yonimāsadaṃ ‖ 13 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोमः । जिगाति । गात्वुविश् । देवानां । ऐति । निःकृतं ।  
> यतस्य । योनिं । आसवं ॥ १३ ॥

> *somaḥ | jigāti | gātvuviś | devānāṃ | aiti | niḥkṛtaṃ |*  
> *yatasya | yoniṃ | āsavaṃ ‖ 13 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निषोमप्रणयने सोमो जिगातीत्याद्यास्ति स ऋचः । सूत्रितं च ।
> सोमो जिगाति गातुविद्देवानां तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विनेत्यर्धर्च आरमेत् ।
> आ. ४-१८ इति ॥
> गातुवित् गातुर्वेदिमार्गः तं जानानः सोमो जिगाति । गच्छति । गंतव्यं
> स्थानं दर्शयति । देवानां संबंधि निष्कृतं संस्कृतमासदं सर्वैरासदनीयमृतस्य
> यज्ञस्य योनिं स्थानं हविर्धानाख्यमेशि । प्राप्नोति ॥ जिगाति । गा स्तुतौ । जुहोत्यादिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Agniṣoma-praṇayana, the seven ṛks beginning सोमो जिगाति (*somo jigāti*) are used; and it is prescribed in the sūtra: सोमो जिगाति गातुविद्देवानां तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विनेत्यर्धर्च आरमेत् (*somo jigāti gātuviddevānāṃ tamasya rājā varuṇastamaśvinetyardharca āramet*) (Ā. 4-18). Soma, who knows the gātu (the path to the altar), goes; he goes and shows the place to be reached. He reaches the place of the sacrifice (ṛta), called the havirdhāna, which belongs to the gods, is prepared, and is to be occupied by all. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गातुनित् (*gātunit*)—knowing his place to be reached
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- जिगाति (*jigāti*)—goes and reaches
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—that which is to belong to the gods
- निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*)—well prepared
- असदं (*asadaṃ*)—

### Printed p. 642
having a seat for the gods
- ऋतस्य योनिं (*ṛtasya yoniṃ*)—as the womb of the sacrifice (in the form of the havirdhāna)
- एति (*eti*)—is transformed into

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Knowing the place he is to reach, Soma reaches the sacrificial altar, which is the seat of the gods and well prepared, and is offered to the gods in the form of the oblation.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Soma, knowing the right path, proceeds (by it) : he goes to the excellent seat of the gods, the place of sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Agniṣoma-praṇayana rite, these three ṛks beginning सोमो जिगाति (*somo jigāti*) are to be recited for the first three ṛks to be recited at that time, as explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra: सोमो जिगाति गातुविद्देवानां तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विनेत्यर्धर्च आरमेत् (*somo jigāti gātuviddevānāṃ tamasya rājā varuṇastamaśvinetyardharca āramet*) (Ā. 4-10).

Gātuvit—the word गातु (*gātu*) means the place to be reached; it also means the path to be gone. This place to be reached is the sacrificial place on earth; this is the path of performance. (It may also be the path of going to the world of the gods.) Here it is explained as the path leading to the sacrificial altar. That this word is also used in the senses of house, hymn, etc., was stated earlier (Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Part 11, p. 503).

ऋतस्य योनिं एति (*ṛtasya yoniṃ eti*)—यज्ञस्य स्थानं हविर्धानाख्यं प्राप्नोति (*yajñasya sthānaṃ havirdhānākhyaṃ prāpnoti*). The purport is that he reaches the sacrificial place called the havirdhāna. Hence here the word गातु (*gātu*) means the womb of ṛta. It was stated earlier that the word योनि (*yoni*) too has meanings such as house, place of origin, and the chief place called Veda. Here it is explained as the chief place called havirdhāna. The pavilion built separately for placing Soma, the chief implement of the Soma sacrifice, is called havirdhāna. Or this name is also well known for the cart that brings the Soma oblation.
यदस्मिन्मोहो भवति हविर्वै देवानाग्ं सोमस्तस्माद्धविधानं नाम (*yadasminmoho bhavati havirvai devānāgṃ somastasmāddhavidhānaṃ nāma*) (Śa. Brā. 3 5-3-2)

### Printed p. 643
The Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa gives its purport thus: since Soma, the oblation of the gods, is placed in it, it is called havirdhāna. The Soma-carrier may be the cart that brings the Soma, or the chief place where it is placed.
यज्ञं वा एतत्संभरंति यत्सोमक्रयणै पदं यज्ञमुखग्ं हविर्धाने यर्हि हविर्धाने प्राची प्रवर्तयेयुः ॥ (*yajñaṃ vā etatsaṃbharaṃti yatsomakrayaṇai padaṃ yajñamukhagṃ havirdhāne yarhi havirdhāne prācī pravartayeyuḥ ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-3-1)
In this description—the havirdhānas are the mouths of the sacrifice; when they are moved forward, oil is to be put on their axles—it is clear that they are carts bringing the Soma. Bhaṭṭabhāskara, explaining the purport of this word, says हवींषि निधीयंते अनयोरिति हविर्धाने शकटे (*havīṃṣi nidhīyaṃte anayoriti havirdhāne śakaṭe*)—the name is because oblations are placed in these—as in the sentence quoted above. Whether the cart that carries Soma or the pavilion built separately to place it, both hold the chief implement of the sacrifice; so the havirdhāna that designates them is well known as the mouth of the sacrifice. In many places this havirdhāna is also used figuratively and contains a profound hidden meaning.
पुरुषो वाव यज्ञः.... .... .... .... (*puruṣo vāva yajñaḥ.... .... .... ....*) (Chā. U. 3-16-1) "The person himself is the sacrifice." Thus in the Chāndogya and others there is a description showing the identity of the limbs of the person with the limbs that are the implements of the sacrifice. Explaining this very point, the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa says:
पुरुषो वै यज्ञः .... शिर एवास्य हविर्धानं । (*puruṣo vai yajñaḥ .... śira evāsya havirdhānaṃ |*)
मुखमेवास्याहवनीयः .... ....। उदरमेवास्य सदः.... ....। (*mukhamevāsyāhavanīyaḥ .... ....| udaramevāsya sadaḥ.... ....|*)
(Śa. Brā. 3-5-3-1 to 24)
As the head is the chief limb of a person, so for the sacrifice, which is of the form of a person, the havirdhāna is chief. The āhavanīya is the mouth; the sadas is the belly; and so on—thus the chief place of the havirdhāna is declared. In many places the pair of carts is specified as the havirdhāna, and it holds a most venerable position.
प्रेतां यज्ञस्य कंभुवा युवामिदा वृणीमहे । अग्निं च हव्यवाहनं ॥ (*pretāṃ yajñasya kaṃbhuvā yuvāmidā vṛṇīmahe | agniṃ ca havyavāhanaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-41-19)
आ नामुपस्थमद्रुहा देवाः सीदंतु यज्ञियाः । इहाद्य सोमपीतये ॥ (*ā nāmupasthamadruhā devāḥ sīdaṃtu yajñiyāḥ | ihādya somapītaye ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-41-21)
In such ṛks both havirdhānas are described as bringing comfort to the sacrifice and as free of hostility. But what is the havirdhāna here? It may be the pair of carts, or it may be heaven and earth. हविर्धाने अनसी तद्रूपे द्यावापृथिव्यौ वा (*havirdhāne anasī tadrūpe dyāvāpṛthivyau vā*): when the two carts that carry the oblation are decorated,

### Printed p. 644
there is a practice of reciting the very mantras that praise heaven and earth while offering them ointment and the like. Heaven and earth themselves are also addressed as havirdhānas. The praise of these at the time of decorating them is stated in the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa thus:
हविर्धानाभ्यां प्रोह्यमाणाभ्यामनुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः । (*havirdhānābhyāṃ prohyamāṇābhyāmanubrūhītyāhādhvaryuḥ |*) (I. Brā. 1-29)
When the Soma carts called havirdhāna are being brought forward, the Adhvaryu gives the order, "Recite the mantra that praises them." Then the Hotṛ recites some ṛk mantras and praises them. The first of them is:
युजे वां ब्रह्म पूर्व्यं नमोभिर्वि श्लोक एतु पथ्येव सूरेः । (*yuje vāṃ brahma pūrvyaṃ namobhirvi śloka etu pathyeva sūreḥ |*)
शृण्वंतु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्रा आ ये धामानि दिव्यानि तस्थुः ॥ (*śṛṇvaṃtu viśve amṛtasya putrā ā ye dhāmāni divyāni tasthuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-13-1)
He recites: "Reciting the ancient mantra, I fill you with the venerable oblation. May your sound reach the gods. May all the sons of the immortal Prajāpati hear your sound."
ब्रह्मणा ना एते देवा आयुंजत यद्धविर्धाने ब्रह्मणैवैने एतद्युंक्ते न वै ब्रह्मण्वद्रिष्यति ॥ (*brahmaṇā nā ete devā āyuṃjata yaddhavirdhāne brahmaṇaivaine etadyuṃkte na vai brahmaṇvadriṣyati ‖*) **NOTE**
"O carts, in the past the gods yoked you reciting this very ancient mantra. Even now the same course is followed. No trouble approaches the person through this recitation." Then he recites the mantras praising heaven and earth beginning "प्रेतां यज्ञस्य.... (*pretāṃ yajñasya....*)". But what is the connection between the praise of the havirdhāna and the praise of heaven and earth?
द्यावापृथिवी वै देवानां हविर्धाने आस्तां ते उ एवाद्यापि हविर्धाने ते हीदमंतरेण सर्वं हविर्यदिदं किं च तस्मात्तृचं द्यावापृथिवीयमन्वाह ॥ (*dyāvāpṛthivī vai devānāṃ havirdhāne āstāṃ te u evādyāpi havirdhāne te hīdamaṃtareṇa sarvaṃ haviryadidaṃ kiṃ ca tasmāttṛcaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīyamanvāha ‖*)
Heaven and earth were the havirdhānas of the gods; even now they are the same. In them all oblations are contained. Therefore the triplet addressed to heaven and earth is to be recited: "प्रेतां यज्ञस्य.... (*pretāṃ yajñasya....*)", "द्यावा नः पृथिवी.... (*dyāvā naḥ pṛthivī....*)", "आ वा मुपस्थमद्रुहा.... (*ā vā mupasthamadruhā....*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-41-19 to 28) — these three are the triplets to be recited at this time.
Continuing the same praise, Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-13-2 is recited and the praise runs thus:

### Printed p. 645
