> *evaiḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने आयोर्मनुष्यस्य दुर्यासु गृहेष्टदब्धाः केनाप्यतिरस्कृता निधारयंतो निवसंतः कवयः क्रांतदृशो देवाः कविं मेधाविनं त्वां शशासुः ;
> होता भवेति शशंसुः । अतः कारणादर्यो यज्ञस्य स्वामी त्वं दृश्यान्दर्शनीयानद्भुतानाश्चर्यरूपोपेतानिंद्रादीनेतान्नेवानेवैर्गमनशीलैः पद्भिः पादैः स्वतेजोभिः पश्येः । जानीयाः ॥ दृश्यान् । दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे । ऋदुपधाच्चाकृपिचृतेः ।
> पा. ३-१-११० । इति कर्मणि क्यप् । कित्वादगुणः । पित्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni! The sages (कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)), the gods of far-reaching vision, who dwell undespised, unslighted by anyone, in the houses of Āyu, that is, of man, have urged you, the wise one (कविं (*kaviṃ*)), to be the Hotṛ." For this reason you, the lord of the sacrifice (आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)), with your swift-moving feet, that is, with your own splendours, behold and know these visible, wondrous gods, Indra and the others, who are endowed with marvellous forms. (The rest is grammar: दृश्यान् (*dṛśyān*) is formed from the root दृशिर् (*dṛśir*) in the sense of seeing.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- आयोः (*āyoḥ*)—of man
- दुरासु (*durāsu*)—in the houses
- अदब्धाः (*adabdhāḥ*)—free from contempt
- निधारयंत (*nidhārayaṃta*)—dwelling
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the sages, of far-reaching vision
- कविं (*kaviṃ*)—you, the wise one
- शशासुः (*śaśāsuḥ*)—praised (saying "you must be the Hotṛ")
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—therefore
- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—the lord
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- दृश्यान् (*dṛśyān*)—those of attractive form
- अद्भुतान् (*adbhutān*)—those of marvellous form
- एतान् (*etān*)—these gods, Indra and the others
- एवैः (*evaiḥ*)—moving
- पद्भिः (*padbhiḥ*)—with your splendours
- पश्येः (*paśyeḥ*)—you behold and know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the sages of far-reaching vision, who dwell undespised in the house of the sacrificer, have praised you, the wise one, saying "you must be the Hotṛ." Therefore you, the lord, behold and know, with your moving splendours, these gods, Indra and the others, who have attractive and marvellous forms.

### Printed p. 719

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The unreviled sages abiding in the dwellings of man have glorified the sage (Agni); therefore, lord of sacrifice, you may proceed with swift-moving feet to behold the admirable and marvellous deities.
#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वम॑ग्ने वा॒घते॑ सु॒प्रणी॑तिः सु॒तसो॑माय विध॒ते य॑विष्ठ ।  
> रत्नं॑ भर शशमा॒नाय॑ घृष्टे पृ॒थु श्चं॒द्रमव॑से चर्षणि॒प्राः॥

> *tvamagne vāghate supraṇītiḥ sutasomāya vidhate yaviṣṭha |*  
> *ratnaṃ bhara śaśamānāya ghṛṣṭe pṛthu ścaṃdramavase carṣaṇiprāḥ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । अग्ने । वाघते । सुप्रनीतिः । सुतसोमाय । विधते । यविष्ठ ।  
> रत्नं । भर । शशमानाय । फृष्टे । पृथु । चंद्रं । अवसे । चर्षणिप्राः ॥ १३ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | vāghate | supranītiḥ | sutasomāya | vidhate | yaviṣṭha |*  
> *ratnaṃ | bhara | śaśamānāya | phṛṣṭe | pṛthu | caṃdraṃ | avase | carṣaṇiprāḥ ‖ 13 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यविष्ठ युवतम फृष्टे दीप्तियुक्त । यद्वा । परेषां घर्षणशील हे
> अग्ने चर्षणिप्रा अपेक्षितप्रदानेन मनुष्याणां कामपूरकः सुप्रणीति: सुसूत्तरवेद्यां प्रणयनीयस्त्वं सुतसोमाय विधते तव परिचरणं कुर्वते शशमानाय
> त्वां स्तुवते वाघते यज्ञनिर्वाहकाय यजमानाय पृथु प्रभूतं चंद्रमाह्लादकारि रत्नमुत्तमं धनमवसे रक्षणाय भर । आहर । प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥ सुप्रणीति: ।
> णीञ् प्रापणे । कर्मणि क्तिन् । तादौ च निति कृतीत्यनंतरप्रशब्दस्योदात्तत्वं ।
> पृथु श्चंद्रमित्यत्र संहितायां ह्रस्वाच्चंद्रोत्तरपदे मंत्र इति सुडागमः ।
> श्चुत्वेन शकारः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Yaviṣṭha, youngest, O फृष्टे (*phṛṣṭe*), endowed with radiance; or else, O one who crushes others; O Agni, you who fulfil men's wishes by granting what they desire (चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*)), and who are to be well led forward (सुप्रणीतिः (*supraṇītiḥ*)) on the northern altar: bring (भर (*bhara*), that is, give) excellent, abundant, delight-giving wealth, for his protection, to the sacrificer who accomplishes the sacrifice, who has pressed Soma for you, who attends upon you, who praises you. (The rest is grammar: सुप्रणीति: (*supraṇīti:*) from the root णीञ् (*ṇīñ*) in the sense of leading; the accent; the augment *suṭ* in पृथु । चंद्रं (*pṛthu | caṃdraṃ*) in the Saṃhitā; the श्चुत्व (*ścutva*) change to the sibilant.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—O extremely young one
- फृष्टे (*phṛṣṭe*)—O destroyer of enemies
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni

### Printed p. 720
- चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*)—you who grant what is desired
- सुप्रणीतिः (*supraṇītiḥ*)—who are established on the northern altar by the excellent rite
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- सुतसोमाय (*sutasomāya*)—to him who has pressed Soma for you
- विधते (*vidhate*)—to him who serves you
- शशमानाय (*śaśamānāya*)—to him who praises you
- वाघते (*vāghate*)—to the sacrificer, who accomplishes the sacrifice
- पृथु (*pṛthu*)—abundant
- चंद्रं (*caṃdraṃ*)—delight-giving
- रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*)—excellent wealth
- अवसे (*avase*)—for his protection
- भर (*bhara*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, extremely young and destroyer of enemies, you who grant what is desired and are established on the northern altar by the excellent rite: provide, for the protection of the sacrificer, who presses Soma and offers it to you, who praises and serves you and accomplishes the sacrifice, abundant, delight-giving and excellent wealth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Resplendent Agni, youngest of the gods, the satisfier of (the desires of) men, who are easily to be conducted (to the altar), bestow joy-yielding and abundant wealth for his preservation upon the worshipper who praises and worships you and offers you libations.
#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधा॑ ह॒ यद्व॒यम॑ग्ने त्वा॒या प॒द्भिर्हस्ते॑भिश्चकृ॒मा त॒नूभिः॑।  
> रथं॒ न क्रंतो॒ अप॑सा भु॒रिजो॑र्ऋ॒तं ये॑मुः सु॒ध्य॑  ॒
> आशुषाणाः ॥ १४ ॥

> *adhā ha yadvayamagne tvāyā padbhirhastebhiścakṛmā tanūbhiḥ|*  
> *rathaṃ na kraṃto apasā bhurijorṛtaṃ yemuḥ sudhya*  
> *āśuṣāṇāḥ ‖ 14 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । ह । यत् । वयं । अग्ने । त्वाया । पट्भिः । हस्तेभिः । चक्रम । तनूभिः ।  
> रथं । न । क्रंतः । अपसा । भुरिजोः । ऋतं । येमुः । सुध्यः । आशुषाणाः ॥१४॥

> *adha | ha | yat | vayaṃ | agne | tvāyā | paṭbhiḥ | hastebhiḥ | cakrama | tanūbhiḥ |*  
> *rathaṃ | na | kraṃtaḥ | apasā | bhurijoḥ | ṛtaṃ | yemuḥ | sudhyaḥ | āśuṣāṇāḥ ‖14‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने अध ह अथ खलु वयं त्वाया त्वत्कामनया पद्भिः पादैर्हस्तेभिर्हस्तेस्तनूभिरन्यैश्चावयवैश्चक्रम यत् यस्मात्कारणात्कर्मसिद्ध्यर्थं त्वामुपपादयामस्तस्मात्तुध्यः सुकर्माण आशुषाणाः कर्माणि व्याप्प्नुवंतस्तेंगिरस ऋतं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, अध ह (*adha ha*) means "now indeed": we have laboured with desire for you (त्वाया (*tvāyā*)), with feet, hands, bodies and other limbs. Because for the success of the rite we thus prepare you, therefore the good workers (सुध्यः (*sudhyaḥ*)), the Aṅgirases, who pervade the rites (आशुषाणाः (*āśuṣāṇāḥ*)), …the true one (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)) (the sentence continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 721

> सत्यभूतं त्वां भुरिजोः । बिभृतः कर्मकरणसामर्थ्यं पदार्थान्वेति भुरिजौ
> बाहू । तयोरपसा मंथनाख्येन कर्मणा येमुः । उद्यच्छंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> रथं न । यथा क्रंतः कारवः शिल्पिनः क्रामंतोऽध्वगा वा हस्तयोर्यथा रथमुद्यच्छंति तद्वत् । यद्वा । भुरिजोः । देवान्मनुष्यांश्च बिभृत इति भुरिजौ द्यावापृथिव्यौ । तयोर्मध्येऽपसा परिचरणकर्मणा सत्यभूतं तमग्निं येमुः । उद्यच्छंति ॥ अध । संहितायां निपातस्य चेति दीर्घः ! क्रंतः । करोतेः शतरि बहुलं
> छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । भुरिजोः । डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोः ।
> भृञ उच्च । उ. २-७१ । इतीजिप्रत्ययः । धातोरुकारो रपरः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing:) …you who are true (सत्यभूतं (*satyabhūtaṃ*)). भुरिजोः (*bhurijoḥ*): the two arms, which bear the capacity to perform work; with the work called churning performed by these two, they lift up (येमुः (*yemuḥ*), "raise") Agni. The example: रथं न (*rathaṃ na*), as craftsmen (क्रंतः (*kraṃtaḥ*)) or travellers lift a chariot with their hands. Or else: भुरिजोः (*bhurijoḥ*) are heaven and earth, which bear gods and men; between these two, by the work of service, they raise Agni, who is true. (The rest is grammar: the lengthening in अध (*adha*) in the Saṃhitā; क्रंतः (*kraṃtaḥ*) from the root करोतेः (*karoteḥ*) with the participial affix; भुरिजोः (*bhurijoḥ*) from डुभृञ् (*ḍubhṛñ*) with the affix *iji*, Uṇ. Sū. 2-71.) **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अध ह (*adha ha*)—afterwards
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- त्वाया (*tvāyā*)—desiring your favour
- पद्भिः (*padbhiḥ*)—with feet
- हस्तेभिः (*hastebhiḥ*)—with hands
- तनूभिः (*tanūbhiḥ*)—with other excellent limbs
- यत् (*yat*)—for which favour
- चक्रम (*cakrama*)—we prepare ourselves for your service (then)
- क्रंतः (*kraṃtaḥ*)—craftsmen
- रथं न (*rathaṃ na*)—as they refine and build a chariot
- सुध्यः (*sudhyaḥ*)—good performers of rites
- आशुषाणाः (*āśuṣāṇāḥ*)—the Aṅgirases, intent on the rites
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—you, who are of the nature of truth
- भुरिजोः (*bhurijoḥ*)—of their arms
- अपसा (*apasā*)—by laborious work
- येमुः (*yemuḥ*)—they make ready

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, when we, desiring your favour, prepare ourselves for your service with our hands, our feet and our other excellent limbs, the Aṅgirases, good performers of rites and intent on the rites, perfect your worship by the labour of their arms, as craftsmen refine and build a chariot.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Therefore, Agni, when we labour for you with hands and feet, and all our members, the pious performers of rites, (the Angirasas), exercise their arms in the work (of attrition), as wheelwrights fabricate a car.

> *divaḥ | putrāḥ | aṃgirasaḥ | bhavema | adriṃ | rujema | dhaninaṃ | śucaṃtaḥ ‖ 15 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वामदेवोऽनैः षड्भिरंगिरोभिः सह ब्रूते । अधापि च मातुरुषसः सकाशात्सप्त सप्तसंख्याका विप्राः प्राज्ञा वयं स्मः । प्रथमाः श्रेष्ठा वयं वेधसोऽग्नेः परिचारकान्नान् वेधसो विधातन् रश्मिन् ना जायेमहि। वयं जनयामः।
> दिवो द्योतमानस्यादित्यस्य पुत्रा वयमंगिरसो भवेम । भूतिमंतः स्याम ।
> शुचंतो दीप्यमाना वयं धनिनमुदकवंतमद्रिं मेघं रुजेम । वर्षार्थं
> भिंद्याम । यद्वा । धनिनं पणिनामकासुरापहृतगोधनयुक्तमद्रिं पर्वतं
> रुजेम । अंगिरसामादित्यपुत्रत्वमेवमाम्नायते । तस्य यद्रेतसः प्रथममुददीप्यत तदसावादित्योऽभवदित्युपक्रम्य येऽंगारा आसंस्थेऽंगिरसोऽभवन् । ऐ.
> ब्रा- ३-३४ । इति ॥ जायेमहि । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । लिजु ज्ञाजनोर्जॆति जादेशः ।
> वेधसः । डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोरित्यस्माद्विधाइतो वेध च । उ- ४-२२४ । इत्यसिप्रत्ययः । धातोर्वॆध इत्यादेशः । दिवस्सुत्रा इत्यत्र संहितायां षष्याः पतिपुत्रेति
> विसर्जनीयस्य सत्वं । रुजेम । रुजो भंगे । अदादिः । लिजु रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vāmadeva speaks together with six other Aṅgirases. "And now, from the mother Uṣas we are seven wise ones (विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)); we are the first, the best. We generate the …, the attendants of Agni, the rays." **NOTE**. "May we, sons of the shining Āditya (heaven), be Aṅgirases, that is, prosperous. Shining, may we split the watery (धनिनं (*dhaninaṃ*)) mountain (अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)), the cloud, for the sake of rain." Or else: may we split the mountain that holds the cattle-wealth carried off by the asura named Paṇi. The sonship of the Aṅgirases to Āditya is thus handed down: beginning "that which first blazed up of his seed became that Āditya," it says that the embers became the Aṅgirases: तस्य यद्रेतसः प्रथममुददीप्यत तदसावादित्योऽभवदित्युपक्रम्य येऽंगारा आसंस्थेऽंगिरसोऽभवन् । ऐ. (*tasya yadretasaḥ prathamamudadīpyata tadasāvādityo 'bhavadityupakramya ye 'ṃgārā āsaṃsthe 'ṃgiraso 'bhavan | ai.*) (Ai. Brā. 3-34). (The rest is grammar: जायेमहि (*jāyemahi*) from जनी (*janī*) with *liṅ* and the substitute जा (*jā*); वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*) with the affix *asi*, Uṇ. Sū. 4-224; the visarga becoming स (*sa*) in दिवस्पुत्रा (*divasputrā*); रुजेम (*rujema*) from रुजो (*rujo*) in the sense of breaking.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रथमाः (*prathamāḥ*)—the best
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven in number (seven persons)
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the wise ones; we
- मातुः (*mātuḥ*)—of the mother of the world
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—from Uṣas
- वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*)—of Agni
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—the rays
- जायेमहि (*jāyemahi*)—we bring forth
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the shining Āditya
- पुत्राः (*putrāḥ*)—sons

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We, the best, seven in number and wise, bring forth the rays of Agni from Uṣas, the mother of the world. May we, who are sons of the shining Āditya and famed as Aṅgirases, be possessed of prosperity. Shining, may we split the mountain that holds cattle-wealth and obtain the cattle.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May we seven priests first in order engender from the maternal dawn the worshippers of the creator (Agni); may we Angirasas be the sons of heaven, and, radiant, divide the wealth-containing mauntain.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—आदित्यस्य पुत्राः अंगिरसः (*ādityasya putrāḥ aṃgirasaḥ*). On the origin of the Aṅgirases see Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 3, p. 520, and Part 10, p. 269; and see also the special topics of the 15th ṛk of the third sūkta.

> हे अग्ने अधापि च परासः श्रेष्ठाः प्रत्नासः पुराणा ऋतं सत्यभूतं यज्ञं
> यथा यथावदाशुषाणा अश्नुवाना नोऽस्माकं पितरोंगिरसः शुचि दीप्तं स्थानमयन । अगच्छन् । तथा दीधितिं तेजश्चागच्छन् । किंच उक्तशास उक्तानां शस्त्राणां शंसितारः क्षाम क्षयकारणं तमः पापं ना भिंदंतो विनाशयंतोऽंगिरसोरुणीररुणवर्णाः पणिभिरपहृता गा उषसो ना अप व्रन् । अपावृण्वन् ।
> प्रकाशितवंत इत्यर्थः ॥ अयन् । इण् गत् । लजूणो यण्णिति यण् । व्यत्ययेनाडागमः । दीधितिं । दीधिज् दीप्ति देवनयोरित्यस्मात् क्तिनि ह्रस्वश्कांदसः । नित्तादाद्युदात्तः । उक्तशासः । उक्तशब्द उपपदे शन्नु स्तुतावित्यस्मान्मंत्रे श्वेतवहोक्षशस्सुरोडाशो ण्णिन्निति ण्णिन् नकारलोपश्च निपातनादेव । पदकाले ह्रस्वश्कांदसः ।
> अरुणीः । गौरादिजीषंतः । एकादेशस्वरः । व्रन् । वृणोतेर्लुङ् मंत्रे घसेत्यादिना चेर्लुक् । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa construes the verse as follows. "O Agni, and further, our fathers the Aṅgirases, who are excellent (परासः (*parāsaḥ*)) and ancient (प्रत्नासः (*pratnāsaḥ*)), having duly (यथा (*yathā*)) attained (आशुषाणाः (*āśuṣāṇāḥ*)) the true sacrifice (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)), went to the bright place (शुचि (*śuci*), "shining"). In the same way they came to radiance (दीधितिं (*dīdhitiṃ*), "lustre"). Moreover, being reciters of the recited śastras (उक्तशासः (*uktaśāsaḥ*)), and splitting the darkness (क्षाम (*kṣāma*), "the cause of decay"), that is sin, the Aṅgirases uncovered the ruddy (अरुणीः (*aruṇīḥ*), "red-coloured") cows carried off by the Paṇis, and the dawns (गा उषसो ना (*gā uṣaso nā*))." अप व्रन् (*apa vran*) means "they opened", that is, they made them manifest.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni!
- अध (*adha*)—and
- परासः (*parāsaḥ*)—excellent
- प्रत्नासः (*pratnāsaḥ*)—ancient
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—fathers, the Aṅgirases
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—the sacrifice, which is true
- यथा (*yathā*)—as prescribed
- आशुषाणाः (*āśuṣāṇāḥ*)—having accomplished
- शुचि (*śuci*)—the shining place
- अयन् (*ayan*)—reached
- दीधितिं (*dīdhitiṃ*)—also obtained lustre
- उक्तशासनः (*uktaśāsanaḥ*)—reciting the śastra-mantras**NOTE**
- क्षाम (*kṣāma*)—the darkness
- भिंदंतः (*bhiṃdaṃtaḥ*)—splitting
- अरुणीः (*aruṇīḥ*)—the golden-hued cows
- अप व्रन् (*apa vran*)—made them shine (made them visible)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, our fathers the Aṅgirases, excellent and ancient, duly performed the true sacrifice and reached the shining place. They themselves also became full of brilliance. Reciting the śastra-mantras and splitting the darkness, they made the golden-hued cows shine forth (become visible).

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Thus, Agni, our excellent and ancient forefathers, celebrators of holy sacrifice, proceeded to (the region of) pure light, and, reciting prayers and dispersing gloom, they made manifest the purple (cows).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आग्रयण आग्नेंद्रस्य हविषः सुकर्माण इति याज्या । सूत्रितं च । सुकर्माणः सुरुचो देवयंतो विश्वे देवास आ गत । आ. २-९ । इति ॥
> सुकर्माणः सुष्पनुष्ठितयागादिकर्माणः सुरुचः शोभनदीप्तयो देवयंतो देवान् कामयमाना देवा देवनशीलाः स्तोतारो जनिम स्वकीयं
> मानुषं जन्म धमंतो यागादिलक्षणेन कर्मणा निर्मलीकुर्वंतः । तत्र दृष्टांतः।

> हविर्भिर्दिर्पयंत इंद्रं ववृधंतः सोमेन स्तुत्या वा वधयंतोंगिरसः
> परिषदंतः परितः सीदंतः संत ऊर्वं महांतं गव्यं गोसंघमग्मन् । प्राप्पुवन् ॥ सुकर्माणः । सोर्मनसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । धमंतः । ध्मा शब्दाग्निसंयोगयोः । शतरि पाघ्रादिना धमादेशः शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे शतुर्लसार्वधातुकस्वरः । ववृधंतः । वृधु वर्धने । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । शतरि शपः श्लुः ।
> गव्यं । गवां समूह इत्यर्थे खलगोरथादिति यः । अगम् । गमर्लुजि ज्लेर्लुकि
> रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Āgrayaṇa, for the oblation of Agni and Indra, सुकर्माणः (*sukarmāṇaḥ*) is the yājyā verse. It is also stated in the sūtra: सुकर्माणः सुरुचो देवयंतो विश्वे देवास आ गत (*sukarmāṇaḥ suruco devayaṃto viśve devāsa ā gata*) (Ā. Sū. 2-9).

The Aṅgirases are "of good works" (सुकर्माणः (*sukarmāṇaḥ*)): their sacrifices and other rites are well performed. They are "of good lustre" (सुरुचः (*surucaḥ*)): their splendour is beautiful. They are देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*), desiring the gods. They are देवाः (*devāḥ*), the praisers, who are "of a shining nature". They purify (धमंतः (*dhamaṃtaḥ*)) their own human birth (जनिम (*janima*)) by rites such as the sacrifice. The illustration is अयो न (*ayo na*): as smiths blow iron with the bellows, so do they. Such as they are, making Agni shine (शुचंतः (*śucaṃtaḥ*)) with oblations, and increasing Indra (ववृधंतः (*vavṛdhaṃtaḥ*)) with soma or with praise, sitting around (परिषदंतः (*pariṣadaṃtaḥ*), "sitting on all sides"), they reached (अग्मन् (*agman*)) the great (ऊर्वं (*ūrvaṃ*)) herd of cows (गव्यं (*gavyaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुकर्माणि (*sukarmāṇi*)—those who perform excellent works
- सुरुचः (*surucaḥ*)—of excellent radiance
- देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*)—desiring godhood
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the Aṅgirases, of divine nature

### Printed p. 726

- अयो न (*ayo na*)—as a smith refines iron in his furnace
- जनिम (*janima*)—their human birth
- धमंतः (*dhamaṃtaḥ*)—made it refined by rites such as the sacrifice (and)
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- शुचंतः (*śucaṃtaḥ*)—making shine
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- ववृधंतः (*vavṛdhaṃtaḥ*)—making him grow strong by praises
- परिषदंतः (*pariṣadaṃtaḥ*)—searching on all sides
- ऊर्वं (*ūrvaṃ*)—great
- गव्यं (*gavyaṃ*)—wealth of cattle
- अग्मन् (*agman*)—obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirases, excellent performers of rites, of splendid radiance, desiring godhood and divine in nature, refined their human birth by rites such as the sacrifice, as a smith refines iron in his furnace. And making Agni shine, making Indra grow strong by praises, and searching on all sides, they obtained great wealth of cattle.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Performers of good works, brilliant and devout, the praises of the gods have freed their birth from impurity, as (a smith heats) iron : exciting Agni, elevating Indra, and wandering about (in search), they have gone to the vast (hidden) herd of cattle.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Āgrayaṇa-iṣṭi, in the oblation-offering made to the deities Agni and Indra, this Ṛk सुकर्माणः (*sukarmāṇaḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is set out by the Āśvalāyana-śrautasūtra, in the sūtra सुकर्माइः सुरुचो देवयंतो विश्वे देवास आ गत (*sukarmāiḥ suruco devayaṃto viśve devāsa ā gata*) (Ā. Sū. 2-9).

> *martānāṃ | cit | urvaśīḥ | akṛpran | vṛdhe | cit | aryaḥ | uparasya | āyoḥ ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उग्र तेजस्विन्ने अग्ने देवानामंगिरसां संबंधि यज्जनिम यं गोसंघमंति पर्वतस्य समीप आख्यत् । आ समंतादिंद्रोऽपश्यत् । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> यूथेव । यथा पश्वः पशूनां गवां यूथानि क्षुमत्यन्नवत्याढ्यगृहे वर्तमानानि
> पश्यंति जनास्तद्वत् । यद्वा । हे अग्ने तव परिचारकोऽंगिरोगणो देवानामिंद्रादीनां यज्ञनिम योऽयं जनोऽंति मदंतिके पश्वः पणिभिरपहृतान्वशूनाख्यत् । समंतात्पश्यति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । यथा क्षुमति शब्दं कुर्वाणे गवां
> यूथा यूथे पशून्त्यंति तद्वत् । मर्तानां चिन्मनुष्याणामुर्वशीरूरुभ्यामश्नुवानाः । उर्वभ्यश्नुत ऊरुभ्यामश्नुत इति यास्कः । नि. ५-१६। प्रजा अकृप्रन् ।
> ताभिरानीताभिर्गोभिः कृप्ता: समर्था अभवन् । चिदपि च अर्यः स्वामी लब्धगोधन उपरस्कोप्तस्य निषिक्तस्यापत्यस्य वृधे वर्धनाय समर्थो भवति । तथायोर्मनुष्यस्य भृत्यादेश पोषणे समर्थो भवति ॥ यूथेव । शसः सप्तम्या ना
> डादेशः । क्षुमति । क्षुदित्यन्ननाम । यद्वा । टुक्षु शब्दे । भावे क्विप् । छांदसस्तकारलोपः । तदस्यास्तीति मतुप् । हस्रनुड्भ्यां मतुबिति मतुप उदात्तत्वं ।
> अख्यत् । ख्या प्रकथने । लुजु चेरस्यतिवक्तिख्यातिभ्योऽज्जात्यजादेशः। आतो लोपः।
> जनिम । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । हृजनिभ्यामिमनिन्नि तीमनिन्नत्ययः । नित्त्वादाम्युदात्तः । अकृप्रन् । कृपू सामर्थ्ये । लजु बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । रुडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O fierce (उग्र (*ugra*)), radiant Agni, the herd of cows belonging to the gods, the Aṅgirases, which (यत् जनिम (*yat janima*)) near (अंति (*aṃti*)) the mountain Indra beheld (आ अख्यत् (*ā akhyat*)) on all sides." The illustration is यूथेव (*yūtheva*): as people see herds of cattle, of cows, living in the house of a rich man who has plenty of food (क्षुमति (*kṣumati*)).

Or else: "O Agni, your attendant band of Aṅgirases sees all around the cattle of the gods, Indra and the others, carried off by the Paṇis, which this person is near me (अंति (*aṃti*))." The illustration: as, when the herd of cows is making a noise, people see the cattle in the herd.

मर्तानां चित् (*martānāṃ cit*): of mortals, men; उर्वशीः (*urvaśīḥ*) are those who pervade with the thighs. Sāyaṇa quotes Yāska: उर्वभ्यश्नुत ऊरुभ्यामश्नुत इति यास्कः (*urvabhyaśnuta ūrubhyāmaśnuta iti yāskaḥ*) (Ni. 5-16).**NOTE** The progeny (प्रजा (*prajā*)) became able (अकृप्रन् (*akṛpran*)), that is, competent, through the cows brought by them. Moreover the master (अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)) who has obtained the wealth of cattle becomes able for the growth (वृधे (*vṛdhe*)) of the offspring sown (उपरस्य (*uparasya*)), and in the same way he is able for the nourishing of men, dependents and so on (आयोः (*āyoḥ*)).**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उग्र (*ugra*)—O radiant Agni
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—belonging to the Aṅgirā seers
- यत् जनिम (*yat janima*)—which herd of cows
- अंति (*aṃti*)—near the mountain
- यूथेव पश्वः (*yūtheva paśvaḥ*)—as people see a herd of cattle
- क्षुमति (*kṣumati*)—in a house provided with wealth of food
- आ अख्यत् (*ā akhyat*)—Indra saw all around. [Or else] 
- हे उग्र (*he ugra*)—O Agni!
- अंगिरोगणः (*aṃgirogaṇaḥ*)—the company of Aṅgirā seers who serve you
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—belonging to the gods, Indra and the others
- पश्वः (*paśvaḥ*)—carried off by the asuras called Paṇis
- क्षुमति (*kṣumati*)—lowing
- यूथेव (*yūtheva*)—like a herd of cows

- यज्ञनिम (*yajñanima*)—as people see it, near
- अंति (*aṃti*)—near
- आ अख्यत् (*ā akhyat*)—Indra saw all around
- मर्तानां चित् (*martānāṃ cit*)—belonging to men
- उर्वशीः (*urvaśīḥ*)—the cows
- अकृपन् (*akṛpan*)—became able to obtain
- चित् (*cit*)—and
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—the master, the householder who has obtained cows
- उपरस्य (*uparasya*)—excellent works
- वृधे (*vṛdhe*)—becomes able to increase
- आयोः (*āyoḥ*)—(and) becomes able also to nourish men, that is, dependents and the like

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O radiant Agni, as one sees the cows in the cattle-shed of a house abounding in food, so Indra saw all around the cows of the Aṅgirā seers carried off by the Paṇis. Or else: as people see well-nourished cattle in a house provided with wealth of food, so Indra saw the cows of the Aṅgirā seers carried off by the Paṇis. The master of the house who has obtained the herd of cows performs excellent works and becomes able to nourish his dependents, sons, grandsons and the rest.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Fierce (Agni), when (Indra) proclaimed the near presence of the herd of the cows of the divine (Angirasas) as a herd of cattle in a well-stored stall, the progeny of mortals were thereby enabled (to perform pious acts) and the master of the family rendered competent to (provide for) the increase of posterity and (the support of) dependents

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The meaning of this Ṛk is not clear. The commentator's explanation too is not lucid, and the seer's intention cannot be known. The commentator has explained the word जनिम (*janima*) as a herd of cows and the word उर्वशीः (*urvaśīḥ*) as progeny; yet it has not been possible to fit a definite meaning to this Ṛk. The scholar Wilson has explained it thus:

आ यूथेव क्षुमति पश्वः अख्यत् (*ā yūtheva kṣumati paśvaḥ akhyat*) देवानां यत् जनिम अंति (*devānāṃ yat janima aṃti*)—The expression literally means, like a herd in food-possessing animals; he had said of the gods that which birth is nigh ; Sayana interprets जनिम (*janima*) as गोसंघं (*gosaṃghaṃ*) and makes out the rest as above, or he proposes an alternative, not more intelligible; the second half of the stanza is equally obscure as the first. मर्तानां चित् उर्वशीः अकृप्रन् (*martānāṃ cit urvaśīḥ akṛpran*) वृधे चित् अर्यः उपरस्य आयोः (*vṛdhe cit aryaḥ uparasya āyoḥ*), उर्वशीः (*urvaśīḥ*) is rendered by Sayana प्रजा (*prajā*) progeny, as if it was the nominative instead of being the accusative plural ; and if so, there is no nominative to अकृप्रन् (*akṛpran*) were made able ; the word is remarkable, and is made more so by Sayana's reference to Yaska निरुक्त (*nirukta*). 5-1 where the word means, as usual अप्सराः (*apsarāḥ*) and the etymology is ऊरुभ्यामश्नुते (*ūrubhyāmaśnute*) who pervades or proceeds from the thigh. conformably to the Pauranik legend of her birth from the thigh of Narayana. See also the विक्रमोर्वशीय (*vikramorvaśīya*) of काळिदास (*kāḷidāsa*) which shows the legend to be of some antiquity.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अक॑र्म ते॒ स्वप॑सो अभूम ऋ॒तम॑वस्रन्नु॒षसो॑ विभा॒तीः ।

> चक्षुः ॥ १९ ॥

> *akarma te svapaso abhūma ṛtamavasrannuṣaso vibhātīḥ |*  
> *anūnamagniṃ purudhā suścaṃdraṃ devasya marmṛjataścāru*  
> *cakṣuḥ ‖ 19 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अकर्म । ते । सुअपसः । अभूम । ऋतं । अवस्रन् । उषसः । विभातीः ।  
> अनूनं । अग्निं । पुरुधा । सुचंद्रं । देवस्य । मर्मृजतः । चारु । चक्षुः ॥ १९ ॥

> *akarma | te | suapasaḥ | abhūma | ṛtaṃ | avasran | uṣasaḥ | vibhātīḥ |*  
> *anūnaṃ | agniṃ | purudhā | sucaṃdraṃ | devasya | marmṛjataḥ | cāru | cakṣuḥ ‖ 19 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने ते तव परिचरणमकर्म । कुर्मः । तेन कर्मणा स्वपसः शोभनकर्माणोऽभूम । विभातीर्वुच्छंत्य उषस ऋतं तेजोऽवस्रन् । आच्छादयंति ।
> धारयंतीत्यर्थः । तथा ता उषसोऽनूनं संपूर्णं पुरुधा बहुधा सुश्चंद्रं
> सुष्ठाह्लादकारिणं यद्वा सुहिरण्यमग्निं धारयंति । किंच देवस्य द्योतमानस्य
> तव चारु मनोहरं चक्षुस्तेजो मर्मृजतः परिचरंतो वयं स्वपसोऽभूमेति पूर्वेणान्वयः ॥ अकर्म । करोतेर्लजु बहुलु छंधसीति विकरणस्य लुक् ।
> मर्मुजतः । मृजूष् शुद्धौ । यज्लुकि रुग्रिकौ च लुकीत्यभ्यासस्य रुगागमः ।
> शतरि नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुरिति नुमभावः । अभ्यस्तस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, we have done (अकर्म (*akarma*), "we do") service to you; by that work we have become (अभूम (*abhūma*)) of good works (स्वपसः (*svapasaḥ*)). The shining dawns (विभातीः (*vibhātīḥ*)), as they break forth, cover or bear (अवस्रन् (*avasran*)) the light (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*), "brightness"), that is, they hold it. In the same way those dawns bear Agni, who is complete (अनूनं (*anūnaṃ*)), in many ways (पुरुधा (*purudhā*)), and who gives excellent delight (सुश्चंद्रं (*suścaṃdraṃ*)), or else is of good gold." Further, serving (मर्मृजतः (*marmṛjataḥ*)) the lovely (चारु (*cāru*)), charming eye, the lustre (चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)), of you, the shining god (देवस्य (*devasya*)), we have become of good works. The construction is with the preceding words.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) विभातीः (*vibhātīḥ*)—shining
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—of the dawn
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—the lustre
- अवस्रन् (*avasran*)—spread out (and)
- अनूनं (*anūnaṃ*)—that which is full and complete, without deficiency
- पुरुधा (*purudhā*)—in many ways

- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—the lustre of Agni (it bears)
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of you, the shining one
- चारु (*cāru*)—beautiful
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—the lustre
- मर्मृजतः (*marmṛjataḥ*)—serving
- ते (*te*)—your worship
- अकर्म (*akarma*)—we perform (and therefore)
- स्वपसः (*svapasaḥ*)—as possessors of excellent work
- अभूम (*abhūma*)—we become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the lustre of the shining dawn spreads everywhere, and it bears the lustre of Agni, which is full and delights in many ways. Serving your beautiful, shining lustre, we perform your worship; and therefore we become possessors of excellent work.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We have worshipped you (Agni), and have thereby become the performers of a good work, adoring the full and variously delighting Agni, the beautiful lustre of the radiant divinity, when the brilliant dawns have arrayed (themselves) in light.

> अवोचाम । वच परिभाषणे । लुजि क्लेरजादेशः । पादादित्वादनिघातः । कृणुहि ।

> हेर्विकल्पेन पित्त्वादजुतश्चति धिरादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O creator (vedhas), O Agni, to you the wise (kavi) we have recited these praises (ukthas, i.e. śastras). Accept them, take pleasure in them. Moreover blaze up; make us exceedingly rich in wealth. That is what is said: O Purūvāra, you who are to be chosen by many, bestow on us great wealth (mahaḥ rāyaḥ, "ample wealth"). The remainder of the block is grammar: the forms avocāma, kṛṇuhi, vasyasaḥ, yandhi.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वेधः (*vedhaḥ*)—O creator
- अग्ने (*agne*)—Agni
- कवये (*kavaye*)—the wise one
- ते (*te*)—addressing you
- एता उक्तानि (*etā uktāni*)—these śastra-mantras
- अवोचाम (*avocāma*)—we recite
- ता (*tā*)—them
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept
- उच्चोचस्व (*uccocasva*)—shine excellently
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- वस्यसः (*vasyasaḥ*)—as possessors of wealth
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—make
- पुरुवार (*puruvāra*)—O Agni, desired by many
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—abundant
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth
- प्र यंधि (*pra yaṃdhi*)—give to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the creator, we recite these śastra-mantras addressed to you, the wise one. Accept them. Shine excellently. Make us possessors of wealth. O Agni, desired by many, give us abundant wealth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Creator, Agni, we have repeated these your praises to you who are all-wise ; do you accept them : blaze aloft ; make us opulent: you are worshipped by many ; bestow upon us ample wealth.

## Sūkta 3 (Maṇḍala 4)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ वो राजानमिति षोडशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं वामदेवस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमाग्नेयं । आ वः षोळशेत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्विनियोग
> उक्तः ॥

> सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि हदिनारु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ वामदेवनु ऋषियु ; अग्नियु
> देवतॆयु ; त्रिष्टुप् छंदस्सु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि आ वः षोळश ऎंदु हेळिरुवुदु. प्रातर

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The third sūkta, आ वो राजानं (*ā vo rājānaṃ*), has sixteen ṛks; its seer is Vāmadeva, its deity Agni, its metre Triṣṭubh; the Anukramaṇī says आ वः षोळश (*ā vaḥ ṣoḷaśa*). Its use (viniyoga) in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Aśvina-śastra has been stated before. The Kannada Anuvāda adds that this is the third sūkta of the first anuvāka. The particulars given: Maṇḍala 4; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 3; Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 4; Vargas 20, 21, 22; number of ṛks in the sūkta 16; Ṛṣi Vāmadeva; Devatā Agni; Chandas Triṣṭubh.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O priests and sacrificers, make Agni yours for protection: the king (lord) of the sacrifice (adhvara), the invoker (hotṛ) of the gods, Rudra — "the roaring one", or "the one who runs", or "the one who makes enemies weep". Alternatively, with the text एषा ना अग्नेस्तनूर्यद्रुद्र (*eṣā nā agnestanūryadrudra*), he is of Rudra's nature. He is the satyayaj of the two worlds (rodasī, heaven and earth): the giver of true food (satya); or the one who sacrifices to the gods with true oblation. Or again, abiding in the two worlds, he is golden-formed, of golden radiance. Such an Agni you should serve, for your protection, before (purā) the unthinking (acitta) one like the thunderbolt (tanayitnu). Tanayitnu is the lightning-bolt, which is sudden; like it is acitta, "that in which there is no thought" — the withdrawal of all the senses marked by thought, that is, death. Before that death, he says, honour Agni on all sides with oblations. The rest of the block is grammar (rudra, tanayitnoḥ, kṛṇudhvam, with Uṇ. Sū. 2-22 and 3-29).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O priests and sacrificers) अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—of the sacrifice
- राजानं (*rājānaṃ*)—the lord
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the caller of the gods
- रुद्रं (*rudraṃ*)—the terrible to enemies
- रोदस्कोः (*rodaskoḥ*)—to both heaven and earth
- सत्ययजं (*satyayajaṃ*)—the giver of true food
- हिरण्यरूपं (*hiraṇyarūpaṃ*)—possessing a golden radiance
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- तनयित्नोः (*tanayitnoḥ*)—sudden like lightning
- अचित्तात् (*acittāt*)—than death
- पुरा (*purā*)—before
- आ कृणुध्वं (*ā kṛṇudhvaṃ*)—worship and serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests and sacrificers, for your protection, before a death as sudden as lightning, worship and serve Agni, the lord of the sacrifice, the caller of the gods, the terrible to enemies, the giver of true food to both heaven and earth, he who has a golden radiance.

### Printed p. 734

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Secure Agni, the king of sacrifice, the afflicter (of foes), the invoker (of the gods), the distributor of food through heaven and earth, the golden-formed, for your protection, before (surprised by) sudden death.

> अयं योनिस्तव स्थानं भवति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । जायेव । यथा पत्य उशती पतिं
> कामयमाना सुवासाः शोभनवस्रोपेता जाया स्वात्मसमीपे तस्य स्थानं
> करोति तद्वत् । हे स्वपाक स्वपस्क सुकर्मन्नग्ने त्वं परिवीतो यष्टव्यदेवैस्तेजोभिर्वा परिवीतोऽर्वाचीनोऽस्मदभिमुखः सन् नि षीद । उत्तरवेद्यामुपविश ।
> तत्र स्थितस्य ते तवेमा ज्वालाः स्तुतयो वा प्रतीचीस्त्वदभिमुखाः प्रवर्तंते ॥
> चक्रम । करॊतेर्लिटि रूपं । वाक्यभेदान्निघाताभावः । अर्वाचीनः । विभाषांचेरदिगिति खः । परिवीतः । वैञ् संवरणे । कर्मणि निष्ठा । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं ।
> गतिरनंतर इति गतेः स्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, the place (the uttaravedi) that we have made for you is your seat (yoni). The illustration: as a wife who longs for her husband (patye uśatī), well clothed, makes a place for him near herself, so too. O Svapāka, of good work, Agni, surrounded (parivīta) by the gods to be worshipped or by lustres, and turned towards us (arvācīna), sit down on the uttaravedi. While you are seated there, these flames, or these praises, move towards you (pratīcīḥ). The rest is grammar (cakrama, arvācīnaḥ, parivītaḥ).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, as a wife who longs for the nearness of her husband and is adorned with excellent garments and the like makes a place for her husband near herself, so the uttaravedi that we have built for you is a sacred seat for you. O Agni of excellent work, sit down, surrounded by lustres and turned towards us. These praises addressed to you are recited facing you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This is the altar which we have decorated for you, as a wife attached to her husband puts on elegant garments (to gratify him) : maturer of good works, sit down in our presence invested (with radiance), while your flames incline towards you.

> स्तौति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । यथा ग्रावा सोमस्य सोता शब्दं करोति । प्रैते वदंतु

> आशृण्वते । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । ईळे । ईड स्तुता । लट लोपस्त
> आत्मनेपदेश्विति तलोपः । यद्वा । लिटि तशब्दस्यॆशादेशे कृते रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Vedhaḥ" means O composer of hymns. Recite (शंस (*śaṃsa*)) the praise (मन्म (*manma*)) and the śastra (शस्तिं (*śastiṃ*)) to that god Agni. He is attentive to hymns (आशृण्वते (*āśṛṇvate*)), unproud and unheedless (अदृपिताय (*adṛpitāya*)), the beholder of men (नृचक्षसे (*nṛcakṣase*)), very gracious (सुमृळीकाय (*sumṛḷīkāya*)), and immortal, free from the nature of death. The sacrificer who presses the Soma (मधुषुत् (*madhuṣut*), presser of the intoxicating Soma) praises this Agni. The comparison is "like the stone": as the pressing-stone presses the Soma, so he does. The construction is: recite to him whom he praises. Or else: the Soma-presser, the sacrificer, praises Agni. The comparison is then that the pressing-stone makes a sound as it presses the Soma. Here the stones are heard as agents in प्रैते वदंतु प्र वयं वदाम ग्रावभ्यः (*praite vadaṃtu pra vayaṃ vadāma grāvabhyaḥ*) (Ṛgve. 10-94-1) **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वेधः (*vedhaḥ*)—O praiser
- सोता (*sotā*)—that presses the Soma
- ग्रावेव (*grāveva*)—like stones, making a sound
- मधुषुत् (*madhuṣut*)—the sacrificer who presses the sweet Soma
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Agni
- ईळे (*īḷe*)—he praises; such (Agni)
- आशृण्वते (*āśṛṇvate*)—who listens attentively to the praise
- अदृपिताय (*adṛpitāya*)—the unheedless one
- नृचक्षसे (*nṛcakṣase*)—who looks upon men
- सुमृळीकाय (*sumṛḷīkāya*)—the giver of happiness
- अमृताय (*amṛtāya*)—free from the nature of death
- देवाय (*devāya*)—and of divine nature; addressing that Agni
- मन्म (*manma*)—the praise
- शस्तिं (*śastiṃ*)—the śastra mantra
- शंस (*śaṃsa*)—recite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, recite the praise and the śastra mantra to that Agni whom the sacrificer, pressing the sweet Soma and making a sound like the stones that press it, praises: Agni who listens attentively to the praise, who is unheedless, who looks upon men, who gives happiness, who is free from the nature of death, and who is of divine nature.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Repeat, oh priest, the praise, the prayer, to the attentive, the affable Agni, the beholder of man, the giver of felicity, the divine, the immortal ; to him whom the effuser of the libation, like the (bruising) stone, adores aloud.

### Printed p. 737

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sotā grāveva: here the sweet sound of the stone, which crushes the Soma-creepers and presses out the juice, is compared to the sound of praising Agni. On this matter, the commentator points out here that there is a whole sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94), प्रैते वदंतु प्र वयं वदाम ग्रावभ्यः (*praite vadaṃtu pra vayaṃ vadāma grāvabhyaḥ*), for praising the stones called grāvāṇaḥ that press out the Soma juice.

> त्वं चि॑न्तः॒ शम्या॑ अग्ने अ॒स्या ऋ॒तस्य॑ बोध्यतचित्स्वा॒धीः ॥  
> क॒दा त॑ उ॒क्था स॑ध॒माद्या॑नि क॒दा भ॑वंति स॒ख्या गृ॒हे ते॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> *tvaṃ cintaḥ śamyā agne asyā ṛtasya bodhyatacitsvādhīḥ ‖*  
> *kadā ta ukthā sadhamādyāni kadā bhavaṃti sakhyā gṛhe te ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । चित् । नः । शम्यै । अग्ने । अस्याः । ऋतस्य । बोधि । ऋतचित् । सुआधीः ।  
> कवा । ते । उक्था । सधर्माद्यानि । कदा ! भवंति । सख्या ! गृहे । ते ॥ ४ ॥

> *tvaṃ | cit | naḥ | śamyai | agne | asyāḥ | ṛtasya | bodhi | ṛtacit | suādhīḥ |*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं चित्त्वमेव शम्यै । शमीशब्दः कर्मनाम । अस्याः शम्यै
> नोऽस्मत्संबंधिनोऽस्य कर्मणो देवता भवसि । हे ऋतचित् सत्यज्ञ हे अग्ने
> स्वाधीः सुकर्मा सुध्यानो वा त्वमृतस्य बोधि । अस्मदीयं स्तोत्रं बुध्यस्व ।
> ते तव सधमाद्यानि सहमदनिमित्तान्युक्का शस्त्राणि कदा कस्मिन्काले भवंति । भविष्यंति ।
> तथास्मदीये गृहे ते त्वया सह सख्या सख्यानि कदा भविष्यंति ॥ सधमाद्यानि । मादयतेर्ण्यंतस्याचो यदिति यत् । सध मादस्थयोरिति सहस्य सधादेशः । भवंति ।
> विभाषा कदाकर्होर्व्यः । पा- ३-३-५ । इति भविष्यदर्थे लट् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you alone are the deity of this our rite; "śamī" is a word for rite (karma), and "śamyai" means of this rite of ours. O Ṛtacit, knower of truth, O Agni, you who do good works or have good thoughts (स्वाधीः (*svādhīḥ*)), know our praise (बोधि (*bodhi*): understand our hymn). When will the śastras that serve for rejoicing together (सधमाद्यानि (*sadhamādyāni*)) with you be recited (भवंति (*bhavaṃti*), "will be")? And when will friendships with you come to be in our house?

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं चित् (*tvaṃ cit*)—you alone
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अस्याः शम्यै (*asyāḥ śamyai*)—the deity connected with this rite
- ऋतचित् (*ṛtacit*)—Agni, knower of truth
- स्वाधीः (*svādhīḥ*)—you, the excellent doer of the rite
- ते (*te*)—for you
- सधमाद्यानि (*sadhamādyāni*)—that give delight
- उक्ता (*uktā*)—the śastra mantras

### Printed p. 738
- कना (*kanā*)—when
- भवंति (*bhavaṃti*)—are made
- गृहे (*gṛhe*)—in our sacrificial house
- ते (*te*)—with you
- सख्या (*sakhyā*)—friendship
- कदा (*kadā*)—when it comes about, then
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—our praise
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you are the deity of this our rite. O Agni, knower of truth, you, the excellent doer of the rite: when the delight-giving śastras are made for you, when friendship with you comes about in our sacrificial house, then know our praise.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You, Agni, preside over this our rite : do you, who are cognizant of truth, and the author of good works, recognize this our adoration, whenever these exhilarating prayers (are addressed) to you, whenever friendly relations with you are (established) in our dwelling.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं तदस्मदीयं पापं वरुणाय कथा गर्हसे । केन हेतुना
> गर्हापूर्वमावेदयेः । हेति पूरणः । दिवे द्युलोकाय द्योतमानाय
> सूर्याय ना कथा कथं तत्पापमावेदयेः । नोऽस्माकमागस्तत्पापं कत्किमस्ति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, why do you reproach that sin of ours to Varuṇa? For what reason would you make it known after reproaching? "Ha" is a filler. To Heaven (the heavenly world, or the shining Sūrya) why would you make known that sin? What (कत् (*kat*)) sin of ours is there? The meaning is that there is none, because of our service to you.

> विभक्तिरिति विभक्ति संज्ञायां किमः कः । पा. ७-२-१०३ । इति कादेशः । मीळ्हुषे । मिह
> सेचने । क्वसौ दाश्वान् साह्वान् मीढ्वांश्चेति निपातितः । ब्रवः । ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां

> द्धातुस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Likewise, why would you speak to Mitra, the showerer of desired fruit, and to Earth? Why would you speak of the offence? To the god Aryaman, and to the god named Bhaga, why would you speak?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, why do you make our sin known to Varuṇa and reproach us? What sin of ours could there be? Why would you make it known to Heaven, to Mitra the granter of desired ends, to Earth, to Aryaman and to Bhaga?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Why, Agni, do you reproach us (for our sin) to Varuna, why to the heaven ? what is our offence ? why repeat it to the bountiful Mitra, to earth, to Aryaman, or to Bhaga ?

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कद्धिषा ्य॑सु वृधसा॒नो अ॑ग्ने॒ कद्वाता॑य॒ प्रत॑वसे शुभं॒ये ।  
> परि॑ज्मने॒ नास॑त्याय॒ क्षे ब्रवः॒ कद॑ग्ने रु॒द्राय॑ नृ॒घ्ने ॥ ६ ॥

> परिज्मने । नासत्याय । क्षे । ब्रवः । कत् । अग्ने । रुद्राय । नृघ्ने ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने धिष्णा स्वाग्नीध्रीयादिधिष्टेषु वृधसानो घृताद्याहुतिभिर्वर्धमानस्त्वं कत्कथं ब्रूयाः । प्रतवसे प्रकृष्टबलाय शुभंये शुभस्य प्रापयित्रे
> परिज्मने परितो गंत्रे नासत्याय सत्यस्य नेत्रे । यद्वा । न विद्यतेऽसत्यं यस्य
> तस्मै वाताय वायवे । यद्वा । नासत्यायेति वचनव्यत्ययः । नासत्याभ्यामश्विभ्यां । क्षे । क्षेति पृथिवीमाह । क्षियंति निवसंत्यस्यां प्राणिन इति । तस्यै क्षे पृथिव्यै
> च कत्कथं ब्रूयाः । हे अग्ने नृष्टे नृणां पापकृतां हंत्री रुद्राय देवाय
> कत्कथमागो ब्रुवः । ब्रूयाः ॥ वृधसानः । वृधु वर्धने । असानजित्यनुवृत्तावृंजिवृधिमंदिसहिभ्यः किदित्यसानच्प्रत्ययः । कित्वादगुणः । चित्वादंतोदात्तः शुभंये । या प्रापणे । विच् । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलमिति द्वितीयाया अप्यलुक् ।
> कृत्स्वरः । क्षे । क्षि निवासगत्योः । अन्वेभ्योऽपि दृश्यत इत्यधिकरणे डः । ततष्टाप् ।
> चतुर्थेकवचन आतो धातोरित्यत्रात इति योगविभागादाकारलोपः । नृष्टे । हन
> हिंसागत्योः । बहुलं छंदसीति क्वप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you who grow in the dhiṣṇyas, the hearths such as the Āgnīdhrīya, with oblations of ghee and the like, why (कत् (*kat*)) would you speak? To Pratavas, of exceeding strength; to Śubhaṃyu, the bringer of good; to Parijman, who goes about everywhere; to Nāsatya, the leader of truth. Or else: the one in whom there is no untruth, namely Vāta, the Wind. Or else "nāsatyāya" is a change of number, meaning the two Nāsatyas, the Aśvins. "Kṣe": क्षेति पृथिवीमाह (*kṣeti pṛthivīmāha*); beings dwell (क्षियंति (*kṣiyaṃti*)) in it. To that Kṣā, Earth, why would you speak? O Agni, to the god Rudra, the destroyer of men who commit sin (नृष्टे (*nṛṣṭe*)), why would you tell of the offence? **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- धिष्ण्यासु (*dhiṣṇyāsu*)—in the sacrificial places
- वृधसानः (*vṛdhasānaḥ*)—you who grow
- प्रतवसे (*pratavase*)—who has excellent strength
- शुभंये (*śubhaṃye*)—the bringer of good
- परिज्मने (*parijmane*)—who moves everywhere
- नासत्याय (*nāsatyāya*)—who is of the nature of truth
- वातायु (*vātāyu*)—to the Wind
- कत् (*kat*)—how would you make my sin known?
- क्षे (*kṣe*)—to Earth
- कत् (*kat*)—why (how) do you tell it
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- नृष्टे (*nṛṣṭe*)—who destroys sinful men
- रुद्राय (*rudrāya*)—to the god Rudra
- कत् (*kat*)—why
- ब्रव (*brava*)—do you tell

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who grow in the sacrificial places, why do you make my sin known to the Wind, who has excellent strength, brings good, moves everywhere and is of the nature of truth, to Earth, and to the god Rudra who destroys sinful men?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Why repeat it when exalted in holy ceremonies ? why tell it to the mightv, benevolent, circumambient, truthful wind (Vayu) ? why, Agni, to earth, why to man-destroying Rudra ?

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने महे महते पुष्टिंभराय पुष्टिधारकाय पूष्ण एतन्नामकाय
> देवाय कथा केन हेतुना पापं ब्रवीथाः । सुमखाय सुपूजनीयाय सुयज्ञाय वा हविर्देऽग्निरूपेण देवानां हविर्दात्रे । यद्वा । स्विष्टकृत्वाद्ध विषो
> दात्रे । रुद्राय कत्कथं ब्रूयाः । तथोरुगायायोरुभिर्बहुभिर्गायमानाय
> यद्वा । प्रभूतकीर्तये विष्णवे रेतः क्षयहेतु पापं कत्कथं वदेः । शरवे ।
> शृणाति पक्वा ओषधीरिति शरुः शरत्संवत्सरः । यद्वा । हिंसिका निर्ऋतिः । बृहत्यै
> महत्यै शरदे निर्ऋत्यै ना कत्कथं पापं ब्रवः । ब्रूयाः ॥ पुष्टिंभराय डुभृञ्
> धारणपोषणयोः । संज्ञायां भृत्यवृजीत्यादिना खच् । अरुर्द्विषदजंतस्य
> मुमिति पूर्वपदस्य मुमागमः। चित्तादंतोदात्तः । समासे कृत्स्वरः । हविर्दे ॥
> अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोप इति सुप उदात्तत्वं । शरवे । शृ हिंसायां ।
> शास्वस्निहित्यसीत्यादिना उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, to great Pūṣan, the bearer of nourishment (पुष्टिंभराय (*puṣṭiṃbharāya*)), a god of that name, for what reason would you speak of the sin? To Rudra, well worthy of worship or of good sacrifice (सुमखाय (*sumakhāya*)), the giver of oblations (हविर्दे (*havirde*)) to the gods in the form of Agni; or else, as Sviṣṭakṛt, the giver of the oblation: why would you speak? Likewise to Viṣṇu, उरुगायाय (*urugāyāya*), sung by many, or of abundant fame: why would you speak of the sin that causes loss of semen (रेतः (*retaḥ*))? "Śaru": that which crushes the ripened herbs, the autumn, the year; or else the violent Nirṛti. To great Śarad or Nirṛti, why would you tell the sin?

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- महे (*mahe*)—of great nature
- पुष्टिंभराय (*puṣṭiṃbharāya*)—the nourisher of the world
- पूष्टे (*pūṣṭe*)—to the god Pūṣan
- कथा (*kathā*)—for what reason (would you make known my sin)
- सुमखाय (*sumakhāya*)—who is worthy of excellent worship
- हविर्दे (*havirde*)—who offers the oblation in the form of Agni
- रुद्राय (*rudrāya*)—to Rudra
- कत् (*kat*)—why do you speak
- शरवे (*śarave*)—to the presiding deity of the year
- बृहत्यै (*bṛhatyai*)—and to Nirṛti
- कत् (*kat*)—how
- ब्रवः (*bravaḥ*)—do you speak
- उरुगायाय (*urugāyāya*)—in many ways

### Printed p. 742
Why should my sin, the cause of decay, be told to Pūṣan, who is of great nature and nourishes the world? Why to Rudra, who is worthy of excellent worship and offers the oblation to the gods in the form of fire? Why to the presiding deity of the year, to Nirṛti, and to Viṣṇu, who is praised in many ways?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, why must my sin, the cause of decay, be told to Pūṣan, who is of great nature and the nourisher of the world; to Rudra, who is worthy of excellent worship and offers the oblation to the gods in the form of fire; to the presiding deity of the year; to Nirṛti; and to Viṣṇu, who is much praised?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Why to the great and nutriment-conveying Pushan ? why to Rudra, the object of worship, the giver of the oblation (to the gods) ? Why to the many-hymned Vishnu ? Why tell our sin to the extensive year ?

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, to the true, moving company of the Maruts, who are strength itself, by what cause would you declare my sin in reply? Being asked by them, how would you speak to that great Sūra? Likewise to Aditi, and to the swift-going Vāyu; "aditaye" is also taken as "to the unimpoverished, swift one". How would you reply with my sin? Since it is so, O Jātavedas ... (continued on the next page).

### Printed p. 743

> मागः कथं प्रतिब्रूयाः । यस्मादेवं तस्मात् हे जातवेदोग्ने चिकित्वान्
> तत्सर्वं जानानस्त्वं दिवो दीप्तान्देवान् साध । साधय । गच्छ । यद्वा । दिवो
> द्युलोकस्य यज्ञवहनलक्षणं कार्यं साध । कुरु ॥ सूरे । सर्वविधीनां छंदसि
> विकल्पितत्वात् जतीर्यत्वाभावः । अतो गुण इति पररूपत्वं । पृच्छमानः । पृच्छ
> ज्ञिप्पायां । कर्मणि यक् । ग्रहिज्यादिना संप्रसारणं । शानचो लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे यक्स्वरः । साध । राध साध संसिद्धौ । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थस्य लोटि व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Since it is so, O Jātavedas Agni, knowing all that, you, the knowing one, bring about (go to) the shining gods; or else accomplish the task of heaven, the carrying of the sacrifice. Grammatical remarks follow on "sūre", "pṛcchamānaḥ" and "sādha"; they are omitted here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋताय (*ṛtāya*)—true in nature
- मरुतां (*marutāṃ*)—of the Maruts
- शर्धाय (*śardhāya*)—to the company
- कथा (*kathā*)—for what reason (shall you tell my sin)
- पृच्छ्यमानः (*pṛcchyamānaḥ*)—even if you are asked
- बृहते (*bṛhate*)—of great nature
- सूरे (*sūre*)—to Sūra
- कथा (*kathā*)—how will you tell
- अदितये (*aditaye*)—to the goddess Aditi
- तुराय (*turāya*)—to the swift-going Vāyu
- प्रति ब्रवः (*prati bravaḥ*)—how do you speak
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, of born wisdom
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—you, having known all
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—to the shining gods
- साध (*sādha*)—go and join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, for what reason will you tell my sin to the company of the true Maruts? Even if you are asked, how will you tell it to the sun of great nature? How will you tell it to the goddess Aditi and to the swift-going Vāyu? O Agni of born wisdom, knowing everything, go and join the shining gods.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Why tell it to the veracious company of the Maruts? why, even when asked, to the mighty sun? Why repeat it to Aditi, or to the swift wind? Fulfil, all-knowing Jatavedas, (the worship) of heaven.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने ऋतेन सत्यभूतेन यज्ञेन नियतमनुस्युतमृतमुदकं गोर्धेनोः पय एळे । आयाचे । सांनाय्यादिहविरर्थं गव्यं पयस्त्वां याच
> इत्यभिप्रायः । आमापक्वा सा गौर्मधुमन्माधुर्योपेतं पक्वं पयः सचा सह
> धारयति । कृष्णा कृष्णवर्णा सत्येषा गौ रुशता श्वेतेन धासिना प्राणिनां धारकेण
> जामर्येण । जायंत इति जाः प्रजाः । ता जा अमर्येणामरणनिमित्तेन तेन
> पयसा पीषाय । प्रजाः स्न्याययति । तवैष महिमा यद्रसान्परिणामयन्नेवं
> करोषि ॥ पीषाय । स्न्यायतेर्लिटि लिड्यजटोश्चति पीभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, by the sacrifice that is truth, I ask for the water that is bound up with it, and for the milk of the cow; the intention is "for the oblations such as sāṃnāyya I ask you for cow's milk". That cow, though unripe, holds sweet, ripe milk with her. Though black, this cow, with white milk that sustains living beings, "jāmarya": "jāḥ" are the offspring, those born; with that milk, the cause of their deathlessness, she makes the offspring swell. "This is your greatness, that you do so, transforming the juices."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—by the sacrifice that is truth
- नियतं (*niyataṃ*)—bound up with
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—water
- गोः (*goḥ*)—the milk of the cow
- आ ईळे (*ā īḷe*)—I ask for
- आमा (*āmā*)—(the cow) even in the unripe state
- मधुमत् (*madhumat*)—sweet
- पक्वं (*pakvaṃ*)—ripe, of milk
- सचा (*sacā*)—holds within herself
- कृष्णा सती (*kṛṣṇā satī*)—being black
- एषा (*eṣā*)—this cow
- रुशता (*ruśatā*)—white
- धासिना (*dhāsinā*)—sustaining living beings
- जामरैण (*jāmaraiṇa*)—causing deathlessness to the offspring
- पयसा (*payasā*)—with milk
- पीपाय (*pīpāya*)—satisfies the offspring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, by the sacrifice that is truth I ask for the water bound up with it and for the milk of the cow. Even though not in the ripe state, this cow holds within herself sweet, ripe milk. This black cow satisfies the offspring with white milk that sustains living beings and causes deathlessness.

### Printed p. 745

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I solicit, Agni, the milk of the cow, essential for the sacrifice yet immature, (she possesses) the sweet and ripe (fluid); black though she be, yet with her white nutritious milk she maintains mankind in existence.

> अस्पं॑दमानो आचरद्वयो॒धा वृषा॑ शु॒क्रं दु॑दुहे॒  ॒॑

> *ṛtena | hi | smṛ | vṛṣabhaḥ | cit | aktaḥ | pumān | agniḥ | payasā | pṛṣṭyena |*  
> *aspaṃdamānaḥ | acarat | vayadhāḥ | vṛṣā | śukraṃ | duduhe | pṛśniḥ | ūdhaḥ ‖10‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषभोऽभिमतफलवर्षकः पुमान् श्रेष्ठः सोऽग्निऋतेन सत्यभूतेन
> पृष्येन धारकेण पयसाक्तः सिक्तो भवति । हि ष्मचित् त्रयः पूरणाः । वयोधा
> अन्नदः सोऽग्निरस्पंदमान एकत्रावस्थितः सन् एवाचरत् । सर्वत्र तेजसा चरति ।
> तथा वृषापां वर्षकः पृश्निः सूर्यः शुक्रं पय ऊधोऽंतरिक्षं मेघं वा
> दुदुहे । दोग्धि ॥ अक्तः । अन्नू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणगतिषु । कर्मणि निष्ठा । दुदुहे ।
> द्विकर्मकोयं धातुः । ऊधः । अकथितं चेति कर्मसंज्ञा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The "vṛṣabha", the showerer of desired fruit, the male, the best, that Agni is sprinkled with the true, sustaining milk; "hi ṣma cit" are three fillers. The giver of food (vayodhāḥ), that Agni, though standing still in one place, moves everywhere with his radiance. Likewise the showerer of waters, Pṛśni, the sun, milks the white milk, the udder, the atmosphere or cloud.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the giver of desired things
- पुमान् (*pumān*)—the best
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—true
- पृष्ठेन (*pṛṣṭhena*)—nourishing
- पयसा (*payasā*)—with milk
- अक्तः (*aktaḥ*)—is sprinkled
- वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)—Agni, the giver of food
- अस्पंदमानः (*aspaṃdamānaḥ*)—though motionless and steady
- अचरत् (*acarat*)—pervades everywhere with his radiance
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the shedder of water
- पृश्निः (*pṛśniḥ*)—the sun
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—watery
- ऊधः (*ūdhaḥ*)—the atmosphere (cloud)
- दुदुहे (*duduhe*)—milks

### Printed p. 746

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the giver of desired things and the best, is sprinkled with true, nourishing milk. Agni, the giver of food, though motionless and steady, pervades everywhere with his radiance. The sun, who pours down water, milks the atmosphere filled with water.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The male Agni, the showerer (of benefits) has been sprinkled by the genuine sustaining milk : the giver of food proceeds unswerving (from his course), and the sun, the shedder of rain, has milked the white (fluid) of the udder (of the firmament).

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒तेनाद्रिं॒ व्य॑सन्‌भि॒दंतः॒ समंगि॑रसो नवंत॒ गोभिः॑ ।  
> शु॒नं नरः॒ परि॑ षदन्नु॒षास॑मा॒विः स्व॑रभवज्जा॒ते अ॒ग्नौ ॥ ११ ॥

> *śunaṃ naraḥ pari ṣadannuṣāsamāviḥ svarabhavajjāte agnau ‖ 11 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋतेन । अद्रिं । वि । असन् । भिदंतः । सम् । अंगिरसः । नवंत । गोभिः ।  
> शुनं । नरः । परि । सदन् । उषसं । आविः । स्वः । अभवत् । जाते । अग्नौ ॥ ११ ॥

> *ṛtena | adriṃ | vi | asan | bhidaṃtaḥ | sam | aṃgirasaḥ | navaṃta | gobhiḥ |*  
> *śunaṃ | naraḥ | pari | sadan | uṣasaṃ | āviḥ | svaḥ | abhavat | jāte | agnau ‖ 11 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अंगिरसो मेधातिथिप्रभृतय ऋतेन यज्ञेन हेतुना गवां निरोधकमद्रिं
> पर्वतं भिदंतो विदारयंतः संतो व्यसन् । व्यक्षिपन् । ततस्ते गोभिः सं नवंत ।
> समगच्छंत । नरः कर्मणां नेतारस्ते शुनं सुखेनोषसं परि सदन् । परितः
> प्राप्नु वन् । ततः स्वः सूर्योऽप्याविरभवत् । सर्वमेतदग्नौ त्वयि जाते मंथनेन
> निष्पादिते सत्यभूदिति ॥ असन् । अस्यतेर्लुजु च्लेरस्यतिवक्तीत्यादिनाजादेशः । अनित्यमागमशासनमिति थुगभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Aṅgirases, Medhātithi and others, by the sacrifice as cause, splitting the mountain that obstructed the cows, threw it open ("vyasan": they cast apart). Then they came together with the cows. The leaders of rites, they happily surrounded (reached on all sides) the dawn. Then Svaḥ, the sun, also became manifest. All this came about when you, Agni, were born, produced by churning.

### Printed p. 747

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्नौ (*agnau*)—you, in the form of Agni
- जाते (*jāte*)—as soon as you were born
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—the Aṅgirases
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—with the help of the sacrifice
- अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)—the mountain that had hidden the cows
- भिदंत (*bhidaṃta*)—splitting
- व्यसन् (*vyasan*)—released and made a way
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with the cows
- सं नवंत (*saṃ navaṃta*)—returned
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—they, the performers of rites
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—happily
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—the dawn
- परि सदन् (*pari sadan*)—obtained all around
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the sun also
- आविः अभवत् (*āviḥ abhavat*)—became manifest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, as soon as you, in the form of Agni, were born, the Aṅgirases, with the help of the sacrifice, split the mountains that had hidden the cows, released them and made a way. And they returned with their cows. The performers of rites obtained the dawn all around. The sun also became manifest. All this is your greatness, as Agni **NOTE**

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
By the sacrifice, the Angirasas, rending the mountain asunder, have thrown it open, and returned with the cows ; the leaders ( of holy rites ) have arrived happily at the dawn, and the sun was manifest as Agni was engendered.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒तेन॑ दे॒वीर॒मृता॒ अमृ॑क्ता॒ अर्णो॑भि॒रापो॒ मधु॑मद्भिरग्ने ।  
> वा॒जी न सर्गे॑षु प्रस्तुभा॒नः प्र सद॒मित्स्रवि॑तवे दधन्युः ॥

> *ṛtena devīramṛtā amṛktā arṇobhirāpo madhumadbhiragne |*  
> *vājī na sargeṣu prastubhānaḥ pra sadamitsravitave dadhanyuḥ ‖*

> वाजी । न । सर्गेषु । प्रस्तुभानः । प्र । सदं । इत् । स्रवितवे । दधन्युः ॥ १२ ॥

> *ṛtena | devīḥ | amṛtāḥ | amṛktāḥ | arṇaḥ 'bhiḥ | āpaḥ | madhumat 'bhiḥ | agne ‖*  
> *vājī | na | sargeṣu | prastubhānaḥ | pra | sadaṃ | it | sravitave | dadhanyuḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने अमृता अमरणहेतव अमृक्ता रक्षःप्रभृतिभिरबाधिता मधुमद्भिर्माधुर्योपेतैरर्णोभिरुदकैर्युक्ता देवीर्देव्यो नद्य ऋतेन सत्येन
> यज्ञेन वा हेतुनाप आप्तव्याः सत्यः सदमित्सदैव स्रवितवे स्रवणाय प्र दधन्युः ।
> प्रगच्छंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । वाजी न । यथा सर्गेषु प्रेरणेषु प्रस्तुभानः प्रोत्साह्यमानोऽश्वः प्रगच्छति तद्वत् ॥ अपः । अप्ल व्याप्तौ । आप्नोतेः क्विप् ह्रस्वश्चेति
> कर्मणि क्विप् । अप्तन्नित्यादिना जसि दीर्घः । प्रस्तुभानः । स्तोभतिरर्चतिकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, the divine rivers (देवीः (*devīḥ*)) are immortal, that is, causes of non-dying, and unobstructed, that is, not hindered by Rākṣasas and the like. They are joined with sweet waters, waters endowed with sweetness. By ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), "by truth" or "by the sacrifice", as the cause, they are to be reached, and so they always flow on. स्रवितवे (*sravitave*) means "for flowing"; प्र दधन्युः (*pra dadhanyuḥ*) means "they go forth". The illustration is वाजी न (*vājī na*): as a horse, urged on in its courses (सर्गेषु (*sargeṣu*)), is encouraged and goes forth, so do the rivers. Sāyaṇa then gives grammar on अपः (*apaḥ*) (root अप्ल (*apla*), "to pervade") and on प्रस्तुभानः (*prastubhānaḥ*) (स्तोभति (*stobhati*) is a root meaning "to praise").

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—the deathless ones
- अमृक्ताः (*amṛktāḥ*)—the unharmed ones
- मधुमद्भिः (*madhumadbhiḥ*)—endowed with sweetness
- ऊर्णोभिः (*ūrṇobhiḥ*)—full of waters
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—the rivers, divine in nature
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—with the help of the sacrifice
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—having obtained power
- सदमित् (*sadamit*)—always
- स्रवितवे (*sravitave*)—to flow
- सर्गेषु (*sargeṣu*)—when urged on
- प्रस्तुभानः (*prastubhānaḥ*)—having received encouragement
- वाजी न (*vājī na*)—as a horse moves swiftly
- प्र दधन्युः (*pra dadhanyuḥ*)—they move on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the rivers, deathless, unharmed, full of sweet waters and divine in nature, gain power through the help of the sacrifice and always flow swiftly, like a horse that has been urged on.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
By sacrifice, Agni, the divine rivers, immortal, unobstructed, continue perpetually to flow with sweet waters, like a horse that is being urged in his speed.
