##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा कस्य॑ य॒क्षं सद॒मिदु॒रो गा॒ मा वे॒शस्य॑ प्रमिन॒तो  
> मापेः ।  
> मा भ्रातु॑रग्ने॒ अनृ॑जोर्ऋ॒णं वे॒र्मा सख्यु॒द्रक्षं॑ रि॒पोर्भु॑जेम ॥ १३ ॥

> *mā kasya yakṣaṃ sadamiduro gā mā veśasya praminato*  
> *māpeḥ |*  
> *mā bhrāturagne anṛjorṛṇaṃ vermā sakhyudrakṣaṃ riporbhujema ‖ 13 ‖*

### Printed p. 750

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । कस्य । यक्षं । सदं । इत् । हुरः । गाः । मा । वेशस्य । प्रमिनतः । मा । आपेः ।  
> मा । भ्रातुः । अग्ने । अनृजोः । ऋणं । वेः । मा । सख्युः । दक्षं । रिपोः । भुजेम ॥

> *mā | kasya | yakṣaṃ | sadaṃ | it | huraḥ | gāḥ | mā | veśasya | praminataḥ | mā | āpeḥ |*  
> *mā | bhrātuḥ | agne | anṛjoḥ | ṛṇaṃ | veḥ | mā | sakhyuḥ | dakṣaṃ | ripoḥ | bhujema ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने हुरोऽस्माकं हिंसकस्य कस्य कस्यचिदपि जंतोर्यक्षं यज्ञं सदमित्सदैव मा गाः । कदाचिदपि मा गच्छ । प्रमिनतो हिंसकस्य वेशस्य प्रातिवेश्यस्य
> यज्ञं मा गाः । तथापेर्मद्व्यतिरिक्तस्य बंधोर्यज्ञं मा गच्छ । तथानृजोः
> कुटिलचित्तस्य भ्रातुर्ऋणवद्देयं हविर्मा वेः । मा कामयेथाः । तथा वयमपि
> सख्युर्मित्रस्य रिपोः शत्रोर्दक्षं भोगसमर्थं धनं मा भुजेम । मा भुंजीमहि । किंतु त्वया दत्तं धनं भुंजीमहि ॥ हुरः । हृ प्रसह्यकरणे । क्विप् । बहुलं
> छंदसीत्युत्वं । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । भुजेम । भुज पालनाभ्यवहारयोः । आशीर्लिजु व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । लिज्याशिष्यज्जत्यज् प्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, never go (मा गाः (*mā gāḥ*)) to the sacrifice (यक्षं (*yakṣaṃ*)) of any creature whatever that is हुरः (*huraḥ*), a harmer of us. Do not go to the sacrifice of a harmful neighbour (वेशस्य (*veśasya*), a प्रातिवेश्य (*prātiveśya*)). Likewise do not go to the sacrifice of a kinsman (आपेः (*āpeḥ*)) other than myself. Do not desire (मा वेः (*mā veḥ*)) the oblation due like a debt from a crooked-minded brother (अनृजोः (*anṛjoḥ*)). So too may we not enjoy (मा भुजेम (*mā bhujema*)) the wealth, able to be enjoyed (दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)), of a friend's enemy; rather may we enjoy the wealth given by you. The rest of the block is grammar on हुरः (*huraḥ*) and भुजेम (*bhujema*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- हुरः (*huraḥ*)—who is a harmer of us
- कस्य (*kasya*)—of whichever sacrificer
- यक्षं (*yakṣaṃ*)—to the sacrifice
- सदमित् (*sadamit*)—ever
- मा गाः (*mā gāḥ*)—do not go
- प्रमिनतः (*praminataḥ*)—who is harmful
- वेशस्य (*veśasya*)—of the sacrificer next door
- मा (*mā*)—do not go to his sacrifice either
- आपेः (*āpeḥ*)—even if a relative of mine, if he is hostile
- मा (*mā*)—do not go to him either
- अनृजोः (*anṛjoḥ*)—who is deceitful
- भ्रातुः (*bhrātuḥ*)—of him, though my brother
- ऋणं (*ṛṇaṃ*)—the oblation
- मा वेः (*mā veḥ*)—do not desire
- सख्युः (*sakhyuḥ*)—to my friend
- रिपोः (*ripoḥ*)—of him who is an enemy
- दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—the wealth of enjoyment
- मा भुजेम (*mā bhujema*)—may we not enjoy it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, never go to the sacrifice of a sacrificer who is a harmer of us. Even if he is our next-door neighbour, if he is harmful and deceitful, do not go there either. Even if he is our brother, do not covet his oblation. We do not want the wealth of enjoyment of one who is an enemy to my friend.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Go not ever, Agni, to the sacrifice of any one who injures us ; nor to that of a malevolent neighbour; nor to that of an (unnatural) relation ; accept not the due (oblation) from an insincere brother ; let us not derive enjoyment from the enemy of a friend.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रक्षा॑ हो अग्ने॒ तव॒ रक्ष॑णेभी रारक्षा॒णः सु॑मुख प्रीणा॒नः ।  
> प्रति॑ ष्टुर॒ वि रु॑ज वी॒ड्वंहो॑ ज॒हि रक्षो॒ महि॑ चिद्वावृधा॒नं ॥

> *rakṣā ho agne tava rakṣaṇebhī rārakṣāṇaḥ sumukha prīṇānaḥ |*  
> *prati ṣṭura vi ruja vīḍvaṃho jahi rakṣo mahi cidvāvṛdhānaṃ ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रक्ष । नः । अग्ने । तव । रक्षणेभिः । ररक्षणाणः । सुमुख । प्रीणानः ।  
> प्रति । स्फुर । वि । रुज । वीळु । अंहः । जहि । रक्षः । महि । चित् । ववृधानं ॥ १४ ॥

> *rakṣa | naḥ | agne | tava | rakṣaṇebhiḥ | rarakṣaṇāṇaḥ | sumukha | prīṇānaḥ |*  
> *prati | sphura | vi | ruja | vīḷu | aṃhaḥ | jahi | rakṣaḥ | mahi | cit | vavṛdhānaṃ ‖ 14 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुमख सुयज्ञ सुधनेति वा हे अग्ने ररक्षणाऽभ्यशमस्माकं रक्षिता
> प्रीणानो हविर्भिः प्रीतस्त्वं तव रक्षणेभिस्त्वदीयैरवनैनोर्नोऽस्मान्रक्ष । पालय ।
> प्रति स्फुर । अस्मान्प्रतिदीप्यस्व । वीळु दृढमंहः पापं वि रुज । विशेषेण नाशय ।
> किंच महि चिन्महदपि वावृधानं वर्धमानं वृद्धं वा बाधकं रक्षो जहि ॥ णः ।
> नश्च धातुस्थोरुषुभ्य इति संहितायां णत्वं । ररक्षणाः । रक्षेर्यज्लुकि चानशि
> रूपं ! जहि । हन हिंसागत्योः । लोटि हंतेर्ज इति जादेशः । आभाच्छास्त्रीयस्यासिद्धत्वादतो हेरिति लुक् न भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, सुमख (*sumakha*) ("of good sacrifice"; or "of good wealth", with the alternative readings सुयज्ञ (*suyajña*) and सुधन (*sudhana*)), you are ररक्षणाः (*rarakṣaṇāḥ*), our protector, and प्रीणानः (*prīṇānaḥ*), pleased with the oblations. With your protections protect and guard us. प्रति स्फुर (*prati sphura*): shine towards us. अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*) is sin; वीळु (*vīḷu*) means "firm"; वि रुज (*vi ruja*): destroy it specially. Further, slay (जहि (*jahi*)) the Rākṣasa who obstructs us, even though he is great and growing or grown strong (वावृधानं (*vāvṛdhānaṃ*)). The rest is grammar on णः (*ṇaḥ*), ररक्षणाः (*rarakṣaṇāḥ*) and जहि (*jahi*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुमख (*sumakha*)—you who have a good sacrifice
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ररक्षणाः (*rarakṣaṇāḥ*)—as our protector
- प्रीणानः (*prīṇānaḥ*)—as one pleased with oblations
- तव (*tava*)—your
- रक्षणेभिः (*rakṣaṇebhiḥ*)—with protections
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- रक्ष (*rakṣa*)—protect
- प्रति स्फुर (*prati sphura*)—shine on our behalf
- वीळु (*vīḷu*)—firmly rooted
- अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—sin
- वि रुज (*vi ruja*)—destroy
- वावृधानः (*vāvṛdhānaḥ*)—who harms excessively
- रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*)—the enemy
- महि जत् (*mahi jat*)—even when powerful **NOTE**
- जहि (*jahi*)—destroy

### Printed p. 751

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of good sacrifice, being our protector and pleased with the oblations, preserve us with your protections. Shine on our behalf. Destroy our sin, firmly planted. Crush the enemy who harms us, even though he is powerful.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, worthily worshipped, conservator, conciliated (by our offerings), protect us with your protections : enlighten us ; entirely extirpate our sin ; overcome the great and exulting Rakshasas.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒भिर्भ॑व सु॒मना॑ अग्ने अ॒र्कैरि॒मान्तस्य॒॑ मन्म॑भिः शूर॒  ॑
> वाजान् ।  
> उ॒त ब्रह्मा॑ण्यंगिरो जुषस्व॒ सं ते॑ श॒स्तिर्दे॒ववा॑ता जरेत ॥१५॥

> *ebhirbhava sumanā agne arkairimāntasya manmabhiḥ śūra*  
> *vājān |*  
> *uta brahmāṇyaṃgiro juṣasva saṃ te śastirdevavātā jareta ‖15‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एभिः । भव । सुमनाः । अग्ने । अर्कैः । इमान् । स्पृश । मन्मभिः । शूर । वाजान् ।  
> उत । ब्रह्माणि । अंगिरः । जुषस्व । सम् । ते । शस्तिः । देववाता । जरेत ॥ १५ ॥

> *ebhiḥ | bhava | sumanāḥ | agne | arkaiḥ | imān | spṛśa | manmabhiḥ | śūra | vājān |*  
> *uta | brahmāṇi | aṃgiraḥ | juṣasva | sam | te | śastiḥ | devavātā | jareta ‖ 15 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने एभिर्मधीयैरर्कॆरर्चनीयैः शस्त्रैः सुमनाः शोभनमनस्को
> भव । हे शूर इमानस्मदीयान्विर्लक्षणान्वाजान्मन्मभिः स्तोत्रैः सह स्पृश । प्रतिगृहाण । उतापि च अंगिरः । अंगति हवींषि प्राप्नोतीत्यंगिरा अग्निः । यद्वा ।
> येऽंगारा आसंस्तेऽंगिरसोऽभवन् । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३४ । इति ब्राह्मणं । तेषामंगिरसां कारणत्वादग्नेरंगिरस्त्वं । तत्कारणत्वे च मंत्रः । ये अंगिरसः सूनवस्ते अग्नेः
> परि जज्जिरे । ऋग्वे. १८-६२-५ । इति । तादृश हे अग्ने ब्रह्माणि मंत्रान् जुषस्व ।
> सेवस्व । देववाता । देवार्थं गता देवान् स्तोतुं प्राप्तेत्यर्थः । तादृशी शक्तिः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, be well-minded, of good mind, through these (एभिः (*ebhiḥ*)) hymns of praise (अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*), "to be worshipped with"), belonging to us. O hero, receive these (इमान् (*imān*)) food-offerings (वाजान् (*vājān*)) of ours together with our praises (मन्मभिः (*manmabhiḥ*)): स्पृश (*spṛśa*) means "accept". And, O अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*): Agni is अंगिराः (*aṃgirāḥ*) because he अंगति (*aṃgati*), that is, reaches the oblations. Or else, there is the Brāhmaṇa: येऽंगारा आसंस्तेऽंगिरसोऽभवन् (*ye 'ṃgārā āsaṃste 'ṃgiraso 'bhavan*) (Ai. Brā. 3-34) **NOTE**. Because those Aṅgirases are the cause, Agni is called Aṅgiras. For his being their cause there is the mantra ये अंगिरसः सूनवस्ते अग्नेः परि जज्जिरे । (*ye aṃgirasaḥ sūnavaste agneḥ pari jajjire |*) (Ṛgve. 18-62-5) **NOTE**. Such as you are, O Agni, accept (जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)) our mantras (ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)), that is, attend to them. देववाता (*devavātā*) means gone for the sake of the gods, come to praise the gods. Such a power, the शस्तिः (*śastiḥ*) ("praise"), shall make you grow (सं जरेत (*saṃ jareta*): let it increase you).

### Printed p. 752

> शंसनं ते त्वां सं जरेत । संवर्धयतु ॥ स्पृश । स्पृश संस्पर्शने । तुदादिः ।
> देवनाता । वा गतिगंधनयोः । गत्यर्थाकर्मकेति कर्तरि क्तः । देवः । पचाद्यजंतः । क्ले चेति चतुर्थ्यंतस्य पदस्य प्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The block continues with grammar on स्पृश (*spṛśa*) (root स्पृश (*spṛśa*), "to touch", of the tud class) and on देवनाता (*devanātā*) (root वा (*vā*) "to go, to move"; the suffix kta in the active sense; देवः (*devaḥ*) ends in ac of the pac class; the accent of the dative-ending word is the natural one).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- एभिः अर्कैः (*ebhiḥ arkaiḥ*)—with these revered śastra-mantras
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—having an auspicious mind
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- शूर (*śūra*)—O mighty one
- इमान् वाजान् (*imān vājān*)—these foods in the form of oblations
- मन्मभिः (*manmabhiḥ*)—with our praises
- स्पृश (*spṛśa*)—accept
- उत (*uta*)—and
- अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*)—O Agni
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—the mantras
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—attend to
- देवताता (*devatātā*)—addressed to the gods **NOTE**
- शस्तिः (*śastiḥ*)—praise
- ते (*te*)—you **NOTE**
- सं जरेत (*saṃ jareta*)—let it make grow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, be of auspicious mind through these revered śastra-mantras. O mighty one, accept these foods in the form of oblations together with our praises. And, O Agni who are in the form of Aṅgiras, attend to these mantras of ours. May this praise, addressed to the gods, make you grow.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Be propitiated, Agni, by these hymns ; accept, hero, these (sacrificial) viands (presented) with praises ; be pleased, Angiras, by our prayers; may the adoration addressed to the gods exalt you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this hymn, and in many other Ṛks of the Ṛgveda, the word अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*) is used to address Agni. An explanation of this is needed. येऽङ्गारा आसंस्तेऽङ्गरसोऽभवन् (*ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃste 'ṅgaraso 'bhavan*) (Ai. Brā. 3-34): "the embers (coals) connected with Agni received the name Aṅgirases." So it is said in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, in the story of Prajāpati's meditation on his daughter. Long ago Prajāpati (Brahmā) contemplated in his mind his own daughter (Uṣas, or the sky) with a bad intention (lust). The gods came to know it and thought of preventing this evil deed. But the gods had no power to punish Prajāpati and restrain him from it. So all the gods gathered together, united their several dreadful forms, brought forth a god named Rudra, and told him to punish Prajāpati. Knowing this, Prajāpati became afraid, took the form of a deer and leapt into the sky. . . .

### Printed p. 753

Prajāpati, in the form of the constellation called Mṛga, can be seen even now. Then Rudra appeared in the form of the constellation Ārdrā and shot an arrow at Prajāpati. Then Prajāpati had an emission of seed. The Maruts scattered that seed in various directions and burnt it. From it (from that seed) first Āditya was born, and afterwards Bhṛgu Vāruṇi. From the remaining embers (coals) the Aṅgirases came into being. So it is said.

In the Purāṇas and elsewhere the sage Aṅgirā is said to be one of the mind-born sons of Brahmā. In the Vedas this Aṅgiras is a very important sage and the original ancestor of many famous sages. The matter is found in the Vana Parva of the Mahābhārata, in the dialogue of Mārkaṇḍeya and Yudhiṣṭhira. For some reason Agni abandoned his duty and went off to the forest in disguise. Then the sage Aṅgirā, in Agni's place, did Agni's work, carrying the shares of oblation to the gods in the sacrifice. He also prayed to Agni to return and perform his duty. Because he performed Agni's duties, this sage Aṅgirā became known as Agni's son, and the descendants of this sage became known as Aṅgirases.

There are some more such stories in the Purāṇas. Besides these, in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā itself: ते अंगिरसः सूनवस्ते अग्नेः परिजज्जिरे । (*te aṃgirasaḥ sūnavaste agneḥ parijajjire |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-62-5), that is, it is clearly said that the sages called Aṅgirases are sons of Agni. It is not known why the commentator did not quote this Ṛk.

It is evident from some Ṛks of the Ṛgveda that this sage Aṅgirā was of very ancient time and that many sages of the Ṛgveda here and there call him the original ancestor of their line.

मनुष्पदग्ने अंगिरस्वदंगिरो ययातिवत्सदने पूर्ववच्चुचे ॥ (*manuṣpadagne aṃgirasvadaṃgiro yayātivatsadane pūrvavaccuce ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-17)

अंगिरस्वन्नहिव्रत प्रस्कण्वस्य श्रुधी हवं (*aṃgirasvannahivrata praskaṇvasya śrudhī havaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-45-3)

दध्यज् ह मे जनुषं पूर्वो अंगिराः प्रियमेधः कण्वो अत्रिर्मनुर्वि दुस्ते मे पूर्वे मनुर्विदुः ॥ (*dadhyaj ha me januṣaṃ pūrvo aṃgirāḥ priyamedhaḥ kaṇvo atrirmanurvi duste me pūrve manurviduḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-139-9)

### Printed p. 754

These Ṛks show that the sage Aṅgirā was the forefather of many sages. Among the descendants of this sage Aṅgirā, Atharvan was the chief. He had three sons, Bṛhaspati, Gotama and Vṛṣaṇa. Vṛṣaṇa was a son born to this Atharvan by his wife named Pathyā. His affairs are indicated in many places in the Veda. Vṛṣaṇa's son was Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa, and this Sudhanvan had three sons, Ṛbhu, Vibhvan and Vāja. These three are spoken of in the Veda as the Ṛbhus. They are said to be pupils of Tvaṣṭā Prajāpati. In the line of this sage Aṅgirā there were three sages named Bṛhaspati. The Ṛbhus mentioned above and Bṛhaspati are regarded as gods, and there are many Ṛks of the Ṛgveda in the form of praises of them. History records that the first of these three Bṛhaspatis killed a Dasyu king named Paṇi and brought back the cows that he had carried off, and that he fought and defeated, with his ten thousand followers, another Dasyu chief named Dāsa who was ruling on the bank of the river Aṃśumatī. The sage Bharadvāja, son of another Bṛhaspati, was the priest of Divodāsa, who slew the demon Śambara. In short, the line of the sage Aṅgirā is very great, and many famous men belonged to it. In many places in the Ṛgveda, that is, in many places where the word Agni would have to be used, the use of the word Aṅgiras is frequent.

The story set out in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 13-23, 24) is given here exactly as it is told there:

प्रजाप्रतिर्नै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यध्यायद्दिवमित्यन्य आहुरुषसमित्कन्ये तामृश्यो भूत्वा रोहितं भूतामभ्यैत्तं देवा अपश्यन्नकृतं वै प्रजापतिः करोतीति ते तम्मैच्छन्य एनमारिष्यत्येतमन्योन्यस्मिन्नाविंदंस्तेषां या एन घोरतमास्तन्व आसंस्ता एकधा समभरंस्ताः संभृता एष देवोऽभवत्तदस्यैतद्भूतवन्नाम भवति वै स योऽस्यैतदेवं नाम वेद ॥ (*prajāpratirnai svāṃ duhitaramabhyadhyāyaddivamityanya āhuruṣasamitkanye tāmṛśyo bhūtvā rohitaṃ bhūtāmabhyaittaṃ devā apaśyannakṛtaṃ vai prajāpatiḥ karotīti te tammaicchanya enamāriṣyatyetamanyonyasminnāviṃdaṃsteṣāṃ yā ena ghoratamāstanva āsaṃstā ekadhā samabharaṃstāḥ saṃbhṛtā eṣa devo 'bhavattadasyaitadbhūtavannāma bhavati vai sa yo 'syaitadevaṃ nāma veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-33) **NOTE**

Long ago, at one time, Prajāpati saw his own daughter and was infatuated, as one is infatuated with a wife. He kept thinking of her form in his mind. As to who that daughter of Prajāpati was, there is a difference of opinion even among the great sages. Some say she was the deity of the sky-world, others that she was the deity Uṣas. Be that as it may. Then Prajāpati took the form of a kind of deer (animal) called Ṛśya. His daughter took the form of a red deer called Rohita. (Here the commentator explains the words रोहितं प्राप्ता (*rohitaṃ prāptā*) as "she became fit for conception".) Prajāpati approached his daughter, who was in the form of Rohita, . . .

### Printed p. 755

…became intent on the act of union. Seeing Prajāpati thus attached to his own daughter and bent on intercourse, the gods spoke among themselves: "This Prajāpati is engaged in a forbidden act that no one has ever done. Who is the person able to stop this deed from taking place?" They searched everywhere. However much they searched, no person capable of restraining Prajāpati was found. The gods put the question to each one among themselves: "If you have the strength, slay Prajāpati." None of them seemed to have that power. Then all the gods together gathered their dreadful forms (it is well known that the gods can assume any form they like; hence "leaving their gentle forms, dreadful shapes" is said here) into one, and created a single person of most dreadful shape. This person received the name Rudra. Hence the names Bhūtavat and Bhūtapati are well known in the world for Rudra. So a person who has taken on this state of being "bhūtavat" of Rudra becomes bhūtimat (prosperous).

तं देवा अब्रुवन्नयं वै प्रजापतिरकृतमकरिमं विध्येति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्स वै वो वरं वृणा इति वृणीष्टेति स एतमेव वरमवृणीत पशूनामाधिपत्यं तदस्यैतत्पशुमन्नाम पशुमान्भवति योऽस्यैतदेवं नाम वेद । (*taṃ devā abruvannayaṃ vai prajāpatirakṛtamakarimaṃ vidhyeti sa tathetyabravītsa vai vo varaṃ vṛṇā iti vṛṇīṣṭeti sa etameva varamavṛṇīta paśūnāmādhipatyaṃ tadasyaitatpaśumannāma paśumānbhavati yo 'syaitadevaṃ nāma veda |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-23)

Then the gods addressed that person (Rudra): "O Rudra, Prajāpati has done a forbidden deed. Therefore, to punish him, strike him with this arrow." Rudra agreed that it should be so. But he asked as a boon that he should become the lord of all animals. The gods gave him the boon accordingly. Therefore Rudra became famous by the name Paśupati. The person who knows this obtains wealth of cattle.

तमभ्यायत्याविध्यत्स विद्ध ऊर्ध्व उदप्रपतत्तमेतं मृग इत्याचक्षते य उ एव मृगव्याधः स उ एव स या रोहित्सा रोहिणी यो एवेषुस्त्रिकांडा सो एवेषुस्त्रिकांडा । (*tamabhyāyatyāvidhyatsa viddha ūrdhva udaprapatattametaṃ mṛga ityācakṣate ya u eva mṛgavyādhaḥ sa u eva sa yā rohitsā rohiṇī yo eveṣustrikāṃḍā so eveṣustrikāṃḍā |*)

Then Rudra came forward, strung his bow, fitted the arrow, drew it back, aimed at Prajāpati and shot. The arrow struck Prajāpati, who was in the form of an ṛśya, and he leapt upward into the atmosphere. Seeing Prajāpati leaping upward in the sky, all people call it the constellation Mṛga (Stars in the Orion). That is, they say it is the Mṛgaśīrṣa star between the stars Rohiṇī and Ārdrā.

### Printed p. 756

The meaning is that Prajāpati exists in the form of a star. Rudra, who shot Prajāpati in the form of a deer with the arrow, appears in the sky by the name Mṛgavyādha. The daughter of Prajāpati, in the form of the red doe called rohita, appears in the sky as the star Rohiṇī. The arrow sent by Rudra came to have three parts: the kāṇḍa (the long shaft of the arrow), the śalya (the barb) and the tip (the sharp point); therefore the arrow has these three parts even now.

तद्वा इदं प्रजापते रेतः सिक्तमधावत्तत्सरोऽभवत्ते देवा अब्रुवन्मेदं प्रजापते रेतो दुषदिति यदब्रुवन्मेदं प्रजापते रेतो दुषदिति तन्मादुषमभवत्तन्मामहस्य मादुषत्वं मादुषं ह वै नामैतद्यन्मानुषं सन्मानुषमित्याचक्षरे परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः (*tadvā idaṃ prajāpate retaḥ siktamadhāvattatsaro 'bhavatte devā abruvanmedaṃ prajāpate reto duṣaditi yadabruvanmedaṃ prajāpate reto duṣaditi tanmāduṣamabhavattanmāmahasya māduṣatvaṃ māduṣaṃ ha vai nāmaitadyanmānuṣaṃ sanmānuṣamityācakṣare parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 13-23)

The semen (seed) of Prajāpati in deer form was abundant; part of it was shed into his daughter, the doe, and the remainder fell on the earth, began to flow like a river in a stream, collected in a low-lying place and became a great lake. Seeing it, the gods wished that people should not think this seed of Prajāpati untouchable (not to be touched) or "mādūṣat", bad. Because the gods called it mādūṣat, the lake, which was the seed of the faultless Prajāpati, came to be named Mādūṣat. People substitute the letter na in place of the da of the word mādūṣa when reciting, and so they call Brahmins, Kṣatriyas and other people "mānuṣa". Rightly considered, the word mānuṣa (mādūṣa) means "faultless". That being so, instead of referring to their bodies by the word mānuṣa of ordinary meaning, people refer to them by a word of indirect meaning (that is, with the excellent sense of mādūṣa); therefore worthy and worshipful persons, like the gods, in worldly usage are fond of the indirect (content with words that have a hidden sense rather than a directly evident one). For example, they are satisfied not so much with the ordinary names, such as Devadatta, given by their parents, as with names suited to their nature, such as Upādhyāya, Ācārya, Svāmin, which make their fame shine. The gods too, not appearing directly but remaining out of sight, accept praises and the like; therefore it is said that the gods are fond of the indirect. So, to show indirectness, in the word mādūṣa the na is put in place of the da and mānuṣa is used.

तदग्निना पर्यादधुस्तन्मरुतोऽधून्वंस्तदग्निर्न प्राच्यावयत्तदग्निना वैश्वानरेण पर्यादधुस्तस्मरुतोऽधून्वंस्तदग्निर्वृश्वानरः प्राच्यावयत्तस्य यद्रेतसः प्रथममुददीप्यत तदसावादित्योऽभवद्यद्वितीयमासीत्तद्भृगुरभवत्तं वरुणो न्यगृह्णीत तस्मात्स भृगुर्वारुणिरथ यत्कृतीयमदीदेदिव त आदित्या अभवन्येऽङ्गारा आसंस्तेऽङ्गरसोऽभवन्यदंगाराः पुनरवशांता उददीप्यंत तद्ब्रहस्पतिरभवत् । (*tadagninā paryādadhustanmaruto 'dhūnvaṃstadagnirna prācyāvayattadagninā vaiśvānareṇa paryādadhustasmaruto 'dhūnvaṃstadagnirvṛśvānaraḥ prācyāvayattasya yadretasaḥ prathamamudadīpyata tadasāvādityo 'bhavadyadvitīyamāsīttadbhṛgurabhavattaṃ varuṇo nyagṛhṇīta tasmātsa bhṛgurvāruṇiratha yatkṛtīyamadīdediva ta ādityā abhavanye 'ṅgārā āsaṃste 'ṅgaraso 'bhavanyadaṃgārāḥ punaravaśāṃtā udadīpyaṃta tadbrahaspatirabhavat |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-34)

### Printed p. 757

Then, after the gods had made the seed of Prajāpati faultless, they thought that this seed, which was in liquid form as a lake, must be made free of liquid; they kindled fire around the lake and began to burn it. While the fire was blazing all around the lake, the wind churned the seed into turmoil in order to dry up the liquid mixed with it. Yet the fire could not, by its heat, remove the liquid state, which was very strong in the seed, and turn it into a lump (a solid, hard substance). Therefore the gods tried to accomplish, by a special form of fire named Vaiśvānara, this work that the fire could not do. This Vaiśvānara fire enters the bellies of all beings as the digestive fire and is engaged in digesting food and drink.

अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः । प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधं ॥ (*ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ | prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidhaṃ ‖*)

"Becoming the Vaiśvānara fire, abiding in the bodies of beings, joined with the breaths prāṇa and apāna, I digest the fourfold food that beings eat" — so the Lord himself has said. Therefore the gods, knowing that the power of the Vaiśvānara fire is special, set the Vaiśvānara fire around the lake to dry up that seed of Prajāpati. The wind too entered the lake as before, churned it into turmoil and began to dry it. Thus, with the help of the wind, the Vaiśvānara fire separated the seed of Prajāpati from its liquid state and turned it into a solid, lump-shaped substance. Thus the seed, turned into many lumps (spherical), began to blaze and shine. Of these, the first lump, a mass of radiance, became the Āditya seen in heaven (the sky). The second lump became the sage Bhṛgu. Varuṇa accepted this Bhṛgu as his son. Therefore the sage Bhṛgu got the name Bhṛgurvāruṇiḥ, "the sage Bhṛgu, son of Varuṇa"; as the son of Varuṇa he is also called Vāruṇi. With this in mind the followers of the Taittirīya branch recite: भृगुर्वैवारुणिः । वरुणं पितरमुपससार (*bhṛgurvaivāruṇiḥ | varuṇaṃ pitaramupasasāra*) (Tai. U. 3-1). Then the third lump, shining exceedingly,

### Printed p. 758

became famous as the sons of Aditi, by the name Ādityas. Āditya means the sun within the orb. It is to be understood that here the word ādityāḥ indicates the other gods, sons of Aditi. Then some other lumps burned well (were consumed) and became embers. From those embers arose the sages called Aṅgiras. And from the embers that were still burning and had not gone out, that is, that began to burn brightly again and again, Bṛhaspati arose.

यानि परिक्षाणान्यासंस्ते कृष्णाः पशवोऽभवन्या लोहिनी मृत्तिका ते रोहिता अथ यद्भस्मासीत्तत्परुष्यं व्यसर्पद्गौरो गवय ऋश्य उष्टो गर्दभ इति ये चैतेऽरुणाः पशवस्ते च । (*yāni parikṣāṇānyāsaṃste kṛṣṇāḥ paśavo 'bhavanyā lohinī mṛttikā te rohitā atha yadbhasmāsīttatparuṣyaṃ vyasarpadgauro gavaya ṛśya uṣṭo gardabha iti ye caite 'ruṇāḥ paśavaste ca |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-34)

Then, when the embers went out and became aṅgāra (charcoal), these became black animals. After the fire had burned, the red clay (earth) lying at the bottom became red animals. From the ashes (bhasma) arose the paruṣya animals, that is, the forest animals gaura, gavaya and ṛśya, and also the camel and the donkey. And so on. By this narrative, the account of the origin of the Aṅgiras sages, the relation between the Aṅgiras sages and Agni, and the reason why Agni got the name Aṅgiras are all explained.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ता विश्वा॑ वि॒दुषे॒ तुभ्यं॑ वेधो नी॒थान्य॑ग्ने नि॒ण्या वचां॑सि ।  
> नि॒वच॑ना क॒वये॒ काव्या॒न्यशं॑सिषं म॒तिभि॒र्विप्र॑ उ॒क्षैः ॥ १६ ॥

> *etā viśvā viduṣe tubhyaṃ vedho nīthānyagne niṇyā vacāṃsi |*  
> *nivacanā kavaye kāvyānyaśaṃsiṣaṃ matibhirvipra ukṣaiḥ ‖ 16 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एता । निश्वा । विदुषे । तुभ्यं । वेधः । नीथानि । अग्ने । निज्या । वचांसि ।  
> निऽवचना । कवये । काव्यानि । अशंसिषं । मतिभिः । विप्रः । उक्तैः ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वेधो विधातर्हे अग्ने विदुषे कर्मविषयज्ञानवते कवये क्रांतदर्शिने
> तुभ्यं नीथानि फलप्रापकाणि निण्या नेयार्थानि गूढानि निवचना नितरां वक्तव्यानि
> काव्यानि कविभिर्मेधाविभिः कृतान्येता विश्वैतानि सर्वाणि वचांसि वाक्यानि मतिभिर्म-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Vedhaḥ" means vidhātaḥ, "O Creator"; the address is to Agni. Vidvas is one who has knowledge concerning ritual action; kavi is one who sees beyond (krāntadarśin). To you, so described, he says, he has recited these words. Nīthāni are those that bring about the fruit; niṇyā are of hidden meaning (neyārtha), obscure; nivacanā are to be spoken constantly; they are poems made by poets, the wise. "These all words" means all these sentences, to be recited with the thoughts (matibhiḥ)… [the explanation continues in the next block].

### Printed p. 759

> ननीयैः स्तोत्रैरुक्थैः शस्त्रैश्च सहितो विप्रः प्राज्ञोऽहमशंसिषं । अवोचं ।
> तानि सेवस्वेत्यर्थः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

…with praises worthy of reflection, with ukthas, that is, śastras: "I, the wise one (vipra, prājña), have recited, have spoken; accept them" is the meaning.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वेधः (*vedhaḥ*)—creator
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- विदुषे (*viduṣe*)—one who has knowledge concerning ritual action
- कवये (*kavaye*)—and one who sees beyond
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to you
- नीथानि (*nīthāni*)—those that bring about the fruit
- निण्या (*niṇyā*)—those of hidden meaning
- निवचना (*nivacanā*)—those worthy of praise
- काव्यानि (*kāvyāni*)—those composed by poets
- एता विश्वा वचांसि (*etā viśvā vacāṃsi*)—all these words of praise too
- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—with worshipful hymns of praise
- उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*)—with śastra-mantras
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—I, the wise one
- अशंसिषं (*aśaṃsiṣaṃ*)—I recite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, creator, to you who have knowledge concerning ritual action and who see beyond, I, the wise one, recite all these words of praise, which bring the fruit, are of hidden meaning, are worthy of praise and are composed by poets, together with worshipful hymns of praise and śastra-mantras.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, creator, to the who are wise, acquainted with the past, I address
oh sage, these soliciting mysterious words, (these) ever-to-be-recited poems,
together with praises and prayers.

## Sūkta 4 (Maṇḍala 4)

The deity of this sūkta is Agni Rakṣohā; that is, Agni who destroys the host of rakṣas, beings such as ghosts and piśācas that obstruct sacrifices. Explaining the word rakṣaḥ, Yāska has given the etymology:

रक्षो रक्षितव्यमस्मात् । रहसि क्षणोतीति ना । रात्रौ नक्षत इति ना ॥ (*rakṣo rakṣitavyamasmāt | rahasi kṣaṇotīti nā | rātrau nakṣata iti nā ‖*) (Ni. 4-8)

That is: the host of beings called rakṣas devours men; from it our body must be protected; because it must be protected from it, it is called rakṣaḥ. Or, because it harms (men) in a solitary place where no one is, or in the dark, it is called rakṣaḥ. Or, because it moves about at night, it is called rakṣaḥ. Thus he has given three kinds of meaning.

### Printed p. 760

There is a difference between the word rakṣaḥ and the word rākṣasa. Rākṣasas are particular persons of human shape, or of other fearful shape that can be seen with the eye. They are of wicked nature, always cause harm to good people and cause obstacles to good deeds. The word rakṣaḥ denotes ghosts, spirits, piśācas and the like that are not visible to the eye (Demons, evil spirits &c.): it is their nature to cause harm to men and to cause the swelling up (of obstruction) to good deeds such as sacrifices. It is customary to pray to Agni in sacrifices and in other rites to remove their affliction and protect us. The Agni who removes this kind of affliction is called Rakṣohā Agni.

The piśācas or bhūtas on the earth are enemies of men. The word that denotes them as a class is rakṣaḥ. This word occurs more than fifty times in the singular and plural; ordinarily it comes together with some deity, in the form of a prayer, "destroy the rākṣasa", or in the form of praise, "you have slain the rākṣasa". In the sūktas 7-104 and 10-87 mention of them is the very subject. Here the words rakṣasaḥ, yātu, yātudhāna and the like indicate them. Since rakṣasaḥ is the name for evil deities, piśācas and all such, it may be understood as the class-name, and yātu as the sub-class name.

These piśācas or bhūtas have the forms of dogs, vultures, owls and other birds (7-104-20 to 22). In bird form they fly about at night (7-104-18). Taking the form of a brother, a husband or a lover, they approach women and wish to destroy their children (10-162-5). In the form of a dog or a monkey they lie in wait to fall upon women (A. Ve. 4-37-11).**NOTE** Hence pregnant women and children are troubled by them. (A. Ve. 8-6). At the time of marriage they move about around the bride; to pierce their eyes (?) they shoot small arrows into the atmosphere (Mā. Gṛ. Sū. 1-10).**NOTE** The description of their form and so on is found in the Atharvaveda itself. They in particular take form like men. Mention is made of their limbs, such as head, eyes, heart; but some deformity is always there: three heads, two mouths, four eyes, five feet, no fingers, feet turned backward, or horns on the hands, and so on (A. Ve. 8-6; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 2-3-7).**NOTE** Blue, yellow or green piśācas are also mentioned (A. Ve. 19-22-4, 5). Among them also there are males and females, families, and kings (A. Ve. 5-22-12; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 2-3-7); they too are mortal (A. Ve. 6-32-2; and so on).

### Printed p. 761
The Yātudhānas eat the flesh of men and of horses, and they drink cow's milk (10-86-16, 17). To satisfy their craving for blood and flesh the Rākṣasas attack men. This attack is generally made by entering them. Agni is prayed to keep the Rākṣasas from entering the worshippers (8-48-20). A disease-spirit, a Piśāca flitting hither and thither, enters men (Atha. Saṃ. 7-76-4). These ghosts and spirits generally enter us through our mouth when we eat or drink (Atha. Saṃ. 5-29-6 to 8); they also enter by other openings (Atha. Saṃ. 8-6-3). As soon as they are inside, they tear out and eat the man's flesh and cause disease (Atha. Saṃ. 5-29-5, 10). They cause madness and destroy the power of speech (Atha. Saṃ. 6-1113; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 1-15-5). They invade men's dwellings (Kau. Sū. 135-9). Some spirits, in the evening, go about the houses dancing and braying like asses, or roam in the forests, or laugh loudly or drink from skulls (Atha. Saṃ. 8-6-10), 11, 14; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 2-3-3).
**NOTE**
**NOTE**
**NOTE**

Their time of roaming is night or evening (7-104-8). In the eastern quarter their sport does not go on; the sun rising there drives them away (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-6.3). A falling meteor is thought to be the form of a spirit (Kau. Sū. 126-9). As the pitch darkness of the new-moon night is fit for the roaming of the departed, so it is the favourable time for the spirits too (Atha. Saṃ. 1-16-1; 4-36-3).

Nothing endangers sacrifices as much as they do. In sacrifices fit for the gods the Piśācas cause defects and omissions, and the Yātus scatter the offered oblations here and there (7-104-18, 21). They cannot bear the sight of praise (10-182-3). Agni is prayed to burn up the spirits and the like, so that no curse may touch the sacrifice (1-76-3). There is a mantra that makes an enemy's sacrifice fail to prosper through the magic of the Yātudhānas and the Rakṣas hosts (Atha. Saṃ. 7-70-2). They come as departed spirits and obstruct the food and water offered to the dead (Atha. Saṃ. 18-2-28; compare Vā. Saṃ. 2-29). In the Purāṇas it is common that these Rakṣas (commonly called Rākṣasas) trouble yogis.

Agni, the dispeller of darkness and the lord of the sacrifice, has a deep hatred of them. Prayer is made to Agni himself: burn them, drive them off, destroy them (10-87-3-6 and so on). It is from this poem that Agni and some other deities have the name "Rakṣohā" (slayer of Rakṣas).

### Printed p. 762
These spirits are not only harmful by nature; they sometimes do harm when impelled by others. The expression rakṣoyujaḥ (those who impel Rākṣasas) is found (6-62-9), and here and there there are the spirits and Yātus of the magicians (7-104-23; 8-60-20). One who is afflicted by a spirit sent by an enemy can drive them away by offering oblation to Agni Yaviṣṭha (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-3-2); and those spirits themselves are commanded to swallow him who sent them (Atha. Saṃ. 2-2-4).

In the sense of spirits the word rakṣaḥ is used in both the masculine and the feminine; in the neuter it also means danger. It may come from the root rakṣ (to trouble), "harmful"; but this use is very rare. It may also come from the common rakṣ, to protect; in that case rakṣaḥ means "that which is to be guarded against".

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कृणुष्वेति पंचदशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं नामदेवस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं रक्षोहाग्नि देवताकं । कृणुष्ट पंचोना राक्षोघ्नमित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ प्रवर्ग्येऽभिष्टवे कृणुष्ट पाज इत्याद्याः पंचर्चो
> विनियुक्ताः । सूत्रितं च । कृणुष्ट पाजः प्रसितिं न पृथ्वीमिति पंच । आ. ४-६ । इति ॥
> अनुवादवु—कृणुष्ट ऎंब ई सूक्तवु मॊदलनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि नाल्कनॆय सूक्तवु.
> इदरल्लि हदिनैदु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ वामदेवनु ऋपियु ; रक्षोहाग्नियु देव
> तॆयु ; त्रिष्टुप् छंदस्सु अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि—कृणुष्ट पंचोना राक्षोघ्नं ऎंदु हेळिरु
> वुदु. प्रातरनुवाक मत्तु आश्विनशस्त्रमंत्र पठनक्कागि ई सूक्तद विनियोगविरुवुदु. प्रवर्ग्य
> वॆंब यागदल्लियू कृणुष्ट पाजः ऎंदु मॊदलागुव ऐदु ऋक्कुगळ विनियोगविरुवुदॆंदु
> आश्वलायनशौतसूत्रद—कृणुष्ट पाजः प्रसितिं न पृथ्वीमिति पंच ऎंब सूत्रदिंद
> (आ. ४-६) विवृतवागिरुवुदु.
> vjoh

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning कृणुष्व (*kṛṇuṣva*) is the fourth sūkta, of fifteen ṛks. Its seer is Vāmadeva, its deity Agni as Rakṣohā (slayer of Rakṣas), its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā says: कृणुष्ट पंचोना राक्षोघ्नमित्यनुक्रमणिका (*kṛṇuṣṭa paṃconā rākṣoghnamityanukramaṇikā*). Viniyoga: the sūkta is used in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Āśvinaśastra. In the Pravargya, in the Abhiṣṭava, the five ṛks beginning कृणुष्ट पाजः (*kṛṇuṣṭa pājaḥ*) are employed; the sūtra says कृणुष्ट पाजः प्रसितिं न पृथ्वीमिति पंच (*kṛṇuṣṭa pājaḥ prasitiṃ na pṛthvīmiti paṃca*) (Ā. 4-6). The Kannada Anuvāda within the block says the same.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, make (spread out) your mass of energy (pājas)." The illustration: as a hunter spreads a wide snare (prasiti) — prasiti is a net, that which is bound (sīyate) out and out — in thick forest to catch birds, so you too spread a great force in front to slay the Rakṣas. "Go (yāhi) to slay Rakṣas, accompanied by a mass of energy free from fear (ibhena)", like a king (amavān): amaḥ is a minister (āmātya), one who is with him; or else amaḥ is illness (amana), the king who is a disease to his enemies; or the king goes against the enemy's army on an elephant (ibha). Further, tṛṣṭī is a word for "swift": following (dronānaḥ) the swift-going prasiti, the superior army. Or else tṛṣṭīm stands in the accusative for the instrumental: going on with the swift, continuous course attached to the host, you, harming the enemy army, are the hurler (astā) of foes. With your hottest (tapiṣṭha) flames pierce (vidhya), strike, the Rakṣas. Here the Nirukta: कुरुष्ट पाजः । पाजः पालनात् । प्रसितिमिव पृथ्वीं । प्रसितिः प्रसहनात्तंतुर्वा जालं वा । याहि राजीनामात्यवानभ्यमनवा- (*kuruṣṭa pājaḥ | pājaḥ pālanāt | prasitimiva pṛthvīṃ | prasitiḥ prasahanāttaṃturvā jālaṃ vā | yāhi rājīnāmātyavānabhyamanavā-*) (continued in the next block).

### Printed p. 764

> न्तस्त्ववान्वेरावता गणेन गतभयेन हस्तिनेति वा । तृष्णानु प्रसित्या द्रोणानः ।
> तृष्टीति क्षिप्रनाम तरतेर्वा त्वरतेर्वा । अस्तासि विध्य रक्षसस्तपिष्ठैस्तप्ततमैस्तपिष्ठतमैरिति वा । नि. ६-१२ । इति ॥ कृणुष्ट । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोः । लोटि धिन्विकृण्वॊर -
> च्छेत्युप्रत्ययः । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । विकरणस्वरस्तु सति शिष्टोऽपि लसार्वधातुक
> स्वरं न बाधत इति लसार्वधातुकस्वरः । म. ६-१-१५८-११ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Nirukta continues: with a troop that has lost fear, or with an elephant; tṛṣṭī is a word for swift, from tarati or tvarate; "you are the hurler, pierce the Rakṣas with the hottest", tapiṣṭha being explained as tapta-tama or tapiṣṭha-tama (Ni. 6-12). The rest of the block is grammar of kṛṇuṣva and is left to the Grammar.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- पृथ्विं (*pṛthviṃ*)—wide
- प्रसितं न (*prasitaṃ na*)—as (a hunter) spreads a net
- पाजः (*pājaḥ*)—your mass of energy
- कृणुष्ट्व (*kṛṇuṣṭva*)—spread out
- इभीन (*ibhīna*)—mounted on an elephant
- अमवान् (*amavān*)—with his retinue
- इव (*iva*)—like a king setting out on a campaign
- इभेन (*ibhena*)—together with your energies
- याहि (*yāhi*)—set out to destroy the enemy
- प्रसितिं (*prasitiṃ*)—the excellent army
- अनु द्रोणानः (*anu droṇānaḥ*)—following
- अस्ता असि (*astā asi*)—you are the scatterer of foes
- तपिष्ठैः (*tapiṣṭhaiḥ*)—with scorching energies
- रक्षसः (*rakṣasaḥ*)—the Rākṣasas
- विध्य (*vidhya*)—beat down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, spread out your mass of energy as a hunter casts and spreads a wide net. As a king mounted on an elephant and accompanied by his retinue sets out on a campaign, so set out with your energies to destroy the enemy. Following the excellent army, you are the scatterer of foes. With scorching energies beat down the Rākṣasas.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Put forth your strength, Agni, as a fowler spreads a capacious snare : proceed like a king attended by his followers on his elephant : you are the scatterer ( of your foes ) ; following the swift-moving host consume the Rakshasas with your fierce flames

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Amavān—In stating the derivation of this word, Yāska has given an explanation of this ṛk कृणुस्व पाजः (*kṛṇusva pājaḥ*): कुरुष्व पाजः । पाजः पालनात् । प्रसितिमिव पृथ्वीं । प्रसितिः प्रसयनात् तंतुर्वा जालं ना! याहि राजीनामात्यवानभ्यमनवान् स्ववान्वेराभृता गणेन गतभयेन हस्तिनेति वा । तृष्णानु प्रसित्या द्रोणाननः । तृष्णिति क्षिप्रनाम तरतेर्वा त्वरतेर्वा । असितासि विध्यरक्षसस्तपिष्ठैस्तप्ततम्मस्तप्ततम्मैः प्रपिष्टतम्मैरिति वा । (*kuruṣva pājaḥ | pājaḥ pālanāt | prasitimiva pṛthvīṃ | prasitiḥ prasayanāt taṃturvā jālaṃ nā! yāhi rājīnāmātyavānabhyamanavān svavānverābhṛtā gaṇena gatabhayena hastineti vā | tṛṣṇānu prasityā droṇānanaḥ | tṛṣṇiti kṣipranāma taratervā tvaratervā | asitāsi vidhyarakṣasastapiṣṭhaistaptatammastaptatammaiḥ prapiṣṭatammairiti vā |*) (नि (*ni*). ६ १ (*6 1*):) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 765
O Agni, spread out your strength. The word pājaḥ indicates the meaning "protection". The word prasiti, formed from the root pra+si, gives the meaning "bind, tie"; therefore prasiti means a cord or a net. Here Agni is addressed: go like a king. The manner of a king's going is described thus: like a king with his amātya (minister), or going terrible to his enemies, or going together with his followers, or going seated on a fearless elephant — so Agni is praised: go like that. Tṛṣṭi means "quickly"; this word may be formed from the root tarati or from tvarati. O Agni, strike the Rākṣasas with arrows, harm them, and pierce, pulverise and destroy them with burning or blazing sharp spears (śalya): so Agni is praised.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, your wandering (bhramāsaḥ), swift-going rays fall (patanti), spread everywhere. Blazing (śośucānaḥ) intensely, touch (spṛśa) the enemies in order, burn them, with your mass of energy that can overpower (dhṛṣatā)." He shows the means of burning: unhindered (asandita) by others, scatter everywhere (viṣvak, vi sṛja) with the juhū, that is the flame, in which oblations are offered, your scorching energies (tapūṃṣi), the flying sparks (patangān) and the brands (ulkāḥ) — these three. The rest of the block is grammar (āśuyā, dhṛṣatā, juhvā, asandita) and continues on the next page.

The block gives only grammatical derivations (asandita, from the root dā, avakhaṇḍane, with the negative compound and its accent).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तव (*tava*)—your

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, your wandering, swift-moving rays spread everywhere. Brightly shining, burn the enemies in order with the energy that checks enemies. Unhindered by enemies, spread everywhere with your flame your burning energies, sparks and brands.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने तूर्णितमस्त्वरिततमस्त्वं स्पशः परबाधकान्रश्मिन् चारान्वा सत्यानृतविवेकार्थं वि सृज । शत्रून्प्रति विशेषेण प्रेरय । अदब्धः केनाप्यहिंसितस्त्वमस्यास्त्वदीयाया विशोऽस्मदादिकायाः प्रजायाः पायु: पालको भव । कस्मात्तद्रक्षण.
> मित्यपेक्षायामाह । नोऽस्माकं दूरे योऽघशंसः । अघं पापात्मकं शंसनमभिलाषः कीर्तनं ना यस्य सोऽघशंसः । यश्चाघशंसोऽ०त्यस्माकं समीपे तिष्ठति
> शस्मादुभयविधाच्छत्रोः पालको भव । किंच ते त्वत्संबंधिनोऽस्मान्माकिर्न
> कश्चिदपि व्यथिर्बाधको राक्षस आ दधर्षीत् । आधर्षयतु । आस्माकं कश्चिदपि
> परिभवं मा करोत्वित्यर्थः ॥ अंति । अंतिकस्य कादिलोप आद्युदात्तत्वं च । अग्ने ।
> षादादित्वात्पाष्ठिकमाद्युदात्तत्वं । माकिष्ट इति संहितायां युष्मत्तत्ततक्षुःष्टंतः
> पादमिति षत्वं । दधर्षीत् । धृष प्रसहने । लजु बहुलं छंदसीति शपः श्लुः ।
> बहुलं छंदसीति तिप ईडागमः । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, swiftest (tūrṇitama), send forth (vi sṛja) your stinging (spaśaḥ) rays — or spies, for the discernment of truth and falsehood — send them forth especially against the enemies. Unharmed (adabdha) by anyone, be the protector (pāyuḥ) of this your people (viś), that is, of us and others." If it is asked from what protection is needed, he says: whoever is far from us as an aghaśaṃsa — one whose utterance (śaṃsana), wish or praise, is aghaṃ, sinful — and whoever stands near us: be the protector against both kinds of enemy. "And let no one, no harassing (vyathi) Rākṣasa, assail (ā dadharṣīt) us who are yours": that is, let no one at all overcome us. The rest of the block is grammar (anti, agne, mākiṣṭe, dadharṣīt).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- तूर्णितमः (*tūrṇitamaḥ*)—you, of swift motion
- स्पशः (*spaśaḥ*)—your rays that harm the enemies
- प्रति वि सृज (*prati vi sṛja*)—spread and send forth
- अदब्धः (*adabdhaḥ*)—you, harmed by none
- अस्याः (*asyāḥ*)—belonging to you
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—to us, your people
- पायुः (*pāyuḥ*)—as protector
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- दूरे (*dūre*)—far away
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- अघशंसः (*aghaśaṃsaḥ*)—sinner
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which sin-wisher
- अंति (*aṃti*)—is near (protect us from all of them)
- ते (*te*)—us who belong to you
- माकिः (*mākiḥ*)—no one at all
- व्यथिः (*vyathiḥ*)—as a harasser
- आ दधर्षीत् (*ā dadharṣīt*)—let him not fall upon (us)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of swift motion, spread your rays that harm the enemies. Unharmed by anyone, protect us, your people, from all sinners, whether far or near. Let no one fall upon us who belong to you and harm us.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> *udagne tiṣṭha pratyā tanuṣṭa nṛmitrāṃ oṣatāttigmahete |*  
> *yo no ārātiṃ samidhāna cakre nīcā taṃ dhakṣyatasaṃ na*  
> *śuṣkaṃ ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । अग्ने । तिष्ठ । प्रति । आ । तनुष्ट । नि । अमित्रान् । ओषतात् । तिग्महेते ।  
> यः । नः । अरातिं । सम्ऽइधान । चक्रे । नीचा । तम् । धक्षि । अतसं । न । शुष्कं ॥

> *ut | agne | tiṣṭha | prati | ā | tanuṣṭa | ni | amitrān | oṣatāt | tigmahete |*  
> *yaḥ | naḥ | arātiṃ | sam 'idhāna | cakre | nīcā | tam | dhakṣi | atasaṃ | na | śuṣkaṃ ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तिग्महेते । तिग्मास्तीक्ष्णा हॆ तयो ज्वाला यस्य स तथोक्तः । तादृश हे अग्ने
> उत्तिष्ठ । रक्षोहननार्थमुद्यतो भव । शत्रून्प्रत्या तनुष्ट । ज्वालासंघं विस्तारय । तैस्तेजःसंघैरमित्रान् शत्रून्नोषतात् । नितरां दह । हे समिधान समिद्भिर्दिष्यमानाग्ने यः पुमान् नोऽस्माकमरातिं । भावप्रधाननिर्देशः । अरातित्वं ।
> शात्रवं चक्रे । कुरुते । अरातिमदानं वा कुरुते । तं पुमांसं नीचा न्यग्भूतं
> धक्षि । दह । तत्र दृष्टांतः . अतसं न। यथा शुष्कमनाद्र्रमतसं काष्ठं दहसि तद्वत्॥
> ओषतात् । उष दाहे । लोटि हेस्तहोरिति तातजादेशः । धक्षि । दहेर्लोटि
> बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुक् । हो ढ इति ढत्वं । भष्भावः । षडोः कः सीति कत्वं ।
> निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Tigmahete: one whose flames (*hètayaḥ*) are sharp. Such an Agni is told to rise, that is, to be ready to slay the Rākṣasas, and to spread the mass of his flames against the enemies. With those masses of fire he is to burn the foes (अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)) completely. "O Samidhāna" means Agni kindled with fuel-sticks. Whatever man makes arāti (enmity) towards us — arāti is stated as an abstract notion, meaning enmity (शात्रवं (*śātravaṃ*)) — or, as the text has it, produces arāti-intoxication (अरातिमदानं (*arātimadānaṃ*)), him Agni is to burn, cast down, as one burns a dry, moistureless piece of timber (अतसं (*atasaṃ*)). **NOTE**

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- उत्तिष्ठ (*uttiṣṭha*)—rise, for the slaying of foes
- पत्या (*patyā*)—your mass of flames **NOTE**
- आ तनुष्प (*ā tanuṣpa*)—spread out
- अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)—the enemies

- समिधान (*samidhāna*)—O Agni, who blaze up with fuel-sticks
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whatever man
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- आरातिं (*ārātiṃ*)—enmity
- चक्रे (*cakre*)—fosters
- तं (*taṃ*)—him
- नीचा (*nīcā*)—thrusting down
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—dry **NOTE**
- आतसं न (*ātasaṃ na*)—as one burns timber
- धक्षि (*dhakṣi*)—burn

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of sharp flames, make yourself ready for slaying the foes. Spread out the mass of your flames. Burn the enemies completely. O Agni, who blaze up with fuel-sticks, burn the man who fosters enmity towards us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Sharp-weaponed Agni, rise up ; spread wide (your flames)against (the Rakshasas) ; entirely consume the foes ; blazing Agni,burn down him who acts as an enemy towards us like a piece of dry timber.

> ऊ॒र्ध्वो भ॑व॒ प्रति॑ वि॒ध्याध्य॒स्मदा॒विष्कृ॑णुष्ट॒ दैव्या॑न्यग्ने ।  
> अव॑ स्थि॒रा त॑नुहि यातु॒जूनां॑ जा॒मिमजा॑मिं॒ प्र मृ॑णीहि॒  ॑

> अव । स्थिरा । तनुहि । यातुजूनां । जामिं । अजामिं । प्र । मृणीहि । शत्रून् ॥

> *ūrdhvaḥ | bhava | prati | vidhya | adhi | asmat | āviḥ | kṛṇuṣṭa | daivyāni | agne |*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने ऊर्ध्वो भव । रक्षोहननार्थमुद्युक्तो भव । अस्मदस्मत्तोऽधि
> अधिकानाक्षसान् प्रति विध्य । प्रत्येकं ताडय । दैव्यानि तेजांसि चाविष्कृणुष्ट ।
> अविष्कुरु । एतत्रयं विधाय यातुजूनां यातयितुं प्राणिनः क्लेशयितुं ये
> जनं कुर्वंति तेषां यातुधानानां स्थिरा दृढानि धनूंष्यव तनुहि । अवगतज्यानि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, be upright, that is, be ready for slaying the Rākṣasas. Pierce each one separately of the Rākṣasas who are more numerous than we are (*asmadadhi*). Make manifest your divine energies. Having done these three things, unstring the strong bows of the Yātujūs, those Yātudhānas who work to torment living beings; make them bowstring-less.

### Printed p. 770

> कुरु । किंच जामिमजामिं बंधुमबंधुं शत्रून् मृणीहि । प्रजहि । यद्वा ।
> जामिं यः पूर्वं प्रहृतस्तं । अजामिं पूर्वमप्रहृतं । एवंभूतान् शत्रून्
> जहि । प्रहृतोऽयमित्यपेक्षां मा कृथाः ॥ आविष्कृणुष्टेत्यत्र संहितायामिदुदुपधस्य चाप्रत्ययस्येति षत्वं । तनुहि । तनोतेर्लोट्युतश्च प्रत्ययाच्छंदसि वावचनमिति हेर्लुगभावः । यातुजूनां । जु गत् । क्विब्बचीत्यादिना क्विप् । दीर्घः । आमि
> छांदसो नुम् । मृणीहि । मृज् प्राणत्यागे । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थस्य लोटि बहुलं
> छंदसीति विकरणस्य श्ना । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Further, destroy the enemies, whether kindred or non-kindred (जामिमजामिं (*jāmimajāmiṃ*)). Or else: jāmi is one who has been struck before, ajāmi one not struck before; slay enemies of both sorts, and do not hesitate with the thought "this one has already been struck."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ऊर्ध्वो भव (*ūrdhvo bhava*)—rise up and stand, for victory over the foes
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—than we
- अधि (*adhi*)—the foes who are greater in number
- प्रति विध्य (*prati vidhya*)—beat down one by one
- दैव्यानि (*daivyāni*)—your divine energies
- आविष्कृणुष्ट्वा (*āviṣkṛṇuṣṭvā*)—make manifest
- यातुजूनां (*yātujūnāṃ*)—of the Rākṣasas
- स्थिरा (*sthirā*)—the strong bows
- अव तनुहि (*ava tanuhi*)—make them without bowstring (jyā)
- जामिं (*jāmiṃ*)—be he a kinsman
- अजामिं (*ajāmiṃ*)—or not a kinsman
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—those who wish us harm
- मृणीहि (*mṛṇīhi*)—conquer and subdue

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, be ready for victory over the foes. Destroy one by one the foes who are more numerous than we. Make your divine energies manifest. Tear off the strings of the strong bows of the Rākṣasas. Whether they are our kinsmen or not, conquer and subdue those who wish us harm.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Rise up, Agni chastise those who overpower us ; manifest your divine energies; slacken the strong (bow strings) of the malignant kings ; destroy those (who are hostile), whether kindred or unallied.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यविष्ठ युवतम । यद्वा । देवानां हवींषि मिश्रयित्यृतम हे अग्ने यः
> पुमानीवते गमनवते कल्याणहेतुभूतागमनाय ब्रह्मणे परिवृढाय तुभ्यं
> गातुं । गीयत उच्चार्यत इति गातुः स्तोत्रं । तदैरत् । प्रेरयति । स पुमान्
> ते तव सुमतिं कल्याणकरीमनुग्रहात्मिकां बुद्धिं जानाति । लभत इत्यर्थः । अस्मै
> स्तोत्रं कृतवते यजमानाय तदर्थ० विश्वानि सुदिनानि शोभनानि दिनानि रायो
> धनानि द्युम्नानि द्युतिमंति रत्नकनकादीनि दुरो गृहानभि अभिलक्ष्यार्यो यज्ञानां स्वामी त्वं वि द्यौत् । विशेषेण द्योतस्व । केचिदत्र वाक्यभेदमंगीकुर्वते ।
> स्तोत्रं कृतवते यजमानाय विश्वानि सुदिनान्यभ्युदयकारीणि भवंति । रायः ।
> रांति क्षीरादीनीति रायो गोधनानि । द्युम्नानि द्योतमानानि कनकादीनि चास्मे
> भवंति। अर्यः कर्मणामनुष्ठाता स यजमानो दुरो गृहानभिवि द्यौत् । विशेषेण द्योतते ॥ ईवते । ई गत् । क्विप् । तदस्यास्तीति मतुप् । छंदसीर इति
> मतुपो वत्वं । ऐरत् । ईर गत् । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । अर्यः । ऋ गत् ।
> अर्यः स्वामिवैश्ययोरिति यत्पत्ययांतो निपातितः । स्वामिन्यंतोदात्तत्वं ।
> द्यौत् । द्युत दीप्तौ । छांदसे लुजु द्युद्भो लुजीति परस्पॆपदं । बहुलु
> छंदसीत्यडभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yaviṣṭha: youngest; or else, the best mixer of the oblations of the gods. O Agni, the man who sends forth a hymn (गातुं (*gātuṃ*), that which is sung or uttered, a stotra) to you, who are ईवते (*īvate*), one who goes and comes for the sake of bringing welfare, and ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*), great — that man obtains (जानाति (*jānāti*), "gains") your sumati, your favourable and gracious mind. For this yajamāna who has made the praise, you, as arya, lord of the sacrifices, shine forth specially, looking towards his houses (दुरः (*duraḥ*)), upon all fair days, riches (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)) and brilliant treasures (द्युम्नानि (*dyumnāni*)) such as jewels and gold. Some accept here a division of the sentence: for the yajamāna who has made the praise all fair days become prosperous; rāyaḥ are cattle-wealth, so called because they give milk and the like; shining things such as gold become his; and arya, the performer of the rites, that yajamāna, shines specially in his houses.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—O youthful Agni
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- ईवते (*īvate*)—to you, who come to the sacrifice
- ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*)—and are Brahman in essence, addressing you
- गातु (*gātu*)—the hymn
- ऐरत् (*airat*)—recites
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- ते (*te*)—your
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—gracious mind
- जानाति (*jānāti*)—obtains
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for such a yajamāna
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- सुदिनानि (*sudināni*)—pleasant days
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—riches
- द्युम्नानि (*dyumnāni*)—treasures such as jewels
- दुरः अभि (*duraḥ abhi*)—in his house
- अरः (*araḥ*)—you, the lord
- विद्यौत् (*vidyaut*)—cause to shine

### Printed p. 772

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O youthful Agni, the man who recites a hymn addressed to you, who come to the sacrifice and are Brahman in essence, obtains your gracious mind. For such a yajamāna, you, the lord, are to make all wealth, gold and other riches shine in his house.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
He experiences your good favour, youngest (of the gods), who offers praise to you, a Brahman, coming quickly (to bestow felicity) ; to him are all prosperous days and wealth (of cattle) and treasures ; you, as the lord of sacrifice, shine upon his dewelling.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने यः पुमान् नित्येन यावज्जीवं संकल्पितेनाग्निहोत्रादिसाधनभूतेन हविषा त्वा त्वां पिप्रीषिति । प्रीणयितुमिच्छति । यश्चोक्ष्यैः शस्त्रैः प्रीण
> यितुमिच्छति सेत् स एव पुमान् सुभगः शोभनधनः सौभाग्यवान्वा सुदानुः-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, the man who with a constant (नित्येन (*nityena*)) oblation, one resolved upon for as long as he lives and serving as the means of the Agnihotra and the like, wishes to please you, and who wishes to please you with ukthya hymns (उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*), read as śastras) — that very man is to be subhaga, possessed of good wealth or of good fortune, and sudānu, possessed of good giving.

### Printed p. 773

> शोभनदानोपेतश्चास्तु किंच दुरोणे दुरवने कृच्छ्रलभ्ये स्वे स्वकीय आयुषि
> शतवर्षाख्ये जीवने तिष्ठतु । अस्मै यजमानाय विश्वा सर्वाणि सुदिना शोभनानि
> दिनानि भवंतु । अस्य सेष्टिः स यज्ञोऽसत् । फलसाधनसमर्थो भवतु ॥ पिप्रीषति ।
> प्रीञ् तर्पणे । धातोः कर्मण इति सन् । असत् । अस्तेर्लेट्यडागमः । इष्टिः ।
> मंत्रे वृषेत्यादिना क्तिन्नुदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Moreover, in his own life, called duroṇa because hard to obtain, that is, in a life of a hundred years, let him abide. For this yajamāna may all days be fair. His iṣṭi, that sacrifice, is to be asat, that is, capable of yielding its fruit.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- नित्येन (*nityena*)—with the eternal
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—oblation
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- पिप्रीषति (*piprīṣati*)—wishes to satisfy
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*)—gladdens with śastra-mantras
- सः इत् (*saḥ it*)—that man himself
- सुभगः (*subhagaḥ*)—possessed of excellent wealth
- सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*)—an excellent giver
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let him be
- दुरोणे (*duroṇe*)—arduous
- स्वे (*sve*)—his own
- आयुषि (*āyuṣi*)—let him gain a life of a hundred years
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for this yajamāna
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- सुदिना (*sudinā*)—let the days also be auspicious
- सा इष्टिः (*sā iṣṭiḥ*)—his sacrifice
- असत् (*asat*)—let it give good fruit

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the man who wishes to satisfy you for ever with oblation, and who always gladdens you with śastra-mantras — may that same man be possessed of excellent wealth and be an excellent giver, and may he gain his arduous life of a hundred years. May all days be auspicious for this yajamāna. May his sacrifice yield good fruit.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May the liberal man ever be prosperous who propitiates you with constant oblations and praises : may all the days in his arduous life be pros- perous, and may this (his) sacrifice be productive of reward).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उखासंभरणीयेष्टावग्नेः क्षत्रभृतोऽर्चामि त इति याज्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> अर्चामि ते सुमतिं घोष्यर्वागितीदंप्रभृतिकर्मणां । आ. ४-१ । इति ॥
> हॆ अग्ने ते तव सुमतिमनुग्रहकरां शोभनां बुद्धिमर्चामि । पूजयामि ।
> ववाता पुनःपुनस्त्वामभिगच्छंतीयमुच्यमाना गीर्वाग्घोषि घोषयुक्तं
> यथा भवति तथार्वाक् त्वदभिमुखु ते त्वां सं जरतां । स्तौतु । वयमपि
> स्वश्वाः शोभनाश्वोपेताः सुरथाश्च । उपलक्षणमेतत् । पुत्रपौत्रादिभिः सहिताः
> संतस्त्वां मर्जयेम । अलंकुर्याम । परिचरेमेति यावत् । त्वं तु अनु
> द्यूनन्वहमस्मै अस्मासु क्षत्राणि धनानि धारयेः । निधेहि ॥ घोषि । घुष शब्दने ।
> औणादिक इन्। नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । नावाता । वा गतिगंधनयोरित्यस्य यज्लुगंतस्य
> निष्ठायां रूपं । मर्जयेम । मृजू शौचालंकारयोः । ण्यंतस्य लिजु रूपं ।
> वृद्धभावश्चांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This verse is the yājyā of Agni Kṣatrabhṛt in the Ukhāsaṃbharaṇīya oblation (iṣṭi). The sūtra says: अर्चामि ते सुमतिं घोष्यर्वागितीदंप्रभृतिकर्मणां (*arcāmi te sumatiṃ ghoṣyarvāgitīdaṃprabhṛtikarmaṇāṃ*) (Ā. 4-1).

"O Agni, I honour your good mind (sumati), which means your gracious and excellent thought. This speech (gīḥ) that is now uttered, going to you again and again, let it praise you (jaratām) facing you, in such a way that it is full of sound (ghoṣi). We also, having good horses (svaśvāḥ) and good chariots, are meant here as accompanied by sons, grandsons and the rest. We would adorn (marjayema) you, that is, serve you. You, day after day, place (dhārayeḥ) among us the kṣatrāṇi, that is, riches."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—your
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—the gracious mind
- अर्चामि (*arcāmi*)—I worship
- ववाता (*vavātā*)—being recited, praising you again and again
- इयं गीः (*iyaṃ gīḥ*)—this speech
- घोषि (*ghoṣi*)—sounding
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—facing you
- ते (*te*)—you
- सं जरताः (*saṃ jaratāḥ*)—let it praise
- स्वश्वाः (*svaśvāḥ*)—those who have excellent horses
- सुरथाः (*surathāḥ*)—those who are accompanied by sons, grandsons and the rest
- त्वा मर्जयेम (*tvā marjayema*)—we adorn you
- अनु द्यून् (*anu dyūn*)—every day
- अस्मे (*asme*)—among us
- क्षेत्राणि (*kṣetrāṇi*)—riches **NOTE**
- धारयेः (*dhārayeḥ*)—place

### Printed p. 775

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, I worship your gracious mind. May this speech, recited in praise of you again and again, sound out, turn towards you and praise you. Having excellent horses and being accompanied by sons, grandsons and the rest, we adorn you. Grant that we may have wealth every day.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I reverence your good favour, Agni ; may this reiterated and resounding hymn convey due praise to your presence : may we be possessed of good horses and good cars, that we may pay you homage; and daily bestow upon us riches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the iṣṭi called Ukhāsaṃbharaṇa, in the Kṣatrabhṛt homa, this ṛk अर्चामि ते (*arcāmi te*) is to be used as a yājyā mantra. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अर्चामि ते सुमतिं घोष्यर्वागितीदंप्रभृतिकर्मणां (*arcāmi te sumatiṃ ghoṣyarvāgitīdaṃprabhṛtikarmaṇāṃ*) (Ā. 4-1).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आग्ने इह रक्षोहननाख्ये कर्मणि यद्वास्मिल्लोके यः पुरुषो दोषावस्ता रात्रावहनि च दीदिवांसं दीप्यमानं त्वामनु द्यूनन्वहं त्मन् आत्मना
> स्वयमेवोप समीपे भूरि भूयिष्ठं यथा भवति तथा चरेत् । परिचरति । तस्माद्वयमपि जनानां शत्रूणां द्युम्ना द्युम्नानि धनान्यभि तस्थिनांसत्वप्रसादादात्मसात्कुर्वंतोऽत एव क्रीळंतः स्वे स्वे गृहे पुत्रपौत्रादिभिः सह संक्रीडमानास्तथा सुमनसः शोभनमनस्काः संतस्त्वां सपेम । परिचरेम । यद्वा । दोषावस्तरिति संबुद्धिः । दोषाया रात्रिकृतस्य तमसो वस्तराच्छादयितर्निवारयितः ॥
> त्मन् । आत्मनब्दस्य तृतीयायाः सुपां सुलुगिति लुक् । मंत्रेष्याज्यादेरात्मन
> इत्याकारलोपः । दोषावस्तः । द्वंद्वपक्षे कार्तकौजपादयश्चति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । संबुद्धिपक्ष आमंत्रितस्य पादादित्वात् षाष्टिकमाद्युदात्तत्वं । सपेम । षप
> समवाये । लिजु रूपं । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, here, that is, in this rite called the slaying of the rakṣas, or else in this world, whatever man serves you, shining (dīdivāṃsam) by night and by day, every day, of himself (tman, by his own self), near you and abundantly (bhūri), therefore we also serve you. We make our own, through your favour, the dyumnā of the enemies (janānām), that is, their riches. For that very reason we sport (krīḷantaḥ), each in his own house, playing with sons, grandsons and the rest. We are well-minded (sumanasaḥ), of good mind, and so we serve you (sapema)."

Or else: दोषावस्तः (*doṣāvastaḥ*) is a vocative, meaning "O you who cover or ward off (vastar) the darkness (doṣā) caused by night."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इह (*iha*)—in this world
- दोषावस्तः (*doṣāvastaḥ*)—night and day
- दीदिवांसं (*dīdivāṃsaṃ*)—shining
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अनु द्यून् (*anu dyūn*)—every day
- त्मन् (*tman*)—each one, of his own inner impulse
- उप (*upa*)—near you
- भूरि (*bhūri*)—exceedingly
- आ चरेत् (*ā caret*)—let him attend upon
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—of the enemy people
- द्युम्ना (*dyumnā*)—the riches
- अभि तस्थिवांसः (*abhi tasthivāṃsaḥ*)—those who make them their own
- क्रीळंतः (*krīḷaṃtaḥ*)—those who rejoice with sons, grandsons and the rest
- सुमनसः (*sumanasaḥ*)—those whose minds are full of devotion
- त्वा सपेम (*tvā sapema*)—we attend upon you (the Kannada prints पचरिसुत्तेवॆ (*pacarisuttevè*)) **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, in this world may every man, of his own inner impulse, worship and attend upon you, who shine night and day, every day. By your favour we make our own the riches of enemy people, we rejoice with sons, grandsons and the rest, and with devout minds we attend upon you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May every one of his own accord diligently worship you, shining in the (hall) morning and evening, every day : thus, sporting in our dwellings, (enjoying) the wealth of (hostile) man, may we with happy hearts worship you.

> यश्च पुमान् ते तदातिथ्यमतिथियोग्यां पूजामानुषगनुक्रमेण जुजोषत्

> सुपेत्यत्र सहेति योगविभागात्समासः । तिपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । तिजु
> चोदात्तवतीति गतेर्निघातः । आतिथ्यं अतिथिशब्दात्तादर्थ्ये अतिथेर्ञ इति इत्यप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । जुजोषत् । जोषयतेर्लजि बहुलं छंदसीति शपः श्लुः ।
> अडागमः । छंदस्युभयथेति तिप आर्धधातुकत्वाण्णिलोपः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, the man who has good horses (svaśva) and good gold (suhiraṇya), that is, wealth fit for sacrifice, and who comes to you (upayāti) together with a chariot (rathena) laden with wealth (vasumatā), such as grain and the like, going near you in order to attend upon you: of that man you are the protector (trātā), the guardian from all misfortunes. And the man who offers you in due order (ānuṣak) the hospitality (ātithya), the worship fit for a guest, of him you are the friend (sakhā); you are his benefactor by giving him the fruit that befits it."

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- स्वश्वः (*svaśvaḥ*)—one who has excellent horses

- वसुमता (*vasumatā*)—wealth-laden
- रथेन (*rathena*)—together with a chariot

- उपयाति (*upayāti*)—approaches and worships
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that man
- त्राता (*trātā*)—protector
- भवसि (*bhavasi*)—you become
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- ते (*te*)—your
- आतिथ्यं (*ātithyaṃ*)—worship fit for a guest

- जुजोषत् (*jujoṣat*)—offers
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that man
- सखा (*sakhā*)—you are the friend

### Printed p. 778

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the man who has excellent horses and wealth that is an instrument of sacrifice, and who approaches and worships you together with a wealth-laden chariot: you are the protector of that man. The man who offers according to rule the worship due to you as a guest: to that man you are a friend.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You, Agni, are the protector of him who, possessed of good horses and a golden car, approches you with a chariot laden with wealth : you are the friend of him who gratifies you by the due performance of hospitality to you.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Hotṛ, caller of the gods, O Yaviṣṭha, youngest, O Sukratu, of good understanding, O Agni: by the kinship (bandhutā) that has arisen through praises (vacobhiḥ) made with you as their aim, I crush (rujāmi), that is, I break, the great (mahaḥ) rākṣasas. Such a speech, of the nature of praise, has come (anviyāya) to me from my father (pituḥ), the seer Gotama." The text then reads मा नामदेवं मामन्वि (*mā nāmadevaṃ māmanvi*) … **NOTE**, breaking off at the page end. **NOTE**

> नोऽस्मदीयस्यास्य वचसः स्तोत्रात्मकमेतद्वाक्यं चिकिद्दि । जानीहि ॥ चिकिद्दि । कित
> ज्ञाने । चौहोत्यादिकः । लोटि रूपं । होतः । पादादित्वात् षाष्ठिकमाद्युदात्तत्वं । इतरयोस्तु नामंत्रिते समानाधिकरण इति प्रथमस्याविद्यमानवद्भावनिषेधादपादादित्वेन निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sentence continues: अन्वियाय (*anviyāya*), "has come to me". Damūnāḥ means one whose mind is self-controlled, or whose mind is given to giving, or one who destroys enemies. "Such as you are, know (cikiddhi), understand, this speech of ours, this sentence of the nature of praise."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—O caller of the gods to the sacrifice
- यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—O most youthful
- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Agni, who have excellent understanding
- वचोभिः (*vacobhiḥ*)—arisen from the praises addressed to you
- बंधुता (*baṃdhutā*)—by the bond of kinship
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—even the rākṣasas who have great power
- रुजामि (*rujāmi*)—I am able to destroy
- तत् (*tat*)—such a word of praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, caller of the gods to the sacrifice, most youthful, of excellent understanding: through the force of the bond of kinship arisen from the praises addressed to you, I am able to destroy even the rākṣasas of great power. Such a word of praise has come to me from our father, the seer Gotama. You who have the power to destroy enemies, know the nature of this word of praise of ours.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Invoker (of the gods), youngest (of the deities) ; possessed of excellent wisdom, through the alliance (with you produced) by holy texts, which came to me from my father Gotama, I demolish the powerful (demons) : you are the humbler (of foes) ; be cognizant of our praises,

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Amūra" means unconfused, all-knowing; or else, O Agni, of unobstructed course. Sāyaṇa glosses the epithets of the rays as follows. अस्वप्नजः (*asvapnajaḥ*): not sleeping, that is, watchful. तरणयः (*taraṇayaḥ*): of constantly moving nature, rescuers from calamities. सुशेवाः (*suśevāḥ*): very pleasant. अतंद्रासः (*ataṃdrāsaḥ*): without drowsiness, not idle, always active. अवृकाः (*avṛkāḥ*): not harming. अश्रमिष्ठाः (*aśramiṣṭhāḥ*): most untiring. सध्रंचः (*sadhraṃcaḥ*): united with one another. पायवः (*pāyavaḥ*): protectors. Such rays of yours, having settled down at our sacrifice, are to protect us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमूर (*amūra*)—all-knowing
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अस्वप्नजः (*asvapnajaḥ*)—watchful
- तरणयः (*taraṇayaḥ*)—of constant movement
- सुशेवाः (*suśevāḥ*)—bestowing comfort
- आतंद्रासः (*ātaṃdrāsaḥ*)—without idleness
- अवृकाः (*avṛkāḥ*)—free from violence
- अश्रमिष्ठाः (*aśramiṣṭhāḥ*)—free from weariness
- सध्र्यंचः (*sadhryaṃcaḥ*)—united with one another
- पायवः (*pāyavaḥ*)—protecting
- ते तव (*te tava*)—those rays of yours
- निषद्य (*niṣadya*)—having occupied this place of our sacrifice
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पांतु (*pāṃtu*)—let them protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O all-knowing Agni, may those well-known rays of yours, which are watchful, of constant movement, bestowers of comfort, free from idleness, free from violence, free from weariness and united with one another, occupy this place of our sacrifice and protect us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
All-wise Agni, may your protecting (rays), unslumbering, alert, propitious, unslothful, benignant, unwearied co-operating, having taken their place (at this sacrifice), preserve us.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa first gives the traditional story. Bṛhaspati, the younger brother of Ucathya, desired Ucathya's pregnant wife, named Mamatā. When he wished to deposit his seed in her, the child in the womb told him: "Do not pour seed here; I dwell here." Thus addressed, Bṛhaspati, his seed obstructed, cursed the embryo: "Obtain long darkness in the form of congenital blindness." Then Dīrghatamas was born of her, and to remove his blindness he praised Agni and obtained sight. This is what the verse now says. O Agni, those protectors, your rays, looking on him with the thought "this one is blind," protected Māmateya, the son of Mamatā, blind, that is, Dīrghatamas, from misfortune, that is, from the curse of blindness, by giving him eyes. You, all-knowing, protected those rays that had done good deeds such as the giving of sight, taking them to yourself with regard. The accomplishment of their being so taken is now stated: the enemies, even while wishing to injure and overcome this Dīrghatamas, did not overcome him.

- पश्यंतः (*paśyaṃtaḥ*)—looking with a gracious eye
- ते (*te*)—your
- ये (*ye*)—those very rays which
- मामतेयु (*māmateyu*)—the son of Mamatā

- अंधं (*aṃdhaṃ*)—blind Dīrghatamas
- दुरितात् (*duritāt*)—from the sin in the form of a curse
- अरक्षन् (*arakṣan*)—protected
- विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*)—you who are all-knowing
- सुकृतः (*sukṛtaḥ*)—having excellent works
- तान् (*tān*)—those rays

- दिप्संत इत् (*dipsaṃta it*)—even though their purpose was destruction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, those rays of yours, protecting and looking with a gracious eye, protected Dīrghatamas, the son of Mamatā and blind, from the sin in the form of a curse. You, the all-knowing, protect those rays that have excellent works. Even though their purpose was destruction, the enemies could not harm him.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Those your protecting ( rays ), Agni, which, beholding (what had chanced), preserved the blind son of Mamata from misfortune : he, knowing all things, cherished those benevolent ( rays ), and his enemies, intending to destroy him, wrought him no harm.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मामतेयं (*māmateyaṃ*)—Regarding the protection of the son of the woman named Mamatā, the commentator has told a historical story. Mamatā, the wife of the sage named Ucathya, was pregnant. Then Bṛhaspati, the younger brother of Ucathya, saw that woman, was infatuated, became attached to her and had intercourse with her. At the time of the emission of seed, the child who was in the womb said to Bṛhaspati: "O Bṛhaspati, I am now in the womb; therefore do not discharge your seed into this woman's womb." Hearing this, Bṛhaspati became angry with that child in the womb, who had obstructed him at the time of releasing the seed, and pronounced a curse that the child in the womb should be born blind. Therefore the child born of that woman was born blind and became a sage famed by the name Dīrghatamāḥ (since he could not see, it always appeared to him as if it were long darkness, dīrgham tamaḥ). There is the narrative that this sage Dīrghatamāḥ praised Agni and obtained his eyes (sight). That very matter is explained here by the sentence मामतेयं दुरितात् अरक्षन् (*māmateyaṃ duritāt arakṣan*).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Apraṇa" (ahrayāṇa) means of unashamed going; "अप्रयाणोऽह्रीतयान इति यास्कः (*aprayāṇo 'hrītayāna iti yāskaḥ*)" (so Yāska). O such Agni, we, the praisers, being "sadhanya," that is, possessed of equal wealth through your favour, protected by you, may through your guidance (प्रणीती (*praṇītī*)), your impulse and leave, attain वाजान् (*vājān*), foods. O सत्यताते (*satyatāte*): one who extends truth, or one in whom truth is extended. O Satyatāti, destroy the two enemies, near and far, who are the utterers (calumniators) of evils. अनुष्टुया (*anuṣṭuyā*): in due order, do कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*), that is, accomplish what has been set forth in this hymn.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अह्रयाण (*ahrayāṇa*)—O Agni, of unhesitating going
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we, the praisers
- त्वया (*tvayā*)—by your favour
- सधन्यः (*sadhanyaḥ*)—possessed of excellent wealth
- त्वोताः (*tvotāḥ*)—protected by you
- तव (*tava*)—your
- प्रणीती (*praṇītī*)—by favour
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—horses**NOTE**
- आश्याम (*āśyāma*)—we obtain
- सत्यताते (*satyatāte*)—O Agni, who increase truth
- शंसा (*śaṃsā*)—desiring sin
- उभा (*ubhā*)—both kinds of enemies, the distant and the near
- सूदय (*sūdaya*)—destroy
- अनुष्टुया (*anuṣṭuyā*)—in order
- तृणुहि (*tṛṇuhi*)—fulfil the purpose of our prayer

### Printed p. 784

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of unhesitating going, we the praisers, possessed through your favour of excellent wealth and protected by you, obtain horses through your favour. O Agni, who increase truth, whether the enemies who wish us treachery are far away or nearby, destroy them; and fulfil the purpose of our prayer.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, you are freed from shame, by you we are made opulent ; by you we are protected ; may we, through your guidance, attain abundant food: cherisher of truth, destroy both ( sorts of calumniators ), those who are nigh, those who are far off, and in due course fulfil (our desires).
