> येन परस्मैपदं मध्यमपुरुषत्वं च ॥ पूर्वत्र तच्छब्दश्रुतेर्यच्छब्दोऽध्याहार्यः । यस्य द्युस्थानस्य वैश्वानरस्य जबारु जवमानरोहि जरमाणरोहि वा
> चारु दीप्तं मंडलं । जबारु जरमाणरोहीति वा जवमानरोहीति वेति यास्कः ।
> नि. ६.१७ । अग्रे पुरस्तात्पूर्वस्यां दिशि रूपः । आरोपयति स्वात्मनि सस्यादीनि रुबिति
> भूमिरुच्यते । तस्याः सकाशात्ससस्य । लुप्तोपममेतत् । स्वपत इव निश्चलस्य पृश्नेः ।
> द्युनामैतत् स्वः पृश्निरिति द्युलोकादित्ययोः साधारणनामसु पाठात् । ज्योतिरादिभिः स्पृश्यमानस्य द्युलोकस्याधि उपरि चर्मन् चर्मणे चरणाय ॥ चरेराणादिको मनिन् । सुपां सुलुगिति चतुर्था लुक् ॥ आरुपितमारोपितं देवैः ।
> तमश्या इति पूर्वत्रान्वयः !

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Since the word "tat" is heard in the earlier part, "yat" must be supplied: the one whose जबारु (*jabāru*), "swiftly rising" or "rising in old age", is the shining orb. Yāska: जबारु जरमाणरोहीति वा जवमानरोहीति (*jabāru jaramāṇarohīti vā javamānarohīti*) (Ni. 6-17). अग्रे (*agre*) means in front, in the eastern direction. रुपः (*rupaḥ*) is the earth, so called because it carries crops and the like; it is "from" the earth. The comparison is elided: "like one asleep", the motionless पृश्नेः (*pṛśneḥ*). This is a name of heaven, since "svaḥ" and "pṛśni" are read among the names common to heaven and the sun. Above the heaven touched by the lights, चर्मन् (*carman*) means "for moving". आरुपितं (*ārupitaṃ*) is "set up" by the gods. "Tam aśyāḥ" connects with what precedes.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Vaiśvānara
- जबारु (*jabāru*)—swiftly rising
- चारु (*cāru*)—brilliant, the orb
- अग्रे (*agre*)—being in front of the sacrificial fire
- ससस्य (*sasasya*)—motionless
- पृश्नेः (*pṛśneḥ*)—of heaven
- अधि (*adhi*)—in the upper part
- चर्मन् (*carman*)—to move
- रुपः (*rupaḥ*)—from the earth
- आरुपितं (*ārupitaṃ*)—raised up (placed in heaven)
- तमित् (*tamit*)—that very Vaiśvānara
- समानं (*samānaṃ*)—since he is the same to gods, humans and others
- समना (*samanā*)—fit to be offered to him
- पुनती (*punatī*)—purifying all
- धीतिः (*dhītiḥ*)—(our) praise
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—joined with the fitting rite
- स्नव (*snava*)—quickly
- अश्याः (*aśyāḥ*)—may it pervade

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The swiftly rising, brilliant orb of that Vaiśvānara was raised up from the earth, stationed in front of the sacrificial fire, to move in the motionless heaven. That same Vaiśvānara, being the same to gods, humans and all, may our praise, fit to be offered to him and purifying all, joined with the rite suited to it, quickly pervade.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May our (self)-purifying praise, suited to his glory, and accompanied by worship, quickly attain to that omniform (Vaishwanara) whose swift-ascending brilliant (orb) is stationed on the east of the earth, to mount, like the sun, above the immoveable heaven.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मे मदीयास्यास्य वक्ष्यमाणस्य वचसो वाक्यस्य किं प्रवाच्यमस्ति । तथ्यमेवोच्यत इत्यर्थः । किं तद्वच इत्युच्यते । उस्रियाणां । गोनामैतत् । क्षीराद्युत्सावीणीनां गवां संबंधि यत्कीरं वारिवोदकमिन तद्यथा सेकेनाविष्कुर्वंति
> तथाप व्रन् । अपवृण्वंति । दोग्धारो निणिक् । नितरां नेनेक्ति शोधयतीति निणिक्
> क्षीरमुच्यते । तादृक् क्षीरमनेन वैश्वानरेण गुहा गुहायामुप हितमुपनिहितं
> वदंति वेत्तारः । किंचायं वेर्वाप्ताया रुपो भूम्याः प्रियं सर्वेषामाधारत्वेन प्रियभूतमग्रं श्रेष्ठं पदं स्थानं पाति । रक्षति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"What is there to be said (प्रवाच्यं (*pravācyaṃ*)) of this word of mine that is to be spoken?" That is, only the truth is spoken. What is that word? उस्रियाणां (*usriyāṇāṃ*) is a name for cows. The milk of the cows that yield milk and so on, as people draw water, so they uncover it by milking (अप व्रन् (*apa vran*)). निणिक् (*niṇik*) is milk, since it cleanses thoroughly. The knowers say that such milk is placed in the cave (गुहा (*guhā*)) by this Vaiśvānara. Further, he protects the dear, foremost place of the earth, which is pervaded (वेः (*veḥ*)), dear as the support of all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उस्रियाणां (*usriyāṇāṃ*)—of the cows
- यत् (*yat*)—which milk (the milkers)
- वारिव (*vāriva*)—like water
- अप व्रन् (*apa vran*)—obtained
- निणिक् (*niṇik*)—that same milk
- गुहा (*guhā*)—in a cave
- उप हितं (*upa hitaṃ*)—as placed
- वदंति (*vadaṃti*)—the wise say (and that the same milk)
- वेः (*veḥ*)—of the pervading
- रुपः (*rupaḥ*)—to the earth

- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—excellent
- पदं (*padaṃ*)—place

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The knowers say that the milk of the cows, which the milkers obtained like water, Vaiśvānara has placed in a cave, and that this same milk protects the dear and excellent place of the all-pervading earth.

> रघुयत् शीघ्रं गच्छत्सूर्यमंडलं विवेद । वैश्वानरमेवेति ज्ञातवानस्मि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

इदमु (*idamu*): this very, that well-known great, worshipful *anīkaṃ* of the great gods, of the form of a multitude, the solar orb, is Vaiśvānara himself (so the sense is completed). पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*) is "belonging to former times" or "fulfilling". The orb which the milk-yielding cow (उस्रिया (*usriyā*)) serves for the agnihotra and the like. ऋतस्य पदे (*ṛtasya pade*): in the place of water, the atmosphere; अधि (*adhi*) is "exceedingly"; or else अधि (*adhi*) restates the sense of the locative. दीद्यानं (*dīdyānaṃ*) is shining; गुहा (*guhā*) in a cave; रघुष्यत् (*raghuṣyat*) flowing swiftly; रघुयत् (*raghuyat*) moving swiftly: that solar orb "I have known" (विवेद (*viveda*)) to be Vaiśvānara himself.

- गौः (*gauḥ*)—cows
- सचित (*sacita*)—serve, and
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water

- इदमु (*idamu*)—this Vaiśvānara fire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have known the ancient solar orb which the milk-yielding cows serve, which shines exceedingly in the atmosphere, the place of water, hidden in a cave, spreading swiftly and moving fast. Which is it? That well-known, great solar orb, of the form of a multitude of the great gods, is this Vaiśvānara fire.

I recognize this adorable assemblage of the great (deities), which from of old the milk-shedding cow affects, shining above the region of the water, (the firmament), in secret ; swift-gliding, swift-moving.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अध (*adha*) is "then". Shining, pervading together (सचा (*sacā*)) the middle between the two parents, heaven and earth, he, being so, desired (अमनुत (*amanuta*): awoke, to drink) with his own mouth (आसा (*āsā*)) the lovely milk of the cow (पृश्नेः (*pṛśneḥ*)) hidden in the udder. (The block breaks off here; it continues on the next page.)

> क्षीरादिनिर्मात्रा गोः परमे पद उत्कृष्टे स्थान ऊधोलक्षणेऽंति सत् समीपे
> विद्यमानं क्षीरं वृष्णः फलानां वर्षितुः शोचिषो दीप्तस्य प्रयतस्याहवनीयादिरूपेण नियतस्य वैश्वानरस्य जिह्वा पातुमिच्छतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing.) He is awakened to drink. He then explains the same sense: of the mother (मातुः (*mātuḥ*)), the cow that makes milk and the like, in her excellent place (परमे पदे (*parame pade*)), the udder, the milk existing close by (अंति सत् (*aṃti sat*)): the tongue of Vaiśvānara, the showerer (वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)) of fruits, the radiant (शोचिषः (*śociṣaḥ*)), the one regulated (प्रयतस्य (*prayatasya*)) in the forms of āhavanīya and the like, desires to drink — this is what is understood to complete the sentence.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध (*adha*)—afterwards
- द्युतानः (*dyutānaḥ*)—shining
- पित्रोः सचा (*pitroḥ sacā*)—Vaiśvānara, who is joined with heaven and earth
- पृश्नेः (*pṛśneḥ*)—of the cow
- चारु (*cāru*)—lovely
- गुह्यं (*guhyaṃ*)—hidden in the udder, the milk
- आसा (*āsā*)—with his mouth
- अमनुत (*amanuta*)—desired to drink
- मातुः (*mātuḥ*)—of the milk-giving
- गोः (*goḥ*)—cow
- परमे पदे (*parame pade*)—in the excellent udder
- अंति सत् (*aṃti sat*)—the milk that remains hidden
- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—of the one who showers desires
- शोचिषः (*śociṣaḥ*)—shining
- प्रयतस्य (*prayatasya*)—regulated in the forms of āhavanīya and the like, of Vaiśvānara
- जिह्वा (*jihvā*)—the tongue (desires to drink)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vaiśvānara, shining and joined with heaven and earth, desired to drink with his mouth the cow's lovely milk hidden in the udder. The tongue of Vaiśvānara fire, the showerer of desires, shining, regulated in the forms of āhavanīya and the like, desires to drink the milk that remains hidden in the excellent udder of the milk-giving cow.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Then, radiant in association with the parents, (heaven and earth), he isa wakened (to drink) the agreeable secretion of the cow, and the tongue of the assiduous (performer of holy rites), the resplendent showerer of benefits,) approaching the excellent station of the maternal (cow ), seeks to drink the milk.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहं यजमानो नमसा नमस्कारेण सह पृच्छ्यमानोऽनैरनुयुज्यमानः सन् ऋतं वोचे । सत्यं ब्रवीमि । किं तदित्युच्यते । हे जातवेदो जातानां
> वेदितर्जातप्रज्ञ वाग्ने तवाशसा त्वत्सुत्या साधनेन यदीदं धनं लब्धमस्माभिः
> स्यात् अस्य धनस्य त्वं क्षयसि । त्वमेवेश्वरो भवसि । तस्य धनस्य यज्ञादिद्वाराग्न्यर्थत्वादिति भावः । अत्यल्पमिदमुक्तं । यद्ध विश्वं यत्पलु कृत्स्नं धनमस्ति
> तस्यापीशिषे । विश्वमिति सामान्येन यदुक्तं तदेव विशदयति । दिवि द्युलोके
> यदु द्रविणं यदेव धनं यच्च पृथिव्यां धनं तस्य सर्वस्य त्वमीश्वरो भवसि ।
> यज्ञार्थं द्रव्यमुत्पन्नमिति स्मरणात् । अग्नि व्यतिरेकेण यज्ञा संभवादिति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: I, the sacrificer, being questioned by others, speak the truth ऋतं वोचे (*ṛtaṃ voce*), together with homage. What that is, is now stated. "O Jātavedas, knower of what is born, O Agni, by your āśas, that is, by the means of your praise, whatever wealth may have been obtained by us, of this wealth you are lord; you alone are its master, because by way of sacrifice and the like that wealth is for Agni." Even this is said to be very little: whatever whole wealth there is, of that too you are master. What was said in general by "viśvam" he now makes clear: whatever wealth is in heaven, and whatever wealth is on earth, of all that you are lord. He grounds this in the tradition that wealth was produced for the sake of sacrifice; without Agni no sacrifice is possible, such is the sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नमसा (*namasā*)—with homage
- पृच्छ्यमानः (*pṛcchyamānaḥ*)—I (the sacrificer), who am questioned
- ऋतं वोचे (*ṛtaṃ voce*)—I declare this answer which is the truth (namely)
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Jātavedas
- तव आशसा (*tava āśasā*)—obtained by the means of your praise
- यदि इदं (*yadi idaṃ*)—whatever this wealth is
- अस्य (*asya*)—of it
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- क्षयसि (*kṣayasi*)—are lord
- यत् ह विश्वं (*yat ha viśvaṃ*)—in the whole world
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the heavenly world
- यत् उ द्रविणं (*yat u draviṇaṃ*)—whatever wealth there is
- यत् पृथिव्यां (*yat pṛthivyāṃ*)—whatever wealth there is on the earth (of all that you alone are master)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, the sacrificer, who am questioned with homage, declare this answer which is the truth. It is this: O Jātavedas, of this wealth obtained by the means of your praise, and also of all the wealth spread through the heavenly world and the earthly world, you alone are the master.

### Printed p. 820

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Interrogated with respect, I declare the truth, that this (wealth is acquired), Jatavedas, by the praise of you : you rule over it, (over) all that (it may be), the wealth that is in heaven or on earth.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वमंत्रेण यस्य धनस्याग्निस्वामित्वमुक्तमस्य धनस्य किं द्रविणं किं साधनभूतं नोऽस्मभ्यं दातव्यं धनमस्ति । कद्ध रत्नं किंच रमणीयं हितकरं धनमस्ति ।
> तद्धनं हे जातवेदो जातधनाग्ने चिकित्वांश्चेतनानावानभिज्ञस्त्वं नोऽस्मभ्यं वि
> वोचः । विब्रूहि । यद्वा । किं दातव्यं द्रविणमस्ति । अस्य द्रविणराशेः कद्ध रत्नमिति
> योज्यं । अस्याध्वनो धनप्राप्तिमार्गस्य यद्दुहा गुहायां निहितं गूढं परममुत्कृष्टं प्राप्तव्यमस्ति तदपि नोऽस्मभ्यं विवोचः । वयं रेकु रिक्तं पदं गंतव्यं
> स्थानं गृहादिकं निदाना अन्नैर्निंद्यमानाः ॥ कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ नागन्म । न
> प्राप्पुमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: of the wealth over which Agni's lordship was stated in the previous mantra, what is the dravinam, what wealth, as a means, is to be given to us? And what ratna, what pleasing and beneficial wealth, is there? That wealth, O Jātavedas, Agni who knows what is born, you who are cikitvān, endowed with understanding and knowing, declare to us (vi vocaḥ, "explain"). Or else: what dravinam is there to be given? The phrase कद्ध रत्नं (*kaddha ratnaṃ*) is to be connected with "of this heap of wealth". Whatever in this path (adhvan) of the attainment of wealth lies hidden in a cave, is supreme and excellent and is to be reached, that too declare to us. May we not go to an empty (rekku, rikta) place, a house and the like that is to be gone to, being reproached (nidānāḥ) by others; that is नागन्म (*nāganma*), "we do not reach".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—to that wealth (of which Agni is the lord)
- किं द्रविणं (*kiṃ draviṇaṃ*)—what is the value?
- नः (*naḥ*)—of this wealth of ours
- कद्द रत्नं (*kadda ratnaṃ*)—what is the chief use? (in what way is it beneficial?)

### Printed p. 821
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O all-knowing Agni
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—you who know everything
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- वि वोचः (*vi vocaḥ*)—explain clearly
- अस्य अध्वनः (*asya adhvanaḥ*)—of this path of the attainment of wealth
- यत् गुहा (*yat guhā*)—what is hidden
- परमं (*paramaṃ*)—and the most excellent place
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us (make known)
- रेकु (*reku*)—empty
- पदं (*padaṃ*)—place
- निदानाः (*nidānāḥ*)—reproached (by others)
- न अगन्म (*na aganma*)—may we not reach it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

What is the value of the wealth of which Agni is the lord? In what way is this wealth beneficial? O all-knowing Agni, you who know everything, explain it clearly to us. Make known to us the hidden and most excellent place on the path of the attainment of wealth, and may we, reproached by others, not reach an empty place.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
What is the value of this (wealth) to us? what's its advantage? Inform us, Jatavedas, for you know ; (tell us) what is the best (course) for us on this secret path, so that we may follow unreproached the direct road.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> का म॒र्यादा॑ व॒युना॒ कद्ध॑ वा॒ममच्छा॑ गमेम र॒घवो॒  ॑
> न वाजं।  
> क॒दा नो॑ दे॒वीर॒मृत॑स्य॒ पत्निः॒ सूरो॒ वर्णे॑न ततनन्नु॒षासः॑॥

> *kā maryādā vayunā kaddha vāmamacchā gamema raghavo*  
> *na vājaṃ|*  
> *kadā no devīramṛtasya patniḥ sūro varṇena tatanannuṣāsaḥ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> का । मर्यादा । वयुना । कत् । ह । वामं । अच्छ । गमेम । रघवः । न । वाजं।  
> कदा । नः । देवीः । अमृतस्य । पत्निः । सूरः । वर्णेन । ततनन् । उषसः ॥ १३ ॥

> *kā | maryādā | vayunā | kat | ha | vāmaṃ | accha | gamema | raghavaḥ | na | vājaṃ|*  
> *kadā | naḥ | devīḥ | amṛtasya | patniḥ | sūraḥ | varṇena | tatanan | uṣasaḥ ‖ 13 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> का मर्यादा का प्रीत्यादिव्यवस्था का च वयुना प्रज्ञानं पदार्थविषयं
> कद्ध किं च नामं वननीयं पदार्थजातं । एतत्सर्वमच्छ गमेम । अभिगच्छेम ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: what is the marygādā, what is the arrangement (vyavasthā) of affection and the like; and what is vayunā, knowledge concerning things; and what class of desirable things (vāmam) is there? All this may we approach (acchā gameṃma, "may we go up to").

### Printed p. 822

> तत्र दृष्टांतः । रघवो न वाजं ! शीघ्रगामिनोऽश्वादयः संग्राममिव तद्वत् ।
> कदा कस्मिन्काले नोऽस्माकं व्यवहाराय देवीर्देव्यो द्योतमाना अमृतस्यामरणधर्मस्यादित्यस्य षत्नीः पत्नीः पालयित्र्यः सूरः प्रसवित्र्य उषासो वर्णेन
> प्रकाशेन ततनन् । विस्तारयेयुः । एवं सूर्यसंबंधिन उषसः स्तुत्या सर्वात्मनो वैश्वानरस्य स्तुतिरवगंतव्या ॥ तनोतेर्लेटि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः ।
> द्विर्भावहलादिशेषौ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: the illustration is रघवो न वाजं (*raghavo na vājaṃ*): as swift-going horses and the like go to battle. When, at what time, for our dealings, would the shining (devīḥ) dawns, the wives (patnīḥ, "protectresses") of the immortal Āditya, who is of deathless nature, the sūraḥ ("bringers-forth"), spread (tatanan) with varṇa, that is, with radiance? Thus, by this praise of the dawns connected with the sun, the praise of Vaiśvānara, the self of all, is to be understood.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—for battle
- रघवो न (*raghavo na*)—like swift-going horses
- अच्छ (*accha*)—towards our desired region
- गमेम (*gamema*)—(the region) to which we go
- मर्यादा (*maryādā*)—the limit (of it)
- का (*kā*)—what is it?
- वयुना (*vayunā*)—the object that becomes perceptible to our knowledge there
- कद्द (*kadda*)—what indeed is there?
- वामं (*vāmaṃ*)—what is its use?
- कदा (*kadā*)—when
- नः (*naḥ*)—for our dealings
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—the shining
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—of the deathless Āditya
- पत्नीः (*patnīḥ*)—the wives
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—who bring forth the world
- उषासः (*uṣāsaḥ*)—the dawn goddesses
- वर्णेन (*varṇena*)—with their splendours
- ततनन् (*tatanan*)—will light up the world

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like swift-going horses that run for battle, we go towards our desired region: what is the limit of that region? What object that becomes perceptible to our knowledge is there, and what is its use? When will the dawn goddesses, shining for our dealings, wives of the deathless Āditya and bringers-forth of the world, light up the world with their splendours?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
What is the limit, what are the objects, which is the desirable (end) to which we rush like swift (chargers) to the battle? when for us will the divine dawns, the brides of the immortal (sun), overspread (the world) with light.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒नि॒रेण॒ वच॑सा फ॒ल्गॆ॑न प्र॒तीत्ये॑न कृ॒धुना॑तृ॒पासः॑ ।  
> ( धा॒ ते अ॑ग्ने॒ किमि॒हा व॑दंत्यनायु॒धास॒ आस॑ता सचंतां ॥

> *anireṇa vacasā phalgèna pratītyena kṛdhunātṛpāsaḥ |*  
> *( dhā te agne kimihā vadaṃtyanāyudhāsa āsatā sacaṃtāṃ ‖*

### Printed p. 823

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अनिरेण । वचसा । फल्ग्येन । प्रतीत्येन । कृधुना । अतृपासः ।  
> अध । ते । अग्ने । किं । इह । वदंति । अनायुधासः । असता सचंतां ॥ १४ ॥

> *anireṇa | vacasā | phalgyena | pratītyena | kṛdhunā | atṛpāsaḥ |*  
> *adha | te | agne | kiṃ | iha | vadaṃti | anāyudhāsaḥ | asatā sacaṃtāṃ ‖ 14 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनिरेण । इरान्नं । तद्रहितेन फल्गनोक्केन प्रतीत्येन प्रतिगंतव्येन ।
> आरोह्येणेत्यर्थः । कृधुना ह्रस्वेन । कृद्विति ह्रस्वनाम कृधुको वम्रक इति तन्नामसूक्तत्वात् । एवंविधेन वचसातृपासोऽतृप्ता जनाः । अध अधुनेहास्मिन् लोके
> हे अग्ने ते त्वां किं वदंति । निर्हविष्केण वचसा न किंचिल्लभ्यत इत्यर्थः। किंत्वनायुधासः। आयुधशब्दः साधनं लक्षयति। हविरादिसाधनरहितास्तेऽसता दुःखेन सचंतां।
> संगच्छंतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: anirena: ira is food; by speech devoid of it; phalguna **NOTE**; pratītyena, "to be approached", that is, "to be climbed" (ārohya); kṛdhunā, "short": kṛdhu is a name for "short", as the lists of its names show (कृधुको वम्रक इति (*kṛdhuko vamraka iti*)). By speech of such kind, unsatisfied (atṛpāsaḥ) people, now (adha) here in this world, O Agni, what do they say to you? By speech without oblation nothing is obtained, that is the sense. But anāyudhāsaḥ: the word āyudha stands for a means; those devoid of means such as oblations, let them meet with asat, that is, with suffering (sacantām, "let them come together").

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अनिरेण (*anireṇa*)—devoid of food
- फल्गेन (*phalgena*)—worthless
- प्रतीत्येन (*pratītyena*)—devoid of what is defined **NOTE**
- कृधुना (*kṛdhunā*)—very short
- वचसा (*vacasā*)—with speech
- अतृपासः (*atṛpāsaḥ*)—unsatisfied
- अध (*adha*)—now
- इह (*iha*)—in this place of sacrifice
- ते (*te*)—addressing you
- किं वदंति (*kiṃ vadaṃti*)—what indeed can they say?
- अनायुधासः (*anāyudhāsaḥ*)—they who are devoid of the means in the form of oblation
- असता (*asatā*)—with suffering
- सचंतां (*sacaṃtāṃ*)—let them be joined

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, unsatisfied by speech that is devoid of food, worthless, devoid of what is defined, and very short, what indeed can they now say here in this place of sacrifice, addressing you? Devoid of the means in the form of oblation, let them be filled with suffering.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
(Men are) not satisfied by unproductive, frivolous, inconclusive, scanty speech; then what, Agni, do they here say to you? devoid of the implements (of worship), let them suffer from distress

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रुशत् । वसानः । सुदृशीकरूपः । क्षितिः । न । राया । पुरुवारः । अद्यात् ॥ १५ ॥

> *asya | śriye | saṃidhānasya | vṛṣṇaḥ | vasoḥ| anekaṃ | dame | ā | ruroca |*  
> *ruśat | vasānaḥ | sudṛśīkarūpaḥ | kṣitiḥ | na | rāyā | puruvāraḥ | adyāt ‖ 15 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समिधानस्य समिध्यमानस्य ॥ कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ वृष्णो वर्षितुः फलस्य
> वसोऽर्वासयितुरस्याग्नेरनीकं तेजःसंघो दमे यागगृह आ रुरोच । सर्वतो
> दीप्यते । किमर्थं । श्रिये श्रेयसे यजमानानां । सोऽग्नि रुशत् । वर्णनामैतत् । दीप्तं तेजो वसान आच्छादयन् अत एव सुदृशीकरूपः सुष्टु दर्शनीयरूपः पुरुवारो बहुभिऋत्विग्भिर्यजमानैर्वर्णनीयः सन्नद्यौत् । द्योतते ।
> किमिव । रायाश्वादिधनेन क्षितिर्न राजादिरिव । क्षितिरिति मनुष्यनाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: of the one being kindled (samidhānasya, "kindled"), of the vṛṣṇaḥ, the showerer of fruit, of vasoḥ, the one who causes dwellings, of this Agni the anīkam, the mass of radiance, has shone all round (ā ruroca) in the dama, the house of sacrifice. For what purpose? श्रिये (*śriye*), for the welfare of the sacrificers. That Agni is ruśat (this is a name for colour), clothing himself, covering himself, in bright radiance; hence he is sudṛśīkarūpaḥ, of beautiful form; and puruvāraḥ, to be chosen by many priests and sacrificers; he shone (adyaut, "shines"). Like what? Like a kṣiti, a king or the like with rāyā, wealth such as horses. Kṣiti is a name for man.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समिधानस्य (*samidhānasya*)—who is kindled by fuel-sticks
- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—who showers desires
- वसोः (*vasoḥ*)—who provides dwellings
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- अनेकं (*anekaṃ*)—the mass of radiances **NOTE**
- दमे (*dame*)—in this house of sacrifice
- श्रिये (*śriye*)—for the welfare (of the sacrificer)
- आ रुरोच (*ā ruroca*)—shines all round
- रुशत् (*ruśat*)—bright radiance
- वसानः (*vasānaḥ*)—who wears
- सुदृशीकरूपः (*sudṛśīkarūpaḥ*)—who has a beautiful form
- पुरुवारः (*puruvāraḥ*)—who is worshipped by many
- राया (*rāyā*)—who shines with wealth
- क्षितिर्न (*kṣitirna*)—like a king
- अद्यात् (*adyāt*)—he shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The mass of radiances of Agni, who is kindled by fuel-sticks, who showers desires and provides dwellings, shines all round in this house of sacrifice for the welfare of the sacrificer. Agni, who wears bright radiance, has a beautiful form and is worshipped by many, shines like a king who shines with wealth.

### Printed p. 825

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
For the prosperity of this ( institutor of the rite ), the host (of the flames) of the kindled (Agni), the showerer (of benefits), the giver of dwell-ings, has blazed in the hall (of sacrifice); clothed in radiance, beatiful in semblance, and glorified by many, he shines like a man with opulence.

## Sūkta 6 (Maṇḍala 4)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु ण इत्येकादशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं वामदेवस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमाग्नेयं । ऊर्ध्व ऊ श्वेकादशेत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाशिनशस्त्रयोराग्नेये क्रत्ौ त्रैष्टुभे छंदसीदं । सूत्रितं च । ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु णः ससस्य यद्वियुतेति पंच । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: the sixth sūkta, of eleven Ṛks, beginning ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु णः (*ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇaḥ*), has Vāmadeva as seer, Agni as deity and Triṣṭubh as metre. The Anukramaṇī says "ūrdhva ū ekādaśa". Its use is in the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra, in the Āgneya Kratu, for the verses in Triṣṭubh metre. It is stated in the sūtra: ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु णः ससस्य यद्वियुतेति पंच (*ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇaḥ sasasya yadviyuteti paṃca*) (Ā. 4-13).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "Ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇaḥ" is the sixth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. Vāmadeva is the seer of this sūkta; Agni is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says "Ūrdhva ū" for it. It is explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta sūtra (Ā. 4-13) "Ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇaḥ, sasasya yad viyuta, these five": the sūkta is applied, at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra mantras, for the Ṛks in Triṣṭubh metre among the mantras connected with the Āgneya Kratu.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta: 6
- Maṇḍala: 4; Anuvāka: 1; Sūkta: 6
- Aṣṭaka: 3; Adhyāya: 5; Varga: 4, 5
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 11
- Ṛṣi: Vāmadeva
- Devatā: Agni
- Chandas: Triṣṭubh

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वरस्य होतर्यागसंबंधिनां देवानामाह्वातः । यद्वा । होतरित्यत्र
> प्रकृत्यंशोऽनुवादः । हे होमनिष्पादकाग्ने यजीयान्यष्टृतमस्तुं नोऽस्माकमूर्ध्व ऊ पु तिष्ठ । उन्नत एव तिष्ठ । नित्यमुन्नतो भवेत्यर्थः । कुत्रेति तदुच्यते । देवताता देवतात् । देवास्तायंते विस्तीर्यंतेऽत्रेति देवतातिर्यज्ञः ।
> तस्मिन् । त्वं हि त्वं खलु विश्वं सर्वं मन्म मननीयं शत्रूणां धनमभ्यसि । अभिभवसि।
> किंच वेधसश्चित् । चित्तूजायां । स्तोतुर्यजमानादेर्मनीषां मतिं स्तुतिं प्र
> तिरसि । प्रवर्धयसि । प्रपूर्वस्ति रतिर्वर्धनार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Hotṛ of the sacrifice": the summoner of the gods connected with the rite. Or else, in होतः (*hotaḥ*) the stem part is only a restatement. O Agni, accomplisher of the oblation, most excellent worshipper, stand erect for us, stand up high; that is, be ever exalted. Where? देवताता (*devatātā*) means देवताता (*devatātā*), in the sacrifice. The sacrifice is called देवतातिं (*devatātiṃ*) because the gods are spread out, extended, in it. In it you indeed overcome all that is to be thought on (मन्म (*manma*)), the wealth of enemies. Further, you promote the thought (मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)), the praise, of the wise (वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*)) praiser, the sacrificer and others; प्र तिरसि (*pra tirasi*) means "you make it grow", the root तिर (*tira*) with प्र (*pra*) having the sense of increase. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—of the sacrifice
- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—O Hotṛ
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—you, the most worshipful
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)—being above
- ऊ षु तिष्ठ (*ū ṣu tiṣṭha*)—occupy the high place
- देवताता (*devatātā*)—in this sacrifice that worships the gods
- त्वं हि (*tvaṃ hi*)—you alone
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—all
- मन्म (*manma*)—and what is to be thought on, the wealth
- अभि असि (*abhi asi*)—you are able to obtain and give
- वेधसः चित् (*vedhasaḥ cit*)—even though the sacrificer is wise
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—his praise also
- प्र तिरसि (*pra tirasi*)—you cause it to grow abundantly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, Hotṛ of the sacrifice, you, the most worshipful, be above us and occupy the high place; in the sacrifice that worships the gods you alone can obtain and give all that is to be thought on, the wealth.

### Printed p. 827
You can make the praise of the wise sacrificer grow as well.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, ministrant of the sacrifice, you are entitled to worship ; be above us in this offering to the gods; for you prevail over all that is desirable ; you inspire the praise of the worshipper.

> प्रचे॑ताः ।  
> ऊ॒र्ध्वं भा॒नुं स॑वि॒तेवा॑श्रे॒न्मेते॑व धू॒मं स्त॑भाय॒दुप॒  
> द्यां ॥ २ ॥

> *amūro hotā nyasādi vikṣugnirmaṃdro vidatheṣu*  
> *pracetāḥ |*  
> *ūrdhvaṃ bhānuṃ savitevāśrenmeteva dhūmaṃ stabhāyadupa*

> *amūraḥ | hotā | ni | asādi | vikṣu | agniḥ | maṃdraḥ | vidatheṣu | pracetāḥ ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमूरोऽमूढः । प्रगल्भ इत्यर्थः । होता होमनिष्पादको मंद्रो
> मदनीयो मादयिता वा प्रचेताः प्रकृष्टज्ञानोऽग्निर्देवो विक्षृतिग्रूपासु
> प्रजासु मध्यॆ विदथेषु यागेषु निमित्तभूतेषु न्यसादि । नितरां स्थापितः । अथ
> तथाभूतोऽग्निर्भानुं दीप्तिं सवितेवोदितः सूर्य इवोर्र्ध्वमश्रेत् । ऊर्ध्वमुखमाश्रयति । किंच मेतेव स्कूणेव । सा यथा स्वाधिष्ठितं वंशादिकं स्तभ्नाति
> तद्वयमुग्निर्धूमं स्वोत्थितं द्यामुप द्युलोकस्योपरि स्तभायत् । स्तभ्नाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अमूरः (*amūraḥ*) is "undeluded", that is, bold. Agni, the god, the accomplisher of the oblation (होता (*hotā*)), delightful or delighting (मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*)), of excellent knowledge (प्रचेताः (*pracetāḥ*)), has been firmly set down among the people (विक्षु (*vikṣu*), the subjects) at the sacrifices (विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)) that are the occasion. Then, being such, Agni, like the risen sun, has raised his radiance (भानुं (*bhānuṃ*)) upward; he betakes himself upward. And like a post (मेता (*metā*)): as a post props bamboo and the like that is set upon it, so Agni props his own risen smoke above heaven, above the world of heaven.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमूरः (*amūraḥ*)—the discerning
- होता (*hotā*)—the accomplisher of the oblation
- मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*)—the attractive
- प्रचेताः (*pracetāḥ*)—and the one of excellent knowledge
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—in the midst of us, the priests

### Printed p. 828
- विदधेषु (*vidadheṣu*)—in the sacrificial house (for the sake of the sacrifice)
- न्यसादि (*nyasādi*)—has been established
- भानुं (*bhānuṃ*)—his light
- सवितेव (*saviteva*)—like the risen sun
- ऊर्ध्वं (*ūrdhvaṃ*)—upward
- अश्रेत् (*aśret*)—he has made to spread
- मेतेव (मेता इव) (*meteva (metā iva)*)—like a pillar
- धूमं (*dhūmaṃ*)—his mass of smoke
- द्यां उप (*dyāṃ upa*)—in the upper part of the atmosphere
- स्तभायत् (*stabhāyat*)—he has made to stand

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the discerning, the accomplisher of the oblation, the attractive, the one of excellent knowledge, has been established among us priests in the sacrificial house for the sake of the sacrifice. Like the risen sun he has made his light spread upward. He has made his mass of smoke stand like a pillar in the upper part of the atmosphere.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The unperplexed, the sagacious, exhilarating Agni, the ministrant priest, has been placed amongst men for ( the celebration of ) sacrifices : like the sun, he spreads light above, and props the smoke above the sky like a pillar.
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒ता सु॑जू॒र्णी रा॒तिनी॑ घृ॒ताची॑ प्रदक्षि॒णिद्दे॒वता॑तिमुरा॒णः।  
> उदु॒ स्वरु॑र्नव॒जा नाक्रः प॒श्वो अ॑नक्ति॒ सुधि॑तः सु॒मेकः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

> *yatā sujūrṇī rātinī ghṛtācī pradakṣiṇiddevatātimurāṇaḥ|*  
> *udu svarurnavajā nākraḥ paśvo anakti sudhitaḥ sumekaḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यता । सुजूर्णिः । रातिनी । घृताची । प्रदक्षिणित् । देवतातिं । उराणः ॥  
> उत् । ऊं इति । स्वरुः । नवजाः । न । अक्रः । पश्वः । अनक्ति । सुधितः । सुमेकः ॥

> *yatā | sujūrṇiḥ | rātinī | ghṛtācī | pradakṣiṇit | devatātiṃ | urāṇaḥ ‖*  
> *ut | ūṃ iti | svaruḥ | navajāḥ | na | akraḥ | paśvaḥ | anakti | sudhitaḥ | sumekaḥ ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यता संयता सुजूर्णिः शोभनजवा सुष्टु जीर्णा पुराणी वा । धृताची
> धृतमंचतीति धृताची जुहूः । रातिनी । रातिर्धनं । हविर्लक्षणधनवती । आज्यपूर्णा
> भवतीत्यर्थः । देवतातिं यज्ञं तथोराण उरु कुर्वाणोऽध्वर्युरग्निर्वा प्रद-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

यता (*yatā*) is "restrained"; सुजूर्णिः (*sujūrṇiḥ*) is "of fine speed", or "well worn", that is, old. धृताची (*dhṛtācī*): she that goes to (carries) ghee, the Juhū ladle. रातिनी (*rātinī*): *rātiḥ* is wealth; possessing the wealth that consists of the oblation, that is, she is full of ghee. The sacrifice (देवतातिं (*devatātiṃ*)) likewise the Adhvaryu, or Agni, making it wide (उराणः (*urāṇaḥ*)), goes round with the right side (प्रदक्षिणित् (*pradakṣiṇit*));

### Printed p. 829

> क्षिणित् । प्रदक्षिणमेतीति प्रदक्षिणित् । प्रदक्षिणगमनो भवति ॥ अकारलोपश्रांदसः॥
> नवजा नवजातस्तदानीमेवोत्पादितः स्वरुर्न । यूपशकलवाची स्परुरत्र यूपं
> लक्षयति । चषालवंतः स्वरवः पृथिव्यां । ऋग्वे. ३-८-१० । इत्यादिषु स्वरुशब्देन
> यूपाभिधानाच्च । नकारः समुच्चये । यूपोऽप्युदु उपसर्गश्रुतेयोग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । उन्नतो भवति । किंच अक्र आक्रमिता । सुमेकः सुदीप्तः सुधितः
> स्वधितिरित्यर्थः । सोऽपि पश्वः पशूननक्ति । गच्छति । यद्वा । सुधितः स्वरुरेवोदु
> उत्कृष्टः पश्वः पशूननक्ति । स्वरुणा पशुमनक्तीति श्रुतेः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

प्रदक्षिणित् (*pradakṣiṇit*) is one who goes keeping the right side toward it; the loss of the vowel a is Vedic. नवजा (*navajā*): newly born, produced just then, like a स्वरुः (*svaruḥ*). The word स्वरु (*svaru*) denotes a splinter of the sacrificial post and here points to the post, since in passages such as "the posts with their knobs on the earth" (Ṛgve. 3-8-10) the post is named by the word स्वरु (*svaru*). The particle न (*na*) is in the sense of conjunction: the post too stands up; the verb is to be supplied from the preposition उदु (*udu*) heard in the text, so that it means "becomes raised". Further, अक्रः (*akraḥ*) is the one that assails. सुमेकः (*sumekaḥ*) is well-shining; सुधितः (*sudhitaḥ*) is the axe (*svadhitiḥ*). It too goes (अनक्ति (*anakti*)) to the animals (पश्वः (*paśvaḥ*)). Or else: the post (स्वरुः (*svaruḥ*)) itself, well placed, is excellent (उदु (*udu*)) and goes to the animals, according to the śruti "with the post he anoints the animal". **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यता (*yatā*)—the refined
- सुजूर्णिः (*sujūrṇiḥ*)—and the very ancient
- धृताची (*dhṛtācī*)—the Juhū vessel
- रातिनी (*rātinī*)—is filled with wealth in the form of the oblation
- देवतातिं (*devatātiṃ*)—the sacrifice that worships the gods
- उराणः (*urāṇaḥ*)—the Adhvaryus who perform
- प्रदक्षिणित् (*pradakṣiṇit*)—are offering homage, keeping the right side toward it
- नवजाः (*navajāḥ*)—newly produced
- स्वरुः न (*svaruḥ na*)—the sacrificial post also
- उदु (*udu*)—stands raised
- अक्रः (*akraḥ*)—the one that assails the animal
- सुमेकः (*sumekaḥ*)—the shining
- सुधितः (*sudhitaḥ*)—the weapon that is the instrument of slaughter
- पश्वः (*paśvaḥ*)—the animals
- अनक्ति (*anakti*)—is approaching

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The well-refined, very ancient Juhū vessel is filled with wealth in the form of the oblation. The Adhvaryus who perform the sacrifice honoured by the gods offer homage, keeping the right side toward it. The newly produced sacrificial post too stands raised. The weapon that assails the animal, shining, the instrument of slaughter, approaches the animals.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The ladle filled (with butter) is prepared : prompt (in act), opulent (with the oblation), the multiplying (priest), conducting (the worship) of the gods, circumambulates (the fire): the newly-trimmed post is set up, the impending shining axe falls upon the victims
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्त्॒रीणे ब॒र्हिषि॑ समिधा॒ने अ॒ग्ना ऊ॒र्ध्वो अ॑ध्व॒युर्जु॑जुषा॒णो अ॑स्थात् ।

> *strīṇe barhiṣi samidhāne agnā ūrdhvo adhvayurjujuṣāṇo asthāt |*

### Printed p. 830

> पर्यग्निः पशुपा न होता तिविष्ट्येत्रिप्रदिव उराणः ॥ ४ ॥

> *paryagniḥ paśupā na hotā tiviṣṭyetripradiva urāṇaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्त्रीणे । बर्हिषि । संइधाने । अग्नौ । ऊर्ध्वः । अध्वर्युः । जुजुषाणः । अस्थात् ।  
> परि । अग्निः । पशुपाः । न । होता । त्रिविष्टि । एति । प्रदिवः । उराणः ॥ ४ ॥

> *strīṇe | barhiṣi | saṃidhāne | agnau | ūrdhvaḥ | adhvaryuḥ | jujuṣāṇaḥ | asthāt |*  
> *pari | agniḥ | paśupāḥ | na | hotā | triviṣṭi | eti | pradivaḥ | urāṇaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बर्हिषि वेद्यां स्तिर्ण आस्तृते सत्यग्नावाहवनीयादिके समिधाने सम्यगिध्यमाने च सत्यध्वर्युरध्वरस्य नेता जुजुषाणो देवान्प्रीणयन्नोध्वोऽस्थात् ।
> तिष्ठति । होता होमनिष्पादकः प्रदिवः । पुराणनामैतत् । पुरातन उराणः स्वल्पमपि हविर्देवयोग्यत्वसंपादनेनोरु कुर्वाणः । उराण उरु कुर्वाण इति
> निरुक्तं । यद्वै देवैर्जोष्यते हविस्तद्दिरिमात्रं वर्धत इति श्रुतेरग्नेरुरुकरणमुचितं । ईदृशोग्निः पशुपा न पशूनां पालक इव पशून् त्रिविष्टि त्रिरावृत्य
> पर्यॆति त्रिर्हि पर्याग्निः क्रियते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the barhis is strewn (स्तीर्णे (*stīrṇe*)) on the vedi, and the fires, the Āhavanīya and the others, are well kindled, the Adhvaryu, the leader of the sacrifice, pleasing the gods (जुजुषाणः (*jujuṣāṇaḥ*)), stands up erect (अस्थात् (*asthāt*)). The Hotṛ, the accomplisher of the oblation, is प्रदिवः (*pradivaḥ*) (a name meaning "ancient"), the ancient one; उराणः (*urāṇaḥ*) is one who makes even a little oblation wide by making it fit for the gods. "उराण (*urāṇa*) is making wide", says the Nirukta. According to the śruti "whatever oblation is enjoyed by the gods, that grows though only a trifle", this making wide is proper to Agni. Such an Agni goes round the animals thrice (त्रिविष्टि (*triviṣṭi*)), repeating three times, like a herdsman (पशुपा न (*paśupā na*)), for the fire is carried round three times.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—the seats of darbha grass
- स्तीर्णे (*stīrṇe*)—being spread
- अग्नौ (*agnau*)—when Agni in the form of the Āhavanīya
- समिधाने (*samidhāne*)—is kindled
- अध्वर्युः (*adhvaryuḥ*)—the leader of the sacrifice
- जुजुषाणः (*jujuṣāṇaḥ*)—the one who satisfies the gods, the Adhvaryu (or Agni)
- ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)—upward-facing
- अस्थात् (*asthāt*)—rises and stands
- होता (*hotā*)—the accomplisher of the oblation
- प्रदिवः (*pradivaḥ*)—the ancient
- उराणः (*urāṇaḥ*)—the promoter of the growth of the sacrifice
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- पशुपा न (*paśupā na*)—like a keeper of animals
- त्रिविष्टि (*triviṣṭi*)—three times
- परि एति (*pari eti*)—goes round

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the seats of darbha grass are spread on the sacrificial altar and Agni in the form of the Āhavanīya is kindled, the Adhvaryu, the leader of the sacrifice, who satisfies the gods, rises and stands upward-facing. Agni, the accomplisher of the oblation, the ancient, the promoter of the growth of the sacrifice, goes round three times like a keeper of animals.

### Printed p. 831

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
When the sacred grass is strewn and the fire is kindled, the Adhwaryu rises, propitiating (the gods), and Agni, the offerer of the oblation, ancient and multiplying (the offering), thrice circumambulates (the victim) like a keeper of cattle.

> उक्तमेवार्थं स्पष्टयति । अयं होता होमनिष्पादकोऽग्निस्त्मनात्मना
> स्वरूपेणैव मितद्रुः परिमितगतिः सन् पर्यॆति । परितो गच्छति पशुं । कीदृशोऽयं । मुंद्रो मादनीयो मोदयिता वा मधुवचा मधुरवचन ऋतावा
> यज्ञवान् । वाजिनो हविष्कृतोऽस्याग्नेः शोका न दीप्तयोऽपि । नशब्दोऽप्यर्थे ।
> द्रवंति । गच्छंति परितः । यद्वा । नकार उपमार्थीयः । वाजिनो न अश्वा इव
> द्रवंतीति योज्यं । यद्यस्मादयमभ्राट् । भ्राजते । तस्माद्विश्वा भुवना सर्वाणि
> भूतजातानि भयंते । भीतानि भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He makes clear the sense already stated. This Hotṛ, Agni the accomplisher of the oblation, goes round (पर्यॆति (*paryèti*)) the animal on every side by himself (त्मना (*tmanā*)), in his own form, moving at a measured pace (मितद्रुः (*mitadruḥ*)). What is he like? मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*): delightful or gladdening; मधुवचाः (*madhuvacāḥ*): of sweet speech; ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*): possessed of the sacrifice. The flames (शोकाः (*śokāḥ*)), the lights, of this Agni, who are bearers of the oblation (वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*)), also run (द्रवंति (*dravaṃti*)), go, all around; the word न (*na*) has the sense of "also". Or else the न (*na*) is one of comparison, and it is to be construed "they run like horses (वाजिनो न (*vājino na*))". Because (यत् (*yat*)) he shines (अभ्राट् (*abhrāṭ*)), therefore all beings (विश्वा भुवना (*viśvā bhuvanā*)) fear (भयंते (*bhayaṃte*)), are afraid.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होता (*hotā*)—the accomplisher of the oblation
- मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*)—the causer of joy
- मधुवचाः (*madhuvacāḥ*)—the one of sweet speech
- ऋताना (*ṛtānā*)—and the possessor of the sacrifice
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—by his own free will [the Kannada text breaks off here]

- परि एति (*pari eti*)—goes round about
- वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*)—of the one possessing oblations
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- शोकाः न (*śokāḥ na*)—the flames also
- द्रवंति (*dravaṃti*)—run round about
- यत् (*yat*)—by whose greatness
- अभ्राट् (*abhrāṭ*)—(because) this Agni shines
- विश्वा भुवना (*viśvā bhuvanā*)—all created beings also
- भयंते (*bhayaṃte*)—are frightened

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the accomplisher of the offering, the gladdener, sweet of speech, possessor of the sacrifice, by his own free impulse moves round about with measured pace. The flames of this Agni, who possesses the oblation, also move round about. Because of the greatness by which this Agni shines, all created beings are frightened.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, the sacrificer, the exhilarator, the sweet-spoken, the object of sacrifice, moving measuredly, circumambulates ( the victim ) of his own (accord); the bright (rays) of him (fed) with (sacrificial) food, spread around; all the regions are alarmed when he blazes.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni of beautiful flame, though you are fearsome, being pervasive everywhere, your form is lovely, praiseworthy and auspicious (the sentence continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 833

> संदृक् संदृष्टिः । सम्यक् दृश्या भवतीत्यर्थः। यद्यस्मात्ते शोचिर्दिप्तिं तमसांधकारेण न वरंत । वारयंति निशाः । यस्माच्च ध्वस्मानो ध्वंसका राक्षसादयस्ते तन्नि
> तव शरीरे रेपः पापं ध्वंसनादिरूपं ना धुः । न दधति । न कुर्वंति । अतः सुदृगिति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Your sight (संदृक् (*saṃdṛk*)) is well seen, that is, you are beautiful to behold. Because the nights do not cover your radiance with darkness, and because destroyers, the Rākṣasas and the like, do not inflict on your body any harm of the nature of destruction, therefore the construction is "of beautiful sight."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वनीक (*svanīka*)—you of auspicious flame
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यत् (*yat*)—by which greatness of yours
- ते (*te*)—your
- शोचिः (*śociḥ*)—radiance
- निशा (*niśā*)—the night
- तमसा (*tamasā*)—with darkness
- न वरंत (*na varaṃta*)—is not covered
- ध्वस्मानः (*dhvasmānaḥ*)—the destroying Rākṣasas
- तन्नि (*tanni*)—in your body
- रेपः (*repaḥ*)—the destructive act of injury
- न आधुः (*na ādhuḥ*)—cannot do (because of that)
- घोरस्य सतः (*ghorasya sataḥ*)—being fear-inspiring
- विषुणस्य (*viṣuṇasya*)—and pervading everywhere
- ते (*te*)—your
- संदृक् (*saṃdṛk*)—sight
- चारुः (*cāruḥ*)—is lovely
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—and auspicious

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni of auspicious flame, by whose greatness the night cannot cover your radiance with darkness and the destroying Rākṣasas cannot do their destructive act of injury to you, for that very reason your sight, though fear-inspiring and all-pervading, is lovely and auspicious.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Bright-shining Agni, beautiful and auspicious is the semblance of you, who are terrible and wide-spreading, for (the nights) hide not your splendour with darkness, nor do the malignant (spirits) inflict any injury on your person.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जनितोर्जनयितुर्वृष्टुत्पादकस्य यस्य वैश्वानरस्य सातुः सनिः पश्वादिलक्षणं
> दानं दीप्तिर्वा नावारि । केनापि न वार्यते । किंच मातरा पितरा मातापितरौ
> द्यावापृथिव्यौ यस्यॆष्टौ प्रेषणे नू चित् क्षिप्रमेव न प्रभवतः । अधापि च मित्रो
> न सखेव सुधितः सुतृप्तः पावकः शोधकोग्निर्मानुषीषु मनोः संबंधिनीषु
> विक्षु प्रजासु दीदाय । दीप्यते ॥ दीपी दीप्ता । पकारलोपश्चांदसः । व्यत्ययेन
> परस्मैपदं । लिट्यभ्यासस्य ह्रस्वे कृते तुजादित्वाद्दीर्घत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of Vaiśvānara, the progenitor, the producer of rain, whose giving (सातुः (*sātuḥ*)) of cattle and the like, or whose radiance, is not checked by anyone. Moreover, Heaven and Earth, the mother and father, are not able to act quickly when he is to be sent forth. And Agni, the purifier, well satisfied like a friend, shines among the human creatures, the peoples belonging to Manu. Grammar remarks: दीदाय (*dīdāya*) is from the root dīp, with loss of p being Vedic, parasmaipada by interchange.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जनितोः (*janitoḥ*)—of the producer of rain
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of that Vaiśvānara
- सातुः (*sātuḥ*)—the giving (or radiance)
- न अवारि (*na avāri*)—cannot be checked by anyone
- मातारा पितरा (*mātārā pitarā*)—Heaven and Earth, mother and father of the world
- इष्टौ (*iṣṭau*)—in the act of sending forth Agni
- नू चित् (*nū cit*)—quickly
- न (*na*)—are not able
- अध (*adha*)—and
- मित्रः न (*mitraḥ na*)—like a friend
- सुधितः (*sudhitaḥ*)—satisfied
- पावकः (*pāvakaḥ*)—purifier
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- मानुषीषु (*mānuṣīṣu*)—in human
- निक्षु (*nikṣu*)—among the peoples **NOTE**
- दीदाय (*dīdāya*)—shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The radiance of Vaiśvānara, the producer of rain, cannot be checked by anyone. Even Heaven and Earth, the mother and father of the world, are not quickly able in the act of sending Agni forth. Agni, satisfied like a friend and a purifier, shines among the peoples of human form.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Of whom, progenitor (of mankind), the benevolence is never checked ; whose parents need not urge him to exertion ; so that the well-satisfied, puri-fying Agni shines like a friend amongst men, the descendants of Manu

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ten sisters, the fingers, dwelling together among human peoples belonging to Manu, engendered Agni by churning (जीजनन् (*jījanan*) from jan, "to appear"; the loss of the augment a is Vedic). What sort of fingers? Like women. What sort of Agni? Awakening at dawn, the eater of oblations, bright, shining with rays, of beautiful mouth, sharp like an axe, that is, the slayer of Rākṣasas (this being the supplied remainder).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मानुषीषु (*mānuṣīṣu*)—belonging to Manu
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—among the peoples
- सं वसानाः (*saṃ vasānāḥ*)—joined together
- द्विः पंच (*dviḥ paṃca*)—ten in number
- अथर्यः न (*atharyaḥ na*)—like women
- स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*)—the fingers
- उषर्बुधं (*uṣarbudhaṃ*)—him who becomes visible at dawn
- दंतं (*daṃtaṃ*)—the eater of oblation
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—the shining
- स्वासं (*svāsaṃ*)—of radiant face
- तिग्मं (*tigmaṃ*)—sharp
- परशुं न (*paraśuṃ na*)—like an axe, the destroyer of Rākṣasas
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which same Agni
- जीजनन् (*jījanan*)—they produced

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The fingers, ten in number, joined together among the peoples belonging to Manu and like women, produced Agni, who becomes visible at dawn, eats the oblation, is shining, of radiant face, and destroys the Rākṣasas like a sharp axe.

dants of Manu, have engendered, like females, (awaking) him at dawn,

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । त्ये । अग्ने । हरितः । धृतस्नाः । रोहितासः । ऋजुअंचः । सुअंचः ।  
> अरुषासः । वृषणः । ऋजुमुष्काः । आ । देव्यतातिं । अह्वंत । दस्माः ॥ ९ ॥

> *tava | tye | agne | haritaḥ | dhṛtasnāḥ | rohitāsaḥ | ṛjuaṃcaḥ | suaṃcaḥ |*  
> *aruṣāsaḥ | vṛṣaṇaḥ | ṛjumuṣkāḥ | ā | devyatātiṃ | ahvaṃta | dasmāḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्ये ते प्रसिद्धास्तव हरितस्त्वत्संबंधिनोऽश्वा देवतातिमस्मदीयं
> यागं प्रत्याह्वंत । ऋत्विभिराहूयंते ॥ लुजु लिपिसिचिश्वश्चेत्यजादेशः ॥ कीवृशाः ।
> धृतस्ना धृतस्न्नुवो बलातिशयान्नासापुटादिस्थानेभ्य उदकं क्षरंतो रोहितासो
> रोहिता लोहितवर्णा ऋज्जंचः । ऋज्जकुटिलमंचंति गच्छंतीत्यृज्जंचः । स्वंच
> सुष्टु गच्छंतः । अरुषास आरोचमाना वृषणो युवानो वर्षितारो वा ॥ वा
> षपूर्वस्य निगम इति विकल्पेन दीर्घविधानादत्र दीर्घाभावः ॥ ऋजुमुष्काः साधनमुष्का दस्मा दर्शनीयाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, those well-known horses of yours are summoned by the priests to our sacrifice (अह्वंत (*ahvaṃta*); the substitution aja by the sūtra on lu). Of what sort? धृतस्नाः (*dhṛtasnāḥ*): through excess of strength they let water flow from the nostrils and other places. रोहितासः (*rohitāsaḥ*): red-coloured. ऋज्जंचः (*ṛjjaṃcaḥ*): going straight (not crooked). स्वंचः (*svaṃcaḥ*): going well. अरुषासः (*aruṣāsaḥ*): shining. वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*): young, or showerers; because the lengthening is optional, no lengthening occurs here. ऋजुमुष्काः (*ṛjumuṣkāḥ*): of effective strength; दस्माः (*dasmāḥ*): beautiful to see.

- ऋज्जंचः (*ṛjjaṃcaḥ*)—of straight gait

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, those rays of yours, renowned, not overcome by enemies, of moving nature, radiant and having the act of service, go and reach their destined region, like horses and, like the company of the Maruts, sounding loudly.

Those, your rays, Agni, triumphant, wide-spreading, radiant, adorable, go like hawk-faced horses ( to their goal ), loud-sounding like the company of the Maruts.

**NOTE**

> आयोर्मनुष्यस्य शंसं शंसनीयं होतारं देवानामाह्वातारमग्निं त्वां नमस्यंतः पूजयंत उशिजः पश्वादिलक्षणं धनं कामयमाना मनुषो मनुष्या
> ऋत्विजो नि षेदुः । उपाविशन् । सेवंत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, being kindled (समिधान (*samidhāna*)), for you, for your sake, a ब्रह्म (*brahma*), that is, a hymn of praise, has been made by us." The hotā recites (शंसाति (*śaṃsāti*) = शंसति (*śaṃsati*)) the uktha, a praise in the form of a śastra. The sacrificer worships you. "For this reason bestow (वि धाः (*vi dhāḥ*) = विधेहि (*vidhehi*)) wealth upon us." The particle उ (*u*) is a filler of the pāda. And further: …

### Printed p. 839

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

… men (मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)), that is, the priests, desiring (उशिजः (*uśijaḥ*)) wealth of the nature of cattle and the like, worshipping you, Agni, the invoker of the gods, who is to be praised (शंसं (*śaṃsaṃ*)) by man (आयोः (*āyoḥ*)), have sat down (नि षेदुः (*ni ṣeduḥ*)), that is, have approached and serve you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समिधान (*samidhāna*)—O kindled Agni
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—with you in view
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—the praise
- अकारि (*akāri*)—has been made
- उकथं (*ukathaṃ*)—the śastra-mantra
- शंसति (*śaṃsati*)—(the hotā) recites
- यजते (*yajate*)—(the sacrificer) worships, (therefore)
- वि धाः (*vi dhāḥ*)—provide wealth
- आयोः (*āyoḥ*)—to man
- शंसं (*śaṃsaṃ*)—the venerable one
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the one who calls the gods
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—you, Agni, the venerable
- नमस्यंतः (*namasyaṃtaḥ*)—worshipping
- उशिजः (*uśijaḥ*)—desiring wealth such as cattle
- मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)—the priests
- नि षेदुः (*ni ṣeduḥ*)—are serving (you)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O kindled Agni, a praise with you in view has been made; the hotā is reciting the praise in the form of a śastra. Therefore provide wealth. The priests, desiring wealth such as cattle, worshipping you, who are venerable to man, who call the gods to the sacrifice, and are venerable, are serving you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Well-kindled Agni, for you the prayer has been composed : may (the priest) propitiate (you) by (his) praise : the (sacrificer) offers worship : bestow upon us manifold (wealth) : desiring (riches), men sit down adoring Agni, the invoker of the gods, the glorifier of mankind.

## Sūkta 7 (Maṇḍala 4)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमिहेत्येकादशर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं वामदेवस्यार्षमाग्नेयं । आद्या
> जगती द्वितीयाद्याः पंचानुष्टुभः शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अयमिहादौ
> जगती पंचानुष्टुभ इति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ अग्निप्रणयनेऽयमिहेति
> वैश्यस्य प्रतिपत् । तथा च सूत्रितं । अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिरिति तु
> राजन्यवैश्ययोराद्ये । आ. २-१७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seventh sūkta, beginning अयमिह (*ayamiha*), of eleven ṛks, has Vāmadeva as seer and Agni as deity. The first verse is a jagatī, the next five are anuṣṭubhs, the rest triṣṭubhs. So the Anukramaṇī says: अयमिहादौ जगती पंचानुष्टुभ इति (*ayamihādau jagatī paṃcānuṣṭubha iti*). The use of the sūkta is by the Liṅga (indicative sign). In the Agnipraṇayana (the leading forth of the fire), अयमिह (*ayamiha*) is the pratipad of the Vaiśya. As the sūtra states: अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिरिति तु राजन्यवैश्ययोराद्ये (*ayamiha prathamo dhāyi dhātṛbhiriti tu rājanyavaiśyayorādye*) (Ā. Sū. 2-17).

### Printed p. 840
Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning आयमिह (*āyamiha*) is the seventh sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has eleven ṛks. Vāmadeva is the seer of this sūkta; Agni is the deity. The first ṛk of this sūkta is in the jagatī metre. From the second ṛk to the sixth the metre is anuṣṭubh; the remaining ṛks are in the triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: अयमिहादौ जगती पंचानुष्टभः (*ayamihādau jagatī paṃcānuṣṭabhaḥ*). The use of the sūkta is by the Liṅga. In the rite called Agnipraṇayana (the rite of carrying the fire, churned and produced at the sacrifice, from the place of its production to the northern altar, is called Agnipraṇayana), this ṛk beginning अयमिह (*ayamiha*) is to be recited by a Vaiśya sacrificer as the ṛk called pratipad; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिरिति तु राजन्यवैश्ययोराद्ये (*ayamiha prathamo dhāyi dhātṛbhiriti tu rājanyavaiśyayorādye*) (Ā. Sū. 2-17).

Sūkta 2**NOTE**

- Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 5; Varga 6, 7
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 11
- Seer: Vāmadeva
- Deity: Agni
- Metre: 1 jagatī; 2–6 anuṣṭubh; 7–11 jagatī

> प्रथमः सर्वॆषां देवानां मुख्योऽयवाहवनीयादिस्थानेषु प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यमानोऽग्निर्धायि । अधायि । निहितः ॥ दधातेः कर्मणि लुज् । बहुलं छंदस्यमाजत्योग इत्यडभावः । तिङ्ङतिज इति निघातः ॥ अयमग्निरित्युक्तं । कोऽसावग्निरित्यत आह । अप्पवानो भृगुसंबंधी कश्चिदृषिः स चान्वे भृगवश्च वनेष्वरण्येषु
> चित्रं दावाग्निरूपेण बहुधा दर्शनीयं विशे विशे । वीप्सया सर्वजनव्याप्तिर्गृह्यते । सर्वस्या विशः प्रजाया विभ्वं विभुमीश्वरं यं देवानां हविर्वाहकत्वेन
> प्रसिद्धमग्निं विरुरुचुः । दीप्तियुक्तं कुर्वंति स्म । यमिति यच्छब्दस्यायमितीदंशब्बेन संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, in this sacrifice, by the dhātṛs (धातृभिः (*dhātṛbhiḥ*)), the adhvaryus who perform the rite for the sacrifice, this Agni has been placed (धायि (*dhāyi*) = अधायि (*adhāyi*), set down): the hotā, the invoker of the gods; यजिष्ठः (*yajiṣṭhaḥ*), the most excellent sacrificer; the one to be praised at the adhvaras, the sacrifices; प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*), first, chief of all the gods; perceived directly in the places of the Āhavanīya and so on.**NOTE** "This Agni" has been said; who is this Agni? He replies: whom Apnavāna, a certain seer connected with Bhṛgu, and the other Bhṛgus, made to shine (विरुरुचुः (*virurucuḥ*), made radiant) in the woods, in the forests; चित्रं (*citraṃ*), wondrous, to be seen in many ways in the form of the forest-fire. विशे विशे (*viśe viśe*): by the repetition the pervasion of all people is understood: for every people. विभ्वं (*vibhvaṃ*), the lord, the master, famed as the bearer of oblations of the gods. The relative यं (*yaṃ*) is connected with the demonstrative अयं (*ayaṃ*) ("this").

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अप्नवानः (*apnavānaḥ*)—the seer named Apnavāna
- भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*)—and the other seers born in the line of Bhṛgu
- वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—in the forests
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—who is worth seeing in the form of forest-fire
- विशे विशे (*viśe viśe*)—for all peoples
- विभ्वं (*vibhvaṃ*)—and lord
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Agni
- विरुरुचुः (*virurucuḥ*)—they made blazing, such
- होता (*hotā*)—who is in the form of the hotā
- यजिष्ठः (*yajiṣṭhaḥ*)—the most venerable
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—in the sacrifices
- ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)—who is praised
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—the first of all gods
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Agni
- धातृभिः (*dhātṛbhiḥ*)—by the adhvaryus who perform the sacrifice
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- धायि (*dhāyi*)—has been established

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Agni, in the form of the hotā, the most venerable, praised in the sacrifices, first of all gods, whom the seer Apnavāna and the other seers born in the line of Bhṛgu made blaze in the forests, he who is worth seeing in the form of forest-fire and lord of all peoples, has been established in this sacrifice by the adhvaryus who perform the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 842

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This invoker of the gods and minister of frequent worship, who is to be glorified at sacrifices, has been placed first (of the gods) by the performers of the rite : Agni whom Apnavana and other Bhrigus lighted in the woods for the sake of all men, marvellous (in his acts), and sovereign (over all).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अप्नवानः (*apnavānaḥ*)—The commentator says that Apnavāna is a certain seer born in the line of Bhṛgu. The name of this seer occurs in the Ṛgveda in the present ṛk and also in the ṛk जीवभृगुवच्छुचिमप्नवानवदा हुवे । अग्निं समुद्रवाससं॥ (*jīvabhṛguvacchucimapnavānavadā huve | agniṃ samudravāsasaṃ‖*) (Mu. Saṃ. 8-102-4).**NOTE** The same mantra is also stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. "I shall invoke as Apnavāna, the seer born in the line of Bhṛgu, invoked Agni": thus the seer Prayoga of the same line speaks here. Although this seer is renowned, there is no occasion to learn more details about him.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ क॒दा त॑ आनु॒षग्भव॑द्दे॒वस्य॒ चेत॑नं ।  
> अधा॒ हि त्वा॑ जगृभि॒रे मर्ता॑सो वि॒क्ष्वीड्यं॑ ॥ २ ॥

> *agne kadā ta ānuṣagbhavaddevasya cetanaṃ |*  
> *adhā hi tvā jagṛbhire martāso vikṣvīḍyaṃ ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । कदा । ते । अनुषक् । भुवत् । देवस्य । चेतनं ।  
> अध । हि । त्वा । जगृभ्रिरे । मर्तासः । विक्षु । ईड्यं ॥ २ ॥

> *agne | kadā | te | anuṣak | bhuvat | devasya | cetanaṃ |*  
> *adha | hi | tvā | jagṛbhrire | martāsaḥ | vikṣu | īḍyaṃ ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्ने कदा त इति। प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोराग्नेये क्रतावानुष्टुभे छंदस्याग्ने कदा त इत्याद्याः पंचर्चः । सूत्रितं च । अग्ने कदा त इति पंच । आ. ४. १३ ।
> इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Use: in the prātaranuvāka and in the Āśvina śastra, in the Āgneya kratu, in the anuṣṭubh metre, the five ṛks beginning अग्ने कदा त (*agne kadā ta*) are used. And it is stated in the sūtra: अग्ने कदा त इति पंच (*agne kadā ta iti paṃca*) (Ā. Sū. 4. 13).

### Printed p. 843

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने अधातः कारणाद्देवस्य द्योतमानस्य ते तव संबंधि चेतनं तेजः
> कदानुषक् अनुषक्तं भुवत् । भवेत् ॥ लेट्यडागमः । बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य
> लुक् । भूसुवोस्तिजीति गुणप्रतिषेधः ॥ अतः कारणादित्युक्तं । कस्माद्धेतोरित्युच्यते । हि यस्मात्कारणान्मर्तासो मनुष्या विक्षु विड्भिः प्रजाभिरीड्यं स्तुत्यं त्वा त्वां
> जगृभ्रिरे । जगृहिरे । गृह्णंति ॥ ग्रहेर्धातोर्लिटि हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वं । बहुलं
> छंदसीति रुडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, when will the light (चेतनं (*cetanaṃ*), brightness) of you, shining (देवस्य (*devasya*)), be continuous (आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*), attached; भुवत् (*bhuvat*) = भवेत् (*bhavet*))? अध (*adha*) = "for this reason"; for what reason is next said: because (हि (*hi*)) mortals (मर्तासः (*martāsaḥ*)), men, among the peoples (विक्षु (*vikṣu*)) have taken you (जगृभ्रिरे (*jagṛbhrire*) = जगृहिरे (*jagṛhire*)), worthy of praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- हि (*hi*)—by whose greatness of yours
- मर्तासः (*martāsaḥ*)—men
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—among the peoples
- ईड्यं (*īḍyaṃ*)—worthy of praise
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- जगृभिरे (*jagṛbhire*)—have taken up**NOTE**
- अध (*adha*)—for that reason
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of the shining
- ते (*te*)—of you
- चेतनं (*cetanaṃ*)—the brightness
- कदा (*kadā*)—when
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—manifest**NOTE**
- भुवत् (*bhuvat*)—becomes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, by whose greatness men have borne you, praised among the peoples, for that reason, when does your brightness, shining, become manifest?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
When, Agni, is the light of you, bright-shining, to be manifested? for therefore have mortals accepted you as to be worshipped amongst mankind.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the recitation of the prātaranuvāka and of the Āśvina śastra mantras, the five ṛks of this sūkta beginning अग्ने कदा ते (*agne kadā te*), in the anuṣṭubh metre, are used for the ṛks related to the Āgneya kratu; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra अग्ने कदा त इति पंच (*agne kadā ta iti paṃca*) (Ā. Sū. 4-13).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒तावा॑नं॒ विचे॑तसं॒ पश्यं॑तो॒ द्यामि॑व॒ स्तृभिः॑ ।  
> विश्वे॑षामध्व॒राणां॑ हस्क॒र्तारं॒ दमे॑दमे ॥ ३ ॥

> *ṛtāvānaṃ vicetasaṃ paśyaṃto dyāmiva stṛbhiḥ |*  
> *viśveṣāmadhvarāṇāṃ haskartāraṃ damedame ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 844

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋतसानं । विचेतसं । पश्यंतः । द्यांइव । स्तुभिः ।  
> विश्वेषां । अध्वराणां । हस्कर्तारं । दमेदमे ॥ ३ ॥

> *ṛtasānaṃ | vicetasaṃ | paśyaṃtaḥ | dyāṃiva | stubhiḥ |*  
> *viśveṣāṃ | adhvarāṇāṃ | haskartāraṃ | damedame ‖ 3 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋतानानममायिनं विचेतसं विशिष्टज्ञानं स्तृभिर्नक्षत्रैः परिवृतं द्यामिव।
> विस्फुलिंगैः समेतं विश्वेषां सर्वॆषामध्वराणां यज्ञानां हस्कर्तारं प्रभासकं
> वृद्धेः कर्तारं वाग्निं पश्यंत ऋत्विगादयो दमे दमे सर्वस्मिन्यज्ञगृहे जगृभिर
> इति पूर्वेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The truthful one (ऋतावानं (*ṛtāvānaṃ*)), free from deceit, of distinguished knowledge, is encircled by stars (स्तृभिः (*stṛbhiḥ*)) as the sky is, that is, he is accompanied by sparks.**NOTE** The priests and others behold this Agni, the "perfecter" of all sacrifices (हस्कर्तारं (*haskartāraṃ*)), that is, the illuminator, the one who brings about increase. In every sacrificial house (दमे दमे (*dame dame*)) they "have borne" him (जगृभिर (*jagṛbhira*)). This is connected with the preceding verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतावानं (*ṛtāvānaṃ*)—the truthful one
- विचेतसं (*vicetasaṃ*)—the one of distinguished intelligence
- स्तृभिः (*stṛbhiḥ*)—with stars
- द्यामिव (*dyāmiva*)—like the sky
- विश्वेषां (*viśveṣāṃ*)—of all
- आध्वराणां (*ādhvarāṇāṃ*)—of the sacrifices
- हस्कर्तारं (*haskartāraṃ*)—the one who brings about illumination, that is, Agni
- पश्यंतः (*paśyaṃtaḥ*)—beholding
- दमे दमे (*dame dame*)—in every sacrificial house (the priests and others bear him)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Beholding Agni, who is truthful, of distinguished intelligence, and who brings illumination to all sacrifices as the sky is adorned with stars, the priests and others bear him in every sacrificial house.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Contemplating you in every dwelling, truthful, intelligent, (brilliant with sparks) like the sky with stars, the perfecter of all sacrifices.
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒शुं दू॒तं वि॒वस्व॑तो॒ विश्वा॒ यश्च॑र्ष॒णीर॒भि ।  
> आ ज॑भ्रुः के॒तुमा॒यवो॒ भृग॑वाणं वि॒शेवि॑शे ॥ ४ ॥

> *āśuṃ dūtaṃ vivasvato viśvā yaścarṣaṇīrabhi |*  
> *ā jabhruḥ ketumāyavo bhṛgavāṇaṃ viśeviśe ‖ 4 ‖*

### Printed p. 845

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आशुं । दूतं । विवस्वतः । विश्वाः । यः । चर्षणीः । अभि ।  
> आ । जभ्रुः । केतुं । आयवः । भृगवाणं । विशेऽविशे ॥ ४ ॥

> *āśuṃ | dūtaṃ | vivasvataḥ | viśvāḥ | yaḥ | carṣaṇīḥ | abhi |*  
> *ā | jabhruḥ | ketuṃ | āyavaḥ | bhṛgavāṇaṃ | viśe 'viśe ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योग्निर्विश्वाश्चर्षणीः सर्वाः प्रजा अभि भवति आयवो मनुष्याः । आयव
> इति मनुष्यनाम आयवो यदव इति मनुष्यनामसु नाठात् । आशुं क्षिप्रगामिनं
> विवस्वतो मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य दूतं । विवस्वत इति मनुष्यनामेदं । केतुं
> प्रज्ञापकं भृगवाणं भृगुवदाचरंतं । दीप्यमानमित्यर्थः ॥ सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यः
> क्विब्वक्तव्य इति क्विप् । तदंताल्लटो व्यत्ययेन शानच् । अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते वृषादेराकृतिगणत्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ तमग्निं विशे विशे
> सर्वस्यॆ प्रजाया आ जभ्रुः । आजह्रुः ॥ हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni who prevails over all peoples (विश्वाश्चर्षणीः (*viśvāścarṣaṇīḥ*)), all subjects—the आयवः (*āyavaḥ*) are men; आयवो यदव इति मनुष्यनामसु नाठात् (*āyavo yadava iti manuṣyanāmasu nāṭhāt*) (read among the names of men)—that Agni, the swift-going (आशुं (*āśuṃ*)), is the messenger (दूतं (*dūtaṃ*)) of Vivasvat, that is, of man, the sacrificer; विवस्वत इति मनुष्यनामेदं (*vivasvata iti manuṣyanāmedaṃ*). He is the "banner" (केतुं (*ketuṃ*)), the one who makes things known, and भृगवाणं (*bhṛgavāṇaṃ*), one who behaves like Bhṛgu, that is, shining. That Agni, for every people (विशे विशे (*viśe viśe*)), they have brought (आ जभ्रुः (*ā jabhruḥ*) = आजह्रुः (*ājahruḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—that very Agni who
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- चर्षणीः (*carṣaṇīḥ*)—peoples
- अभि (*abhi*)—is lord over (such a one)
- आशुं (*āśuṃ*)—the swift-going one
- विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)—of the sacrificer
- दूतं (*dūtaṃ*)—the messenger (who calls the gods)
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—the giver of knowledge
- भृगवाणं (*bhṛgavāṇaṃ*)—the resplendent one; that Agni
- विशेविशे (*viśeviśe*)—in every sacrificial house
- आयवः (*āyavaḥ*)—men, the sacrificers
- आ जभ्रुः (*ā jabhruḥ*)—have brought

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni is the lord of all peoples. That Agni, who is swift-going, the messenger who calls the gods for the sacrificer, the giver of knowledge, the resplendent one, men the sacrificers have brought to every sacrificial house.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Men have brought, for the sake of all people, the swift messenger of the worshipper (to the gods), who (rules) over all mankind, the manifester, the resplendent.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमीं॒ होता॑रमानु॒षक् चि॑कि॒त्वांसं॒ न षे॑दिरे ।

> रण्वं । पावकशोचिषं । यजिष्ठं । सप्त । धामभिः ॥ ५ ॥

> *taṃ | īṃ | hotāraṃ | ānuṣak | cikitvāṃsaṃ | ni| sedire |*  
> *raṇvaṃ | pāvakaśociṣaṃ | yajiṣṭhaṃ | sapta | dhāmabhiḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋत्विगादयो मनुष्या आनुषक् आनुपूर्व्येण होतारं देवानामाह्वातारं चिकित्वांसं जानंतं ॥ कित ज्ञाने । लिटः क्वसुः । द्विर्भावहलादिशेषचुत्वदीर्घाः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥ तमीं तमिममग्निं नि षेदिरे । निषादयंति स्म । कीदृशं ।
> रण्वं रमणीयं पावकशोचिषं शोधकदीप्तिं यजिष्टं यष्टृतमं सप्त सप्तभिर्धामभिस्तेजोभिर्युक्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests and others, men, have seated (नि षेदिरे (*ni ṣedire*), निषादयंति स्म (*niṣādayaṃti sma*)) that very Agni in due order (आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*), आनुपूर्व्येण (*ānupūrvyeṇa*)). He is the invoker (होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)) of the gods, the one who knows (चिकित्वांसं (*cikitvāṃsaṃ*), from the root कित ज्ञाने (*kita jñāne*)). Of what kind? Delightful (रण्वं (*raṇvaṃ*)), of purifying radiance (पावकशोचिषं (*pāvakaśociṣaṃ*)), the best sacrificer (यजिष्टं (*yajiṣṭaṃ*), यष्टृतमं (*yaṣṭṛtamaṃ*)), endowed with seven (सप्त (*sapta*)) abodes, that is, with seven lustres (धामभिः (*dhāmabhiḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the one who invokes the gods (to the sacrifice)
- चिकित्वांसं (*cikitvāṃsaṃ*)—the wise one
- रण्वं (*raṇvaṃ*)—the one of delightful form
- पावकशोचिसं (*pāvakaśocisaṃ*)—the one of purifying radiance
- यजिष्ठं (*yajiṣṭhaṃ*)—the most worshipful (the frequent sacrificer)
- सप्त धामभिः (*sapta dhāmabhiḥ*)—endowed with seven lustres
- तमीं (*tamīṃ*)—that same Agni
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—following the order of his place
- नि षेदिरे (*ni ṣedire*)—(the priests) establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That same Agni, who invokes the gods to the sacrifice, who is wise, of delightful form, of purifying radiance, most worshipful, endowed with seven lustres, the priests establish following the order of his place.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
They (the worshippers) have seated him in his due order, the invoker (of the gods) the intelligent, the agreeable, the purifyingly-radiant, the performer of frequent sacrifice, (brilliant) with seven flames.

### Printed p. 847

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सप्त धामभिः (*sapta dhāmabhiḥ*)—Agni has seven flames known as Kālī, Karālī and so on. The meaning is: with such flames.
#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं शश्व॑तीषु मा॒तृषु॒ वन॒ आ वी॒तमश्रि॑तं ।  
> चि॒त्रं संतं॒ गुहा॑ हि॒तं सु॒वेदं॑ कूचिद॒र्थिनं॑ ॥ ६ ॥

> *taṃ śaśvatīṣu mātṛṣu vana ā vītamaśritaṃ |*  
> *citraṃ saṃtaṃ guhā hitaṃ suvedaṃ kūcidarthinaṃ ‖ 6 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । शश्वतीषु । मातृषु । वने । आ! वीतं। अश्रितं ।  
> चित्रं । संतं । गुहा । हितं । सुवेदं । कूचित् अर्थिनं ॥ ६ ॥

> *taṃ | śaśvatīṣu | mātṛṣu | vane | ā! vītaṃ| aśritaṃ |*  
> *citraṃ | saṃtaṃ | guhā | hitaṃ | suvedaṃ | kūcit arthinaṃ ‖ 6 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शश्वतीषु बह्वीषु मातृष्टप्पु । तार्क सस्यादिनिर्मातृकत्वान्मातर इत्युच्यंते ।
> वन आ वृक्षसमूहे च । आकारश्चार्थे । संतं विद्यमानं वीतं कांतमश्रितं प्राणिभिर्वाहभयादसेवितं । दुरासदमित्यर्थः । चित्रं चायनीयं गुहा गुहायां
> हितं निहितं सुवेदं सुविज्ञानं सुधनं वा कूचिदर्थिनं क्वापि हविष्यर्थिनं समिदाज्यपुरोडाशादि हविः स्वीकुर्वंतं ॥ क्वेत्यत्र वकारस्य छंदसे संप्रसारणे परपूर्वत्वे च हल इति दीर्घत्वं ॥ एवंभूतमग्निं निषेदिग इति पूर्वेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

शश्वतीषु (*śaśvatīṣu*) means many; in the many mothers (मातृषु (*mātṛṣu*)), the waters—they are called mothers because they produce plants and the like. And in the forest (वने (*vane*)), in the groups of trees; the आ (*ā*) has the sense of "and". Agni is existing (संतं (*saṃtaṃ*)), desirable (वीतं (*vītaṃ*)), not resorted to (अश्रितं (*aśritaṃ*)) by creatures through fear of burning, that is, hard to approach.**NOTE** He is wonderful (चित्रं (*citraṃ*), चायनीयं (*cāyanīyaṃ*)), placed in a cave (गुहा हितं (*guhā hitaṃ*)), easily known (सुवेदं (*suvedaṃ*)) or of good wealth, desiring (अर्थिनं (*arthinaṃ*)) an oblation anywhere (कूचित् (*kūcit*)), accepting oblations such as kindling-sticks, ghee and cake. Such an Agni "they have seated"—this is connected with the preceding verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शश्वतीषु (*śaśvatīṣu*)—of many kinds
- मातृषु (*mātṛṣu*)—in the waters that have the form of mothers
- वने आ (*vane ā*)—and in groups of trees
- संतं (*saṃtaṃ*)—the one who is hidden
- वीतं (*vītaṃ*)—the attractive one
- अश्रितं (*aśritaṃ*)—one served (by all) (or one who cannot be approached)
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—the one of charming form
- गुहा (*guhā*)—in a cave
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—placed
- सुवेदं (*suvedaṃ*)—the one of excellent wealth
- कूचिदर्थिनं (*kūcidarthinaṃ*)—the one who accepts oblations, that is, Agni (the priests and others have established)

### Printed p. 848

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is hidden in the waters that stand in the place of mothers and in trees, who is attractive, served by all, of charming form, placed in a cave, of excellent wealth, who accepts oblations, the priests and others have established.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Him, abiding in the maternal (water) and in the woods, loved, yet unapproached, wonderful, hidden in a cave, endowed with knowledge, seeking (oblations) from any quarter.
#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒सस्य॒ यद्वियु॑ता॒ सस्मि॒न्नूध॑न्नृ॒तस्य॒ धाम॑न्र॒णयं॑त दे॒वाः ।  
> म॒हा अ॒ग्निर्नम॑सा रा॒तह॑व्यो॒ वेर॑ध्व॒राय॒ सद॒मिदृ॒तावा॑ ॥

> *sasasya yadviyutā sasminnūdhannṛtasya dhāmanraṇayaṃta devāḥ |*  
> *mahā agnirnamasā rātahavyo veradhvarāya sadamidṛtāvā ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ससस्य । यत् । वियुता । सस्मिन् । ऊधन् । ऋतस्य । धामन् । रणयंत । देवाः ।  
> महान् । अग्निः । नमसा । रातहव्यः । वेः । अध्वराय । सदं । इत् । ऋतवा ॥७॥

> *sasasya | yat | viyutā | sasmin | ūdhan | ṛtasya | dhāman | raṇayaṃta | devāḥ |*  
> *mahān | agniḥ | namasā | rātahavyaḥ | veḥ | adhvarāya | sadaṃ | it | ṛtavā ‖7‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोस्त्रैष्टुभे छंदसि ससस्य यद्वियुतेत्याद्याः पंचर्चः । सूत्रितं च । ससस्य यद्वियुतेति पंच । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥
> यद्यमग्निं देवाः स्तोतारः ससस्य स्वप्नस्य वियुता वियुते वियोगे ।
> उषसीत्यर्थः। ऋतस्योदकस्य धामन् धामनि स्थाने सस्मिन् सर्वस्मिन्नूधन्नूधनि यज्ञे
> रणयंत । रमयंति । स्तोत्रैरिति शेषः । महान्प्रभूतो नमसा नमस्कारेण
> रातहव्यो दत्तहविष्क ऋतावा सत्यवान् सोऽग्निः सदमित्सदैनाध्वरायाध्वरं यजमानैः कृतं यज्ञं ॥ सुपां सुपो भवंतीति व्यक्तव्यं । म. ७-१-३९ । इति वचनादत्र द्वितीयार्थे चतुर्थि ॥ वेः । वेत्ति । जानाति । यद्वा । देवा इंद्रादयः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Prātaranuvāka and in the Āśvina-śastra, in the triṣṭubh metre, the five Ṛks beginning ससस्य यद्वियुता (*sasasya yadviyutā*) are used; and it is stated in the sūtra: ससस्य यद्वियुतेति पंच (*sasasya yadviyuteti paṃca*) (Ā. Sū. 4-13).
The Agni whom the gods, that is, the praisers, delight (रणयंत (*raṇayaṃta*), रमयंति (*ramayaṃti*), the words "with hymns" to be supplied) at the separation (वियुता (*viyutā*)) from sleep (ससस्य (*sasasya*)), that is, at dawn; in the place (धामन् (*dhāman*)) of water (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)), in every sacrifice (सस्मिन्नूधन् (*sasminnūdhan*)). That Agni is great, to whom oblations are given with homage (नमसा (*namasā*)), truthful (ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*)); for the sacrifice (अध्वराय (*adhvarāya*)), the sacrifice performed by the sacrificers, he always (सदमित् (*sadamit*)) वेः (*veḥ*), that is, "knows" (वेत्ति (*vetti*), जानाति (*jānāti*)). The fourth-case ending here stands in the sense of the second, by the statement quoted.
Or else: the gods, Indra and others—

### Printed p. 849

> ससस्य ऋत्विग्भिः सेव्यस्य यद्यस्याग्निर्वियुता विशिष्टे सस्मिन् भजनीय ऋतस्य सत्यस्य
> धामन् धामनि योनावूधन्नूधनि यज्ञे रणयंत । रमयंते । महान्प्रभूतो नमसा हविषा रातहव्यो दत्तहविष्क ऋताना सत्यवान् सोऽग्निरध्वराय
> यज्ञार्थं सदमित्यदैव वेः । गंता भवति । अध्वराय यज्ञं वेः कामयते वा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing the alternative:) the gods delight, in the sacrifice served by the priests, in the worshipful (भजनीय (*bhajanīya*)) place of truth (ऋतस्य सत्यस्य (*ṛtasya satyasya*)), the womb (*yonau*).**NOTE** The great Agni, to whom the oblation is given with homage, i.e. with the oblation, who is truthful, for the sake of the sacrifice, always becomes वेः (*veḥ*), a goer; or he desires the sacrifice (अध्वराय यज्ञं वेः कामयते वा (*adhvarāya yajñaṃ veḥ kāmayate vā*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Agni
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the praisers
- ससस्य (*sasasya*)—of sleep (the state of slumber)
- वियुता (*viyutā*)—at the time of its ending (at dawn)
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water
- धामन् (*dhāman*)—near
- सस्मिन् ऊधन् (*sasmin ūdhan*)—at the time of every sacrifice
- रणयंत (*raṇayaṃta*)—they worship (such a one)
- महान् (*mahān*)—the one of mighty form
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with praise
- रातहव्यः (*rātahavyaḥ*)—the one to whom the oblation is offered
- ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*)—the truthful one
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- सदमित् (*sadamit*)—always
- अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—the sacrifice
- वेः (*veḥ*)—knows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni whom the praisers worship at dawn, near the water, at the time of every sacrifice, that Agni, of mighty form, truthful, to whom the oblation is offered with praise, always knows the sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Whom, when they desist from slumber, the devout propitiate in the abode of water at every sacrifice : the mighty Agni, to whom oblations are to be offered with reverence, who, truthful always, accepts the sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The use of the five Ṛks of this sūkta beginning ससस्य यद्वियुता (*sasasya yadviyutā*) is, for the triṣṭubh Ṛks, at the time of the Prātaranuvāka and of the recitation of the Āśvina-śastra mantras, as it is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra ससस्य यद्वियुतेति पंच (*sasasya yadviyuteti paṃca*) (Ā. 8-13).**NOTE**
Sāyaṇa has explained this Ṛk in another way also: Indra and the other gods delight in the sacrifice that is performed by the priests and in which Agni is the principal figure. In that sacrifice the very great Agni always comes to the sacrificial ground in order to accept the oblation given by the sacrificer, and he also desires the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 850
#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वेर॑ध्व॒रस्य॑ दू॒त्या॑नि वि॒द्वानु॒भे अं॒ता रोद॑सी संचिकि॒त्वान् ।  
> दू॒त ई॑यसे प्र॒दिव॑ उरा॒णो वि॒दुष्ट॑रो दि॒व आ॒राध॑नानि ॥

> *veradhvarasya dūtyāni vidvānubhe aṃtā rodasī saṃcikitvān |*  
> *dūta īyase pradiva urāṇo viduṣṭaro diva ārādhanāni ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वेः । अध्वरस्य । दूत्यानि । विद्वान् । उभे इति । अंतरिति । रोदसी इति । संचिकित्वान् ।  
> दूतः । ईयसे । प्रदिवः । उराणः । विदुःतरः । दिवः । आरोधननानि ॥ ८ ॥

> *veḥ | adhvarasya | dūtyāni | vidvān | ubhe iti | aṃtariti | rodasī iti | saṃcikitvān |*  
> *dūtaḥ | īyase | pradivaḥ | urāṇaḥ | viduḥtaraḥ | divaḥ | ārodhananāni ‖ 8 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने विद्वान् सर्वं जानानस्त्वमध्वरस्य यज्ञस्य संबंधीनि दूत्यानि
> दूतकर्माणि वेः । वेत्सि कामयसे वा । यद्वा । वेरिति यज्ञविशेषणं । वेर्यजमानस्याभीष्टफलजनकस्याध्वरस्य यागस्य संबंधीनि दूत्यानि दूतकर्माणि विद्वान्
> जानन् उभे रोदसी उभयो रोदस्कोर्द्यानापृथिव्योरंतर्मध्यॆ स्थितमंतरिक्षं संचिकित्वान् सम्यक् जानन् प्रदिवः पुराणः । पुराणानामेदं प्रश्नं प्रदिव
> इति पुराणनामसु पाठात् । उराणोल्पमपि हविरुरु बहुकुर्वाणः । उराण
> उरु कुर्वाण इति यास्केनोक्तत्वात् । विदुष्टरो विद्वत्तरो देवानां दूतस्त्वं
> दिवः स्वर्गस्यारोधनान्यारोहणानि । आरोहणार्हाणि स्थानानीत्यर्थः । देवानां
> हवींष्यर्पयितुमीयसे । गच्छसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you, knowing (विद्वान् (*vidvān*)) everything, वेः (*veḥ*)—you know (वेत्सि (*vetsi*)) or desire (कामयसे (*kāmayase*)) the messenger-offices (दूत्यानि (*dūtyāni*), दूतकर्माणि (*dūtakarmāṇi*)) connected with the sacrifice (अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)). Or else: वेः (*veḥ*) is an epithet of the sacrifice, the sacrifice of the sacrificer, that produces the desired fruit; knowing the messenger-offices connected with that rite, and fully knowing (संचिकित्वान् (*saṃcikitvān*)) both रोदसी (*rodasī*), heaven and earth, and the atmosphere standing between them (अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)). प्रदिवः (*pradivaḥ*) is "ancient"—पुराणानामेदं प्रश्नं प्रदिव इति पुराणनामसु पाठात् (*purāṇānāmedaṃ praśnaṃ pradiva iti purāṇanāmasu pāṭhāt*), as it is read among the names of the ancient. उराणः (*urāṇaḥ*) is one who makes much even of a small oblation, since Yāska has said उराण उरु कुर्वाण इति (*urāṇa uru kurvāṇa iti*). विदुष्टरः (*viduṣṭaraḥ*) is more knowing. You, the messenger of the gods, go (ईयसे (*īyase*), गच्छसि (*gacchasi*)) to offer the oblations to the gods, to the ascents (आरोधनानि (*ārodhanāni*), *ārohaṇāni*) of heaven (दिवः (*divaḥ*)), that is, the places fit for ascending.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—(O Agni) the all-knowing one
- अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—of the sacrifice
- दूत्यानि (*dūtyāni*)—the messenger-offices
- वेः (*veḥ*)—knowing them
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—and the atmosphere that lies between them
- संचिकित्वान् (*saṃcikitvān*)—having fully known

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने रुशतो रोचमानस्य ते तव संबंध्यत्रैम । एमञ्शब्देन गमनमार्ग उच्यते । एम वर्त्म कृष्णं कृष्णवर्णं भवति । भास्तव संबंधीनि दीप्तिः पुरः
> पुरस्ताद्भवति । चरिष्णु संचरणशीलमर्चिस्त्वदीयं तेजो वपुषां वपुष्मतां रूपवतां । तेजस्विनामित्यर्थः । एकमिन्मुख्यमेव भवति । यद्यं त्वामप्रवीता अनुपगता यजमाना गर्भं त्वज्जननहेतुमरणिं दधते ह । धारयंति खलु । स त्वं
> सद्यश्चित्सद्य एव जात उत्पन्नः सन् दूतो भवसीदु । यजमानस्य दूतो भवस्येव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressing Agni, "the shining one", Sāyaṇa explains एम (*ema*) as the path of going; this path of yours is black in colour. Your radiance (भाः (*bhāḥ*)) lies in front. Your moving flame (चरिष्णु (*cariṣṇu*) अर्चिः (*arciḥ*)), your brilliance, is the chief of all embodied, form-bearing, radiant beings. When the sacrificers who have approached you (अप्रवीता (*apravītā*)) hold the "germ" (गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)), meaning the fire-drill, the cause of your birth, you, born that very moment, become the sacrificer's messenger.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, your path, shining one, is black in colour. Your radiance is well known before you. Your moving flame has a splendour peculiarly its own even among all those of luminous form. When the sacrificers filled with faith hold the fire-drills that beget you, you, born at that very moment, become the messenger of the gods.

Dark is the path of you who are bright ; the light is before you ; your moving radiance is the chief of (all luminous) bodies : when the present (worshippers) take up the germ (in the sticks of attrition) you are speedily generated, and become indeed the messenger (of the sacrifice.)
