##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अमृत अमरणशीलाग्ने देवयंतो देवानिच्छंतो मर्ता मनुष्या
> यजमानास्तां धीभिः स्तुतिभिः कर्मभिर्वा आ विवासंति । समंतात्परिचरंति। कीदृशं
> त्वां । प्रथमं देवानामाद्यं देवं द्योतमानं मंद्रजिह्वं । देवानां मादयित्रि जिह्वा यस्य तं । द्वेषोयुतं द्वेषसां पापानां पृथक्कर्तारं दमूनसं
> रक्षसां दमनकरेण मनसोपेतं । दमूनःशब्दस्य कथमयमर्थ इति दमूना
> दममना वा दानमना वा दांतमना वापि वा दम इति गृहनाम तन्ननाः स्यादिति
> यास्केनोक्तत्वादिति ॥ दमु उपशमने । दमेरूनसिरित्याणादिक ऊनसिप्रत्ययः ॥
> गृहपतिं गृहाणां पालयितारममूरममूढं । प्रगल्भमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O immortal Agni, mortals, the sacrificers who desire the gods, serve you all around with praises or rites. You are the first of the gods, shining (deva), mandrajihva, one whose tongue gladdens the gods; dveṣoyuta, the separator of hateful sins; damūnas, one whose mind is subduer of the rākṣasas. Why this meaning of damūnas? Because Yāska says: "damūnas is of subdued mind, or of giving mind, or of restrained mind; or else dama is a name for house, so one whose mind is on the house." The affix ūnasi is Uṇādi. Gṛhapati is the protector of houses; amūra is not bewildered, i.e. bold.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमृत (*amṛta*)—deathless
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*)—the god-devoted
- मर्ताः (*martāḥ*)—mortal sacrificers
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—chief among the gods
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—the shining one
- मंद्रजिह्वं (*maṃdrajihvaṃ*)—one whose tongue satisfies (the gods)
- द्वेषोयुतं (*dveṣoyutaṃ*)—the separator of sinners
- दमूनसं (*damūnasaṃ*)—the destroyer of rākṣasas
- गृहपतिं (*gṛhapatiṃ*)—the protector of houses
- अमूरं (*amūraṃ*)—the wise
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—by rites accompanied by praise
- आ विवासंति (*ā vivāsaṃti*)—serve all around

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deathless Agni, the god-devoted mortal sacrificers serve you all around with rites accompanied by praise—you who are chief among the gods, shining, with a tongue that satisfies the gods, separator of sinners, destroyer of rākṣasas, protector of houses, wise.

### Printed p. 890

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Immortal Agni, devout mortals worship with holy rites you the first deity (of the gods), whose tongue exhilarates ( them ), the dissipator of sin, the humiliator (of the demons), the lord of the mansion, the unperplexed.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒रे अ॒स्मदम॑तिमा॒रे अंह॑ आ॒रे विश्वां॑ दुर्म॒तिं यन्नि॒पासि॑ ।  
> दो॒षा शि॒वः स॑हसः सूनो अग्ने॒ यं दे॒व आ चि॒त्सच॑से स्व॒स्ति ॥

> *āre asmadamatimāre aṃha āre viśvāṃ durmatiṃ yannipāsi |*  
> *doṣā śivaḥ sahasaḥ sūno agne yaṃ deva ā citsacase svasti ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आरे । अस्मत् । अमतिं । आरे । अंहः । आरे । विश्वां । दुःमतिं । यत् । निपासि ।  
> दोषा । शिवः । सहसः । सूनोऽइति । अग्ने । यं । देवः । आ । चित् । सचसे । स्वस्ति ॥

> *āre | asmat | amatiṃ | āre | aṃhaḥ | āre | viśvāṃ | duḥmatiṃ | yat | nipāsi |*  
> *doṣā | śivaḥ | sahasaḥ | sūno 'iti | agne | yaṃ | devaḥ | ā | cit | sacase | svasti ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वस्त्ययन्यामारे अस्मदिति स्वस्तिमतोऽग्नेयाज्या । सूत्रितं च । आरे
> अस्मदमतिमारे अंहः । आ. २-८० । इति ॥
> हे सहसः सूनो बलस्य पुत्र । मध्यमानोऽग्निर्मथनकारिणां हि बलेन
> जायत इत्यग्नेर्बलपुत्रत्वं । हे अग्ने दोषा रात्रौ शिवः शिवकरो देवो द्योतमानस्त्वं यं यानस्मान् स्वस्त्रविनाशाय आ सचसे । परितः सेवसे। चिदिति पूरणः।
> यद्यस्मात्कारणान्निपासि । यजमानान्वितरां पालयसि । तेभ्योऽस्मदस्मत्तोऽमतिं
> पापरूपामशनेच्छामारे दूरे कुरु । अशनाया वै पाप्मामतिः । ऐ. ब्रा. २-२ ।
> इति ब्राह्मणं । आरे दूरेऽस्मत्तोऽंहः पापं कुरु । आरे इति दूरनामैतत् ।
> अस्मत्त आरे दूरे दुर्मतिं दुर्मनस्त्वं कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the yājyā of Agni Svastimat in the Svastyayanī ishti; it is prescribed in the sūtra आरे अस्मदमतिमारे अंहः (*āre asmadamatimāre aṃhaḥ*) (Ā. 2-80). "O son of strength (sahas)": fire, when churned, is born from the strength of the churners, hence Agni is called the son of strength. O Agni, auspicious by night, shining, you attend all around us for our well-being (चित् (*cit*) is expletive); since you protect the sacrificers, remove far from us amati, i.e. the desire to eat, which is sin. Quoted: अशनाया वै पाप्मामतिः (*aśanāyā vai pāpmāmatiḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 2-2), thus the Brāhmaṇa. Make sin (aṃhas) far from us. आरे (*āre*) is a name for "far". Make ill-mindedness far from us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O son of strength
- अग्ने (*agne*)—Agni
- दोषा (*doṣā*)—in the nights
- शिवः (*śivaḥ*)—auspicious
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—you, the shining
- यत् (*yat*)—with which gracious intention
- स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—for imperishable welfare
- यं (*yaṃ*)—us, the sacrificers whom
- आ सचसे चित् (*ā sacase cit*)—you attend all around
- निपासि (*nipāsi*)—you protect us the sacrificers
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us
- अमतिं (*amatiṃ*)—evil-mindedness
- आरे (*āre*)—keep far
- अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—sin
- आरे (*āre*)—make far
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- दुर्मतिं (*durmatiṃ*)—even sinful thought
- आरे (*āre*)—make far from us

### Printed p. 891

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of strength, you who are auspicious by night and shining, with whatever gracious intention you attend all around us the sacrificers for imperishable welfare, make evil-mindedness, the sin caused by poverty, and all sinful thought remain far from those same sacrificers, us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, son of strength, since you protect (your worshippers), far (remove) from us all iniquity ; far ( remove from us ) sin; far (from us) all evil thoughts; for prosperous is he of whom you, who are radiant by night, promote the well-being.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the ishti called Svastyayanī, this Ṛk आरे अस्मत् (*āre asmat*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra when the oblation is offered to Agni Svastimat. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra आरे अस्मदमतिमारे अंहः (*āre asmadamatimāre aṃhaḥ*) (Ā. 2-10). The bhāṣyakāra quotes the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence अशनाया वै पाप्मामतिः (*aśanāyā vai pāpmāmatiḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 2-2). This matter was explained clearly when we expounded Ṛk 3-8-2 (Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 15, pp. 82-83).**NOTE**

## Sūkta 12 (Maṇḍala 4)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्त्वामग्न इति षडृचं द्वितीयं सूक्तं । वामदेव ऋषिः । त्रैष्टुभं
> छंदः । अग्निर्देवता । यस्त्वामित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोः पूर्वसूक्तेन सहोक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second sūkta, of six Ṛks, beginning यस्त्वामग्न (*yastvāmagna*). The seer is Vāmadeva, the metre Triṣṭubh, the deity Agni; the Anukramaṇī says यस्त्वां (*yastvāṃ*). Its application, together with the preceding sūkta, is stated for the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina śastra.

### Printed p. 892

> अनुवादवु—यस्त्वामग्ने ऎंब ई सूक्तवु ऎरडनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि ऎरडनॆय सूक्तवु.
> इदरल्लि आरु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ वामदेवनु ऋषियु ; अग्नियु देवतॆयु ; त्रिष्टुप्
> छंदस्सु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि—यस्त्वां ऎंदु मॊदलागि हेळिरुवुदु. प्रातरनुवाक मत्तु
> आश्विनशस्त्रमंत्रपठनक्कागि हिंदिन सूक्तदॊडनॆ ई सूक्तद विनियोगवू इरुवुदु.
> सूक्त-१२
> मंडल—४ ॥ अनुवाक—२ ॥ सूक्त—१२
> अष्टक—३ ॥ अध्याय—५ ॥ वर्ग—१२ ॥
> सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—६
> ऋषिः—वामदेवः
> देवता—अग्निः
> छंदः—त्रिष्टुप् ॥

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्त्वाम॑ग्न इ॒नध॑ते य॒तसु॒क्‌त्रिस्ते॒ अन्नं॑ कृ॒णव॒त्सस्मि॒न्नह॑न् ।  
> स सु द्यु॒म्नैर॒भ्य॑स्तु प्र॒सक्ष॒त्तव॒ क्रत्वा॑ जातवेदश्चिकि॒त्वान् ॥१॥

> *yastvāmagna inadhate yatasuktriste annaṃ kṛṇavatsasminnahan |*  
> *sa su dyumnairabhyastu prasakṣattava kratvā jātavedaścikitvān ‖1‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । त्वां । अग्ने । इनधते । यत्स्रुक् । त्रिः । ते । अन्नं । कृणवत् । सस्मिन् ।  
> अहन् ।  
> सः । सु । द्युम्नैः । अभि । अस्तु । प्रसक्षत् । तव । क्रत्वा । जातवेदः । चिकित्वान् ॥१॥

> *yaḥ | tvāṃ | agne | inadhate | yatsruk | triḥ | te | annaṃ | kṛṇavat | sasmin |*  
> *ahan |*  
> *saḥ | su | dyumnaiḥ | abhi | astu | prasakṣat | tava | kratvā | jātavedaḥ | cikitvān ‖1‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने यतस्रुक् स्रुचा संबद्धो यो यजमानस्त्वामिनधते । दीप्तियुक्तं कुर्यात् । यः सस्मिन्नहन् सर्वस्मिन्नहनि ते तुभ्यं त्रिस्तिवारं सवनत्रयेऽन्नं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं कृणवत् । कुर्यात् । हे जातवेदो जातानां वेदितरग्ने

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, the sacrificer who, ladle in hand, kindles you, makes you blazing; who on every day offers you the oblation-food three times, at the three libations; O Jātavedas, knower of all that is born—

### Printed p. 893

> तव तोषकेण क्रत्वेंधनादिहेतुना कर्मणा प्रसक्षत् प्रसहमानं त्वदीयं तेजश्चिकित्वान् जानन् स यजमानो द्युम्नैर्धनैर्यशोभिर्वा सु अत्यंतमभ्यस्तु ।
> शत्रूनभिभवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes his gloss. Through क्रत्वा (*kratvā*) he means the act that pleases Agni, the act that is the cause of kindling and the like. The worshipper who knows प्रसक्षत् (*prasakṣat*), Agni's overpowering splendour, is to prevail greatly (सु अत्यंतं (*su atyaṃtaṃ*)) with wealth or with fame. In other words, he is to overcome his enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni of born (perfect) wisdom
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यतस्रुक् (*yatasruk*)—holding up the ladle
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the sacrificer who
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- इनधते (*inadhate*)—makes you radiant
- सस्मिन्नहन् (*sasminnahan*)—on all days
- ते (*te*)—addressed to you
- त्रिः (*triḥ*)—at the three times of the pressings
- अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—food in the form of the oblation
- कृणवत् (*kṛṇavat*)—offers
- सः (*saḥ*)—that sacrificer
- तव (*tava*)—your
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—by acts that please you
- प्रसक्षत् (*prasakṣat*)—your unobstructed splendour
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—having known
- द्युम्नैः (*dyumnaiḥ*)—with riches and with fame as well
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- अभ्यस्तु (*abhyastu*)—may he defeat his enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of born wisdom: the sacrificer who, holding up the ladle, makes you shine, and who on all days, addressing you, offers food in the form of the oblation at the three times of the pressings — let that sacrificer, knowing your unobstructed splendour through acts that please you, overcome his enemies exceedingly, with riches and with fame.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May he who with uplifted ladle kindles you, and thrice every day presents to you the (sacrificial) food, knowing your glory, Jatavedas, to be invigorated by the act, surpass (all others) in riches.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इद्धं यस्ते जभरच्छश्रमाणो मदो अग्ने अनेकमा  
> सपर्यन् ।  
> स इ॑धा॒नः प्रति॑ दो॒षामु॒षासं॒ पुष्य॑न्व॒यिं स॑चते॒ घन्न॒मित्रा॑न् ॥ २ ॥

> *iddhaṃ yaste jabharacchaśramāṇo mado agne anekamā*  
> *saparyan |*  
> *sa idhānaḥ prati doṣāmuṣāsaṃ puṣyanvayiṃ sacate ghannamitrān ‖ 2 ‖*

### Printed p. 894

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इध्मं । यः । ते । जभरत् । शश्रमाणः । महः । अग्ने । अनेकं । आ । सपर्यन् ।  
> सः । इधानः । प्रति । दोषां । उषसं । पुष्यन् । रयिं । सचते । घ्नन् । अमित्रान्॥

> *idhmaṃ | yaḥ | te | jabharat | śaśramāṇaḥ | mahaḥ | agne | anekaṃ | ā | saparyan |*  
> *saḥ | idhānaḥ | prati | doṣāṃ | uṣasaṃ | puṣyan | rayiṃ | sacate | ghnan | amitrān‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने यो यजमानस्ते तुभ्यमिध्वं होमसाधनं समिज्ञातं जभरत् ।
> आहरेत् ॥ हृञ् हरणे । लिजर्थे लेट् । तस्य तिप इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः ।
> बहुलं छंदसीति शपः श्लुः । द्विर्वचनादिकार्यं । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वं ॥ शश्रमाण इध्माद्याहरणे श्राम्यन्महो महतस्तवानीकं । आकारश्चार्थे । तेजश्च सपर्यन्परिचरन् यो यजमानो दोषां प्रति रात्रिं लक्ष्मीकृत्योषसं प्रत्युषःकालं च लक्ष्मीकृत्य । कालद्वयेऽपीत्यर्थः । इधान इंधानस्त्वां
> दीप्तियुक्तं करोति पुष्यन् प्रजाभिः पशुभिश्च पुष्टः सन् स यजमानोऽमित्रान्
> शत्रून् घ्नस्सिंसन्रयिं धनं सचते । सेवते । सर्वदा पश्वादिधनसमृद्धो भवतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, the sacrificer who brings you इध्मं (*idhmaṃ*), the fuel, that is, the means of the oblation, known as the samidh. जभरत् (*jabharat*) means "would bring"; the root is हृञ् (*hṛñ*) in the sense of carrying. शश्रमाणः (*śaśramāṇaḥ*) is one who toils in fetching the fuel and the rest. महः (*mahaḥ*) is "of the great you", your *anīkaṃ*, and आ (*ā*) has the sense of "and"; the sacrificer serves (सपर्यन् (*saparyan*)) your splendour as well. Taking the night (दोषां प्रति (*doṣāṃ prati*)) and the dawn-time (उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)) as his marks, that is, at both times, he kindles you (इधानः (*idhānaḥ*)) and makes you blazing. Nourished (पुष्यन् (*puṣyan*)) with offspring and cattle, that sacrificer, wishing to destroy his enemies, obtains wealth (रयिं सचते (*rayiṃ sacate*)); सचते (*sacate*) means "enjoys". The sense is that he is always rich in cattle and other wealth. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the sacrificer who
- ते (*te*)—addressed to you
- इध्मं (*idhmaṃ*)—the samidh sticks, parts of the oblation
- जभरत् (*jabharat*)—lays on
- शश्रमाणः (*śaśramāṇaḥ*)—taking toil at the time of fetching the fuel
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of you, of great nature
- आ अनेकं (*ā anekaṃ*)—the splendour
- सपर्यन् (*saparyan*)—worshipping
- दोषां प्रति (*doṣāṃ prati*)—at night
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—at dawn
- इधानः (*idhānaḥ*)—who makes you blaze
- सः (*saḥ*)—that sacrificer
- पुष्यन् (*puṣyan*)—attaining increase of offspring
- अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)—enemies
- घ्नन् (*ghnan*)—destroying
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth of cattle and the like
- सचते (*sacate*)—enjoys

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the sacrificer who, addressing you, brings the samidh sticks that are parts of the oblation, taking toil at the time of fetching the fuel, worships your splendour of great nature, and makes you blaze at night and at dawn — that sacrificer attains increase of offspring, destroys his enemies, and obtains wealth of cattle and the like.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
He who, labouring diligently, brings you fuel, honouring Agni, your great glory ; he who kindles you in the evening and at dawn ; he, prosperous and destroying his enemies, acquires riches.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निरी॑शे बृह॒तः क्ष॒त्रिय॑स्या॒ग्निर्वाज॑स्य पर॒मस्य॑ रा॒यः ।  
> दधा॑ति॒ रत्नं॑ विध॒ते यवि॑ष्टो॒ व्या॑नु॒षज्मर्त्या॑य स्व॒धावा॑न्॥

> *agnirīśe bṛhataḥ kṣatriyasyāgnirvājasya paramasya rāyaḥ |*  
> *dadhāti ratnaṃ vidhate yaviṣṭo vyānuṣajmartyāya svadhāvān‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निः । ईशे । बृहतः । क्षत्रियस्य । अग्निः । वाजस्य । परमस्य । रायः ।  
> दधाति । रत्नं । विधते । यविष्ठः । वि । आनुषक् । मर्त्याय । स्वधाऽवान् ॥ ३ ॥

> *agniḥ | īśe | bṛhataḥ | kṣatriyasya | agniḥ | vājasya | paramasya | rāyaḥ |*  
> *dadhāti | ratnaṃ | vidhate | yaviṣṭhaḥ | vi | ānuṣak | martyāya | svadhā 'vān ‖ 3 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उखासंभरणीयेष्टावग्नेः क्षत्रभृतोऽनुवाक्या । तथा च सूत्रितं । अग्निरीशे बृहतः क्षत्रियस्यार्चामि ते सुमतिं घोषर्वाक् । आ. ४-१ । इति ॥
> अग्निर्बृहतो महतः क्षत्रियस्य बलस्येशे । ईश्वरो भवति ॥ वर्तमानार्थे
> लिट् ॥ किंच अग्निः परमस्योत्कृष्टस्य वाजस्यान्नस्य रायः पश्वादेर्धनस्य चेशे ।
> यविष्टो युवतमः स्वधावानन्नवान् तेजस्वी वाग्निर्विधते । परिचरते । विधतिः
> परिचरणकर्मति यास्कः । मर्त्याय मनुष्याय यजमानाय रत्नं रमणीयं
> धनमानुषक् अनुषक्तं वि दधाति । करोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The verse is the anuvākyā for Agni Kṣatrabhṛt in the Ukhāsaṃbharaṇīya offering. So it is laid down in the sūtra: अग्निरीशे बृहतः क्षत्रियस्यार्चामि ते सुमतिं घोषर्वाक् (*agnirīśe bṛhataḥ kṣatriyasyārcāmi te sumatiṃ ghoṣarvāk*) (Ā. 4-1). Agni is lord (ईशे (*īśe*), "is master"; a perfect in the sense of the present) of great (बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)) strength (क्षत्रियस्य (*kṣatriyasya*)). Further, Agni is lord of the highest food (वाजस्य (*vājasya*)) and of wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)) such as cattle. यविष्टो (*yaviṣṭo*) is the youngest; स्वधावान् (*svadhāvān*) is possessed of food, or full of splendour. Agni विधते (*vidhate*), serves; Yāska says विधतिः (*vidhatiḥ*) is a word for the act of service. To the mortal, the man, the sacrificer, he वि दधाति (*vi dadhāti*), provides precious (रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*), delightful) wealth, आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*), in continuous succession.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—of very great
- क्षत्रियस्य (*kṣatriyasya*)—strength
- ईशे (*īśe*)—is the lord
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—that same great Agni
- परमस्य (*paramasya*)—of the most excellent
- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—food
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—and of wealth of cattle and the like, is the lord
- यविष्ठः (*yaviṣṭhaḥ*)—the very young
- स्वधावान् (*svadhāvān*)—and splendid Agni
- विधते (*vidhate*)—serves (the sacrificer)
- मर्त्याय (*martyāya*)—to the human sacrificer
- रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*)—delightful wealth
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—according to each man's act
- वि दधाति (*vi dadhāti*)—provides

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni is lord of great power. That same great Agni is lord of the most excellent food and of wealth of cattle and the like. Agni, very young and splendid, serves the sacrificer. To the human sacrificer he provides delightful wealth according to each man's act.

### Printed p. 896

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni is the possessor of great strength, of excellent food, of riches, the youngest ( of the gods ) : abounding in sustenance, he gives to the mortal who worships him precious (wealth) according to (his devotion)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Ukhāsaṃbharaṇa offering, when a Kṣatriya makes the oblation addressed to Agni, this Ṛk, अग्निरीशे बृहतः (*agnirīśe bṛhataḥ*), is to be recited as the puronuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra अग्निशरीरे बृहतः क्षत्रियस्यार्चामि ते सुमतिं घोष्यर्वाक् (*agniśarīre bṛhataḥ kṣatriyasyārcāmi te sumatiṃ ghoṣyarvāk*) (Ā. 4-1). **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यच्चि॒द्धि ते॑ पुरुष॒त्रा य॑वि॒ष्ठा चि॑त्तिभिश्चक्र॒मा कच्चि॒दागः॑ ।  
> कृ॒धी स्व१॒॑गस्मै अदि॑ते॒रना॑गा॒न्वैेनां॑सि शिश्रथो॒ विश्व॑गग्ने ॥ ४ ॥

> *yacciddhi te puruṣatrā yaviṣṭhā cittibhiścakramā kaccidāgaḥ |*  
> *kṛdhī svagasmai aditeranāgānvaienāṃsi śiśratho viśvagagne ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । चित् । हि । ते । पुरुषत्रा । यविष्ठ । अचित्तिभिः । चक्रम । कत् । चित् । आगः।  
> कृधि । सु । अस्मान् । आदितेः । अनागान् । वि । एनांसि । शिश्रथः । विस्वक् । अग्ने ॥ ४ ॥

> *yat | cit | hi | te | puruṣatrā | yaviṣṭha | acittibhiḥ | cakrama | kat | cit | āgaḥ|*  
> *kṛdhi | su | asmān | āditeḥ | anāgān | vi | enāṃsi | śiśrathaḥ | visvak | agne ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यविष्ठ युवतमाग्ने यच्चिद्धि यद्यपि खलु ते त्वदीयेषु पुरुषत्रा
> परिचारकेषु पुरुषेष्वचित्तिभिरज्ञानैः कच्चिदागः किंचिदपि पापं वयं चक्रम तथापि
> हे अग्ने अस्मानदितेर्भूमेरनागाननागसः पापरहितान् सु अत्यंतं कृधि । कुरु ।
> हे अग्ने विश्वक् सर्वतो विद्यमानानेनांस्यस्माभिः कृतानि पापानि वि शिश्रथः ।
> विश्लथय । शिथिली कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O youngest Agni, even if we have committed some offence, through ignorances (अचित्तिभिः (*acittibhiḥ*)), against the men who are your servants (पुरुषत्रा (*puruṣatrā*)), nevertheless make us अनागान् (*anāgān*), free of fault and sin, of Aditi, the earth; make us so exceedingly (सु (*su*)). And loosen, slacken, weaken (वि शिश्रथः (*vi śiśrathaḥ*)) the offences (एनांसि (*enāṃsi*)), the sins we have committed, which are present everywhere (विश्वक् (*viśvak*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—O very young
- अग्ने (*agne*)—Agni
- यच्चिद्धि (*yacciddhi*)—for some reason (by accident)
- ते (*te*)—in your matter
- पुरुषत्रा (*puruṣatrā*)—common to man
- अचित्तिभिः (*acittibhiḥ*)—through ignorances
- कच्चिदागः (*kaccidāgaḥ*)—any sin
- चक्रम (*cakrama*)—if we have done
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us

- अदितेः (*aditeḥ*)—earthly
- अनागान् (*anāgān*)—sinless
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make
- विष्वक् (*viṣvak*)—all-pervading
- एनांसि (*enāṃsi*)—sins
- वि शिश्रथः (*vi śiśrathaḥ*)—destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O very young Agni, if in your matter we have by accident, through ignorances natural to man, committed any sin, make us free of that earthly sin. Destroy those all-pervading sins of ours.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
If, youngest (of the gods), with the inconsiderateness common to men, we have ever committed any offence against you, make us free from the defects of earth ; efface entirely, Agni, our offences.

> *mahaḥ | cit | agne | enasaḥ | abhīke | ūrvāt | devānāṃ | uta | martyānāṃ |*  
> *mā | te | sakhāyaḥ | sadaṃ | it | riṣāma | yaccha | tokāya | tanayāya | śaṃ |*  
> *yoḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने देवानामिंद्रादीनामुत अपि च मर्त्यानां मनुष्याणामभिकेऽंतिके । अभीक इत्यंतिकनामैतत् । अस्माभिर्यत्पापं कृतं महश्चिन्महतोऽपूर्वाद्विस्त्रतादस्मादेनसः पापात्ते त्वदीयाः सखायो मित्रभूताः स्तोतारो वयं
> सदमित्सर्वदैव मा रिषाम । मा हिंसिता भूम । हे अग्ने त्वं तोकाय पुत्राय
> तनयाय पौत्राय शं पापरूपोपद्रवाणां शांतिं योः सुकृतोत्पादितं सुखं
> च यच्छ । देहि ॥
> Vol 17.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, near (अभीके (*abhīke*), "near"; अभीक इत्यंतिकनामैतत् (*abhīka ityaṃtikanāmaitat*)) the gods, Indra and the rest, and also the mortals, men — whatever sin we have committed — may we, your friends, your praisers, never be harmed (मा रिषाम (*mā riṣāma*)) by (महश्चित् (*mahaścit*)) this great, unprecedented, extensive offence (एनसः (*enasaḥ*)). O Agni, give (यच्छ (*yaccha*)) to our son (तोकाय (*tokāya*)) and grandson (तनयाय (*tanayāya*)) शं (*śaṃ*), the quieting of the troubles that take the form of sin, and योः (*yoḥ*), happiness produced by good deeds.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—in the matter of the gods
- उत (*uta*)—and
- मर्त्यानां (*martyānāṃ*)—of men
- अभीके (*abhīke*)—near
- ते (*te*)—your
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—we, who are your friends
- महश्चित् (*mahaścit*)—from the very great
- ऊर्वात् (*ūrvāt*)—and extensive
- एनसः (*enasaḥ*)—fruit arising from sin
- सदमित् (*sadamit*)—always
- मा रिषाम (*mā riṣāma*)—may we not be harmed
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- तोकाय (*tokāya*)—to our sons
- तनयाय (*tanayāya*)—and grandsons
- शं (*śaṃ*)—sin-free peace
- योः (*yoḥ*)—and happiness
- यच्छ (*yaccha*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, grant that we, your friends, when through ignorance we have committed sin, may receive no kind of harm from the gods or from men. Even if our sin is very great, let its fruit not harm us. O Agni, give to our sons and grandsons also sin-free peace and happiness.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Let not us, Agni, who are your friends, ever suffer harm from any great or comprehensive offence against either gods or men: bestow forgiveness upon our sons and grandsons, the reward of what has been well done.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॑ ह॒ त्यद्व॑सवो गौ॒र्यं॑ चित्प॒दि षि॒ताममुं॑चता  
> यजत्राः ।  
> ए॒वो ष्व१॒॑गस्मन्मुं॑चता॒ व्यंहः॒ प्र ता॑र्यग्ने प्रत॒रं न॒ आयुः॑॥

> *yathā ha tyadvasavo gauryaṃ citpadi ṣitāmamuṃcatā*  
> *yajatrāḥ |*  
> *evo ṣvagasmanmuṃcatā vyaṃhaḥ pra tāryagne prataraṃ na āyuḥ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । ह । त्यत् । वसवः । गौर्यं । चित् । पदि । सितां । अमुंचत । यजत्राः ।  
> एवो इति । सु । अस्मत् । मुंचत । वि । अंहः । प्र । तारि । अग्ने । प्रतरं । नः ।  
> आयुः ॥ ६ ॥

> *yathā | ha | tyat | vasavaḥ | gauryaṃ | cit | padi | sitāṃ | amuṃcata | yajatrāḥ |*  
> *evo iti | su | asmat | muṃcata | vi | aṃhaḥ | pra | tāri | agne | prataraṃ | naḥ |*  
> *āyuḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

### Printed p. 899

> यजत्रा यजनीयाः पूजार्हा हे वसवो निवासयितारोऽग्नयो
> यूयं यथा ह यथैव त्यत्यां तां पदि पादे सितां बद्धां गौर्यं चित् गौरीं
> गामप्यमुंचत । त्यक्तवंतो भूयास्त । एवो एवमेवास्मदस्मत्तोऽहः पापं
> सु अत्यंतं वि मुंचत । विमुक्तं कुरुत । बहुवचनं पूजार्थं । हे अग्ने त्वया
> प्रतरं प्रवृद्धं नोऽस्मदीयमायुः प्र तारि । प्रवृद्धं क्रियता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the Vasus: "O यजत्रा (*yajatrā*), worthy of worship, O Vasus, Agnis who give dwelling." He says: "Just as you released even the cow Gaurī that was bound by the foot, so release sin from us completely." The plural (बहुवचनं (*bahuvacanaṃ*)) is for honour. Then, addressing Agni: "By you let our life be made प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*), that is, increased (प्रवृद्धं (*pravṛddhaṃ*)); let it be made to grow."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*)—O you who are worthy of worship
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—Agnis who give dwelling
- यथा ह (*yathā ha*)—in what manner
- त्यत् (*tyat*)—that famous one
- पदि (*padi*)—at the foot
- सितां (*sitāṃ*)—bound
- गौर्यं चित् (*gauryaṃ cit*)—the cow also
- अमुंचत (*amuṃcata*)—you caused to be freed
- एवो (*evo*)—in the same manner
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us
- अ०हः (*a0haḥ*)—sin
- सु (*su*)—completely
- वि मुंचत (*vi muṃcata*)—release and destroy
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*)—most dear **NOTE**
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life
- प्र तारि (*pra tāri*)—graciously grant that it grow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agnis, worthy of worship and givers of dwelling, in the manner in which you caused even the famous cow, bound at the foot, to be freed, in the same manner release sin from us also and destroy it completely. By your favour may our dear life attain increase.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Adorable Vasus, in like manner as you have liberated the cow bound by the foot, so set us free entirely from sin; and may our existence, be prolonged.

## Sūkta 13 (Maṇḍala 4)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रत्यग्निरिति पंचर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं नामदेवस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमाग्नेयं
> तत्तन्मंत्रवर्णाभिधेयोषःप्रभृतिदैवतं वा । तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्रत्यग्निः पंच
> लिंगोक्तदैवतं त्वेक इति ॥ लैंगिको विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta प्रत्यग्निः (*pratyagniḥ*) of five verses is the third sūkta. Its seer is Vāmadeva, its metre Triṣṭubh, and its deity Agni; or else its deities are those denoted by the words of the respective mantras, beginning with Uṣas. So the Anukramaṇī says: प्रत्यग्निः पंच लिंगोक्तदैवतं त्वेक इति (*pratyagniḥ paṃca liṃgoktadaivataṃ tveka iti*) **NOTE**. The application is by the indicatory mark (लैंगिको विनियोगः (*laiṃgiko viniyogaḥ*)).

### Printed p. 900

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "Pratyagniḥ" is the third sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has five ṛks. Its seer is Vāmadeva; its deity is Agni; its metre is Triṣṭup. In this sūkta, along with the Agni praised in the respective ṛks, Savitṛ and the others are the deities of the respective ṛks. The Anukramaṇī says: "Pratyagniḥ pañca liṅgoktadaivataṃ taike." The application is by indicatory mark.

Sūkta—13
Maṇḍala—4; Anuvāka—2; Sūkta—13
Aṣṭaka—3; Adhyāya—5; Varga—13
Number of ṛks in the sūkta—5
Ṛṣi—Vāmadeva
Devatā—Agni
Chandas—Triṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रत्य॒ग्निरु॒षसा॒मग्र॑मख्यद्विभाती॒नां सु॒मना॑ रत्न॒धेयं॑ ।  
> या॒तम॑श्विना सु॒कृतो॑ दुरो॒णमुत्सूर्यो॒ ज्योति॑षा दे॒व  ॑
> एति ॥ १ ॥

> *pratyagniruṣasāmagramakhyadvibhātīnāṃ sumanā ratnadheyaṃ |*  
> *yātamaśvinā sukṛto duroṇamutsūryo jyotiṣā deva*  
> *eti ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रति । अग्निः । उषसां । अग्रं । अख्यत् । विभातीनां । सुमनाः । रत्नधेयं ।  
> यातं । अश्विना । सुकृतः । दुरोणं । उत् । सूर्यः । ज्योतिषा । देवः । एति ॥

> *prati | agniḥ | uṣasāṃ | agraṃ | akhyat | vibhātīnāṃ | sumanāḥ | ratnadheyaṃ |*  
> *yātaṃ | aśvinā | sukṛtaḥ | duroṇaṃ | ut | sūryaḥ | jyotiṣā | devaḥ | eti ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुमनाः शोभनमनस्कोग्निर्विभातीनां व्युच्छंतीनामुषसामुषोदेवतानां रत्नधेयं रत्नधानं । धनप्रकाशकमित्यर्थः । अग्रं प्रति पूर्वकालं लक्षीकृ-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*) is Agni of good mind. विभातीनां (*vibhātīnāṃ*) means of the dawns (Uṣas deities) that are shining forth. रत्नधेयं (*ratnadheyaṃ*) is "the bearer of wealth", that is, it reveals wealth. Taking as his aim the front part (अग्रं प्रति (*agraṃ prati*)) at the earlier time, he अख्यत् (*akhyat*): he becomes fully grown. (The sentence continues on the next page.)

### Printed p. 901

> त्याख्यत् । प्रवृद्दो भवति । हे अश्विनास्विन् युवां सुकृतो यजमानस्य दुरोणं
> गृहं । दुरोण इति गृहनाम दुरोणे दुर्या इति गृहनामसु पाठात् । यातं ।
> गच्छतं । सूर्य ऋत्विगादीनां प्रेरको देवो ज्योतिषा स्वेन तेजसोदेति ।
> उषःकाले प्रादुर्भवतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Aśvins, go (यातं (*yātaṃ*)) to the house (दुरोणं (*duroṇaṃ*)) of the sacrificer who does good deeds." दुरोण (*duroṇa*) is a name for "house", because it is read among the names of house: दुरोणे दुर्या इति गृहनामसु पाठात् (*duroṇe duryā iti gṛhanāmasu pāṭhāt*). Sūrya, the god who impels the priests and others, rises with his own splendour; that is, he appears at the time of dawn.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—of excellent mind
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- विभातीनां (*vibhātīnāṃ*)—of those that shine widely
- उषसां (*uṣasāṃ*)—of the dawn goddesses
- रत्नधेयं (*ratnadheyaṃ*)—that which reveals wealth
- अग्रं प्रति (*agraṃ prati*)—with regard to the front part, which is full of radiance
- अख्यत् (*akhyat*)—has shone, fully grown
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- सुकृतः (*sukṛtaḥ*)—of the sacrificer who does good deeds
- दुरोणु (*duroṇu*)—the house
- यातं (*yātaṃ*)—come and join
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the one who is of divine nature
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—Sūrya, the impeller of priests and others
- ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)—with his own radiance
- उदेति (*udeti*)—has appeared

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, of excellent mind, has shone, grown, having regard to the front part of the widely radiant dawn goddesses, which reveals wealth and is full of radiance. O Aśvin deities, come to the house of the sacrificer who does good deeds. Sūrya, who is of divine nature and the impeller of priests and others, has appeared with his own radiance.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Favourably-minded, Agni has manifested (his might) in regard to the wealth-bestowing procession of the resplendent dawns : proceed, Ashwins, to the dwelling of the pious (worshipper) : the divine sun rises with splendour.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऊ॒र्ध्वं भा॒नुं स॑वि॒ता दे॒वो अ॑श्रेद्ध्र॒प्सं दवि॑ध्वद्गवि॒षो  ॑
> न सत्या ।  
> अनु॑ व्र॒तं वरु॑णो यंति मि॒त्रो यत्सूर्यं॑ दि॒व्या॑रो॒हयं॑ति ॥ २ ॥

> *ūrdhvaṃ bhānuṃ savitā devo aśreddhrapsaṃ davidhvadgaviṣo*  
> *na satyā |*  
> *anu vrataṃ varuṇo yaṃti mitro yatsūryaṃ divyārohayaṃti ‖ 2 ‖*

### Printed p. 902

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऊर्ध्वं । भानुं । सविता । देवः । अश्रेत् । द्रप्सं । दविध्वत् । गोऽइषः । न ।  
> सत्वा ।  
> अनु । व्रतं । वरुणः । यंति । मित्रः । यत् । सूर्यं । दिवि । आरोहयंति ॥२॥

> *ūrdhvaṃ | bhānuṃ | savitā | devaḥ | aśret | drapsaṃ | davidhvat | go 'iṣaḥ | na |*  
> *satvā |*  
> *anu | vrataṃ | varuṇaḥ | yaṃti | mitraḥ | yat | sūryaṃ | divi | ārohayaṃti ‖2‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सविता प्रेरको देव ऊर्ध्वमुन्मुखं भानुमश्रेत् । आश्रयति । यद्यदा
> रश्मयः सूर्यं दिवि द्युलोक आरोहयंति । आरोहणं कारयंति । तदा
> वरुणो रात्र्यभिमानी देवो मित्रोऽहरभिमान्यन्ने देवाश्च व्रतं तत्संबंधि
> कर्मानु यंति । अनुगच्छंति । अनुगमने दृष्टांत उच्यते । द्रप्पं पार्थिवं रजो
> दविध्वद्दुन्वन् । विकिरन्नित्यर्थः । गविषो गा इच्छन् सत्वा न वृषभ इव तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Savitṛ, the impelling god, takes refuge in (obtains) the upward-facing light (भानुं (*bhānuṃ*)). When (यत् (*yat*)) the rays make Sūrya ascend in the sky, in heaven, then Varuṇa, the deity presiding over night, Mitra, the deity presiding over day, and the other gods follow the व्रतं (*vrataṃ*), the work connected with it (their own duty). An illustration of the following is given: like a bull that is desirous of cows, shaking and scattering the earthly dust (द्रप्पं (*drappaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the one of divine nature
- सविता (*savitā*)—Savitṛ
- ऊर्ध्वं (*ūrdhvaṃ*)—facing upward
- भानुं (*bhānuṃ*)—the light (his own radiance)
- अश्रेत् (*aśret*)—takes refuge in (obtains)
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- सूर‍्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—Sūrya
- दिवि (*divi*)—in heaven
- आरोहयंति (*ārohayaṃti*)—(the rays) make him climb (then)
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra also (the other deities too)
- द्रप्सं (*drapsaṃ*)—the earthly dust
- दधिध्वत् (*dadhidhvat*)—stirring up and scattering all around
- गविषः (*gaviṣaḥ*)—desiring to join the cow
- सत्वा न (*satvā na*)—like a bull (in eagerness)
- व्रतं (*vrataṃ*)—their respective duties
- अनु यंति (*anu yaṃti*)—follow and observe

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The divine Savitṛ, rising facing upward, obtains his own radiance. When the rays make Sūrya climb in the sky, that is, when Sūrya, endowed with rays, ascends the sky, then Varuṇa, Mitra and the other deities also, eagerly, like a bull seeking a cow, stirring up the dust on the ground and scattering it all around and following the cow alone, follow and observe their own duties and functions.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The divine Savitri diffuses his light on high, dispersing the dew, and like a vigorous (bull) ardent for the cow : then Varuna, and Mitra, and other (divinities), hasten to (fulfil) their offices when they elevate the sun in the sky.

### Printed p. 903
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यं सी॒मकृ॑ण्व॒नम॑से वि॒पृचे॑ ध्रु॒वक्षे॑मा॒ अन॑वस्यंतो॒  ॑
> अर्थं ।  
> तं सूर्यं॑ ह॒रितः॑ स॒प्त य॒ह्वीः स्पशं॒ विश्व॑स्य॒ जग॑तो वहंति॥

> *yaṃ sīmakṛṇvanamase vipṛce dhruvakṣemā anavasyaṃto*  
> *arthaṃ |*  
> *taṃ sūryaṃ haritaḥ sapta yahvīḥ spaśaṃ viśvasya jagato vahaṃti‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । सीं । अकृण्वन् । तमसे । विपृचे । ध्रुवक्षेमाः । अनवस्यंतः । अर्थं ।  
> तं । सूर्यं । हरितः । सप्त । यह्वीः । स्पशं । विश्वस्य । जगतः । वहंति ॥ ३ ॥

> *yaṃ | sīṃ | akṛṇvan | tamase | vipṛce | dhruvakṣemāḥ | anavasyaṃtaḥ | arthaṃ |*  
> *taṃ | sūryaṃ | haritaḥ | sapta | yahvīḥ | spaśaṃ | viśvasya | jagataḥ | vahaṃti ‖ 3 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ध्रुवक्षेमाः स्थिरनिवासाः सृष्टिकर्तारो देवाः सीं सर्वतस्तमसे तमसो
> विपृचे पृथक्करणायार्थं जगल्लक्षणं कार्यमनवस्यंतोऽविमुंचंतः कुर्वंत एव
> यं सूर्यमकृण्वन् । असृजन्नित्यर्थः । यह्वीर्महत्यः सप्त सप्तसंख्याका हरितोऽश्वा विश्वस्य समस्तस्य जगतः प्राणिसमूहस्य स्वशं प्रेरकत्वेन ज्ञातारं तं
> सूर्यं वहंति । धारयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ध्रुवक्षेमाः (*dhruvakṣemāḥ*) are the gods of firm abode, the creators. All around (सीं (*sīṃ*)), for separating (विपृचे (*vipṛce*)) from darkness (तमसे (*tamase*)), never leaving off (अनवस्यंतः (*anavasyaṃtaḥ*)) but continually doing the work (अर्थं (*arthaṃ*)) that has the form of the world, they made (अकृण्वन् (*akṛṇvan*)), that is, created, Sūrya. Seven great (यह्वीः (*yahvīḥ*)) horses (हरितः (*haritaḥ*)) carry that Sūrya, known (स्पशं (*spaśaṃ*)) as the impeller of the whole world, of the entire multitude of beings; वहंति (*vahaṃti*) means they bear him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ध्रुवक्षेमाः (*dhruvakṣemāḥ*)—gods of firm abode
- सीं (*sīṃ*)—all around
- तमसे (*tamase*)—of darkness
- विपृचे (*vipṛce*)—for separation
- अर्थं (*arthaṃ*)—the work that has the form of the world
- अनवस्यंतः (*anavasyaṃtaḥ*)—doing without cease
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whom
- अकृण्वन् (*akṛṇvan*)—they created
- तं (*taṃ*)—such a one
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of the whole
- जगतः (*jagataḥ*)—of the entire multitude of beings
- स्पशं (*spaśaṃ*)—the one known as the impeller
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—Sūrya
- यह्वीः (*yahvīḥ*)—possessing greatness
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven in number
- हरितः (*haritaḥ*)—horses
- वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—bear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods of firm abode, continually doing the work that has the form of the world in order to destroy darkness, created Sūrya, who is known as the impeller of the entire multitude of beings; the great seven horses bear that Sūrya.

### Printed p. 904

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Seven great coursers convey that sun, whom the (deities), occupants of enduring mansions, and not heedless (of their offices), have formed for the driving away of darkness, (and who is) the animator of the whole world.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वहि॑ष्ठेभिर्वि॒हर॑न्यासि॒ तंतु॑मव॒व्यय॒न्नसि॑तं देव॒ वस्म॑ ।  
> दवि॑ध्वतो र॒श्मयः॒ सूर्य॑स्य॒ चर्मे॒वावा॑धु॒स्तमो॑  ॒१॒॑
> अप्स्वगन्तः ॥ ४ ॥

> *vahiṣṭhebhirviharanyāsi taṃtumavavyayannasitaṃ deva vasma |*  
> *davidhvato raśmayaḥ sūryasya carmevāvādhustamo*  
> *apsvagantaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वहिष्ठेभिः । विहरन् । यासि । तंतुं । अवव्ययन् । असितं । देव । वस्म ।  
> दविध्वतः । रश्मयः । सूर्यस्य । चर्मइव । अव । अधुः । तमः । अप्सु ।  
> अंतरिति ॥ ४ ॥

> *vahiṣṭhebhiḥ | viharan | yāsi | taṃtuṃ | avavyayan | asitaṃ | deva | vasma |*  
> *davidhvataḥ | raśmayaḥ | sūryasya | carmaiva | ava | adhuḥ | tamaḥ | apsu |*  
> *aṃtariti ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देव द्योतमान सूर्य त्वं जगन्निर्वाहात्मकस्य रसस्यादानार्थ० तंतुं
> रश्मिसमूहं विहरन्विस्तारयन् असितं कृष्णवर्णं वस्म नक्तंचराणां निवासभूतां
> रात्रिमवव्ययन् अवाचीनं यथा भवति तथा संवृण्वन् । तिरस्कुर्वन्नित्यर्थः । वहिष्ठेभिर्वोढुमत्यंतं शक्त्यैरश्वैर्यासि । गमनमार्गं गच्छसि । अस्यामृचि पूर्वार्धे सूर्यस्य प्रत्यक्षमर्थ० प्रतिपाद्योत्तरार्धे परोक्षनुर्थ० प्रतिपादयितुमाह।
> दविध्वतो धुनानाः सूयर्स्य संबंधिनो रश्मयः किरणा अप्स्वंतरिक्षे । आस
> इत्यंतरिक्षनाम आकाशमापः पृथिवीति तन्नामसु पाठात् । अंतर्मध्यॆ चर्मेव
> चर्मवत्स्थितं तमोऽंधकारमवाधुः । अवाचीनमदधुः । तिरस्कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O god, shining Sūrya, you spread (विहरन् (*viharan*)) the तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*), the mass of rays, in order to take the sap that sustains the world. Shutting out downward the black-coloured वस्म (*vasma*), the night that is the dwelling of the night-wanderers, that is, putting it down, you travel with the very strong bearers (वहिष्ठेभिः (*vahiṣṭhebhiḥ*)), the horses; you go on your path of travel." In this ṛk, having stated in the first half the visible matter concerning Sūrya, in the second half he speaks to state the invisible matter: the shaking rays belonging to Sūrya, अप्सु (*apsu*), in the atmosphere (आस इत्यंतरिक्षनाम आकाशमापः पृथिवीति तन्नामसु पाठात् (*āsa ityaṃtarikṣanāma ākāśamāpaḥ pṛthivīti tannāmasu pāṭhāt*): "āpas" is a name of the atmosphere, because it is read among its names), in the middle, cast down (*avādhuḥ*) the darkness that stands like a skin (चर्मेव (*carmeva*)); they put it down, they set it aside.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*)—O shining Sūrya
- तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*)—(your) mass of rays
- विहरन् (*viharan*)—spreading (for taking the sap)
- असितं (*asitaṃ*)—black-coloured
- वस्म (*vasma*)—and the dwelling of the rākṣasas **NOTE**

### Printed p. 905
- …the night. (अवव्ययन् (*avavyayan*))—bringing to an end
- वहिष्ठेभिः (*vahiṣṭhebhiḥ*)—with horses having the power of carrying
- यासि (*yāsi*)—you travel
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- दविध्वतः (*davidhvataḥ*)—trembling
- रश्मयः (*raśmayaḥ*)—rays
- अप्सु (*apsu*)—of the firmament
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle region
- चर्मेव (*carmeva*)—spread like a skin
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—the darkness
- अवाधुः (*avādhuḥ*)—they destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Sun, spreading out your mass of rays for the drawing up of the waters, and bringing to an end the night, which is black in colour and the dwelling of the rākṣasas, you travel with horses that have the power of carrying. The trembling rays of the Sun destroy the darkness that is spread like a skin in the middle region of the firmament.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Divine (sun), you proceed with most powerful (horses), spreading your web (of rays), and cutting down the black abode (of night); the tremulous rays of the sun throw off the darkness which is spread like a skin over the firmament.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अना॑यतो॒ अनि॑बद्धः क॒थायं नृज्ज॑ुत्ता॒नोऽव॑ पद्यते॒ न ।  
> कया॑ याति स्व॒धया॒ को द॑दर्श दि॒वः स्कं॒भः समृ॑तः पाति॒  ॑
> नाकं ॥ ५ ॥

> *anāyato anibaddhaḥ kathāyaṃ nṛjjuttāno 'va padyate na |*  
> *kayā yāti svadhayā ko dadarśa divaḥ skaṃbhaḥ samṛtaḥ pāti*  
> *nākaṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अनायतः । अनिबद्धः । कथा । अयं । न्यज् । उत्तानः । अव । पद्यते । न ।  
> कया । याति । स्वधया । कः । ददर्श । दिवः । स्कंभः । संऋतः । पाति । नाकं ॥ ५ ॥

> *anāyataḥ | anibaddhaḥ | kathā | ayaṃ | nyaj | uttānaḥ | ava | padyate | na |*  
> *kayā | yāti | svadhayā | kaḥ | dadarśa | divaḥ | skaṃbhaḥ | saṃṛtaḥ | pāti | nākaṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आयतशब्दो दूरवाची । तद्विपरितोऽनायत आसीनः सन्नयं प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यमानो मंडलाभिमानी सूर्योऽनिबद्धः । केनापि बद्धो न क्रियते । अपि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The word आयत (*āyata*) means "far". Its opposite is अनायत (*anāyata*), "near": this sun, the deity of the disc, who is seen directly, is अनिबद्ध (*anibaddha*), not bound, not made captive by anyone. (The sentence continues in the next block.)

### Printed p. 906

> चायं सूरो नृज्जुर्वाङ्मुखः सन् केनचित्कथा कथं नाव पद्यते । न हिंस्यते ।
> किंचायमुत्तान ऊर्ध्वमुखत्वेन तिष्ठन् कया स्वधया केन बलेन याति । गच्छति ।
> स्वधाशब्दोऽन्नवाच्यत्र तत्कार्यं बलं लक्षयति । अपि च दिवो द्युलोकस्य स्कंभः
> स्तंभः समृतो नाकेन समवेतः सूर्यो नाकं स्वर्गं पाति । पालयति । को
> ददर्श । तत्त्वतः कः पश्यति । न कोऽपि जानातीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Moreover, this sun, though moving with his face turned downwards, how is he not harmed by anyone? And standing with his face turned upwards (उत्तान (*uttāna*)), by what स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—by what strength—does he travel? The word स्वधा (*svadhā*) here means food and points to the strength that results from it. Further, the Sun, the pillar of heaven, joined with the sky (नाक (*nāka*)), protects the heaven. Who has truly seen this? No one knows it, is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अनायतः (*anāyataḥ*)—one who moves near
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Sun, who is also of the form of a disc
- अनिबद्धः (*anibaddhaḥ*)—has a course that is checked by no one
- न्यङ्क (*nyaṅka*)—even while moving with face turned downwards
- कथा (*kathā*)—how
- न अव पद्यते (*na ava padyate*)—is not harmed by anyone
- उत्तानः (*uttānaḥ*)—being with face turned upwards
- कया स्वधया (*kayā svadhayā*)—with what strength
- याति (*yāti*)—he travels
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- स्कंभः (*skaṃbhaḥ*)—like a pillar
- समृतः (*samṛtaḥ*)—dwelling in the firmament **NOTE**
- the Sun—नाकं (*nākaṃ*) heaven; पाति (*pāti*)—protects, this matter
- को ददर्श (*ko dadarśa*)—who indeed could have seen it in truth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Sun, who moves near and is of the form of a disc, has a course that is checked by no one. Even while moving with face turned downwards, how is he not harmed by anyone? With what strength does he travel while facing upwards? The Sun, who is like a pillar of the heavenly world and dwells in the firmament, protects heaven. Who indeed can know in truth such a Sun, of such great deeds?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This sun, not far removed, and unobstructed, whether (looking) downwards or looking upwards, is harmed by no one: what is the power by which he travels? who has (truly) beheld him who, as the collective pillar of heaven, sustains the sky ?

## Sūkta 14 (Maṇḍala 4)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रत्यग्निरुषस इति पंचर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं वामदेवस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमाग्नेयं मांत्रवर्णिकदैवतं वा । तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्रत्यग्निरिति । लिंगोक्तदैवतं
> त्विति तुशब्दादस्यापि सूक्तस्य लिंगोक्तदैवतत्वं ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta beginning प्रत्यग्निरुषसः (*pratyagniruṣasaḥ*), of five verses, is the fourth sūkta. Its seer is Vāmadeva; its metre is triṣṭubh; its deity is Agni, or else the deities named in the mantras. So the Anukramaṇī says, beginning प्रत्यग्निः (*pratyagniḥ*); by the word तु (*tu*) in लिंगोक्तदैवतं तु (*liṃgoktadaivataṃ tu*) this sūkta too has deities as indicated by the text. The application (viniyoga) is as indicated by the text (लैंगिकः (*laiṃgikaḥ*)).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta प्रत्यग्निरुषसः (*pratyagniruṣasaḥ*) is the fourth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has five ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Vāmadeva; the deity is Agni, or else the others who are spoken of in the mantras; the metre is triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it begins with प्रत्यग्निः (*pratyagniḥ*). Because the word तु (*tu*) is used in लिंगोक्तदैवतं तु (*liṃgoktadaivataṃ tu*), the deities of this sūkta are those who are praised in the respective mantras. The application is as indicated by the text.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 14
- Maṇḍala 4; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 14
- Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 5; Varga 14
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Ṛṣi: Vāmadeva
- Devatā: Agni, or the deities indicated by the text
- Chandas: Triṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रत्य॒ग्निरु॒षसो॑ जा॒तवे॑दा॒ अख्य॑द्दे॒वो रोच॑माना॒ महो॑भिः।  
> आ ना॑सत्योरुगा॒या रथे॑ने॒मं य॒ज्ञमुप॑ नो यात॒मच्छ॑॥

> *pratyagniruṣaso jātavedā akhyaddevo rocamānā mahobhiḥ|*  
> *ā nāsatyorugāyā rathenemaṃ yajñamupa no yātamaccha‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रति । अग्निः । उषसः । जातवेदाः । अख्यत् । देवः । रोचमानाः । महभिः ।  
> आ । नासत्या । उरुगाया । रथेन । इमं । यज्ञं । उप । नः । यातं । अच्छ ॥

> *prati | agniḥ | uṣasaḥ | jātavedāḥ | akhyat | devaḥ | rocamānāḥ | mahabhiḥ |*  
> *ā | nāsatyā | urugāyā | rathena | imaṃ | yajñaṃ | upa | naḥ | yātaṃ | accha ‖*

### Printed p. 908

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवो द्योतमानो जातवेदा जातधनोऽग्निर्महोभिस्तेजोभी रोचमाना दीप्यमाना उषसः प्रत्युषसो लक्ष्मीकृत्याख्यत् । प्रवृद्धो भवति । उरुगाया प्रभूतगमनौ हे नासत्याश्विन् रथेन नोऽस्मदीयमिमं यज्ञमच्छाभिमुखमुप यातु । उपगच्छतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the shining god, जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*)—one whose wealth is born—with his splendours, having made the shining, radiant dawns his aim, अख्यत् (*akhyat*): he becomes grown. O far-going Nāsatyas, Aśvins, may you come with your chariot toward this sacrifice of ours; approach it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवः (*devaḥ*)—shining
- जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*)—one of born wisdom
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- महोभिः (*mahobhiḥ*)—with splendours
- रोचमानाः (*rocamānāḥ*)—shining
- उषसः प्रति (*uṣasaḥ prati*)—toward the dawns
- अख्यत् (*akhyat*)—he grows
- उरुगाया (*urugāyā*)—you who are abundantly praised
- नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—O Aśvin gods
- रथेन (*rathena*)—with your chariot
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*)—this sacrifice
- अच्छ (*accha*)—facing
- उप आ यातं (*upa ā yātaṃ*)—please come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is shining, of born wisdom and of born wealth, grows for the dawns that shine with brilliance. O Aśvin gods, who are abundantly praised, come facing this sacrifice of ours, with your chariot.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The resplendent Agni, by whom all is known, has manifested (his might) in regard to the dawns radiant with lustre : far-going Nasatyas, come with your car to this our sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऊ॒र्ध्वं के॒तुं स॑वि॒ता दे॒वो अ॑श्रे॒ज्योती॒र्विश्व॑स्मै॒ भुव॑नाय कृ॒ण्वन् ।  
> आप्रा॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी अं॒तरि॑क्षं॒ वि सूर्यो॑ र॒श्मिभि॒श्चेकि॑तानः ॥

> *ūrdhvaṃ ketuṃ savitā devo aśrejyotīrviśvasmai bhuvanāya kṛṇvan |*

> आ । अप्राः । द्यावापृथिवी इति । अंतरिक्षं । वि । सूर्यः । रश्मिभिः । चेकितानः ॥ २ ॥

> *ūrdhvaṃ | ketuṃ | savitā | devaḥ | aśret | jyotiḥ | viśvasmai | bhuvanāya | kṛṇvan |*  
> *ā | aprāḥ | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | aṃtarikṣaṃ | vi | sūryaḥ | raśmibhiḥ | cekitānaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

### Printed p. 909

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वस्मै सर्वस्मै भुवनाय लोकाय ज्योतिस्तेजः कृण्वन् कुर्वन् सविता
> प्रेरको देव ऊर्ध्वमुन्मुखं केतुं प्रकाशकं भानुमश्रेत् । आश्रयति । वि
> चेकितानः सर्वं विशेषेण पश्यन् सूर्यो रश्मिभिः स्वकीयैः किरणैर्द्यावापृथिवी
> द्युलोकभूलोकौ चांतरिक्षं चाप्राः । समंतादपूरयत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Savitṛ, the impelling god, making light, brilliance, for the whole world, resorts to the upward-turned केतु (*ketu*), the illuminating radiance (भानु (*bhānu*)). The Sun, who sees everything in particular, with his own rays filled heaven, earth and the firmament completely on every side.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वस्मै (*viśvasmai*)—for the whole
- भुवनाय (*bhuvanāya*)—world
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—brilliance
- कृण्वन् (*kṛṇvan*)—making
- सविता (*savitā*)—the impeller of the whole world
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—god Savitṛ
- ऊर्ध्वं (*ūrdhvaṃ*)—turned upward
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—the radiance (भानु (*bhānu*)) that shines like a banner
- अश्रेत् (*aśret*)—he resorts to
- वि चिकितानः (*vi cikitānaḥ*)—who sees everything in a special way
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the Sun
- रश्मिभिः (*raśmibhiḥ*)—with his rays
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the firmament
- आ प्राः (*ā prāḥ*)—has filled completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Making brilliance for the whole world, the god Savitṛ, the impeller of the whole world, resorts, turned upward, to the radiance that shines like a banner. The Sun, who sees the whole world in a special way, has filled heaven, earth and the firmament completely with his rays.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The divine Savitri displays his banner on high, diffusing light through all worlds : contemplating (all things) the sun has filled heaven earth and the firmament with his rays.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

आवहंती (*āvahaṃtī*) is bearing wealth; अरुणीः (*aruṇīḥ*) is of red colour. Uṣas, joined with light, great, wonderful (beautiful to see) with her rays, knowing, has come. Moreover, arousing the sleepers, the shining Uṣas goes with her well-yoked chariot, सुविताय (*suvitāya*), for the one who has attained happiness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Uṣas, who is rich in wealth, of golden colour, endowed with splendour, of great nature, of attractive form through her rays, and who knows all affairs, rises and comes. Waking those who lie asleep, the shining Uṣas comes with a chariot yoked with excellent horses, to bring about welfare.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The great and intelligent dawn, variegated with (many-coloured) rays of purple tint, bringing opulence, has come with (her) lustre. the divine Ushas, arousing (the sleepers) proceeds with her well-harnessed car (to distribute) felicity.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, here in this sacrifice, those well-known chariot-horses of yours, the best of carriers (वहिष्ठा (*vahiṣṭhā*) = *voḍhṛtamāḥ*) and swift goers (रथा (*rathā*) = *raṃhaṇā gaṃtāraḥ*), are to bring you at the time of the dawning (व्युष्टौ (*vyuṣṭau*) = व्युच्छनकाल (*vyucchanakāla*)) of the deity Uṣas; that is, to lead you here from every side. For (हि (*hi*)) these Soma juices are for your drinking of the honey, the Soma. O showerers (वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*) = showerers of desires), delight yourselves in this sacrifice, that is, rejoice.

- अश्वासः (*aśvāsaḥ*)—horses

- इमे सोमाः (*ime somāḥ*)—these Soma juices

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, showerers of desires, may the well-known and swift horses, which bear you and bring you to this sacrifice, bring you at the rising of the dawn. May these Soma juices gladden you in this sacrifice, for your drinking of the honey.

> *anāyataḥ | anibaddhaḥ | kathā | ayaṃ | nyaj | uttānaḥ | ava | padyate | na |*  
> *kayā | yāti | svadhayā | kaḥ | dadarśa | divaḥ | skaṃbhaḥ ! saṃṛtaḥ | pāti | nākaṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आयतशब्दो दूरवाची । तद्विपरितोऽनायत आसीनः सन्नयं प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यमानो मंडलाभिमानी सूर्यो निबद्धः । केनापि बद्दो न क्रियते । अपि
> चायं सूरो नृज्जुर्वाङ्मुखः सन् केनचित्कथा कथं नाव पद्यते । न हिंस्यते ।
> किंचायमुत्तान ऊर्ध्वमुखत्वेन तिष्ठन् कया स्वधया केन बलेन याति । गच्छति ।
> स्वधाशब्दोऽन्नवाच्यत्र तत्कार्यं बलं लक्षयति । अपि च दिवो द्युलोकस्य स्कंभः
> स्तंभः समृतो नाकेन समवेतः सूर्यो नाकं स्वर्गं पाति । पालयति । को
> ददर्श । तत्त्वतः कः पश्यति । न कोऽपि जानातीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The word आयत (*āyata*) means "far"; its opposite अनायत (*anāyata*) is "near": the Sun, the deity of the orb, seen directly as he sits, is अनिबद्धः (*anibaddhaḥ*), bound by no one. Moreover, though this Sun moves with his face turned downward (न्यज् (*nyaj*) = *arvāṅmukhaḥ*), how is he not harmed (नाव पद्यते (*nāva padyate*) = न हिंस्यते (*na hiṃsyate*)) by anyone? Further, standing with his face upward (उत्तानः (*uttānaḥ*)), by what स्वधा (*svadhā*), by what strength, does he go? Here the word स्वधा (*svadhā*) means food and indicates the strength that is its result. And again, the Sun, the pillar (स्कंभः (*skaṃbhaḥ*) = स्तंभः (*staṃbhaḥ*)) of the heavenly world, united with heaven (नाकेन समवेतः (*nākena samavetaḥ*)), protects (पाति (*pāti*) = पालयति (*pālayati*)) heaven (नाकं (*nākaṃ*) = स्वर्गं (*svargaṃ*)). Who has truly seen this? The meaning is that no one knows it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अनायतः (*anāyataḥ*)—one who moves near
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—and this Sun, of the form of a disc
- अनिबद्धः (*anibaddhaḥ*)—has a course that is stopped by no one
- न्यज् (*nyaj*)—even though he moves with face turned downward
- कथा (*kathā*)—how indeed!
- न अव पद्यते (*na ava padyate*)—he is harmed by no one

### Printed p. 913

- उत्तानः (*uttānaḥ*)—being with face turned upward
- कया स्वधया (*kayā svadhayā*)—with what strength
- याति (*yāti*)—he moves
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- स्कंभः (*skaṃbhaḥ*)—pillar-like
- समृतः (*samṛtaḥ*)—abiding in the atmosphere
- नाकं (*nākaṃ*)—heaven
- पाति (*pāti*)—protects: this matter
- को ददर्श (*ko dadarśa*)—who indeed can truly see it?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Sun, who moves near and is of the form of a disc, has a course that no one stops. That, though he moves with face turned downward, he is harmed by no one is a wonder. And who indeed knows the secret of the strength with which he moves, facing upward, and how, as the pillar-like support of the heavenly world and abiding in the atmosphere, he protects heaven?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This sun, not far removed and unobstructed, whether looking downwards or upwards, is harmed by no one: what is the power by which he travels ? who has (truly)beheld him who, as the collective pillar of heaven. sustains the sky.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sūkta 15. Introduction. An account of the rite called Paryagnikaraṇa.

In the first three Ṛks of this sūkta a part of a rite performed in a sacrifice called Paryagnikaraṇa is described. Paryagnikaraṇa is a rite to be performed in order that the substances offered in the fire (the animal, the cooked rice, the oblation, the ghee and so on) become pure and fit to be accepted by the gods in the sacrifice. When an animal is to be offered, it is first tied to the sacrificial post on the sacrificial altar. After it has been consecrated with ghee and the like, the priest called Āgnīdhra takes a burning brand from the Āhavanīya fire and carries it three times round the animal, clockwise. This rite is done not only in the sacrifice but also in the domestic rites, that is, in the homas performed in houses at marriages and the like; there, to purify the oblation substances such as cooked rice and ghee that are to be offered, fire is kindled with pieces of darbha grass, carried round the oblation substance three times, and then put into the fire.

Here the offering is purified by carrying the fire round it. This is still done in all rites. In the Aśvamedha sacrifice there is a slight difference in this matter: instead of bringing the fire round the animal, the animal itself is made to circumambulate the fire. As the Ṛk एषः भागः पुरो अश्वेन वाजिना पूष्टो भागो नीयते विश्वदेव्यः ॥ (*eṣaḥ bhāgaḥ puro aśvena vājinā pūṣṭo bhāgo nīyate viśvadevyaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-3) says, in the Aśvamedha the horse and the he-goat are the animals; of these the he-goat is led round the fire in front, and behind it the horse. For the first three Ṛks of this sūkta, which explain this Paryagnikaraṇa procedure, the meaning explained in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa is given here:
पर्यग्नये क्रियामाणायानुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः (*paryagnaye kriyāmāṇāyānubrūhītyāhādhvaryuḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 6-5).

When the rite called Paryagnikaraṇa is performed in the sacrifice, the priest called Āgnīdhra takes a burning brand from the Āhavanīya fire and, reciting the Ṛk परिवाजपतिः (*parivājapatiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-1-3), carries it three times round the animal, clockwise. For this rite the Adhvaryu addresses the Hotṛ (or the priests of the Hotṛ class) and directs them by the Praiṣa mantra: पर्यग्नये क्रियमाणायानुब्रूहि (*paryagnaye kriyamāṇāyānubrūhi*), "recite the mantras to be recited for the Paryagni rite." Then, accordingly, the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa recites the three Ṛks beginning अग्निर्होता (*agnirhotā*). There is a special point here: although the Adhvaryu directs that the Hotṛ should recite these mantras, the Maitrāvaruṇa recites them with the Hotṛ's permission. This manner of reciting is called Upapraiṣa mantra. In some sacrifices, the Soma and others, the Maitrāvaruṇa himself gives the Praiṣa mantra for the recitation of the Yājyā mantras. As the sign of his authority to give this direction the Maitrāvaruṇa has a staff (daṇḍa). Holding that staff, the Maitrāvaruṇa exercises his authority by directing the various priests in the rites each has to perform. This is stated in the Yajurveda sentence:
क्रीते सोमे मैत्रावरुणाय दंडं प्रयच्छति मैत्रावरुणो हि पुरस्तादृत्विग्भो वाचं विभजति । (*krīte some maitrāvaruṇāya daṃḍaṃ prayacchati maitrāvaruṇo hi purastādṛtvigbho vācaṃ vibhajati |*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 6-1-4-2). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 914

The three Ṛks that the Maitrāvaruṇa recites are explained thus:
आग्निर्होता नो अध्यस्त इति तृचमाग्नेयं गायत्रमन्वाह पर्यग्निक्रियमाणे स्वयैवैनं तद्देवतया स्वेन छंदसा समर्धयति । (*āgnirhotā no adhyasta iti tṛcamāgneyaṃ gāyatramanvāha paryagnikriyamāṇe svayaivainaṃ taddevatayā svena chaṃdasā samardhayati |*).

### Printed p. 915

Because the fire is carried round the animal, this rite is called Paryagni. That in this rite the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa should recite the three Ṛks beginning अग्निर्होता (*agnirhotā*) has been stated by the sage Āśvalāyana in the Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra प्रेषितो मैत्रावरुणोऽग्निर्होता न इति तृचं पर्यग्नयेऽन्वाह (*preṣito maitrāvaruṇo 'gnirhotā na iti tṛcaṃ paryagnaye 'nvāha*). Since the name of Agni stands at the beginning of these three Ṛks, not only is Agni the deity of these mantras, but Gāyatrī, the metre of Agni, is the metre of all three Ṛks. Thus, since Agni is the deity of the mantras and the metre too is Gāyatrī, which is dear to the deity Agni, by reciting mantras furnished with the deity and metre suited to this rite, the prominence of the deity is, as it were, increased.

वाजी सन्परिणीयत इति वाजिनमिव ह्येनं संतं परिणयंति ॥ (*vājī sanpariṇīyata iti vājinamiva hyenaṃ saṃtaṃ pariṇayaṃti ‖*). The word वाजी (*vājī*) means "one who has food" or "one who has motion". Therefore the priests here praise Agni with the word वाजि (*vāji*) and make him go round the animal. Here the animal offered to the gods is the food (the oblation); the three-fold circuit is Agni's motion. Thus the qualities that are the meanings of the word वाजि (*vāji*), having food and having motion, are, as it were, in Agni.

परित्रिविष्ट्यध्वरं यात्यग्नी रथीरिवेत्येष हि रथीरिवाध्वरं परियाति । परि वाजपतिः कविरित्येष हि वाजानां पतिः ॥ (*paritriviṣṭyadhvaraṃ yātyagnī rathīrivetyeṣa hi rathīrivādhvaraṃ pariyāti | pari vājapatiḥ kavirityeṣa hi vājānāṃ patiḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 6-5). The sentence in the mantra परित्रिविष्टध्वरं परियात्यग्नी रथीरिव (*paritriviṣṭadhvaraṃ pariyātyagnī rathīriva*) means that in this sacrifice Agni circles swiftly round the animal, as a charioteer seated in a chariot travels swiftly. The sentence परिवाजपतिः कविः (*parivājapatiḥ kaviḥ*) means that this Agni, the far-seeing one (who knows everything), is the lord of food, or the carrier of the oblation suited to Indra and the other gods.

The explanation of the rite-part called Paryagnikaraṇa is ended.

### Printed p. 916

## Sūkta 15 (Maṇḍala 4)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निर्होतेति दशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं वामदेवस्यार्षं गायत्रं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । अग्निर्होता दश गायत्रमृषिर्भोधदित्याभ्यां सोमकं साहदेव्यमभ्यवदत्पराभ्यामस्याश्विनावायुरयाचतेति । बोधद्यदिति दृचेन सोमकराजा स्तूयत एष नामिति द्वृचेनाश्विन् शिष्टाभिः षढ्भिरग्निः स्तूयते । अतस्ता एव
> क्रमेण देवताः ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ पशोः पर्यग्निकरणेऽग्निर्होता न
> इत्याद्यस्तृचोऽनुवचनीयः । तथा च सूत्रितु । अग्निर्होता न इति तृचं पर्यग्न्ययेऽन्वाह । आ. ३-२ । इति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकेऽप्याग्नेये क्रत् गौयत्रे छंदस्याश्विनशस्त्रे चायं तृचो विनियुक्तः । तथा च सूत्रितं। अग्निर्होता नो अद्वर इति तिस्रः
> आ- ४-१३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta अग्निर्होता (*agnirhotā*) has ten Ṛks and is the fifth sūkta; its seer is Vāmadeva, its metre Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇikā is quoted: the first six Ṛks are to Agni, the two beginning बोधद्यत् (*bodhadyat*) (Ṛks 7 and 8) praise King Somaka Sāhadevya, the two beginning एष नां (*eṣa nāṃ*) (Ṛks 9 and 10) the Aśvins, and the remaining six Agni; so the deities are those same ones in that order. The use of the sūkta is by indication (लैंगिकः (*laiṃgikaḥ*)). In the Paryagnikaraṇa of the animal the triplet beginning अग्निर्होता नः (*agnirhotā naḥ*) is the verse to be recited (*anuvacanīyaḥ*); so the sūtra: अग्निर्होता न इति तृचं पर्यग्न्ययेऽन्वाह (*agnirhotā na iti tṛcaṃ paryagnyaye 'nvāha*) (Ā. 3-2). This triplet is also used in the Prātaranuvāka, for the Āgneya Kratu in the Gāyatra metre and in the Āśvina Śastra; so the sūtra: अग्निर्होता नो अद्वर इति तिस्रः (*agnirhotā no advara iti tisraḥ*) (Ā. 4-13). **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning अग्निर्होता (*agnirhotā*) is the fifth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. Vāmadeva is its seer; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: अग्निर्होता दश गायत्रमृषिर्भोधत् इत्याभ्यां सोमकं साहदेन्यमभ्यवदत्पराभ्यामस्याश्विनानायुरयाचत (*agnirhotā daśa gāyatramṛṣirbhodhat ityābhyāṃ somakaṃ sāhadenyamabhyavadatparābhyāmasyāśvinānāyurayācata*). In the two Ṛks beginning बोधद्यत् (*bodhadyat*) (Ṛks 7 and 8) there is praise of King Somaka; in the two Ṛks beginning एष नां (*eṣa nāṃ*) (Ṛks 9 and 10) there is praise of the Aśvin deities, and in the remaining Ṛks praise of Agni. Therefore the deities of the respective Ṛks are, in order, those praised in them. The use of the sūkta is by indication. And in the rite called Paryagnikaraṇa, carrying fire round the animal, the three Ṛks beginning अग्निर्होता नः (*agnirhotā naḥ*) are to be recited as the Anuvacanīya mantra, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अग्निर्होता न इति तृचं पर्यग्न्ययेऽन्वाह (*agnirhotā na iti tṛcaṃ paryagnyaye 'nvāha*) (Ā. 3-2). And at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, the three Ṛks beginning अग्निर्होता नः (*agnirhotā naḥ*) are used for the Gāyatrī-metre mantras connected with the Āgneya Kratu and for the recitation of the Āśvina Śastra mantras, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अग्निर्होता नो अध्वर इति तिस्रः (*agnirhotā no adhvara iti tisraḥ*) (Ā. 4-13).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निर्होता॑ नो अध्व॒रे वा॒जी सन्परि॑णीयते ॥  
> दे॒वो दे॒वेषु॑ य॒ज्ञियः॑ ॥ १ ॥

> *agnirhotā no adhvare vājī sanpariṇīyate ‖*  
> *devo deveṣu yajñiyaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निः । होता । नः । अध्वरे । वाजी । सन् । परि । नीयते ।  
> देवः । देवेषु । यज्जियः ॥ १ ॥

> *agniḥ | hotā | naḥ | adhvare | vājī | san | pari | nīyate |*  
> *devaḥ | deveṣu | yajjiyaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> होता देवानामाह्वाता होमनिष्पादको वाग्निर्नोऽस्मदीयेऽध्वरे
> यागे । वाजीत्येतल्लुप्तोपमाकं । वाजी शीघ्रगामिा वोढाश्व इव तथा देवेभ्यो
> हविर्वाहकः सन् परि णेयते । परितः समंतात्पाप्यते । तथा ब्राह्मणं च भवति ।
> वाजी सन्सरि णेयत इति वाजिनमिव ह्येनं संतं परिणयंति । ऐ. ब्रा. २-५ । इति ।
> कीदृशोऽग्निः। देवेषु द्योतमानेस्विंद्रादिषु मध्यॆ देवो द्योतमानो यज्जियो यज्ञार्हः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is the Hotṛ, the caller of the gods, or the accomplisher of the homa, in our sacrifice (अध्वरे (*adhvare*) = यागे (*yāge*)). वाजी (*vājī*) has its simile dropped (लुप्तोपमाकं (*luptopamākaṃ*)): like a swift-going horse that bears a load, so, being the carrier of the oblation to the gods, he is led round (परि णेयते (*pari ṇeyate*)), that is, conducted on every side. So also says a Brāhmaṇa: वाजी सन्सरि णेयत इति वाजिनमिव ह्येनं संतं परिणयंति । (*vājī sansari ṇeyata iti vājinamiva hyenaṃ saṃtaṃ pariṇayaṃti |*) (Ai. Brā. 2-5). **NOTE**
What kind of Agni is he? Among the shining gods, Indra and the others, he is the shining god, यज्जियः (*yajjiyaḥ*), worthy of sacrifice.

- होता (*hotā*)—the accomplisher of the oblation
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods, Indra and the others
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the shining one
- यज्ञियः (*yajñiyaḥ*)—the one worthy of sacrifice
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- वाजी सन् (*vājī san*)—being the bearer of the oblation like a swift-going horse
- परिणीयते (*pariṇīyate*)—is led around

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the accomplisher of the oblation, shining among the gods Indra and the others, and worthy of sacrifice, is led around in our sacrifice as the bearer of the oblation to the gods, like a swift-going horse.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, the invoker (of the gods), like a horse (that bears a burden), is brought to our sacrifice; a deity adorable amongst deities.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॑ त्रिवि॒ष्ट्य॑ध्व॒रं यात्य॒ग्नी र॒थीरि॑व ।  
> आ दे॒वेषु॒ प्रयो॒ दध॑त् ॥ २ ॥

> *pari triviṣṭyadhvaraṃ yātyagnī rathīriva |*  
> *ā deveṣu prayo dadhat ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । त्रिविष्टि । अध्वरं । याति । अग्निः । रथीः इव ।  
> आ । देवेषु । प्रयः । दधत् ॥ २ ॥

> *pari | triviṣṭi | adhvaraṃ | yāti | agniḥ | rathīḥ iva |*  
> *ā | deveṣu | prayaḥ | dadhat ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवेषु द्योतमानेष्ट्विंद्रादिषु । प्रय इत्यन्ननामेदं । प्रयो यजमानैर्दत्तं हवीरूपमन्नमा दधत् आ समंताद्धारयन्नग्निरंगनादिगुणविशिष्टोऽग्निस्त्रिविष्टि त्रिवारं । सवनत्रयेऽपीत्यर्थः । परि परितः समंतादध्वरं यजमानैः
> कृतं यागं याति । गच्छति । परिगमने दृष्टांतः । रथीरिव । रथवान्पुरुषो यथा
> शीघ्रं याति तद्वत् । तथा च ब्राह्मणं । परि त्रिनिष्ट्यध्वरं यात्यग्नी रथीरिवेत्येष हि
> रथीरिवाध्वरं पर्योति । ऐ. ब्रा. २-५ इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among the gods, the shining Indra and the rest, Agni, endowed with qualities such as that of going forward, holds fully the food, the oblation given by the sacrificers; त्रिविष्टि (*triviṣṭi*) means "thrice", that is, at all three pressings. He goes all around the sacrifice performed by the sacrificers, as a man with a chariot goes swiftly; this is the illustration of his going around. The Brāhmaṇa says the same: परि त्रिनिष्ट्यध्वरं यात्यग्नी रथीरिवेत्येष हि रथीरिवाध्वरं पर्योति (*pari triniṣṭyadhvaraṃ yātyagnī rathīrivetyeṣa hi rathīrivādhvaraṃ paryoti*) (Ai. Brā. 2-5).**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among (for) the gods Indra and the others
- प्रयः (*prayaḥ*)—oblations
- आ दधत् (*ā dadhat*)—bearing fully
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- त्रिविष्टि (*triviṣṭi*)—at all three times of the sacrifice
- परि (*pari*)—around
- अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—the sacrifice
- रथीः इव (*rathīḥ iva*)—as a charioteer comes swiftly
- याति (*yāti*)—approaches

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who bears the oblations for the gods Indra and the others, comes swiftly at all three times of the sacrifice, like a charioteer coming swiftly, and is ready in the sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, thrice (a day), comes to our sacrifice like a charioteer, bearing the sacrificial food to the gods.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॒ वाज॑पतिः क॒विर॒ग्निर्ह॒व्यान्य॑क्रमीत् ।  
> दध॒द्रत्ना॑नि दा॒शुषे॑ ॥ ३ ॥

> *pari vājapatiḥ kaviragnirhavyānyakramīt |*  
> *dadhadratnāni dāśuṣe ‖ 3 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । वाजपतिः । कविः । अग्निः । हव्यानि । अक्रमीत्. ।  
> दधत् । रत्नानि । दाशुषे ॥ ३ ॥

> *pari | vājapatiḥ | kaviḥ | agniḥ | havyāni | akramīt. |*  
> *dadhat | ratnāni | dāśuṣe ‖ 3 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाजपतिर्वाजानामन्नानां पतिः पालकः । परि वाजपतिः कविरित्येष हि वाजानां पतिः । ऐ. ब्रा. २-५ । इति ब्राह्मणं । कविः क्रांतदर्शि मेधावी ना दाशुषे
> हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय रत्नानि रमणीयानि धनानि दधत् प्रयच्छन्नग्निर्हव्यानि
> हवींषि पर्यक्रमीत् । परितः क्रामति । व्याप्नोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वाजपतिः (*vājapatiḥ*) is the lord and protector of वाज (*vāja*), foods. The Brāhmaṇa says: परि वाजपतिः कविरित्येष हि वाजानां पतिः (*pari vājapatiḥ kavirityeṣa hi vājānāṃ patiḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 2-5). कविः (*kaviḥ*) is the far-seeing, the wise. Agni, giving delightful riches to the sacrificer who has given the oblation, has gone around the oblations; पर्यक्रमीत् (*paryakramīt*) means he strides around, he pervades.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजपतिः (*vājapatiḥ*)—the protector of foods
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—the far-seeing
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the one who offers the oblation
- रत्नानि (*ratnāni*)—delightful riches
- दधत् (*dadhat*)—the giver
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- हव्यानि (*havyāni*)—the oblations
- परि अक्रमीत् (*pari akramīt*)—has surrounded, pervaded and stands

### Printed p. 920

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the lord and protector of foods, the wise, the giver of delightful riches to the sacrificer who offers the oblation, stands surrounding and pervading the oblations.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The sage, Agni, the lord of food, has encompassed the oblation, giving precious things to the donor.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं यः सृंज॑ये पु॒रो दै॑ववा॒ते स॑मि॒ध्यते॑ ।  
> द्यु॒मा अ॑मित्र॒दंभ॑नः ॥ ४ ॥

> *ayaṃ yaḥ sṛṃjaye puro daivavāte samidhyate |*  
> *dyumā amitradaṃbhanaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । यः । सृंजये । पुरः । दैववाते । संइध्यते ।  
> द्युमान् । अमित्र्यदंभनः ॥ ४ ॥

> *ayaṃ | yaḥ | sṛṃjaye | puraḥ | daivavāte | saṃidhyate |*  
> *dyumān | amitryadaṃbhanaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः प्रसिद्धोऽयं प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यमानोऽग्निर्दैववाते देववातस्य
> पुत्रे सृंजये । सृंजयो नाम कश्चित्सोमयाची । तस्मिन्निमित्तभूते सति तद्यागार्थमित्यर्थः । सृंजयस्य यष्टत्वं तैत्तिरीया आमनंति । वासिष्ठो ह सात्यहव्यो देवभागं पप्रच्छ यत्सृंजयान्बहुयाजिनोऽयीयजः । तै. स. ६-६-२-२।
> इति । पुरः पूर्वस्यां दिशि स्थितायामुत्तरवेद्यां समिध्यते । सम्यग्गीप्यते । अमित्रदंभनः शत्रूणां हिंसकः सोऽग्निर्द्युमान् दीप्तिमान् भवतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This well-known Agni, perceived before our eyes, is kindled for Sṛñjaya, son of Devavāta; Sṛñjaya was a Soma-sacrificer, and Agni is kindled because of him, for his sacrifice. The Taittirīyas record Sṛñjaya's sacrificing: वासिष्ठो ह सात्यहव्यो देवभागं पप्रच्छ यत्सृंजयान्बहुयाजिनोऽयीयजः (*vāsiṣṭho ha sātyahavyo devabhāgaṃ papraccha yatsṛṃjayānbahuyājino 'yīyajaḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-6-2-2). पुरः (*puraḥ*): on the northern altar situated in the eastern direction he is well kindled. He, the destroyer of foes, becomes द्युमान् (*dyumān*), radiant; "becomes" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the well-known
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—the visible Agni
- दैववाते (*daivavāte*)—of the son of Devavāta
- सृंजये (*sṛṃjaye*)—for the sacrifice of one named Sṛñjaya, as he appeared visibly before
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—on the northern altar in front
- समिध्यते (*samidhyate*)—is kindled
- अमित्रदंभनः (*amitradaṃbhanaḥ*)—that same destroyer of foes
- द्युमान् (*dyumān*)—shines, endowed with brilliance

### Printed p. 921

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The well-known, visible Agni is kindled on the northern altar in front, as he appeared visibly before for the sacrifice of Sṛñjaya, son of Devavāta; and that same destroyer of foes shines, endowed with brilliance.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Radiant in this Agni, the subduer of foes, who is kindled on the (altar) of the east as (he was kindled) for Srinjaya, the son of Devavata.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sṛñjaye: the commentator says that Sṛñjaya was a Soma-sacrificer, the son of Devavāta, and that Agni blazed well in the sacrifice he performed. The name of this Sṛñjaya is mentioned in this Ṛk and also in the Ṛk
स सृंजयाय तुर्वशं परादाद्व्रजीवतो दैववाताय शिक्षन् । (*sa sṛṃjayāya turvaśaṃ parādādvrajīvato daivavātāya śikṣan |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-27-7).
Here it is said that Indra subjected the king Turvaśa to the king Sṛñjaya, son of Devavāta. Sṛñjaya is to be understood as king of the people of that name (the Sṛñjayas). The defeat of these Sṛñjayas in battle is mentioned in the Yajurveda:
वासिष्ठो ह सात्यहव्यो देवभागं पप्रच्छ यत्संजयान्बहुयाजिनोयीयजो यज्ञे यज्ञं प्रत्यतिष्ठिपा यज्ञपताविति सहोवाच यज्ञपताविति सत्याद्वै संजयाः पराबभूवुरिति होवाच ॥ (*vāsiṣṭho ha sātyahavyo devabhāgaṃ papraccha yatsaṃjayānbahuyājinoyīyajo yajñe yajñaṃ pratyatiṣṭhipā yajñapatāviti sahovāca yajñapatāviti satyādvai saṃjayāḥ parābabhūvuriti hovāca ‖*)
(Śai. Saṃ. 6-6-2-2, 3)**NOTE**
The matter of these Sṛñjayas will be explained in the sixth Maṇḍala. See also the account of Somaka, a king of this same line, given in the 7th Ṛk of this same sūkta.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस्य॑ घा वी॒र ईव॑तो॒ऽग्नेरी॑शीत॒ मर्त्यः॑ ।  
> ति॒ग्म जं॑भस्य मी॒ळ्हुषः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

> *asya ghā vīra īvato 'gnerīśīta martyaḥ |*  
> *tigma jaṃbhasya mīḷhuṣaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

### Printed p. 922

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्य । घ । वीरः । ईवतः । अग्नेः । ईशीत । मर्त्यः ।  
> तिग्मृजंभस्य । मीळ्हुषः ॥ ५ ॥

> *asya | gha | vīraḥ | īvataḥ | agneḥ | īśīta | martyaḥ |*  
> *tigmṛjaṃbhasya | mīḷhuṣaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वीरः स्तुता विक्रांतो मर्त्यो मरणधर्मा यजमानस्तिग्मजंभस्य तीक्ष्णतेजसो माळ्हुषोऽभिलषितफलानां सेक्तुरीवतो गमनवतोऽस्याग्नेरीशीत ।
> ईश्वरो भवेत् । घेति पादपूरणः । एतेन यजमान आत्माभीष्टफलं कारयितुं
> समर्थो भवतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The वीरः (*vīraḥ*), the praising, valiant mortal, that is the sacrificer subject to death, may become master of this Agni, who is तिग्मजंभस्य (*tigmajaṃbhasya*) of sharp splendour, मीळ्हुषः (*mīḷhuṣaḥ*) the sprinkler (showerer) of the fruits desired, and ईवतः (*īvataḥ*) endowed with movement. ईशीत (*īśīta*) means "may be master". घ (*gha*) is a mere verse-filler. By this the sacrificer becomes able to bring about the fruit he desires.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वीरः (*vīraḥ*)—one who has power in praise
- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—the human sacrificer
- तिग्मजंभस्य (*tigmajaṃbhasya*)—of him who has sharp splendour
- मीळ्हुषः (*mīḷhuṣaḥ*)—the giver of the desired fruit
- ईवतः (*īvataḥ*)—of him whose nature is movement
- अस्य अग्नेः (*asya agneḥ*)—of this same Agni
- ईशीत (*īśīta*)—may be master

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the human sacrificer, who has extraordinary power in praise, be master of this same Agni, who has sharp splendour, gives the desired fruit and is of the nature of movement.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May the mortal who is strenuous (in worship) acquire authority over this Agni, the sharp-rayed, the showerer (of benefits).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तनुर्वं॑तं॒ न सा॑न॒सिम॑रु॒षं न दि॒वः शिशुं॑ ।  
> म॒र्मृ॒ज्यंते॑ दि॒नेदि॑ने ॥ ६ ॥

> *tanurvaṃtaṃ na sānasimaruṣaṃ na divaḥ śiśuṃ |*  
> *marmṛjyaṃte dinedine ‖ 6 ‖*

### Printed p. 923

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । अर्वंतं । न । सानसिं । अरुषं । न । दिवः । शिशुं ।  
> मर्मृज्यंते । दिवेदिवे ॥ ६ ॥

> *taṃ | arvaṃtaṃ | na | sānasiṃ | aruṣaṃ | na | divaḥ | śiśuṃ |*  
> *marmṛjyaṃte | divedive ‖ 6 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यजमाना अर्वंतं न शीघ्रगामिनमश्वमिव सानसिं संभजनीयं दिवः शिशुं
> न द्युलोकस्य पुत्रभूतं सूर्यमिवारुषमारोचमानं तमग्निं दिवे दिवे प्रतिदिनं मर्मृज्यंते । भृशं परिचरणं कुर्वंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificers daily, every day, worship intensely that Agni, who is like a swift-going horse, सानसिं (*sānasiṃ*) worthy of being served, and अरुषं (*aruṣaṃ*) shining, like the sun, the son of the heavenly world. मर्मृज्यंते (*marmṛjyaṃte*) means they attend on him greatly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अर्वंतं न (*arvaṃtaṃ na*)—who is like a swift-going horse
- सानसिं (*sānasiṃ*)—the venerable
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the firmament
- शिशुं न (*śiśuṃ na*)—like the son, the sun
- अरुषं (*aruṣaṃ*)—of attractive colour
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Agni
- दिवे दिवे (*dive dive*)—every day
- मर्मृज्यंते (*marmṛjyaṃte*)—(the priests and others) attend on greatly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The priests and others daily attend greatly on Agni, who is like a swift-going horse, venerable, and of attractive colour like the sun, the son of the firmament.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
They diligently worship him daily who is like a horse (to convey oblations), who is liberal and resplendent as the son of heaven, (the sun).

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बोध॒द्यन्मा॒ हरि॑भ्यां कुमा॒रः सा॑हदे॒व्यः ।  
> आच्चा न हूत उदरं ॥ ७ ॥

> *bodhadyanmā haribhyāṃ kumāraḥ sāhadevyaḥ |*  
> *āccā na hūta udaraṃ ‖ 7 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बोधत् । यत् । मा । हरिभ्यां । कुमारः । साहदेव्यः ।  
> अच्छ । न । हूतः । उत् । अरं ॥ ७ ॥

> *bodhat | yat | mā | haribhyāṃ | kumāraḥ | sāhadevyaḥ |*  
> *accha | na | hūtaḥ | ut | araṃ ‖ 7 ‖*
